wps.title: Backend-Lint auf golangci-lint v2 lauffähig machen
wps.user_goal: golangci-lint v2 runs green on all three Go modules, with the version pinned identically in CI and the Makefile, so that every WP can show the DOD-01 claim 'keine Lint-Befunde'.
wps.implementation:
Commit cd23a05, merged as PR #40 (8db32ed). The merge message is 'WP-001/WP-002: golangci-lint v2 für alle Go-Module, grüne Frontend-Pipeline' and mentions no follow-up WP.

backend/.golangci.yml:
- :1 version "2"
- :12-24 linters
- :39-54 exclusions (presets and rules)
- :59-63 baseline comment ('~580 findings in ~200 files … cleared in a follow-up work package')
- :64 new-from-rev 257e6fa0…
- :66-71 formatters gofmt and goimports

.github/workflows/ci.yml, lint job :233-262:
- matrix :239
- GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION v2.14.0 :242
- fetch-depth 0 :248
- pin-equality grep :255
- golangci-lint-action@v8

Makefile:
- :72 GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION := v2.14.0
- :79-83 check-golangci-lint
- lint-backend, lint-collector and lint-edgecore targets
wps.tests:
There is no automated test.

Baseline logs:
- runs/lint-backend.log, lint-collector.log and lint-edgecore.log each report '0 issues.'.

Verifier runs with <SP>/bin/golangci-lint v2.14.0:
- edgecore with the repository config → '0 issues.'
- Config copy without new-from-rev (plus relative-path-mode gomod), saved as /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Reticora-CMDB/fbd8a132-b968-552a-84eb-515fd3e8f807/scratchpad/work/verify-B01/nobaseline.yml:
  - backend → '429 issues' in 164 distinct files, exit 1, 18.8s (verify-B01/lint-backend-nobaseline.txt). Counts: errcheck 8, gocritic 291, gofmt 11, goimports 3, govet 80, ineffassign 22, staticcheck 6, unconvert 1, unused 7.
  - edgecore → '6 issues' (verify-B01/lint-edgecore-nobaseline.txt).
  - collector: the auditor's 37 issues were not re-run, because its config is identical (diff shows only the new-from-rev line differs).
- `gofmt -l backend collector edgecore` → 12 files, e.g. backend/internal/search/opensearch.go and collector/collectorcmd/collectorcmd.go.

criteria.criterion: backend/.golangci.yml migrated to v2 schema (version: "2"); previously enabled linters retained
criteria.evidence: The v1 config (git show cd23a05^:backend/.golangci.yml) enabled errcheck, govet, staticcheck, unused, gosimple, ineffassign, typecheck, gofmt, goimports, misspell, unconvert, gocritic, revive and exportloopref. The v2 config maps them all. gosimple is part of staticcheck. typecheck is implicit. gofmt and goimports are formatters (:66-69). exportloopref became copyloopvar. Settings and exclusions are carried over (:25-54). v2.14.0 accepts the config: 0 issues, exit 0.

criteria.criterion: golangci-lint version pinned identically in ci.yml and Makefile
criteria.evidence: ci.yml:242 is v2.14.0 and Makefile:72 is v2.14.0. CI step ci.yml:255 runs `grep -qx "GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION := ${GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION}" Makefile`. Makefile:79-83 enforces the exact local version.

criteria.criterion: Lint job runs for backend/, collector/, edgecore/ (go.work modules) and is green
criteria.evidence: The matrix [backend, collector, edgecore] is at ci.yml:239, and fetch-depth 0 provides the baseline commit. Local runs with the pinned version and the repository config show 0 issues for all 3 modules (baseline, plus my edgecore re-run). The GitHub run itself is not observable.

criteria.criterion: New findings fixed; if >~10 files, set issues.new-from-rev baseline AND create a follow-up WP (documented in PR)
criteria.evidence: The baseline is set (.golangci.yml:64), and the comment at :59-63 promises a follow-up WP. No follow-up WP exists: grep -i 'golangci|new-from-rev|lint' over docs/plan/phase2/* finds nothing, and docs/plan/implementierungsplan.md mentions new-from-rev only in WP-001 itself (:185). The PR #40 merge message does not mention one. Re-verified backlog: backend 429 issues (164 files), edgecore 6, collector 37 (auditor) – 472 in total.

layers.ux: N/A: CI tooling
layers.api: N/A
layers.data: N/A
layers.e2e: OK: the lint chain was reproduced locally with the pinned v2.14.0 and the repository config: 0 issues in all 3 modules
layers.robustness: GAP: lint is green only for code changed since 257e6fa. 472 older findings stay hidden, including 8 unchecked errors (for example json.Unmarshal in internal/agent/pg_repository.go:38 and internal/desk/pg_repository.go:42), 22 ineffectual assignments, 7 unused functions, and 12 files not formatted per gofmt.

wps.soll_ist:
Required: lint on v2, green for all modules, and a new-from-rev baseline only together with a documented follow-up WP.
Actual: the v2 migration, the version pinning and the module matrix are correct and green, but only because of the baseline. The follow-up WP that should clear the 472-finding backlog and remove the baseline was never created, so the backlog is permanently invisible.
wps.evidence:
- runs/lint-{backend,collector,edgecore}.log: '0 issues.'
- /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Reticora-CMDB/fbd8a132-b968-552a-84eb-515fd3e8f807/scratchpad/work/verify-B01/lint-backend-nobaseline.txt: '429 issues', exit=1, 164 files
- verify-B01/lint-edgecore-nobaseline.txt: '6 issues'
- gofmt -l: 12 files
- grep of docs/plan and docs/plan/phase2 for a lint follow-up WP: no hit
wps.deviation: AC4: the new-from-rev baseline was set without a follow-up WP. 472 older findings are permanently hidden, so DOD-01 'keine Lint-Befunde' is only true for changed code.
wps.dependencies: none

findings.title: Lint baseline hides 472 older findings; the promised follow-up WP was never created
findings.repro:
1. Copy backend/.golangci.yml without the new-from-rev line (verifier copy: verify-B01/nobaseline.yml).
2. In backend/, run golangci-lint v2.14.0 `run --config <copy> ./...` → '429 issues', exit 1, 164 files.
3. In edgecore/ → 6 issues. In collector/ → 37 issues.
4. `gofmt -l backend collector edgecore` → 12 files.
5. grep docs/plan/implementierungsplan.md and docs/plan/phase2/* for a lint follow-up WP → none.
findings.expected: Per WP-001 AC4, a follow-up WP exists in the plan that clears the backlog and then removes new-from-rev.
findings.actual:
new-from-rev 257e6fa is still active at HEAD, and no follow-up WP exists in the Phase 1 or Phase 2 plan.
Examples of hidden findings:
- unchecked json.Unmarshal at internal/agent/pg_repository.go:38 and internal/desk/pg_repository.go:42
- unchecked error at cmd/server/main.go:94
- unchecked json Encode in internal/credential/handler.go:85, 105, 126 and 170
- 22 ineffassign findings
- 12 files not formatted per gofmt
findings.user_impact: The quality debt is invisible. The DOD-01 and PR-template claim 'Lint ohne Befunde' is only true for new code. Older defects such as silently ignored JSON decode errors (possible silent data loss when reading corrupt JSONB) are never flagged.
findings.cause: The plan was not amended when the baseline was set. This is confirmed by the config comment at backend/.golangci.yml:59-63, the absence of any plan entry, and the merge message of PR #40.
findings.recommendation: Add a follow-up WP to the plan that clears the backlog by linter category: first errcheck, ineffassign, gofmt/goimports and unused, then govet and gocritic. Then remove new-from-rev. Until then, add a non-blocking CI step that reports the backlog count for each module.
findings.retest: All 3 modules linted without new-from-rev report 0 issues, or the follow-up WP exists in the plan and the CI reports the backlog count.

test_gaps.description: No automated check of the lint configuration contract (v2 schema, linter superset, pin equality, every go.work module in the matrix)
test_gaps.proposed_test:
Positive cases:
- backend/.golangci.yml contains `version: "2"`.
- The enabled linters plus formatters include {errcheck, govet, staticcheck, unused, ineffassign, misspell, unconvert, gocritic, revive, copyloopvar, gofmt, goimports}.
- GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION in ci.yml equals the value in the Makefile.
- Every `use` entry of go.work appears in the lint matrix.

Negative cases, run against a temporary copy: a removed linter, a mismatched pin or a missing module → the check fails.

Edge case: go.work with a trailing comment.

test_gaps.description: The backlog is neither visible nor tracked
test_gaps.proposed_test: Add a non-blocking step that runs golangci-lint with a config copy without new-from-rev and prints the issue count per module (uploaded as an artifact). Once the follow-up WP is done, add a blocking assertion that new-from-rev is absent and the count is 0.

wps.upgrade_conditions: Either a follow-up WP for the 472-finding backlog exists in the plan, or the backlog is fixed and new-from-rev removed (a lint run without the baseline reports 0 issues for all 3 modules). In addition, the automated toolchain-contract shell test passes.
wps.verifier_note:
Confirmed by re-execution:
- backend lint without the baseline: 429 issues in 164 files, the same count as the auditor
- edgecore: 6 issues; with the repository config: 0 issues
- gofmt -l: 12 files
- v1→v2 linter mapping re-checked against git show cd23a05^
- no follow-up WP in docs/plan or docs/plan/phase2, and none in the PR #40 merge message

Corrected line reference: new-from-rev is at .golangci.yml:64, not :62.

Status and priority (P2) unchanged.

findings.title: CI summary only fails on one specific DB skip message
findings.repro: Copy the summary step from ci.yml:152-167 into a script (verify-B01/wp003/summary.sh). Feed it a test-db.json in which internal/jobs TestQueueIntegration is skipped with the output 'TEST_NATS_URL not set'. Output: 'passed=1 failed=0 skipped=1', exit=0.

findings.actual:
Only the literal 'TEST_DATABASE_URL not set' fails the job. These skips would pass silently:
- 'TEST_REDIS_URL not set' (identity/revocation_integration_test.go:21)
- 'TEST_NATS_URL not set' (jobs/queue_integration_test.go:31, discovery/consumer_integration_test.go:197)

wps.title: Abhängigkeits- und Container-Scans in CI
wps.user_goal: Every PR scans the Go modules (govulncheck), the frontend npm dependencies and all built container images (Trivy). Blocking thresholds follow SEC-11, and the reports are uploaded.
wps.implementation:
Commit a8fea01.

ci.yml:
- govulncheck :370-413: matrix [backend, collector, edgecore] at :375; pinned v1.8.0; evaluation :393-405 blocks reachable findings only; upload :407-413
- npm-audit :415-453: `npm audit --omit=dev` at :429; evaluation :432-445 blocks prod High/Critical; upload :447-453
- image-scan :455-507: matrix backend, collector and frontend at :461-469; trivy 0.75.0 with --severity CRITICAL,HIGH --ignore-unfixed --ignorefile security/scan-exceptions.txt --exit-code 1 (:489); upload :499-507

Other files:
- docs/security/abhaengigkeitsscans.md
- security/scan-exceptions.txt: '<ID> exp:<date>', in .trivyignore format
- release.yml:117-129 builds 4 images, including reticora-postgres from deploy/docker-compose/postgres/Dockerfile (ARG TIMESCALE_IMAGE=timescale/timescaledb:latest-pg16 at :7, unpinned)
wps.tests:
There is no automated test.

Verifier runs:
(1) Real npm audit. registry.npmjs.org is reachable directly, because it is in the proxy's noProxy list. I ran it on a scratch copy of frontend/package.json and package-lock.json:
- --omit=dev: critical=0, high=0, moderate=2 (react-router and react-router-dom, e.g. GHSA-jjmj-jmhj-qwj2)
- all dependencies: critical=2 (tinypool through vitest), high=10, moderate=6
- the CI evaluation logic copied verbatim, run on these real reports with the repository's scan-exceptions.txt → exit 0, so the npm-audit job would be green at HEAD (verify-B01/wp004/evalnpm.sh)

(2) govulncheck evaluation logic, verbatim (verify-B01/wp004/go/eval.sh):
- no exception → BLOCK
- exp:2026-10-20 → PASS
- exp:2026-10-01 (expired) → BLOCK
- no exp → BLOCK
- exp:2099-01-01 → PASS
- imported-only finding → not blocking

(3) A real govulncheck run is impossible: vuln.go.dev answers 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403' (proxy policy). There is no Trivy binary, and image builds are blocked (context.md).

criteria.criterion: Explicit Go dependency scan (govulncheck) for all three Go modules
criteria.evidence: The job is defined for all 3 modules (ci.yml:370-413), and its evaluation logic was verified by probe. The real scan was not executable here, because vuln.go.dev is blocked with CONNECT 403.

criteria.criterion: Explicit npm audit step for frontend/ with a defined threshold
criteria.evidence: ci.yml:426-445: High/Critical in production dependencies block; dev dependencies are only reported. Executed with the real registry and the real lockfile: production 0 High/Critical, and the CI evaluation exits 0. The report and threshold work end to end.

criteria.criterion: Container image scan with Trivy for the built images (E-31)
criteria.evidence: The scan matrix covers backend, collector and frontend (ci.yml:461-469). The fourth image, reticora-postgres, is built and released by release.yml:127-129 and is never vulnerability-scanned (release.yml only runs syft for an SBOM, :44-64). No Trivy run was possible locally.

criteria.criterion: Thresholds and blocking per the SEC-11 text (CVE-Fix-SLA Critical 7 days / High 30 days)
criteria.evidence: High/Critical findings block, and exceptions need exp: for govulncheck and npm. The SLA cap is not enforced by machine: exp:2099-01-01 is accepted (probe). For Trivy, the same file is used as a .trivyignore, whose documented semantics treat an entry without exp: as a permanent ignore. This contradicts docs/security/abhaengigkeitsscans.md:41 ('Ein Eintrag ohne exp: gilt nicht als Ausnahme'); not reproduced because Trivy is unavailable.

criteria.criterion: Result artifacts uploaded
criteria.evidence: upload-artifact with if: always() for govulncheck (:407-413), npm-audit (:447-453) and trivy (:499-507), each kept 30 days.

layers.ux: N/A
layers.api: N/A
layers.data: N/A
layers.e2e: GAP: npm audit was executed for real and passes. govulncheck and Trivy cannot be executed here (vuln.go.dev 403, no image build), so only their evaluation logic was tested with synthetic input.
layers.robustness: GAP: the reticora-postgres image is never scanned and is built on an unpinned base (latest-pg16). The SLA cap on exception expiry is not enforced. Trivy treats an exception without exp: as permanent. The dev toolchain has 2 Critical and 10 High npm advisories (e.g. tinypool RCE gadget via vitest), reported only, by design.

wps.soll_ist:
Required: Go, npm and container scans on every PR for all built images, with SEC-11 thresholds and uploaded artifacts.
Actual:
- the jobs and documentation exist
- npm audit works end to end and passes at HEAD
- the Go evaluation logic works
- one shipped image (reticora-postgres) is outside the scan matrix
- no real govulncheck or Trivy run could be observed
wps.evidence:
- /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Reticora-CMDB/fbd8a132-b968-552a-84eb-515fd3e8f807/scratchpad/work/verify-B01/wp004/npm-audit-prod.json (critical 0, high 0, moderate 2)
- verify-B01/wp004/npm-audit-all.json (critical 2, high 10)
- evalnpm.sh exit 0

- release.yml:117-129 compared with ci.yml:455-470
- curl to vuln.go.dev → CONNECT 403
wps.deviation: The reticora-postgres image, built and released since WP-100, is not scanned with Trivy. The SLA cap for exceptions is not enforced, and a Trivy entry without exp: never expires. govulncheck and Trivy cannot be verified locally.

findings.title: Released image reticora-postgres is never vulnerability-scanned
findings.repro: Compare the build-push matrix in .github/workflows/release.yml:117-129 (reticora-server, reticora-collector, reticora-frontend, and reticora-postgres from deploy/docker-compose/postgres/Dockerfile) with the image-scan matrix in ci.yml:455-470 (backend, collector, frontend). `grep -n -i 'trivy|grype' release.yml` → no hit; only syft is used, at :44-64. The Dockerfile's ARG TIMESCALE_IMAGE is timescale/timescaledb:latest-pg16 (:7).
findings.expected: Per WP-004 AC3 and SEC-11, every built image is scanned with Trivy, and Critical/High findings with an available fix block.
findings.actual: The postgres image ships without any vulnerability scan. It contains pgBackRest built from source plus Alpine libraries on an unpinned base image.

findings.cause: WP-100 (commit ea1b6fe) added a new Dockerfile and release matrix entry without extending the CI image-scan matrix.
findings.recommendation: Add {image: postgres, context: deploy/docker-compose/postgres, dockerfile: deploy/docker-compose/postgres/Dockerfile} to the image-scan matrix, and scan the release images in release.yml before pushing. Pin the base image by digest. Add a structural check that the scan matrix covers every release image.

findings.title: Exception expiry is not checked against the SEC-11 SLA cap (and Trivy accepts entries without exp:)
findings.repro: Run the verbatim evaluation from ci.yml:393-405 (verify-B01/wp004/go/eval.sh) on a report with a reachable GO-2099-0001, with security/scan-exceptions.txt containing 'GO-2099-0001 exp:2099-01-01 # far' → PASS (exit 0). The same file is passed to Trivy as --ignorefile (ci.yml:486), and in .trivyignore format a line without exp: is an indefinite ignore (documented Trivy behaviour; not executed here).
findings.expected: An exception lasts at most 7 days (Critical) or 30 days (High) from first report, and an entry without exp: suppresses nothing (docs/security/abhaengigkeitsscans.md:39-41).
findings.actual: Any future date is accepted. For Trivy, an entry without exp: would suppress a CVE forever. Enforcement relies only on reviewers (doc :45).
findings.user_impact: Vulnerabilities can be suppressed far beyond the SLA, or indefinitely, by mistake.
findings.cause: The awk filter only compares exp >= today, and the shared file format means Trivy's own default applies to entries without exp.
findings.recommendation: Add a CI pre-check of security/scan-exceptions.txt. Every non-comment line must have exp:, plus since:<date> and a severity, and exp must not be later than since+7 days (Critical) or since+30 days (High). Alternatively cap exp at today+30 days.
findings.retest: An exception without exp:, or with exp more than 30 days out, makes the pre-check fail.

findings.title: Roundtrip test fails on shared PostgreSQL clusters (cluster-wide role reticora_app dropped)
findings.repro:
Private cluster with two databases, rt2 (empty) and rt3 (migrated to 138 with golang-migrate). Running `TEST_DATABASE_URL=…/rt2 go test -run 'TestMigrationsRoundtrip$' ./internal/database/` → FAIL after 3.81s: 'apply 000056_rls_enforcement.down.sql: ERROR: role "reticora_app" cannot be dropped because some objects depend on it (SQLSTATE 2BP01)'.

The same happens on the shared audit cluster: BEGIN; DROP OWNED BY reticora_app; DROP ROLE reticora_app → '614 objects in database audit_db_01 …'; ROLLBACK (role intact). The cause is 000056_rls_enforcement.down.sql:70 `DROP ROLE IF EXISTS reticora_app;`.
findings.expected: The developer and CI test tooling works on any migrated test database.
findings.actual: It works only on a dedicated cluster, as in CI. This is already known in docs/plan/implementierungsplan.md:10137.
findings.user_impact: Developers cannot run `make test-db` or `make migrate-roundtrip` on shared clusters, and the test also leaves its database dirty at version 55. Production impact is low, because migrating down to 0 is not an operational path.
findings.cause: A role is a cluster-level object, but it is managed inside a per-database migration.
findings.recommendation: Make the role drop conditional, e.g. skip it when pg_shdepend shows dependencies in other databases, or run the roundtrip in a temporary dedicated cluster or container. Document this in the Makefile target.
findings.retest: Run TestMigrationsRoundtrip on a cluster with two migrated databases → PASS, and the other database still works.

findings.title: Compliance evaluation by a client-scoped principal returns and overwrites other clients' results
findings.repro: Principal of org A with Scope.Clients=[c1] and compliance:write; CIs exist in c1 and c2; one active rule; a prior org-wide evaluation exists. POST /api/v1/compliance/evaluations (probe TestVerifyB03Compliance, audit_db_07).
findings.expected: Evaluation and response limited to c1 CIs (or the endpoint refused for non-org-wide principals); c2 results neither returned nor modified.
findings.actual: 200; the response 'results' contain the c2 CI id, ci_type, status and details, and the overall scores span both clients. The c2 compliance_result row (client_id=client 2) is deleted and re-inserted with a new id and evaluated_at. GET /compliance/results for c1 correctly hides c2, so only the POST response and the write path leak.
findings.user_impact: Cross-client disclosure of CI ids and compliance posture of other customers, and integrity loss of other clients' result history. TEN-09 rates any cross-client exposure Critical. Reachable by a standard 'engineer' assigned at client level.
findings.cause: compliance/evaluator.go:28-35 (added in ea88c47) replaces the request TenantScope with database.OrgWideScope. compliance/handler.go:129-134 returns the complete EvaluationResponse. TestComplianceScope (compliance_scope_integration_test.go:32-42) codifies the cross-client write, and the commit message's 'die Ergebnisliste bleibt gescopt' does not hold for the POST response.
findings.recommendation: Keep the caller's scope (evaluate, return and replace only visible CIs/results), or require an org-wide principal for POST /compliance/evaluations (403 otherwise) and run org-wide work through an allowlisted system path. Never return results outside the caller's scope, and rewrite TestComplianceScope accordingly.
findings.retest: Re-run TestVerifyB03Compliance: foreignCI-in-body=false and the c2 result id and evaluated_at are unchanged, or C1-EVALUATE returns 403.

findings.title: Client-scoped principal can rename, cancel and delete maintenance windows that cover another client's CIs
findings.repro: An org-wide principal creates a window with ci_ids [c1 CI, c2 CI]. Client-1 principal: PATCH /api/v1/maintenance-windows/{id} {"title":"changed-by-c1","status":"cancelled"}, then DELETE /api/v1/maintenance-windows/{id} (probe TestVerifyB03maintenance, audit_db_07).
findings.expected: Writes to a window covering CIs outside the caller's scope are rejected (403/404), or the decision is documented. Rows of client 2 are not changed.
findings.actual: PATCH 200 (DB title 'changed-by-c1'); DELETE 204; the window and the c2 maintenance_window_ci rows are deleted (c2-link-rows-left=0). GET as c1 hides the c2 CI id, so there is no disclosure, only a cross-client write.
findings.user_impact: A user of customer 1 can cancel or delete maintenance planning that also concerns customer 2, without customer 2 seeing why. This is a cross-client write path that TEN-09 requires to be isolated.
findings.cause: windowVisible (maintenance/pg_repository.go:41-43) grants access when at least one CI is visible, and it is reused for UPDATE (line 181) and DELETE (line 200). The FK ON DELETE CASCADE from maintenance_window_ci bypasses the restrictive delete policy on maintenance_window_ci.

findings.expected: Non-2xx response (or atomic rollback) and a logged error. The access request stays pending, or a task exists.

findings.cause: iga/handler.go:345-347 '_ = h.repo.CreateTask(...)'. DecideAccessRequest and CreateTask run in separate WithTenant transactions. The real trigger is any DB error after the decision commits (e.g. concurrent connector deletion, DB outage).
findings.recommendation: Run the decision and task creation in one transaction (WithRequestTenantTx), or return and log the error via WriteRepoError. Handle the other ignored writes the same way.

findings.title: Webhook retry drops a partially claimed batch when one organization's claim fails; no fair org ordering
findings.repro: Code path: PGDeliveryStore.ClaimDue (webhook/pg_delivery_store.go:149-160) returns (records, err) on the first failing org. Dispatcher.ProcessDue (webhook/dispatcher.go:504-509) logs, counts and returns on err without processing the records already leased. Orgs come from SELECT DISTINCT without ORDER BY (lines 129-135) and are capped by defaultClaimBatch. Not reproduced at runtime.
findings.expected: A failing org does not delay other orgs (like ExpireDue with errors.Join); claimed records are processed; orgs are served fairly.
findings.actual: Leased deliveries of earlier orgs wait until lease expiry; an org that fails persistently can delay others every cycle; a large backlog can crowd out other orgs within the batch limit.
findings.user_impact: Delayed webhook deliveries for unrelated tenants (cross-tenant availability); no data loss.
findings.cause: Early return in ClaimDue/ProcessDue and an unordered DISTINCT org list. Confirmed by code reading only; runtime impact not reproduced.
findings.recommendation: Continue with the other orgs and join errors; process the records returned alongside an error; order orgs by oldest next_retry_at and cap each org's share.
findings.retest: Integration test with 2 orgs where org 1's claim fails (injected store error): org 2 deliveries are claimed and sent in the same cycle, and org 1 records are not stranded until lease expiry.

findings.title: Review items without candidate CIs leak across clients through GET /api/v1/review-items
findings.repro: probe_review_no_candidate.sql: org with clients c1/c2, collector of c2 with a job; unmatched discovery_result plus review_item kind unclassified_device, candidate_ci_ids '{}' and payload name/management_ip/serial (as discovery.go:1174-1190 writes it). As reticora_app with app.client_scope=c1: discovery_result → 0 rows; review_item with the exact Go predicate of reviews/pg_repository.go:29-31 → 1 row 'c2-secret-fw/10.2.0.1'. HTTP: TestB04VerifierProbe (reviews.NewHandler + PGRepository, client-1 scope) → 'P3 client1 GET review-items: 200 contains client-2 device=true'.
findings.expected: A client-scoped principal sees no review items about devices, collectors or subnets of another client (TEN-05/TEN-06: a wrong client scope yields 0 rows). The review item inherits the scope its discovery_result gets (the collector's client).
findings.actual: Items without candidate CIs (unclassified_device for an unknown type or no profile match, unlicensed_ci, scope_suggested) pass the 'all candidates visible' predicate vacuously, and the DB policy is org-only. Their payload exposes device name, management IP, serial number, raw_data or the collector name, CIDR and client_id of another client. A client-scoped principal with review:resolve can also open and resolve them by id.
findings.user_impact: Users restricted to one customer (client), e.g. a viewer or engineer assigned with scope_client_id, see discovery details of other customers' networks in the review queue. This is a cross-customer confidentiality breach within an MSP organisation.
findings.cause: review_item has no client_id/site_id (000061 omitted it), and reviews/pg_repository.go:29-31 treats an empty candidate list as visible.
findings.recommendation: Add derived client_id/site_id to review_item: from the candidate CIs, or for items without a CI from the collector/discovery job that produced them (as derive_discovery_result_scope does). Add client and site policies with E-09 semantics. Until then, make the Go predicate fail closed for items without candidates for client- or site-scoped principals. Extend TestChannelMatrix with a no-candidate review from a client-2 collector.
findings.retest: Re-run probe_review_no_candidate.sql (expect 0) and TestB04VerifierProbe P3 (expect contains=false). Committed integration test in backend/internal/tenant/rls plus a review channel case in TestChannelMatrix.

findings.title: review_item and metric_sample carry no client_id/site_id; DB-level scope is org-only (AC1)
findings.repro: psql audit_db_08: information_schema.columns for review_item lists id, organization_id, kind, status, payload, candidate_ci_ids, resolved_by, resolved_at, resolution, created_at, updated_at, object_key, action (no client_id/site_id). pg_policies review_item_isolation USING organization_id only. 000071: metric_sample_v WHERE organization_id = app.org_id only. ADR 0001 item 4 defers client/site predicates for metrics.
findings.expected: Per WP-025 AC1 and TEN-02/TEN-05, review items and metric samples carry derived client_id/site_id and client/site policies (or a documented, accepted exception).
findings.actual: Scope exists only in Go: reviews/pg_repository.go:29-31 (fails open, see P1 finding), monitoring/pg_store.go:184-187 and :99-101 (correct, CI-based).
findings.user_impact: No DB defense-in-depth. Any new read path (export, report, job) exposes review payloads or metrics of other clients. The catalog test cannot flag it because the columns are missing.
findings.cause: Migration 000061 omitted both tables. ADR 0001 for metrics was written later and only says 'if client/site scopes later apply'.
findings.recommendation: metric_sample_v: add the sub-select predicate on ci (ADR 0001 item 4). review_item: see the P1 finding. Otherwise record a PO decision and a documented catalog exception with its own test.
findings.retest: Integration test: a client-1 principal selects review_item and metric_sample_v rows of client-2 CIs directly in WithTenant → 0 rows. Inserting through metric_sample_v for a foreign CI is rejected.

findings.title: Derived edge scope goes stale when a client- or site-scoped principal moves a CI; DB then shows edges naming invisible CIs
findings.repro: probe_edge_stale_after_move.sql: CIs X(c1) and Y(c3), edge X→Y created by an org-wide writer. A principal with app.client_scope=c1,c2 runs UPDATE ci SET client_id=c2 WHERE id=X → 'edge after move (superuser view)|t|t', i.e. ci now c2 but edge source_client_id still c1. An observer with scope c1,c3: 'sees CI X|0', 'sees edge naming X|1'. Control: the same move by an org-wide principal re-derives (src = c2|t). probe_edge_stale_site.sql: a principal with sites s1,s2 moves X s1→s2 via location_id → 'edge source_site still s1|t|t'; a sites s1,s3 observer sees the edge (1) but not X (0).
findings.expected: The derived source_/target_ scope always equals the endpoint CI's scope (AC2), so the two-endpoint policy (AC3) hides edges to invisible CIs.
findings.actual: propagate_ci_scope (000061:131-148) runs under the mover's RLS. The edge to the out-of-scope endpoint is invisible to the mover, so it is skipped and keeps the old source scope.
findings.user_impact: A DB-level isolation guarantee breaks. Principals whose scope covers the old and the far endpoint see an edge naming a CI they may not see, and can learn of it via savedview has_relationship filters (savedview/filter.go:117). The relationship list and traversal APIs mask it with Go endpoint checks. The same pattern can stale other multi-reference rows.
findings.cause: The propagation triggers are SECURITY INVOKER and update only rows visible to the mover.
findings.recommendation: Run the propagation (or the whole derivation) as SECURITY DEFINER with a fixed search_path and organization guard, or forbid scope changes of CIs that have edges to out-of-scope CIs. Add a test with a scoped mover.
findings.retest: Re-run both probes: edge source scope must follow (c2/s2) and the observer must see 0 edges. Committed test in ci_children_integration_test.go with the move performed through WithTenant by a multi-client and a multi-site principal.

findings.title: Client-scoped principal cannot create a relationship to an org-wide (client NULL) CI it can see
findings.repro: Re-ran probe_edge_orgwide.sql on audit_db_08: 'client1 sees org-wide CI|1', then INSERT ci_relationship own→shared → 'ERROR: new row violates row-level security policy for table ci_relationship'. The same happens for network_interface on the org-wide CI.
findings.expected: Unspecified (needs a PO decision): E-09 forbids writing org-wide rows, but an edge from an own CI to shared infrastructure is not itself org-wide.
findings.actual: WITH CHECK requires both endpoint clients in scope (000061:239-241, 000063:84-86).
findings.user_impact: MSP technicians restricted to one client cannot model dependencies on shared org-wide infrastructure.
findings.cause: Strict both-endpoint WITH CHECK.
findings.recommendation: Get a PO decision. If allowed: (source NULL or in scope) AND (target NULL or in scope) AND at least one endpoint non-NULL and in scope, analogous for site.
findings.retest: Re-run probe_edge_orgwide.sql and add a case to ci_children_integration_test.go.

findings.title: POST /api/v1/relationships with an out-of-scope endpoint answers 500 instead of a 4xx
findings.repro: TestB04VerifierProbe (relationship handler + PG repo, client-1 scope): 'P1 client1 POST relationship own->foreign(client2): 500 {"detail":"the request could not be completed"…}'; control own→own2 → 201. Real-stack log SP/work/tenant-iso-final.log T14 shows the same 500 cross-org.
findings.expected: 403/404/422 problem response (API-03), nothing stored.
findings.actual: Create returns fmt.Errorf('not found') when the INSERT … WHERE EXISTS(ci) selects no row (pg_repository.go:188-217). WriteRepoError maps unknown errors to 500 (api/dberrors.go:83-88).

findings.cause: Plain 'not found' error not mapped by the handler.
findings.recommendation: Return a typed not-found error and map it to 404 (or 422 with field source_ci_id/target_ci_id).
findings.retest: HTTP test: client-1 principal POST to a client-2 target → 404/422 and no row; cross-org → 404.

wps.user_goal: One canonical location tree (site > building > room > rack; site > warehouse > zone > shelf > bin) with an ltree path. The DB enforces the parent matrix and the cycle guard, and site/client are derived from the tree and protected by RLS.

wps.title: Modultabellen mit Objektbezug erben Bereichsrechte (Dokumente, Tickets, Wartung, Schlüssel)
wps.user_goal: Documents, tickets, ticket comments, maintenance windows and key assignments inherit client/site of the referenced CI/asset/ticket/key. Scoped principals neither see nor change module data of other clients or sites.
wps.implementation: backend/migrations/000064_module_object_scope.up.sql: derived columns for ticket, ticket_comment, document_link, maintenance_window_ci, key_assignment (client only) :27-33, triggers :37-102, propagation :106-156; link counters link_count/ci_count with SECURITY INVOKER count triggers :160-193 and visible-parent guard :198-220; document/maintenance_window policies 'count = 0 OR EXISTS visible link', WITH CHECK org-only :275-287; restrictive document_/maintenance_window_scoped_update/delete are org-only (000079, pg_policies). Go: document/pg_repository.go:80-81 documentVisible (same semantics), :326-337 Delete; maintenance/pg_repository.go:42-43. disposal_record untouched (org-only policy; Go disposalVisible disposal/pg_repository.go:38-39).

wps.soll_ist: SOLL: module rows inherit client/site from the referenced object, and writes outside the scope are rejected. IST: inheritance works for links/tickets/comments/window CIs/key assignments. document/maintenance_window use an 'any visible link' model. Through the real API, a partially scoped principal can delete shared documents (other clients' links cascade away), create and change org-wide documents (against E-09), and hijack org-wide documents. The counters behind the policy drift and can be tampered with. disposal_record (MGT-02 'schließt') remains org-only at DB level.

Verifier: probe_http.out P4 lines, probe_doc_link_count.out, re-run of probe_doc_shared_delete.sql ('DELETE 1', 'client2 asset links|0') and probe_window_shared_delete.sql ('client2 window entries left|0').

findings.title: Partially scoped principal can modify/delete a shared document or maintenance window; FK cascade deletes other clients' links (reproduced via HTTP API)
findings.repro: TestB04VerifierProbe: document linked to a client-1 CI and a client-2 asset; a client-1 principal sends DELETE /api/v1/documents/{id} → 204; Admin counts client-2 asset links → 0. SQL: re-run probe_doc_shared_delete.sql ('client1 sees links|1', 'UPDATE 1', 'DELETE 1', 'client2 asset links|0') and probe_window_shared_delete.sql ('client2 window entries left|0').
findings.expected: Writes affecting objects outside the principal's scope are rejected (AC2). A client-1 principal may remove only its own link, not the multi-client row.
findings.actual: USING admits the row once one link is visible. The restrictive document_/maintenance_window_scoped_update/delete policies check only the org. The FK cascade on document_link/maintenance_window_ci removes client-2 rows. Go documentVisible/windowVisible use the same semantics.
findings.user_impact: A technician of client A deletes or renames documents or maintenance windows shared with client B, silently removing B's references (cross-client data loss). G1 exposure is limited because the modules are off by default, but E-03 requires this fix.
findings.cause: 000064:275-287 and 000079 restrictive policies check only the org; the visibility rule is 'any link visible'.
findings.recommendation: Restrictive UPDATE/DELETE policies requiring all links visible (e.g. link_count = (SELECT count(*) FROM document_link l WHERE l.document_id = document.id), counted under RLS; analogous for ci_count). Alternatively allow partial principals only to unlink their own links. Align the Go predicates.
findings.retest: Re-run TestB04VerifierProbe P4 (expect 404/403 and client-2 links intact) and both SQL probes. Add the negative cases to module_object_integration_test.go.

findings.title: Unlinked documents/windows are org-wide but client-scoped principals can create, change, delete and 'hijack' them (E-09/TEN-05)
findings.repro: TestB04VerifierProbe as a client-1 principal: PATCH /api/v1/documents/{orgWideDoc} → 200; POST /api/v1/documents (no link) → 201; POST /api/v1/documents/{orgWideDoc}/links to an own CI → 201, after which a client-2 principal gets GET /api/v1/documents/{orgWideDoc} → 404. SQL: probe_doc_link_count.sql part C (UPDATE 1 / INSERT / DELETE 1 on the unlinked document).
findings.expected: E-09 / TEN-05: a client-scoped principal can read but not create or change org-wide rows. Linking an org-wide document must not remove it from other clients' view.
findings.actual: An unlinked document (link_count = 0) passes USING for every principal, and WITH CHECK and the restrictive policies only check the org.
findings.user_impact: Client-scoped users can rename or delete organisation-wide policies and manuals, create org-wide documents, and remove shared documents from other clients' view by linking them to their own CI.
findings.cause: The multi-object policy design treats 'no links' as org-wide but does not apply the E-09 write restriction to it.
findings.recommendation: Restrictive INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE: for scoped principals require link_count > 0 and all links visible. Linking an org-wide document requires an org-wide principal, or a PO decision on intended semantics.
findings.retest: HTTP test: client-1 PATCH/DELETE of an unlinked document → 403/404; POST without link → 403 (or create-with-link only); a link from client 1 to an org-wide document → 403. Org-wide principal → allowed.

findings.title: link_count/ci_count drift under RLS and are directly writable; documents can become invisible to everyone or be exposed to unrelated clients
findings.repro: probe_doc_link_count.sql. A: document linked to a c1 CI and a c2 asset (link_count 2). A client-1 principal deletes its own link → 'actual links / link_count|1|2'. A client-2 principal deletes the last link → '|0|2', and an org-wide principal sees it: 'A3 …|0'. B: a client-1 principal runs UPDATE document SET link_count = 0 on a c1+c2 document → 'B1 client-3 principal (no link) sees the c1+c2 document after tampering|1|shared c1+c2 (B)'.
findings.expected: 000064:20-23 states 'the counters stay exact; a decrement finds no row only when the parent is deleted'. Counters must not be writable by tenants.
findings.actual: count_document_links/count_maintenance_window_cis run as invoker. The decrement UPDATE is skipped silently when the remover no longer sees the parent. link_count/ci_count are ordinary writable columns with an org-only WITH CHECK.
findings.user_impact: Currently DB-level only: there is no unlink endpoint (document/handler.go:66-75) and UpdateRequest has no link_count. Any future unlink feature or internal job would orphan documents (unreachable through the application) or leak them to clients without a link.
findings.cause: SECURITY INVOKER counter triggers, no guard against direct counter writes.
findings.recommendation: Make the counter triggers SECURITY DEFINER (or replace the counters with an EXISTS-based policy) and reject direct changes of link_count/ci_count (BEFORE UPDATE trigger or column privilege).
findings.retest: Re-run probe_doc_link_count.sql: A2 link_count 0 and A3 = 1, and B rejected.

Unlinked document: client-1 PATCH/DELETE/POST-link → rejected; org-wide principal → allowed. Same for maintenance windows with CIs of both clients. Positive: a document linked only to client-1 objects can be updated/deleted by client 1.

test_gaps.description: Counter integrity of link_count/ci_count
test_gaps.proposed_test: A client-1 principal removes its own link of a two-client document → link_count = number of links. Removing the last link → document visible as org-wide. A direct UPDATE of link_count by the app role → rejected.

test_gaps.description: Site-scoped principal on module tables (only client scope tested)
test_gaps.proposed_test: CIs at site1/site2 with ticket/document_link/maintenance_window_ci rows per CI. A site1 principal sees only site1 plus NULL-site rows, cannot insert for a site2 CI, and cannot move a ticket to a site2 CI.

test_gaps.proposed_test: Move an asset client1→client2: ticket(related_asset) and document_link(asset) follow. Move a ticket's CI: comments and document_link(ticket) follow. Move key_item: key_assignment follows. The client-1 principal loses visibility.

wps.upgrade_conditions: (1) Shared and org-wide multi-object writes are restricted (all links visible; E-09 for unlinked rows), covered by HTTP+PG negative tests. (2) Counters are exact and not tenant-writable. (3) MGT-02 traceability corrected or disposal_record DB-scoped. (4) Site-scope and propagation tests for module tables pass.
wps.verifier_note: Re-ran both auditor probes (identical). Went beyond DB level with a PG-backed HTTP probe through document.NewHandler: client-1 DELETE of a shared document → 204 and client-2 links 0. This confirms the AC2 violation through the real API, so AC2 moves from partial to no and the priority from P2 to P1 (E-03 keeps M0 scope fixes mandatory despite the G1 module gate). findings.title: Metric series names of a foreign-client CI are visible via GET /api/v1/cis/{id}/metrics (MetricNames without scope predicate)
findings.repro:
Verifier overlay test TestProbeV05CIMetricsFullRouter (internal/tenant/rls, reuses newChannelEnv: server.NewRouter + PostgresRepositories + TenantMiddleware) on audit_db_05:
1) scopetest.Seed; CI 'pv5-foreign-mon' in client 2; PGMetricStore.Ingest of metric 'pv5_secret_metric';
2) as a principal with Clients={client1}: GET /api/v1/cis/{foreign} → 404, but GET /api/v1/cis/{foreign}/metrics → 200 with series name pv5_secret_metric and empty points.

findings.expected: A principal whose client scope excludes the CI gets 404 or an empty series list (TEN-06: a wrong client scope yields 0 rows).
findings.actual: Series names of the foreign CI are returned with 200 (points are filtered by metricWhere), disclosing the CI's existence and its metric names.

findings.cause:
- The views are org-only (000071, ADR item 4).
- Scope is enforced only by metricWhere (pg_store.go:189-191).
- MetricNames (pg_store.go:230-236, WP-190 commit d80d173) omits that predicate.
- CIMetrics (monitoring.go:836-872) does not check CI visibility.
findings.recommendation:
- Add the ci-visibility predicate to MetricNames.
- Return 404 from CIMetrics for invisible CIs.
- Preferably add the scope predicate to both views.
- Add a table-driven scope test over all store read paths.

findings.title: Deactivation request blacklists sessions of users in other organizations (cross-tenant forced logout)
findings.repro: Real PG (audit_db_06), overlay probe V/xtenant_revoke_probe_test.go: org-A admin context, PATCH /api/v1/users/{id of a user in org B} body {"status":"inactive"} through user.NewHandler(...).WithSessionRevoker(revocations).
findings.expected: 404 with no effect on org B (tenant isolation); revocation only after the user is found in the caller's organization
findings.actual: 404 'user not found', yet session-revoked:<orgB-user> is written and the org-B user's existing session is rejected (ErrSessionRevoked); the call can be repeated to keep the victim logged out
findings.user_impact: A tenant admin (any self-signup org) who knows or obtains a foreign user's UUID can repeatedly log that user out. This affects availability and integrity across tenants. The precondition (a UUID) lowers exploitability.
findings.cause: user/handler.go:219-225 calls h.revokeSessions(ctx, id) before h.repo.UpdateUser verifies that the user exists in t.OrganizationID; SessionRevocations.RevokeUser keys only on the user id (session.go:63-74). Anonymize has the same pattern (WP-042 commit 7732250, handler lines added at +125/+134).
findings.recommendation: Look up the user org-scoped (or lock it in the tx) before writing the blacklist; or key the blacklist by org+user and have Validate check org+subject. Apply the same to Anonymize.

findings.title: Agent follows https→http redirects and sends its Bearer credential in cleartext
findings.repro: Overlay probe V/agent_redirect_probe_test.go in backend/cmd/agent: httptest TLS server (CA given via agentConfig.CAPEM) answers POST with 302 or 307 to http://127.0.0.1:<plain>/api/v1/agents/telemetry; sendDirect returns nil; the plain server receives Authorization 'Bearer secret-agent-token' (and, for 307, the telemetry body).
findings.expected: AGT-03 / WP-051: agent traffic only over TLS, no HTTP fallback, even when a server or proxy answers with a redirect
findings.actual: The default Go redirect policy is used (httpClientFor sets no CheckRedirect); same-host redirects keep the Authorization header regardless of scheme
findings.user_impact: A misconfigured TLS-terminating proxy that emits absolute http redirects exposes the agent's 1-year credential (agent:ingest for that agent) and telemetry on the network; an attacker can then submit forged telemetry
findings.cause: cmd/agent/main.go:147-165 builds http.Client without CheckRedirect; sendDirect checks only the initial URL scheme (:266-272)
findings.recommendation: Set CheckRedirect to refuse redirects (or any non-https target); treat 3xx as an error; apply the same to the collector relay's upstream client
findings.retest: Unit: TLS server redirecting to http → sendDirect returns an error and the plain server sees no request; https→https same host may be allowed or refused as decided

wps.title: Instanzattribute: Discovery-Schutz und Audit

wps.title: Manuelle Schreibpfade erzeugen Overrides; RFC-7396-Merge-Patch
wps.user_goal: A manual CI change applies field-granular JSON Merge Patch semantics (null removes), and every manually changed field becomes a protected override with author, time and reason, so that discovery can never overwrite it. This holds for every manual path: edit form, API PATCH and bulk.
wps.implementation:
Backend:
- backend/internal/ci/mergepatch.go:9-26 (MergePatch), 30-43 (changedKeys).
- ci/handler.go:471-516: Update sets req.Manual at line 486; the fallback at line 507 maps every other error to 404.
- ci/pg_repository.go:
  - 783-788: a request without Manual goes through dropOverriddenFields.
  - 795-821: addStringField, where nil means unchanged and "" means NULL.
  - 826-835: MergePatch for attributes only.
  - 847-850: an empty SET returns success.
  - 883-886 and 1452-1478: recordManualOverrides.
- ci/bulk.go:142-160: runBulk calls s.Update(ctx, orgID, id, UpdateRequest{Status: &status}) without Manual.

Frontend:
- frontend/src/pages/CIFormModal.tsx:46-49 optionalValue('') → undefined.
- CIFormModal.tsx:156-164: the update payload contains all form fields, including untouched ones and status.
- Commit 3cf961b.
wps.tests:
- **Baseline (results-backend.tsv), all pass:** internal/ci TestMergePatchRFC7396, TestChangedKeys, TestManualPatchCreatesOverridesDiscoveryKeeps (PG, real handler; attributes merge patch, overrides with author and reason, ingest keeps the values, one override_conflict per field).
- **Verifier re-run on audit_db_07** (SP/work/verify-B07/probe-ci.log, overlay zz_verify_b07_ci_test.go, real ci handler + PG):
  - PROBE1 PATCH {"hostname":null} → 200, hostname_after=host-a, override(hostname)=0.
  - PROBE2 bulk set_status maintenance → 200 ok, status=maintenance, override(status)=0.
  - PROBE3a PATCH status inactive → override(status)=1.
  - PROBE3b bulk set_status active → 200 {succeeded:1, result:ok, code:200}, ci.status=inactive.
  - PROBE3c control without the override → active.
  - PROBE1b PATCH {"hostname":""} → NULL.
- **Verifier probe** (SP/work/verify-B07/probe-404.log): a repo Update returning errors.New(...) → PATCH answers 404 'CI not found'.
- **Real stack (frontend/e2e-real/ci-lifecycle.spec.ts; SP/work/verify-ci-lifecycle/single-L05.log, single-L05b.log, run2.log):**
  - ✘ L05: Firmware cleared in the edit form → still '9.9.9' in the UI after reload and in the DB.
  - ✘ L05b: PATCH {firmware_version:null} → 200 but the value stays '1.2.3'.
  - ✘ L12b: a stale save of untouched fields → 409 'fields changed since the If-Match version: model'; session 1's manufacturer is not saved.
  - ✓ L04, L06, L13.
- **Real stack discovery-override.spec.ts** (SP/work/verify-discovery-override/full.log): ✓ D04, where the edit-form PATCH creates an override with override_author and discovery does not overwrite it.

criteria.criterion: PATCH /cis/{id} applies RFC 7396 recursively (NULL deletes)
criteria.evidence: Only the attributes sub-document follows RFC 7396 (TestMergePatchRFC7396, PG test). For top-level members null is silently ignored: the verifier PROBE1 gives 200 with the value unchanged, and real-stack L05b fails. Only "" clears a field, which is not RFC 7396.

criteria.criterion: Every manual field change creates/updates an override in the same transaction (author, time, reason)
criteria.evidence: The single-CI PATCH path is correct (PG test, real-stack D04). The manual bulk status change (POST /cis/bulk, used by CIListPage) creates no override (PROBE2). Under an existing status override, the bulk change is silently discarded while reporting ok (PROBE3b, with the PROBE3c control).

criteria.criterion: Test: after a manual PATCH an ingest does not overwrite the value
criteria.evidence: TestManualPatchCreatesOverridesDiscoveryKeeps (PG) and real-stack D04 (edit form → override → discovery run keeps the value, with one override_conflict per field) both pass.

wps.soll_ist:
Expected: an RFC 7396 PATCH with null deletion, field-granular manual edits, and an override for every manual field change. Actual: correct for PATCH attributes and the single-CI PATCH override path (PG and real stack). Violated in several places:

- Criterion 2 is violated for the manual bulk status path, which silently loses changes under an override.

wps.dependencies: WP-011, WP-010. Interacts with WP-181 (bulk API), WP-058 (decision), 1b6671f (dropOverriddenFields), and the API-07 If-Match WPs.

findings.title: Manual bulk status change silently dropped when the CI has a status override, reported as success
findings.repro:
Verifier probe on audit_db_07 (SP/work/verify-B07/probe-ci.log, real handler + PG):
1. PATCH /api/v1/cis/{id} {"status":"inactive"} → override(status)=1.
2. POST /api/v1/cis/bulk {"action":"set_status","ids":[id],"status":"active"} → 200 {"succeeded":1,"items":[{"result":"ok","code":200}]}, but ci.status=inactive.
3. Control: after deleting the status override row, the same bulk call sets active.

UI reachability: CIFormModal sends status on every edit (CIFormModal.tsx:156-158), and CIListPage uses the bulk API.
findings.expected: A user's manual bulk status change is applied and recorded as an override (CH9: manual wins), or at least reported as failed or in conflict.
findings.actual: A silent no-op with an 'ok' result; the CIListPage bulk action reports success.
findings.user_impact: Operators believe CIs were set to maintenance or decommissioned when they were not. This leads to wrong lifecycle and monitoring state with no indication.
findings.cause: ci/bulk.go:152 calls Update without Manual. pg_repository.go:783-788 therefore runs dropOverriddenFields, which nils req.Status. setClauses is empty, so Update returns the unchanged CI without error (847-850).
findings.recommendation: Mark user-initiated bulk updates as manual (Manual{Author: tenant user}, with a change reason). Report a request whose every field was dropped as a conflict rather than success.
findings.retest:
Integration test:
- PATCH status (override), then bulk set_status → status changed, override updated with the bulk author, result ok.
- Negative: an automation (non-Manual) status write under an override stays dropped.

findings.title: Manual bulk status change creates no override
findings.repro: Verifier PROBE2 on audit_db_07: POST /api/v1/cis/bulk set_status maintenance on a CI without an override → status=maintenance, override(status)=0 (no ci_field_value row with override_at).
findings.expected: Every manual field change creates or updates an override with author, time and reason in the same transaction. A manual write (rank 100) raises the version (API-07).
findings.actual: There is no override, no author and no reason, and the version is not raised (pg_repository.go:852-854 requires Manual or Authoritative).
findings.user_impact: A later automated status write, such as the discovery sighting unknown→active (discovery.go:1416-1420) or a workflow, can override the user's manual decision.
findings.cause: The bulk path is not marked manual (ci/bulk.go:152).
findings.recommendation: Pass Manual{Author} and a ChangeReason from the bulk request.
findings.retest: Bulk set_status → ci_field_value(status) has override_at set, override_author = user and protected = true, and the version is incremented.

findings.title: PATCH null on top-level CI fields is ignored (not RFC 7396)
findings.repro:
- Verifier PROBE1: PATCH /api/v1/cis/{id} {"hostname":null} → 200, hostname unchanged ('host-a'), no override.
- PROBE1b: {"hostname":""} clears it.
- Real stack L05b: PATCH {firmware_version:null} → 200, value stays '1.2.3'.
findings.expected: CI-04 and WP-057: JSON Merge Patch, where a null member removes or clears the field.
findings.actual: null is decoded into a nil *string (meaning unchanged); the client gets 200.
findings.user_impact: API and integration clients following RFC 7396 cannot clear fields, and get no error.
findings.cause: UpdateRequest uses *string (model.go:120-143) and addStringField skips nil (pg_repository.go:795-801). RFC 7396 is applied only to attributes (826-835).
findings.recommendation: Decode the PATCH into a presence-aware structure (a map of json.RawMessage or Optional[T]), and treat null as clear (NULL plus a manual override with a null value). Alternatively, reject null with 422 and document it.
findings.retest:
- PATCH {hostname:null} → hostname NULL, with an override with a null value.
- Real-stack L05b passes.
- A following ingest reporting a hostname → override_conflict; the value stays NULL.

findings.title: CI edit form cannot clear optional fields
findings.repro: Real stack L05 (SP/work/verify-ci-lifecycle/single-L05.log): clear Firmware in the edit form and save → after reload the UI shows '9.9.9' ('Expected: —'), and the DB firmware_version is '9.9.9'. Cause in code: optionalValue('') → undefined (CIFormModal.tsx:46-49), so JSON omits the key.
findings.expected: Emptying a field and saving clears it (CI-04, field-granular PATCH).
findings.actual: The value silently persists while the modal closes as successful.
findings.user_impact: Users cannot remove wrong manufacturer, model, serial, management IP or firmware values through the UI.
findings.cause: The update payload is built with optionalValue for both create and update (CIFormModal.tsx:156-164).
findings.recommendation: In edit mode, send "" (or null once supported) for fields that were non-empty and are now empty.
findings.retest:
- Vitest: editing with the manufacturer cleared → the PATCH body contains manufacturer "" or null.
- Real-stack L05 passes.

findings.title: CI edit form sends untouched fields: concurrent edits of different fields end in 409 (PATCH not field-granular in UI)
findings.repro: Real stack L12b (SP/work/verify-ci-lifecycle/run2.log:391-424): session 2 changes model; session 1 (stale) changes only manufacturer and saves. The result is 409 {"detail":"fields changed since the If-Match version: model","fields":["model"]}, and the stored manufacturer stays 'Vendor-0'.
findings.expected: CI-04 says PATCH is field-granular. API-07 says 409 only for an intervening manual change of the same field. An edit of only the manufacturer must merge with another session's model change.
findings.actual: The form sends every field, including the stale model value. The server correctly detects a conflict on model and refuses the whole save.
findings.user_impact: Two users editing different fields of the same CI block each other. The later user's change is not saved and must be redone after a reload.
findings.cause: CIFormModal.tsx:156-164 builds the update payload from all form values instead of the diff against the loaded CI.
findings.recommendation: Send only the fields whose value differs from the loaded CI, including cleared fields.
findings.retest:
- Vitest: editing only the manufacturer → the PATCH body is {manufacturer} only.
- Real-stack L12b passes.

findings.title: Update handler maps all unexpected errors to 404 'CI not found'
findings.repro: Verifier probe (SP/work/verify-B07/probe-404.log): the ci handler over a repo whose Update returns errors.New("record manual overrides: connection reset") → PATCH /api/v1/cis/{id} returns 404 {"detail":"CI not found"}.
findings.expected: 500 for internal failures; 404 only for a missing CI.
findings.actual: A misleading 404 hides failed override writes and other internal errors.
findings.user_impact: Diagnosis of failed manual changes is misleading, and clients may treat the CI as deleted.
findings.cause: The fallback branch at ci/handler.go:507 is `api.WriteError(w, http.StatusNotFound, …)`.
findings.recommendation: Map not-found explicitly via a sentinel; default to 500 or api.WriteRepoError.
findings.retest: Unit test: a stub error → 500; the not-found sentinel → 404.

wps.title: Zentrale fail-closed Schreibentscheidung für Automationsquellen mit Rangtabelle
wps.user_goal: Every automated write of a reported CI field value is decided centrally. The decision uses the exact REC-03 rank table, never writes over a manual override (a conflict review instead), and fails closed with a counter when override or provenance state cannot be read.
wps.implementation:
- backend/internal/override/decide.go:
  - 18-35: SourceRanks exactly as in REC-03, plus ipmi=90 per E-32 (entschieden 2026-10-05, entscheidungen.md:876-884).
  - 84-98: decisionFailures and RegisterMetrics (reticora_override_decision_failures_total), registered at server/router.go:600.
  - 112-160: DecideAutomatedWrite. A read error → ReasonError and the counter; an override → equal/no-op or Conflict; an empty value is filled; otherwise rank and observed_at decide.
- discovery/discovery.go:
  - 594-601: decide wrapper.
  - 1380-1412: every typed field (name, manufacturer, model, serial_number, hardware_uuid, management_ip) and every attribute goes through decide; a Conflict → queueOverrideConflict (603-630, deduplicated).
  - Writes outside decide: last_seen_at, the REC-07 sighting status unknown→active (1416-1420, still override-protected by dropOverriddenFields), fingerprint and raw_data system keys, and the CI-11 generic type raise.
- Migration 000076: override_conflict kind with a unique open index.
- server/report_adapters.go:97-107 overrideProvenance.
- override/model.go:65-70: the legacy DefaultPriorities, used only by the source-policy API; ResolveEffective ignores priorities (model.go:77).
- Commit 38cd83f.
wps.tests:
- **Baseline (results-backend.tsv), all pass:**
  - internal/override: TestSourceRanksFollowREC03, TestDecideAutomatedWrite, TestDecisionFailuresAreCounted, TestIsProtectedFailsClosed, TestDecideComparesObservedAtPerField, TestMigrationRanksFollowTheRankTable.

findings.repro:
PG, audit_db_08: SP/work/verify-B08/agentprobe/pg_probe_test.go TestVerifyB08ProbeAgentMergedPG.
1. Two CIs with hostname laptop-77; agent agent-e8 linked to the victim.

findings.expected: No duplicate (AGT-05, REC-11, OVR-02). Follow ci.merged_into_id to the survivor; otherwise apply the unique exact-hostname match; with several matches stay unlinked.
findings.actual: A new endpoint CI is created and linked, so the merge is silently undone on the next telemetry.
findings.user_impact: Every merge or dedupe of an agent-managed device is reverted within one telemetry interval. Inventory counts and licence counting (unlicensed_ci) are inflated, and operators can only work around it by always choosing the agent CI as the survivor.
findings.cause: agent/handler.go:455-463: anchorCI returns nil,nil for any GetByID error on ag.CIID. reconcileCI :414 runs the ambiguity/match logic only when ag.CIID=="" and then creates a CI. ci/merge.go:239-267 does not move endpoint_agent.ci_id. GetByID filters deleted_at (ci/pg_repository.go:310).
findings.recommendation: In anchorCI, on ErrNotFound follow merged_into_id (ci.PGRepository.MergedInto exists, merge.go:582); otherwise fall back to the exact-hostname matching (unique -> relink, several -> unlinked). Add endpoint_agent.ci_id to mergeReferences. Return transient DB errors instead of treating them as 'gone'.
findings.retest: PG integration test in backend/internal/agent: merge the linked CI -> telemetry ci_id == survivor and the CI count is unchanged. Delete the linked CI with no other match -> exactly one new CI. A GetByID failure that is not 'not found' -> error and no CI created.

findings.title: Override set/clear does not raise ci.version, so a stale If-Match PATCH silently overwrites the newer manual override
findings.repro:
PG audit_db_08, real HTTP handlers (override.NewHandler(PG) plus ci.NewHandler(PG) on one router), SP/work/verify-B08/ciprobe/probe_test.go:
1. GET /cis/{id} -> ETag "1".
2. PUT /cis/{id}/fields/model/override {value:'manual-model', protected:true} -> 200; GET ETag still "1", ci_change rows 0.
3. PATCH {model:'stale-model'} with If-Match "1" -> 200, ETag "2".
4. DB: ci.model='stale-model', override_value='stale-model'.
5. DELETE override -> ETag unchanged.
Control: two PATCHes with the same stale ETag -> 200, then 409.
findings.expected: API-07: the override is a manual write (rank 100), so the version rises and ci_change records ci_version. The stale PATCH of 'model' gets 409 with fields=[model].
findings.actual: Version unchanged, the PATCH is accepted, and the newer protected override is replaced without warning.
findings.user_impact: Editor A sets a protected override in the CI detail provenance section while editor B has the edit modal open. B's save silently destroys A's manual value: the lost update API-07 exists to prevent, on protected manual data (OVR-01: silent loss is Critical).
findings.cause: override/pg_repository.go:323-360 SetOverride and :414-450 ClearOverride call syncCIField (:613-645), which updates the ci row without 'version = version + 1' and inserts no ci_change row with ci_version. ci/pg_repository.go:1585-1597 checkPrecondition only looks at ci_change.ci_version > If-Match.
findings.recommendation: In SetOverride and ClearOverride (when the effective value changes), raise ci.version and record ci_change (field_name, ci_version) in the same transaction. Return the new ETag; optionally accept If-Match on the override endpoints.
findings.retest: PG integration test: GET v1 -> PUT override -> GET ETag "2". PATCH of the same field with If-Match "1" -> 409 fields=[model]. PATCH of another field with If-Match "1" -> 200. DELETE override with a restored observed value raises the version.

findings.title: User bulk set_status does not raise ci.version; a stale PATCH silently reverts the bulk change

wps.title: Spool ohne stillen Verlust: 24-h-Pufferung, Backpressure, Verlustmeldung, Reihenfolge
wps.user_goal: During a backend outage the collector keeps all unacknowledged results for at least 24 h and throttles collection instead of deleting at the size limit. Every unavoidable loss is counted, logged and reported to the server, and the backlog is delivered in source-time order before new data, without a per-cycle cap.

- :384-405 runDiscoveryLoop pauses on backpressure
- :644-675 uploadRecordsAt (queues behind the backlog; a 4xx is spooled like an outage)
- :700-722 postPayload (status >= 400 -> generic error)
- :810-862 flushSpool (64 per pass, loops, stops at the first failure, unknown topics skipped)
- :868-880 replayAgentTelemetry (unreadable or 4xx -> dropped, return nil, no loss counted)
- :939-955 spoolReport (current-instance Stats only)
backend/internal/discovery/discovery.go:907-962 heartbeat accepts the spool report and only logs it.

findings.title: Spool loss counters are not persisted; losses before a restart never reach the server
findings.repro: SP/work/verify-B08/spoolprobe/main.go: a DiskBuffer at the cap -> Enqueue returns ErrSpoolFull and DroppedMessages=1. A new DiskBuffer on the same dir (restart) -> DroppedMessages=0. The heartbeat (collectorcmd.go:939-955) reports only the current instance's Stats.
findings.expected: Every unavoidable loss is reported to the server, including losses that happened during an outage spanning a collector restart.
findings.actual: The counter resets on restart; only the local log line collector.spool.data_lost remains.
findings.user_impact: Long outages, which usually include reboots or updates, can lose data with no server-side indication.
findings.cause: buffer.go droppedMsgs/droppedBytes are struct fields without persistence. The server only logs (discovery.go:954-962).
findings.recommendation: Persist unreported loss totals atomically in the spool dir and clear them after the server acknowledges the heartbeat. Persist the report or emit a metric/notification on the server.
findings.retest: Buffer test: loss, then a new instance on the same dir still reports the loss until acknowledged. Collector test: after a restart the heartbeat carries the previous loss.

findings.title: Head-of-line blocking: a corrupt spool file or a permanently rejected batch stops all delivery
findings.repro: (1) Torn head file -> PeekBatch returns a decode error and Len=2; flushSpool returns at :824-827 every cycle. (2) Verifier collector probe: 3 batches spooled while the backend is down; the backend then answers 400 for the batch containing 'poison-host' and 202 otherwise -> after 5 flushSpool cycles rejected=5, delivered=0, spoolLen=3, logged as 'spool flush postponed; backend still unreachable ... status 400'. uploadRecordsAt :660-666 queues all new data behind the backlog.
findings.expected: Unreadable or permanently rejected entries are quarantined and counted as a loss (event plus server report), and the remaining backlog is delivered.
findings.actual: Delivery stalls until MaxAge (default 72 h) removes the entry. That removal happens only on Enqueue, which stops once backpressure pauses discovery, so the stall can become permanent (by code reading).
findings.user_impact: One bad file or batch silently stops all discovery data delivery and later pauses discovery itself.
findings.cause: PeekBatch aborts on the first decode error (buffer.go:263-266). flushSpool treats every error as transient (:845-853). postPayload maps every status >= 400 to a generic error. A live 4xx is spooled (:668-674). Writes are not atomic (buffer.go:135).
findings.recommendation: Atomic writes (temp + fsync + rename). PeekBatch skips and quarantines corrupt files (counted loss). Treat a 4xx other than licence-expired as poison: quarantine, count, report; do not spool it on live upload. Run age cleanup in the flusher too.
findings.retest: Buffer test: corrupt head -> the other messages are returned plus one loss counted. Collector test: 400 for batch 1 and 202 for the rest -> 2 delivered, 1 loss reported, spool empty. 503 for batch 1 -> nothing delivered or dropped, order kept.

findings.title: Spooled agent telemetry rejected (4xx) or unreadable is dropped without loss counter or server report
findings.repro: Verifier collector probe: spoolAgentTelemetry(relay message) while the backend is down; then the backend answers 403 -> flushSpool logs 'spooled agent telemetry rejected; dropped', the spool is empty, and spoolReport is {"messages":0,...,"dropped_messages":0}.
findings.expected: WP-062 criterion 2: every loss (also deliberate drops) is counted and reported.
findings.actual: Dropped with a warning log only.
findings.user_impact: Agent telemetry lost after an outage (e.g. a disabled or re-enrolled agent) is invisible server-side.
findings.cause: collectorcmd.go:868-880 replayAgentTelemetry returns nil for unreadable or rejected messages, so flushSpool Acks them and recordLoss is never called.
findings.recommendation: Record a loss (reason rejected/unreadable) via the buffer's loss counter before acknowledging.

wps.title: DDL-Vertrag CH19 für die App-Rolle; FORCE für alle Mandantentabellen
wps.user_goal: The application role can create runtime indexes (CH19/DB-04) without SUPERUSER or BYPASSRLS. Every tenant table enforces RLS even for its owner, and the server refuses to start if the effective database rights deviate from this contract.
wps.implementation: backend/migrations/000078_app_role_ddl_contract.up.sql (reticora_owner NOLOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS with CREATE on public; GRANT reticora_owner TO reticora_app WITH INHERIT FALSE, SET TRUE; ENABLE+FORCE; ownership transfer; event triggers) plus .down.sql. backend/internal/database/role_check.go:41-92 roleContractQuery: the reachable roles start from current_user only (:42); session_user and its RESET ROLE path are not inspected. :107-130 VerifyRoleContract. backend/internal/database/pool.go:61-99 NewPool (logs in with the DSN user, AfterConnect 'SET ROLE reticora_app', then VerifyRLSEnforced/VerifyRoleContract). cmd/server/main.go:207-211 (exit 1). Packaged install: deploy/docker-compose/docker-compose.yml:47-49 POSTGRES_USER=reticora (the timescale image creates it as SUPERUSER), :287 RETICORA_DATABASE_URL=postgres://reticora:...; no init script creates a non-superuser login (deploy/docker-compose/postgres/Dockerfile). docs/schema-baseline.md:87 describes 'Login-Rolle (z. B. reticora) ... der Pool wechselt per SET ROLE'.

findings.title: Server logs in as a SUPERUSER in the packaged install; the startup role check only inspects current_user and accepts it, so RESET ROLE escapes RLS
findings.repro:
1. deploy/docker-compose/docker-compose.yml:47-49 POSTGRES_USER=reticora (the official timescale/postgres entrypoint creates it as SUPERUSER) and :287 RETICORA_DATABASE_URL=postgres://reticora:...; pool.go:73 only executes SET ROLE reticora_app.
2. Baseline: every PG test builds NewPool with the superuser login 'reticora', and VerifyRoleContract returns nil (TestRoleContractStartupCheck:144).
3. psql -f SP/work/verify-B08/reset_role_probe.sql (rolled back): after SET ROLE reticora_app, current_user=reticora_app (not superuser), session_user=reticora (superuser), and 0 SUPERUSER roles are reachable from current_user. With a foreign org GUC the app sees 0 organization rows. RESET ROLE -> current_user=reticora, rolsuper=t, and it sees all rows.
findings.expected: TEN-03/CH19: the DB role of the application has no SUPERUSER/BYPASSRLS. The startup check (WP-064 criterion 3) refuses a connection whose session can regain superuser or BYPASSRLS, including via RESET ROLE or SET ROLE back to the login role.
findings.actual: The check reports a clean contract and the server starts with a session that is one 'RESET ROLE' away from superuser (RLS bypass for all tenants; superuser also allows e.g. COPY ... TO PROGRAM).
findings.user_impact: Not exploitable without SQL execution on an app connection. Any SQL injection, however, becomes full cross-tenant read/write and DB-host command execution instead of being contained by RLS. The auditor's TRUNCATE gap is a weaker subset of this.
findings.cause: role_check.go:42 seeds 'reachable' with current_user only; session_user/rolsuper is never checked. VerifyRLSEnforced checks current_user too. The installer reuses the bootstrap superuser as the runtime login (no separate NOSUPERUSER login role in the member chain of reticora_app).
findings.recommendation: (a) Extend VerifyRoleContract/VerifyRLSEnforced to also check session_user (rolsuper, rolbypassrls, and roles reachable from it) and refuse to start. (b) Let the installer and the k8s docs create a dedicated LOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role (member of reticora_app only) for RETICORA_DATABASE_URL; keep the superuser for migrations only. (c) Hand over to WP-208.
findings.retest: Integration test: NewPool with a superuser login plus SET ROLE reticora_app -> *RoleContractError mentioning the session user. NewPool with a NOSUPERUSER login member of reticora_app -> success, and 'RESET ROLE; SELECT rolsuper' is false. Compose install-smoke: the server's session_user is not a superuser.

findings.title: reticora_owner (SET ROLE-able from reticora_app) can TRUNCATE tenant tables across organizations despite FORCE RLS
findings.repro: psql -d audit_db_08 -f SP/work/audit-B08/truncate_probe.sql (single transaction, rolled back). SET LOCAL ROLE reticora_app: TRUNCATE job -> 'permission denied for table job'. SET LOCAL ROLE reticora_owner with app.org_id = org A: SELECT sees 1, DELETE affects 1, TRUNCATE job -> 'TRUNCATE TABLE'. RESET ROLE -> 0 rows of both orgs.
findings.expected: The CH19 owner path is limited to index DDL. No privilege on the SET ROLE path bypasses tenant isolation, and VerifyRoleContract would flag one.
findings.actual: Owner TRUNCATE (an implicit owner privilege) ignores RLS. Neither the event trigger nor the role check covers it.
findings.user_impact: Exploitable only with arbitrary SQL on an app connection: a cross-tenant mass deletion becomes a one-liner. Defense-in-depth.
findings.cause: Table ownership implies TRUNCATE. Event triggers do not fire on TRUNCATE. roleContractQuery does not inspect it.
findings.recommendation: Statement-level BEFORE TRUNCATE guard triggers on tenant tables that raise for reticora_app/reticora_owner, and have VerifyRoleContract report missing guards.
findings.retest: Integration test: as owner after SET ROLE, TRUNCATE on a tenant table -> 42501 and both orgs' rows remain. VerifyRoleContract reports a table without the guard.

wps.user_goal: Users get 15-minute RS256 session tokens with the AUT-02 claims and a kid header, and stay signed in through a rotating HttpOnly refresh cookie. Logout and deactivation revoke sessions at once via a Redis blacklist.

Frontend: auth/session.ts:16-45 (POST /auth/refresh with no body and no Content-Type, clearSession on !ok), api/client.ts:392-410 (refresh per 401, no single-flight), auth/authStore.ts:29-71 (sessionStorage, hasValidSession only checks expiresAt). Defect: middleware/openapi.go:233 bodyJSON and :301 registers 'POST /api/v1/auth/refresh' (RequiresBody + JSON); the validator is in the production chain (cmd/server/main.go:447).
