findings.title: SPA refresh POST /api/v1/auth/refresh always rejected with 400 by the OpenAPI validator
findings.repro: Real stack: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/auth/refresh -H 'Cookie: reticora_refresh=x' -> 400 'Content-Type must be application/json'. Same through http://localhost:5173. With Content-Type and no body -> 400 'request body is required'; with -d '{}' -> 401 (handler reached). Browser: e2e-real roles-authz.spec.ts:1058 test 14 'SPA refresh (Content-Type: none) -> 400' (final-run.log:269).
findings.expected: A cookie-only POST, as sent by session.ts:22-25 and as the request in api/openapi.yaml, reaches Handler.Refresh and returns 200 with a new token and a rotated cookie.
findings.actual: 400 validation-error before the handler. refreshSession() sees !ok and calls clearSession(), so the user is signed out at the first 401 after 15 minutes.
findings.user_impact: Every user must sign in again about every 15 minutes; the rotating refresh cookie of AUT-02 has no effect in production.
findings.cause: middleware/openapi.go:301 lists 'POST /api/v1/auth/refresh' among the bodyJSON routes (RequiresBody + application/json), a leftover from the token-in-body refresh. Handler tests call h.Refresh directly, and real-stack test 11's helper sends {} with Content-Type, so neither saw it.
findings.recommendation: Remove the route from the bodyJSON list (or register it with an empty RouteSpec that accepts no body and no Content-Type). Add a router-level test through the production middleware chain.
findings.retest: Go router+chain test: cookie-only POST /api/v1/auth/refresh -> 200 with a rotated Set-Cookie. Real stack: e2e-real roles-authz tests 14 and 14b pass.

findings.title: Concurrent 401 responses trigger parallel refreshes that revoke the refresh family
findings.repro: Vitest probe (verifier re-run, SP/work/verify-B09/vprobe/refresh.probe.test.ts): three concurrent fetchAPI calls answered 401 -> 3 POST /auth/refresh. TestRefreshRotatesAndDetectsReuse (pass) proves that the second use of a cookie gives 401 'already used' and revokes the family.
findings.expected: One refresh per expiry (single-flight); the other requests wait for it and retry with the new token.
findings.actual: Each 401 calls refreshSession() separately (client.ts:400-406). All requests carry the same not-yet-rotated cookie, so the second one revokes the family and clears the session.
findings.user_impact: Even after the F1 fix, users are signed out when several queries hit the expiry at once (dashboard load, window refocus).
findings.cause: auth/session.ts refreshSession has no shared in-flight promise.
findings.recommendation: Make refreshSession single-flight (module-level promise); optionally allow a short server-side grace window for immediate reuse.
findings.retest: Vitest: 3 concurrent 401s -> exactly 1 refresh call and 3 retries with the new token. e2e-real: parallel queries after expiry, the user stays signed in.

findings.title: Expired stored session redirects to /login without trying the refresh cookie (reload, navigation, new tab)
findings.repro: Real stack e2e-real roles-authz.spec.ts:1091 test 14b: after setting the stored expiresAt to the past and reloading, the POST /auth/refresh list stays [] (final-run.log:300-323). Vitest probe: an expired stored session gives isAuthenticated()=false with 0 fetch calls.
findings.expected: AUT-02: the session continues with the refresh cookie; the SPA renews the access token on boot or navigation.
findings.actual: RequireAuth renders the login redirect based on the local expiresAt only. A new tab has no user in sessionStorage, so refreshSession() returns false (session.ts:17-20).
findings.user_impact: After 15 minutes idle, a reload or route change ends the session although the refresh cookie is still valid.
findings.cause: authStore.hasValidSession checks only expiresAt; there is no boot-time or scheduled refresh.
findings.recommendation: Before redirecting, call refreshSession() when a session marker exists; schedule a refresh shortly before exp.
findings.retest: Vitest guard test; e2e-real 14b passes.

findings.title: API key rotation/revocation by a non-owner: privilege escalation to the owner's rights and takeover/kill of foreign keys
findings.repro: Verifier probe TestProbeV09 (scratch copy, audit_db_05). The admin (org-wide ci:read, ci:delete, apikey:manage, user:manage, role:manage) creates key K with [ci:read, ci:delete, user:manage, role:manage]. User R (custom role {ci:read, apikey:manage}, scope client 1; request scope client-restricted) calls POST /api/v1/api-keys/{K}/rotate {overlap_seconds:0} -> 201 with the plaintext. APIKeyService.Validate(plaintext) -> owner=admin, scopes [ci:read ci:delete user:manage role:manage], org-wide. The admin's original K -> 'API key has expired'. R: DELETE /api/v1/api-keys/{another admin key} -> 204. R creating a role:manage key directly -> 403.
findings.expected: Only the owner (or a holder of all key permissions in at least the owner's scope) may rotate or revoke; the successor never gives the rotating caller more than they hold (AUT-04 intersection, RBA-03).
findings.actual: Rotate copies CreatedBy and permissions and returns the plaintext to any apikey:manage holder of the organization; revoke ends any key.
findings.user_impact: A user with apikey:manage through a custom role (also client-scoped) can obtain org-admin-level API access (user:manage, role:manage, so a full tenant takeover is possible) or silently break other teams' integrations.
findings.cause: apikey_handler.go:184-229 check only the principal type; apikey_store.go:208-245 keeps CreatedBy/Permissions; there is no ownership or rights comparison. Only org_admin among the system roles holds apikey:manage, so exploitation needs a custom role (precondition lowers likelihood, not impact).
findings.recommendation: Allow rotate and revoke only for the owner, or require the caller to hold every key permission in at least the owner's scope (otherwise 403). Consider restricting list visibility likewise.
findings.retest: Go integration: a non-owner rotate -> 403 with the old key unchanged and its expires_at unchanged; a non-owner revoke -> 403; owner rotate -> 201; an admin rotating a lesser user's key keeps the owner's rights.

B revokes A's key -> 403. A rotates its own key -> 201. Tenant isolation: an org-B principal rotates or revokes an org-A key id -> 404.

wps.title: Service-Accounts mit Rollen und Scopes; Webhook-Subscriptions daran binden
wps.user_goal: Organizations create service accounts with role and scope assignments; API keys and webhook subscriptions can be bound to them, and a bound subscription receives only events whose object the account may read.
wps.implementation: Migration 000082 (service_account, service_account_role, FORCE RLS; composite FKs from api_key and webhook_subscription). user/service_account.go:77-97 CanReadEvent (empty client/site = in scope), :318-346 SetServiceAccountRoles (role must belong to the org; no rights or scope check of the caller), :349-400 ServiceAccountGrants. user/service_account_handler.go (routes; PUT /{id}/roles needs only user:manage, while user role assignment POST /roles/assign needs role:manage: route_permissions.txt:455,503). webhook/dispatcher.go:105-127 EventReadPermission and eventObjectScope (top-level client_id/site_id only), :141-150 mayDeliver, :256-268 Consume (outbox payload passed unchanged). identity/apikey_handler.go:145-157 service_account_id accepted without any check; apikey.go:218-227 a bound key uses the SA grants. Event payloads without scope: ci/merge.go:400-401 (survivor_id, victim_id, merge_id), relationship/cleanup.go:217-220 (relationship.removed). relationship.created is never emitted (only listed in webhook.go:102).
wps.tests: results-backend.tsv pass: user TestServiceAccounts (PG: create, duplicate 409, roles with client scope, unknown role 422, CanReadEvent matrix incl. ('ci:read','')=true, deactivated SA grants nothing, delete of a bound SA 409, audit); webhook TestDispatcherFiltersBoundSubscriptions (fakeAccess map; payloads always carry client_id). Verifier Go probe TestProbeV09 (SP/work/verify-B09/probe-v09.log).

Filtering leaks: verifier V3 with the REAL ci.merged outbox payload of a PG merge of two client-2 CIs and the real relationship.removed payload shape -> delivered to a client-1 SA (1 each, plus alias relationship.deleted 1); ci.created(client2) -> 0. Binding and SA role assignment are unauthorized (V2, V4).

Event filtering leaks scope-less events across clients. Key binding lets a client-scoped user borrow an org-wide account's scope, and SA role assignment lets a user:manage holder grant roles beyond their own rights.
wps.evidence: SP/work/verify-B09/probe-v09.log: 'V2a client-scoped user binds key to org-wide SA: 201', 'V2b creator's own key: org-wide=false clients=[...c1]', 'V2c bound key: scopes=[ci:read] org-wide=true clients=[]', 'V4b same user assigns org-wide role {user:manage,role:manage,apikey:manage,webhook:manage,ci:*} to the SA: 200', 'V4c SA grants now: perms=[apikey:manage ci:delete ci:read ci:write role:manage user:manage webhook:manage] org-wide=true', 'V3 real ci.merged outbox payload: {"merge_id": ..., "victim_id": ..., "survivor_id": ...}', 'V3 deliveries client-1 SA: ci.created(client2)=0 ci.merged(client2 CIs)=1 relationship.removed(client2 CIs)=1 relationship.deleted alias=1'.

findings.title: Service-account binding and role assignment are not authorized against the caller's rights and scope (escalation)
findings.repro: Verifier probe TestProbeV09 (audit_db_05). (a) SA 'v9-sa-orgwide' with an org-wide {ci:read} role. User R (custom role {ci:read, apikey:manage}, scope client 1, client-restricted request scope) calls POST /api/v1/api-keys {permissions:[ci:read], service_account_id: SA} -> 201. Validate -> scope org-wide, while R's own key is limited to client 1. (b) User U (custom role {user:read, user:manage}, scope client 1, no role:manage) creates an SA (201) and calls PUT /api/v1/service-accounts/{id}/roles with an org-wide role holding user:manage, role:manage, apikey:manage, webhook:manage and ci:* -> 200; SA grants are now those permissions org-wide.
findings.expected: A caller binds keys only to accounts whose rights and scope they cover, and assigns SA roles only within their own rights and scope (user role assignment requires role:manage; SAs are 'gleichgestellt' with users per RBA-08).
findings.actual: Create checks only permission names (p.Has); SetServiceAccountRoles checks only that the role belongs to the org; the route needs only user:manage.
findings.user_impact: Client-scoped staff (MSP technicians with custom roles) can read or write all clients' data through keys bound to broader service accounts, and user:manage holders can mint org-admin-level service accounts.
findings.cause: identity/apikey_handler.go:145-157 does not authorize service_account_id; user/service_account.go:318-346 does not check the caller's rights or scope; authz maps PUT /service-accounts/{id}/roles to user:manage (route_permissions.txt:503) instead of role:manage.
findings.recommendation: Bind only when the caller's scope covers the SA scope for every key permission (otherwise 403). Gate SA role assignment with role:manage plus a 'never grant more than you hold, in your scope' check, the same rule for every grant path (keys, SA roles, rotation).
findings.retest: Integration: client-scoped creator binding to an org-wide SA -> 403; org-wide admin -> 201. User:manage without role:manage assigning roles to an SA -> 403. A bound key's scope is never broader than its creator's.

findings.title: Webhook filter delivers merge and relationship events of other clients to client-scoped service accounts
findings.repro: Verifier probe TestProbeV09: two client-2 CIs merged through ci.PGRepository.WithEvents(outbox).Merge. The ci.merged row read from event_outbox ({merge_id, victim_id, survivor_id}) and a relationship.removed payload shaped exactly like relationship/cleanup.go:217-220 are passed to webhook.Dispatcher.Consume (the production outbox entry point) with the real user.ServiceAccountAccess over PG. A client-1 SA receives ci.merged=1, relationship.removed=1 and the alias relationship.deleted=1; ci.created with client_id=client2 -> 0.
findings.expected: RBA-08/RBA-07: a bound subscription receives only events whose object the account may read; merges and relationships of client-2 CIs are not readable for a client-1 account.
findings.actual: eventObjectScope (dispatcher.go:110-127) finds no client_id/site_id, and CanReadEvent treats '' as an org-wide object (service_account.go:89-92), so the event is delivered.
findings.user_impact: Client separation is broken for webhook consumers: CI ids, relation types and merge ids of other clients reach a client-scoped integration.
findings.cause: Scope is derived from top-level payload fields only; ci.merged (ci/merge.go:400-401) and relationship.removed (relationship/cleanup.go:217-220) carry no client/site; the unit test asserts ('ci:read','')=true. Note: relationship.created, used in the auditor's repro, is never emitted in production code.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the object scope server-side (look up the CI or relationship endpoints), fail closed for scoped accounts when the scope cannot be determined, or add client_id/site_id to every event payload.
findings.retest: Dispatcher integration test with real payloads and a real SA: ci.merged and relationship.removed between client-2 CIs -> 0 deliveries to a client-1 SA, 1 to an org-wide SA.

test_gaps.description: End-to-end event filtering with real payloads and real SA grants
test_gaps.proposed_test: PG fixture: SA1 (client1 ci:read), SA2 (org-wide). Create, merge and relate CIs in client1 and client2 via the real repositories with the outbox; run events.Publisher with the dispatcher consumer and an httptest receiver. Assert SA1 gets only client1 ci.*/relationship.* events (including ci.merged and relationship.removed), SA2 gets all, an unbound subscription gets all, and a deactivated SA gets none.

wps.title: Operator-Pfad /admin mit Operator-Token und eigener Audit-Hashkette
wps.user_goal: Platform operators reach /api/v1/admin/* only with a personalised operator identity (Keycloak group operators, MFA) or the break-glass token. Tenant sessions are refused, every action lands in an org-wide hash-chained operator_audit, and break-glass use raises an alarm.
wps.implementation: operator/auth.go:16-21 (15-min operator session), :33-60 Config (group default 'operators', MFA by amr or acr '2'), :84-100 break-glass (constant-time compare, slog.Error 'SECURITY ALERT', counter reticora_operator_break_glass_total), :101-121 session must carry opr=true, :135-151 Middleware (audit recorded after the handler, refused requests included), :155-160 record (failure only logged). operator/handler.go:57-101 Callback (OIDC code+PKCE via the same OIDC client), :105-121 issue (requires id.Groups contains the group AND MFASatisfied(id.AMR, id.ACR)). identity/oidc.go:269-331 (amr/acr read from the ID token). Migration 000083 (operator_audit, append-only). middleware/auth.go (tenant API refuses operator sessions). config.go:225-227. deploy/keycloak/realm-reticora*.json: groups ['reticora-admin'], realm role 'operator', flow browser-mfa, reticora-app mappers groups+organization_id, defaultClientScopes [profile, email].
wps.tests: results-backend.tsv pass: operator TestOperatorLoginRequiresGroupAndMFA (5 subtests, fake IdP), TestOperatorPathAdmitsOperatorsOnly, TestEntryHashCoversEveryField, TestOperatorAuditChain (PG), TestOperatorCreatesOrganizations, TestEntitlementsAreWrittenByOperatorsOnly, TestOperatorEntitlementAudit; server TestEveryOperationRequiresItsExpectedPermission (admin routes = operator). Real stack (verifier, 2026-10-15): curl GET :8080/api/v1/admin/me -> 401 'operator authentication required'; e2e DB operator_audit rows 202-204 chained (prev hash of 204 = entry hash of 203). Keycloak: real PKCE login of admin@reticora.local to reticora-app, ID token decoded (SP/work/verify-B09/kc/idtoken-claims.txt).

The personalised OIDC path cannot work with the shipped realm: the reticora-app ID token carries neither acr nor amr and there is no 'operators' group, so issue() always refuses (403). Only break-glass is usable out of the box.

criteria.criterion: operator_audit with its own hash chain; break-glass use raises an alarm
criteria.evidence: Hash chain, append-only and tamper detection proven on PG (TestOperatorAuditChain) and observed on the real stack (rows 202-204 chained). The 'alarm' is an ERROR log line plus a counter (exposed on the live /metrics: reticora_operator_break_glass_total 0). deploy/monitoring has alertmanager.yaml but no rule for that metric (grep: no match).

criteria.evidence: authz.go routeOperator; route_permissions.txt lists the admin routes as 'operator'; TestEveryOperationRequiresItsExpectedPermission passes.

wps.soll_ist: SOLL: personalised MFA operators for /admin, break-glass alarmed, every action in a hash-chained operator_audit. IST: path isolation and the audit chain are implemented and tested. The OIDC/MFA operator path is code-complete against a fake IdP, but the shipped realm never provides the MFA signal or the group, so operators must use the shared break-glass token. The break-glass alarm is a log line and a metric without a shipped alert rule.

Keycloak (running, imported from deploy/keycloak/realm-reticora-dev.json): groups=['reticora-admin']; reticora-app defaultClientScopes=['profile','email'] (the 'acr' scope with oidc-acr-mapper is not attached); no amr mapper; acr.loa.map unset; ID token claim keys without acr/amr. grep deploy/: no rule for operator_break_glass.

findings.title: Break-glass 'alarm' is only a log line and a counter; no alert rule is shipped
findings.repro: grep -rn operator_break_glass deploy/ -> no match; deploy/monitoring has only alertmanager.yaml, slo-rules.yaml and worker-rules.yaml (alerts: HighErrorRate, HighReadLatency, Down, Worker*). The live /metrics exposes reticora_operator_break_glass_total.
findings.expected: SEC-07: every use of RETICORA_OPERATOR_TOKEN raises an alarm.
findings.actual: Nobody is notified unless an operator builds custom log or metric alerting.

findings.cause: No PrometheusRule or notification for reticora_operator_break_glass_total.
findings.recommendation: Ship an alert rule (increase(reticora_operator_break_glass_total[5m]) > 0, severity critical) in deploy/monitoring and the k8s manifests and/or a platform notification.

findings.title: Personalised operator OIDC login is impossible with the shipped Keycloak realm (no acr/amr in the ID token, no operators group)
findings.repro: Real PKCE authorization-code login of admin@reticora.local against the running Keycloak (realm imported from deploy/keycloak/realm-reticora-dev.json), client reticora-app, scope 'openid profile email'. The decoded ID token has the keys at_hash, aud, auth_time, azp, email, email_verified, exp, family_name, given_name, groups, iat, iss, jti, name, organization_id, preferred_username, session_state, sid, sub, typ; acr=None, amr=None. Keycloak admin read: groups=['reticora-admin']; reticora-app defaultClientScopes=['profile','email']; acr.loa.map unset. operator/handler.go:107 requires the group 'operators' AND MFASatisfied(amr, acr), which is false for amr=[] and acr=''.
findings.expected: SEC-07: operators in the Keycloak group 'operators' with mandatory MFA log in personally to /admin.
findings.actual: Every OIDC operator login is refused with 403 'login is not an operator with MFA', whatever factors the user used. Only the break-glass token works.
findings.user_impact: Operators must share the break-glass token for routine work (entitlements, org creation), which defeats personalised accountability and floods the break-glass signal.
findings.cause: The realm exports lack an 'operators' group, an amr mapper and the acr client scope or LoA mapping on reticora-app; docs/README.md:277-284 does not describe the required IdP setup.
findings.recommendation: Add the 'operators' group, attach the acr scope (with acr.loa.map so that OTP yields acr=2) or an amr mapper to reticora-app in both realm exports, and document it.
findings.retest: e2e-real: an operator-group user with OTP logs in via POST /api/v1/admin/auth/callback -> 200 operator token and GET /api/v1/admin/me 200; the same user without OTP -> 403; a non-operator with OTP -> 403.

test_gaps.proposed_test: promtool test rules: reticora_operator_break_glass_total 0 -> 1 fires ReticoraOperatorBreakGlassUsed within 1m; a constant series does not fire.

The realm finding is upgraded from P3 (unconfirmed hypothesis) to P2 with cause_confirmed=true: I ran a real PKCE login against the running Keycloak and decoded the ID token (no acr, no amr) and read the realm and client config read-only via the admin API (no operators group, only the profile and email scopes on reticora-app). Run `cd backend && go test -count=1 -run 'TestEntitlementsAreWrittenByOperatorsOnly$' -v ./internal/operator/`. The test uses NewAuditor(nil), whose Record always returns an error.

findings.title: Linking a CI to an asset without a location silently clears the CI's location, site and room
findings.repro:
Overlay probe SPV/overlay/ci_verify_b10_test.go (scopetest tag b2, audit_db_13):
1. svc.Create a CI with LocationID=room1.
2. Insert an asset without a location.
3. svc.Update(ctx, org, ci, UpdateRequest{AssetID:&asset, Manual:&ManualChange{}}). This is the PATCH /api/v1/cis/{id} {asset_id} path.
Output: err=<nil>; location|site|room before=room1|site|room1, after=||.
findings.expected: No silent loss of the location: either the asset takes the CI's location (as the 000088 backfill does at :19-21) or the request is refused with 422.
findings.actual: ci_mirror_asset_location sets NEW.location_id := NULL (000088:65). trg_ci_derive_location then clears site_id and room_id. The service has no guard (service.go:297-363).
findings.user_impact: The CI loses its location and site/room scope. This can change site-scoped RLS visibility and break location-based views. Exposure in G1 is limited: assets are created via the P2 inventory API.

findings.title: A client-scoped principal can set parent_ci_id to a CI of another client
findings.repro:
Overlay probe SPV/overlay/ci_verify_b10_test.go on audit_db_13:
1. c1 = CI of Client1; c2 = CI of Client2.
2. svc.Update(f.ClientCtx(Client1), org, c1, UpdateRequest{ParentCIID:&c2, Manual:…}) (the PATCH /api/v1/cis/{id} path).
3. Result: err=<nil>; ci.parent_ci_id stored = c2; the client-1 GET of c1 returns parent_ci_id=c2; the client-2 chassis now has 1 child of client 1.
findings.expected: TEN-05 client scope: a client-1 principal can only reference CIs it can see. Setting a parent that is invisible to it is refused with 422 parent_ci_id 'parent CI not found'.
findings.actual: The composite FK (id, organization_id) is checked without RLS, and neither the service nor the cycle trigger checks visibility or client consistency.
findings.user_impact: Cross-client integrity breach in MSP orgs: a scoped user can attach its devices under another client's chassis (given a leaked or guessed id). Client 2's composition is altered by a foreign client and reports become inconsistent.
findings.cause: FK checks bypass RLS; ci/service.go and pg_repository.go do not verify that the parent is visible (systemic; same pattern as subnet.vlan_id in WP-081).
findings.recommendation: In the repository transaction, SELECT the parent under RLS (422 'parent CI not found' if invisible) and require the same client (or an org-wide parent), or enforce it with a trigger.
findings.retest: PG test: a client-1 ctx sets the parent to a client-2 CI → 422 parent_ci_id, nothing stored. Same-client and org-wide parents succeed.

findings.title: Migration 000089 turns cyclic legacy 'contains' rows into a parent_ci_id cycle

1. ctx = scopetest ClientCtx(Client1), i.e. app.client_scope=client1.

3. repo.UpdateVRF(ctx, org, <default global>, {Name:'renamed-by-client1', Description:…}) → err=<nil>; name is now 'renamed-by-client1'.
4. repo.DeleteVRF(ctx, org, vb10-scoped) → err=<nil>.
The same holds in SQL as reticora_app (SPV/probe_vrf_clientscope.sql). These are the functions behind POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/vrfs.
findings.expected: TEN-05: 'Ein client-gescopter Nutzer kann keine org-weiten Zeilen anlegen oder ändern' and 'Tabellen ohne site_id (z. B. contact, subnet, vrf) unterliegen Org- und Client-Bedingung'. Client-scoped principals cannot create, change or delete VRFs (org-level per CH10) unless they also hold an org-wide role.

findings.user_impact: In MSP orgs a client-scoped engineer can alter or delete the org-wide routing domains of all clients. IP/subnet uniqueness semantics (per VRF) and reports for other clients are affected. The default VRF's name 'global' (CH10) can be changed.

1. Ingest a DeviceRecord with observed_at=now-30h (new CI).
2. Set last_seen_at=now-30h and status=unknown.
3. Ingest the same device with observed_at=now-20h.
findings.expected: GLO-12: time comparisons in ingest are based on the source observed_at. last_seen_at = max(stored, observed_at), i.e. about 20h old; first_seen_at of the new CI is about 30h old.

findings.title: One failing record dead-letters (queue) or rejects (HTTP) the valid records behind it in the same group/lane
findings.repro:
Verifier probe TestVerifyB11PoisonRecordOnQueuePath (package discovery, PG audit_db_14, WithIngestLanes(4)).
1. Build messages with newIngestMessages under f.ClientCtx(Client1): POISON-E2 (client_id=Client2, oldest observed_at) and GOOD-E2-0..7 (client_id=Client1).
2. consumeBatch with fake deliveries at Delivered=1, then again at Delivered=5.
findings.expected: Each valid record is processed and acked (REC-01). Only POISON-E2 is rejected or dead-lettered.
findings.actual: At Delivered=1, POISON-E2, GOOD-E2-2 and GOOD-E2-6 (lane 3) get nak. At Delivered=5 all three get term, and GOOD-E2-2 and GOOD-E2-6 have no CI rows. Valid records in lanes 0-2 are acked and persisted. Synchronous path (auditor probe): HTTP 403 and good=0.
findings.user_impact: Valid discovery data that the server has already confirmed with 202 is silently dropped after 5 deliveries (only a log line and a metric remain) whenever one record of the lane fails deterministically (scope mismatch, constraint violation).
findings.cause: processItems stops at the failing record (discovery.go:1076). consumeBatch decides the fate of every unsettled message of the group from that single error: Term at Delivered()>=ingestMaxDeliver (consumer.go:981-985), otherwise Nak (:989).
findings.recommendation: Isolate failures per record. Classify non-retryable errors (42501 RLS, permission, check or unique violation, validation), dead-letter only that record and settle it, then continue with the rest of the group. Return per-record results (rejected count) on the synchronous HTTP path instead of a blanket 403.
findings.retest: PG plus NATS: a group with one out-of-scope record and two valid records in the same lane. The valid ones are persisted and acked at Delivered==1; only the bad one is terminated or counted (IngestDeadLetters+1). The HTTP inline path answers 202 with a rejected count. A transient error (DB restart) still redelivers without loss.

findings.title: 'new' on resurrected_device creates an org-wide CI without identity: cross-client visibility and an endless review loop
findings.repro:
Verifier probe TestVerifyB11ResurrectNew (PG audit_db_14).
1. A Client1 CI with primary_mac 00:1b:21:e6:e6:01 is soft-deleted.
2. Ingest a DeviceRecord with that MAC and client_id=Client1 (no serial): a resurrected_device review opens.
3. POST /api/v1/review-items/{id}/resolve {"action":"new"} returns 200.
4. Read the new CI as a principal restricted to Client2.
5. Ingest the device twice more.
findings.expected: The new CI belongs to Client1, carries the MAC (and UUID or fingerprint) and is invisible to Client2. The next sighting updates it (Updated=1, no review).
findings.actual: The new CI has client_id=NULL and primary_mac=NULL. The Client2 principal can read it (GetByID err=nil). The next sightings give created=0, updated=0, resurrected=1, and an open resurrected_device review persists.
findings.user_impact: Devices of one client (customer) become visible to users of other clients. Discovery never maintains the device again (stale CI), and the operator gets the same review again after each resolution. Choosing 'merge' afterwards creates a real duplicate (new CI plus reactivated one).
findings.cause: discovery/review.go:164-187 ActionNew builds ci.Item only from name, type, manufacturer, model, serial, IP, hostname and FQDN (no ClientID, PrimaryMAC, HardwareUUID, fingerprint, SysObjectID or provenance). reviewItemFromConflict does not store client_id. identity.go:182 then excludes the org-wide CI for a client-bound record.
findings.recommendation: Store client_id, site_id and vrf_id in the review payload. Create the 'new' CI through the same path as discovered CIs (discoveredCI), with client binding, hardware_uuid, primary_mac, fingerprint, sys_object_id and provenance. Apply the same to ambiguous_identity 'new'.
findings.retest: PG: repeat the probe and assert client_id=Client1, primary_mac set, and that a Client2 principal gets not found. The next sighting gives Updated=1, Resurrected=0 and no open review. Same for ambiguous_identity 'new'. A client-2-scoped resolver gets 404 for the review.

findings.retest: API test through the full router: a foreign resolved_by stores the caller's id (or returns 400), and the unlicensed_ci audit_log actor is the caller.

findings.title: A dismissed override_conflict value stays suppressed after the reported value changed
findings.repro:
Verifier probe TestVerifyB11DismissSuppressionUntilChange (reviews_test, PG audit_db_14, real override repository, same adapter semantics as production).
S1:
1. Override model=manual-model.
2. redfish reports seen-1 (item A); dismiss A.
3. The source reports manual-model (no conflict).
4. The source reports seen-1.
S2:
1. Dismiss seen-1.
2. seen-2 opens B; accept B (override removed, model=seen-2).
3. Set a new override manual-2.
4. The source reports seen-1.
findings.expected: REC-12: suppression ends with the next change of the reported value. Both S1 step 4 and S2 step 4 open a new override_conflict.
findings.actual: Both give ReviewItems=0 and no open override_conflict, although _observed/discovered_value=seen-1 diverges from the override. Control: an undismissed value (seen-9) opens an item.
findings.user_impact: A divergence between source and manual override is silently not reviewed. This is especially the case after a new override, where the old dismissal belonged to a different decision context.
findings.cause: OpenUnlessDismissed (reviews/service.go:89-101) compares the incoming value only with the newest dismissed item of the object and kind. Intervening observations, acceptances and override changes do not reset the suppression.
findings.recommendation: Tie the suppression to the observation history. Store the dismissed value on ci_field_value (e.g. suppressed_value) and clear it when the reported value changes or the override is set or cleared. Alternatively, consider only a dismissal newer than the last observed value change and the last override change.
findings.retest: PG: repeat S1 and S2 and assert a new override_conflict opens. The direct repeat of the dismissed value without an intervening change is still suppressed.

test_gaps.description: Dismiss suppression edge cases (intervening value change, accept, override change)

Downgraded from BESTANDEN to TEILWEISE/P3. I checked that the test adapter pgOverrides matches production overrideProvenance (report_adapters.go:97-123), so the PG evidence for the direct path holds.

I reproduced two scenarios on PG where a changed reported value does not lift the suppression, with a positive control. REC-12 'bis zur nächsten Änderung' is therefore only partly met.

findings.title: Manually documented IPs (type reserved/static) and interfaces on a discovered CI are deleted after three discovery runs
findings.repro:
Verifier probe TestVerifyB11MissResetAndReservedIP (PG).
1. A discovered CI with eth0 (192.0.2.243).
2. INSERT ip_address 192.0.2.244 type='reserved' on eth0.
3. Three records reporting eth0 with only 192.0.2.243.
findings.expected: Unclear. REC-07 says 'Interfaces/IPs werden nach 3 Fehlläufen entfernt'. The NET-03 type column (discovered, reserved, static, dhcp) and the REC-03 rank principle (manual 100 > snmp 80) suggest that non-discovered entries should not be removed by automation.
findings.actual: The reserved address is deleted (rows left=0), with only a ci_change history row.
findings.user_impact: Manually maintained IPAM data on discovered devices can disappear without user action.
findings.cause: missAndRemove counts every ip_address of the CI's interfaces and every network_interface of the CI that the record did not report (ipam/pg_repository.go:619-640), without filtering on ip_address.type or on any source of the interface.

findings.retest: PG: a reserved or static IP and a manual interface on a discovered CI, then 3 records without them. Assert the decided behaviour (kept, or removed with history).

findings.title: Manual override endpoint accepts reserved namespace names; _instance values are destroyed permanently
findings.repro:
Verifier probe TestVerifyB11FullRouter (NewRouter with authz and middleware.OpenAPIValidation, PG). CI with attributes {"owner":"ops","_instance":{"slot":"7"}} and an instance definition 'slot'.
1. PUT /api/v1/cis/{id}/fields/_instance/override {"value":"x","reason":"vprobe"}.
2. PUT .../_provenance/override.
3. DELETE .../_instance/override.
findings.expected: 400 naming the reserved field (GLO-13, E-23), attributes unchanged, no ci_field_value row.
findings.actual: 200 for all three calls. attributes._instance = "x", and after DELETE it is still "x" (slot=7 lost). _provenance is temporarily replaced by "x". Two ci_field_value rows with field_name _instance and _provenance remain.
findings.user_impact: A user with override:write can, even by mistake via the API, irreversibly destroy a CI's instance attributes and corrupt the CI-10 namespaces that the API read view and reconciliation rely on.
findings.cause: override.PGRepository.SetOverride refuses only structuralFields (pg_repository.go:327). syncCIField (:613) writes jsonb_set(attributes, '{<fieldName>}', value). The handler (handler.go:67-127) and OpenAPI (name: type string, no pattern) do not check reserved names.
findings.recommendation: Reject fieldmeta.ReservedNames in SetOverride and ClearOverride, and in the handler with 400 and the field name. Add a DB check constraint ci_field_value.field_name NOT IN ('_overrides','_observed','_provenance','_instance'), and a pattern in OpenAPI.
findings.retest: API test through the full router: PUT and DELETE for each of the 4 names return 400 with the field. attributes._instance and the projections are unchanged, and there is no ci_field_value row. A normal attribute override still returns 200.

test_gaps.description: Reserved names on the override endpoints
test_gaps.proposed_test: For each of the 4 names: PUT and DELETE /api/v1/cis/{id}/fields/{name}/override return 400 with the field. attributes._instance and the projections are unchanged and there is no ci_field_value row. Positive: a normal attribute override returns 200.

test_gaps.description: POST /api/v1/cis over HTTP and the merge path with reserved keys (repository tests)
test_gaps.proposed_test: HTTP POST /api/v1/cis with attributes {_observed:{}} returns 400 with violations[].field=attributes._observed (the verifier probe shows this today). POST /cis/{id}/merge where the victim carries legacy reserved top-level keys does not copy them into business keys.

test_gaps.description: Migration 000099 backfill and down on seeded data (repository test)
test_gaps.proposed_test: Execute the 000099 up data statements and the down data statements in a rolled-back transaction on seeded legacy CIs (as in SP/work/verify-B11/mig099_probe.sql). Assert the _provenance, _overrides and _observed projection, the _instance move and the reversal.

wps.upgrade_conditions: BESTANDEN once the override endpoints reject reserved names (API test passing for PUT and DELETE with all four names, plus a DB constraint), together with HTTP-level create and merge negative tests and a repository data test of the 000099 backfill and down path.
wps.verifier_note:
Upheld FEHLGESCHLAGEN/P2. I tried to refute it via the production middleware. The OpenAPI path parameter 'name' has no pattern and middleware/openapi.go only checks content type and valid JSON. The full-router probe reproduces 200 for PUT _instance and _provenance.

The probe adds two things: DELETE is also accepted, and the original _instance values stay lost after clearing, so the data loss is permanent. POST and PATCH /cis are correctly refused over HTTP (400 with field).

Criterion 3 changed from partial to yes. A verbatim execution of the 000099 up and down data statements on seeded legacy data (rolled-back transaction) gives the correct CI-10 document and a clean reversal. A repository test is still listed as a gap.

wps.title: TLS/ACME im Installer: Erkennung, Kettenprüfung, funktionsfähiger Standardpfad
wps.user_goal: With a TLS domain the installer serves a bootstrap certificate, then obtains, validates (chain) and serves a trusted Let's Encrypt certificate that stays renewed. Without a domain no TLS config is rendered and the default HTTP path works.
wps.implementation: install-cloud.sh:784-790 tls_cert_is_trusted (openssl verify -untrusted), 796-798 tls_cert_is_selfsigned, 803-809 tls_template_source, 815-863 bootstrap_tls_cert (self-signed placeholder written directly into letsencrypt/live/<domain>/, chmod 644 at 862), 876-913 validate_tls_material, 923-961 issue_tls_certificate ('compose run --rm --no-deps --entrypoint certbot certbot certonly --webroot', 942-946); main order 1657-1661 (bootstrap -> start_stack -> issue). docker-compose.yml:370 (frontend 'user: nginx'), 382 (letsencrypt :ro), 388 (RETICORA_NGINX_TLS_TEMPLATE), 415-426 (certbot renew loop, no deploy hook); frontend/docker-entrypoint.d/25-reticora-tls-optional.sh; nginx-tls.conf.template:47-48 (live/<domain>/fullchain.pem, privkey.pem).
wps.tests: tests/install-cloud-helpers.test.sh TLS cases ok (SP/runs/sh-install-cloud-helpers.log). The ACME test stubs certbot by copying a chain into live/ (tests/install-cloud-helpers.test.sh:199-204). Verifier probe V/certbot/cli_probe.py -> V/certbot/cli_probe.log drives the REAL certbot 2.11.0 CLI (certbot._internal.main.main ['certonly','--webroot',…]); only account registration and the ACME order are patched. Starting from the exact bootstrap_tls_cert state: run 1 'CertStorageError: live directory exists for cmdb.example.com', ACME orders=1, renewal/cmdb.example.com.conf size 0. Run 2 (re-run) 'Successfully received certificate … live/cmdb.example.com-0001/', ACME orders=2, live/<domain>/fullchain.pem still the placeholder (openssl verify 'error 18 … self-signed', rc=2). Modes created by certbot: archive/ 700 root, archive/<lineage>/privkey1.pem 600 root. A uid 101:101 container reading the bind mount: bootstrap privkey (installer chmod 644) READ_OK; certbot-issued privkey.pem and fullchain.pem DENIED.

criteria.criterion: Detection of self-signed certificates by chain validation (openssl verify)
criteria.evidence: tls_cert_is_trusted (784-790), real openssl tests with a private CA (helpers log); verifier openssl verify on the placeholder -> error 18.

criteria.criterion: ACME path works with the container entrypoint; without a TLS domain the TLS template is not mounted
criteria.evidence: Entrypoint override correct (942) and template selection correct (tls_template_source + compose variable + 25-reticora-tls-optional.sh). The ACME path itself does not work: (a) certbot cannot store the lineage beside the placeholder (real CLI probe); (b) even when stored, the files are unreadable for the nginx user the frontend runs as (uid 101 probe).

criteria.criterion: Default HTTP/ACME paths match the working installation path required by TEC-09
criteria.evidence: ACME path non-functional (above). Default HTTP path only CI-claimed (g1-installation.md). The domain path aborts even earlier at the WP-095 issuer check.

layers.ux: GAP: failed issuance only warns, and the self-signed bootstrap stays (browser warnings); a re-run dies in validate_tls_material
layers.api: N/A
layers.data: FAIL: certbot leaves an empty renewal/<domain>.conf and a stray <domain>-0001 lineage; issued key material is unreadable (0700/0600 root) for the uid 101 frontend
layers.e2e: FAIL: Let's Encrypt issuance cannot be stored or served (real certbot CLI probe). The HTTP default path is only CI-documented.
layers.robustness: FAIL: a re-run after a failed issuance stores <domain>-0001 while live/<domain> keeps the placeholder, so validate_tls_material(domain,1) dies; each attempt consumes an ACME order (rate limits). No nginx reload after 'certbot renew'.

wps.soll_ist: SOLL: a working ACME path with chain validation; no TLS template without a domain. IST: chain validation and template selection work. ACME issuance fails at certbot's storage step (pre-populated live dir). The certbot-issued files would also be unreadable by the unprivileged nginx, and renewals are never reloaded.
wps.evidence: V/certbot/cli_probe.py + cli_probe.log (real certbot CLI, runs 1 and 2); stat/uid-101 read probe output (cited in tests); W/probe-certbot/probe.py (auditor, direct new_lineage); install-cloud.sh:815-863, 923-961; docker-compose.yml:370,382,415-426; tests/install-cloud-helpers.test.sh:191-208.

findings.title: certbot certonly cannot store the Let's Encrypt certificate because the bootstrap placeholder occupies letsencrypt/live/<domain>/
findings.repro: V/certbot/cli_probe.py with W/venv-certbot/bin/python -I (certbot 2.11.0 = the pinned image version). Create the placeholder exactly like bootstrap_tls_cert in <tmp>/letsencrypt/live/cmdb.example.com/. Call certbot._internal.main.main(['certonly','--webroot','-w',…,'-d','cmdb.example.com','--config-dir',<tmp>/letsencrypt,'--non-interactive','--agree-tos','--register-unsafely-without-email']) with only _determine_account / Client.__init__ / Client.obtain_certificate patched (no network). Run twice.
findings.expected: After issue_tls_certificate, letsencrypt/live/<domain>/fullchain.pem is the issued chain, validate_tls_material <domain> 1 passes, nginx serves it, and a re-run is idempotent.
findings.actual: Run 1: one ACME order is consumed, then 'CertStorageError: live directory exists for cmdb.example.com'; renewal/cmdb.example.com.conf is left empty (0 bytes); the placeholder stays. Run 2 (installer re-run): certbot succeeds into live/cmdb.example.com-0001 (second ACME order), while live/cmdb.example.com/fullchain.pem stays self-signed (openssl verify error 18), so validate_tls_material(domain,1) at install-cloud.sh:947 dies.
findings.user_impact: Domain installations never get a trusted certificate (permanent browser warnings). Re-running the installer aborts, and Let's Encrypt orders and rate limits are consumed on each attempt.
findings.cause: issue_tls_certificate runs 'certbot certonly' without removing or moving the placeholder in live/<domain>. certbot storage.py new_lineage (lines 1086-1089) refuses a non-empty live dir after obtain_certificate (client.py:517-528). The unit test replaces certbot with a file copy (tests/install-cloud-helpers.test.sh:199-204).
findings.recommendation: Before certonly, move live/<domain> (and any archive/<domain>, renewal/<domain>.conf) aside and restore it on failure; or keep the placeholder outside certbot's tree and point nginx at a stable path/symlink switched after issuance. Replace the certbot stub with a Pebble integration test.
findings.retest: Pebble plus certbot/certbot:v2.11.0 with the bootstrap present: issue_tls_certificate -> live/<domain>/fullchain.pem chains to the Pebble root, validate_tls_material <domain> 1 passes; second installer run: no new order, no -0001 lineage, no die.

findings.title: Certbot-issued key and chain are unreadable for the unprivileged nginx user of the frontend container
findings.repro: After run 2 of V/certbot/cli_probe.py: stat shows letsencrypt/archive 700 root, archive/cmdb.example.com-0001/privkey1.pem 600 root. 'docker run --rm --user 101:101 -v <tmp>/letsencrypt:/etc/letsencrypt:ro redis:7-alpine cat …' -> live/cmdb.example.com/privkey.pem (installer chmod 644) READ_OK; live/cmdb.example.com-0001/privkey.pem and fullchain.pem 'Permission denied'. The frontend runs nginx:alpine as 'user: nginx' (uid 101; docker-compose.yml:370) and reads /etc/letsencrypt/live/<domain>/{fullchain,privkey}.pem (nginx-tls.conf.template:47-48).
findings.expected: Once issuance is fixed, nginx loads the issued certificate on reload and on every restart.
findings.actual: certbot (root in its container) creates archive/ 0700 and privkey 0600. No chmod/chgrp or deploy hook exists (install-cloud.sh chmods only the bootstrap at 848/862). nginx -s reload fails inside the container, but the installer only checks the exit code of the signal send, and the next frontend restart fails to load the key.
findings.user_impact: Latent: after the lineage bug is fixed, HTTPS would keep serving the placeholder from memory, and the frontend (whole UI) would fail to start after the next restart or host reboot.
findings.cause: The bootstrap path makes files world-readable for the uid 101 nginx, but certbot-managed archive/ and privkey files keep certbot's restrictive default modes; nothing adapts them.
findings.recommendation: Add a certbot --deploy-hook (both in the installer's certonly and the renew loop) that sets group-readable modes for a shared gid (or copies fullchain/privkey to an nginx-readable location), then reloads nginx. Assert readability by uid 101 in the Pebble test.
findings.retest: Pebble integration: after issuance and after a forced 'certbot renew --force-renewal', 'docker compose exec frontend cat /etc/letsencrypt/live/<domain>/privkey.pem' succeeds, 'nginx -t' passes as uid 101, and 'docker compose restart frontend' becomes healthy serving the Pebble-issued chain.

findings.title: Renewed certificates are never loaded: no nginx reload after 'certbot renew'
findings.repro: docker-compose.yml:423 certbot loop runs 'certbot renew … --quiet' every 12 h without --deploy-hook. grep -rn reload frontend/docker-entrypoint.d frontend/Dockerfile deploy/docker-compose/docker-compose.yml shows nothing; install-cloud.sh reloads only during installation (950, reload_frontend_after_bootstrap).
findings.expected: A renewed certificate is served within the renewal window without a manual restart.
findings.actual: nginx keeps the certificate loaded at start/reload in memory; after renewal (~day 60) it serves the old certificate until it expires (day 90) unless the frontend is restarted.
findings.user_impact: Expired-certificate outage roughly 90 days after issuance on long-running hosts.
findings.cause: No deploy hook or periodic reload links the certbot container's renewal to the frontend's nginx.
findings.recommendation: A deploy hook that signals the frontend (shared PID namespace/docker socket is not desirable). Alternatively a periodic 'nginx -s reload' loop in the frontend entrypoint (common nginx-certbot pattern) or an inotify watcher.

findings.title: OIDC issuer check runs before the frontend (issuer proxy) is started, so domain/TLS installations abort
findings.repro: V/issuer/order.sh <dir>: sources HEAD install-cloud.sh (minus main; diff against the repo is empty) and stubs compose/wait/sync/migrations/admin. curl answers https://cmdb.example.test/* only after 'up -d server frontend'; the Keycloak host port localhost:8180 always answers. Set RETICORA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://cmdb.example.test, RETICORA_TLS_DOMAIN=cmdb.example.test, RETICORA_OIDC_ISSUER_URL=https://cmdb.example.test/realms/reticora (the default from install-cloud.sh:603). Call start_stack.
findings.expected: A fresh installation with a public domain completes, and both issuer checks pass once the issuer endpoint is served.
findings.actual: start_stack rc=1: '✘ Error: The OIDC issuer https://cmdb.example.test/realms/reticora is not reachable from this host …'. Compose calls stop after 'up -d keycloak'. Every re-run aborts at the same point.
findings.user_impact: The production installation path with domain/TLS (TEC-09) is blocked. Operators must fall back to http://<ip>:8180, contrary to the documented reverse-proxy form.
findings.cause: check_issuer_from_host/check_issuer_from_container were appended to validate_keycloak_bootstrap, which start_stack calls (1385) before 'up -d server frontend' (1389). The shell tests stub curl and never model a frontend-served issuer.
findings.recommendation: Run the strict host and container issuer checks after the server and frontend are up (stop before admin/summary on failure), or probe Keycloak directly with the public Host / X-Forwarded-Proto headers while the frontend is down. Add a sequencing regression test.
findings.retest: Shell: start_stack with a public-hostname issuer whose curl stub answers only after the frontend start -> rc=0, both checks executed after 'up -d server frontend'. Re-read start_stack (1385 before 1389), the issuer default (603), the frontend /realms/ proxy, and the troubleshooting doc, which itself recommends https://<domain>/realms/reticora behind the reverse proxy (i.e. the blocked form). findings.title: Re-run does not apply a rotated Keycloak admin password, OIDC client secret or other realm changes to an existing Keycloak
findings.repro: V/kcrot/run.sh: throwaway compose (timescale as keycloak-db, keycloak/keycloak:24.0 'start --import-realm --hostname-strict=false', import dir bind-mounted like docker-compose.yml:238). Phase 1: KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD=old-admin-1, realm 'rot' with client 'app' secret SECRET_A -> ready; kcadm login old rc=0; client-secret SECRET_A. Phase 2 (as an installer re-run with rotated values): re-render the realm file with SECRET_B, 'up -d' with KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD=new-admin-2 (container recreated).
findings.expected: After the re-run, Keycloak accepts the rotated admin password used by create_initial_admin, the client secret in Keycloak equals RETICORA_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET in .env, and realm settings re-rendered by configure_realm take effect (as troubleshooting-installation.md:152 promises).
findings.actual: Keycloak logs 'Realm 'rot' already exists. Import skipped'. kcadm login with new-admin-2 rc=1, with old-admin-1 rc=0; client secret still SECRET_A. Applied to install-cloud.sh: create_initial_admin dies 'Could not log in to the Keycloak admin API as admin' (1514-1516), and with a rotated client secret the server's token exchange uses SECRET_B against Keycloak's SECRET_A (login broken).
findings.user_impact: Operators following INS-05 rotation (or deleting a secret from .env, which the docs say regenerates it) get an aborted installer or broken sign-in. The documented 'Invalid redirect uri: re-run the installer' fix does not work.
findings.cause: KEYCLOAK_ADMIN/KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD only bootstrap the master admin on first start, and --import-realm skips existing realms. The installer has no kcadm step to update the admin password, client secret or redirect URIs (kcadm is used only for users in create_initial_admin).
findings.recommendation: On re-run, apply rotations through kcadm: authenticate with the previous admin password (kept in .env history or asked for) and set the new one; 'kcadm update clients/<id> -s secret=…' and redirectUris/webOrigins from the rendered realm. Alternatively document rotation as manual steps and stop promising re-run fixes for realm settings.
findings.retest: Real Keycloak 24 integration (docker-gated): first install with A, rotate KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD, RETICORA_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET and RETICORA_OIDC_REDIRECT_URL in .env, run the installer's Keycloak steps -> kcadm login with the new password OK, the client secret equals .env, redirectUris contain the new URL, and a client_credentials token request with the new secret returns 200 (old secret 401).

findings.title: object_storage readiness dials the raw RETICORA_S3_ENDPOINT, so URL-form or portless endpoints accepted by the S3 client keep /readyz at 503 forever
findings.repro: V/probe-s3-readyz.sh: HEAD binary (port 18915, DB audit_db_15, Redis db 15, shared MinIO with the existing bucket), once with RETICORA_S3_ENDPOINT=localhost:9000 and once with http://localhost:9000.
findings.expected: Any endpoint form NewS3Store accepts (blob.go:172-186 parses 'http(s)://host[:port]'; minio-go accepts host without port) is probed at the same host:port, so /readyz is 200 when S3 works.

findings.actual: Only a daily full backup over TLS to an external 'reticora-db' host. WAL archiving and the pgbackrest TLS server on that host are left to the operator (configmap comments 1-9, backup-dr.md:81-84).

findings.title: Backup bucket versioning/replication not enforced; Terraform 'production requires replica' is warning-only (executed)
findings.repro: terraform 1.9.8 in a scratch copy of deploy/terraform: init -backend=false, then plan -var environment=production gives exit 0 and 'Warning: Check block assertion failed' (main.tf:53). plan -var environment=production -var region=eu-central-1 -var backup_replica_region=eu-central-1 also gives exit 0 with a warning. tests/backup-config.test.sh:74 only greps for the check block.
findings.expected: Versioned and replicated buckets (NFR-05), enforced for production.
findings.actual: No bucket resources exist. The backup_policy output has the literal versioning=true. The pgBackRest S3 bucket gets neither versioning nor replication from any code. A production plan passes.
findings.user_impact: Backups and documents can live in a single region, unversioned, without any gate noticing (NFR-05).
findings.cause: A provider-neutral skeleton, and a `check` block (warning semantics) used instead of a validation or precondition.
findings.recommendation: Use a variable validation or lifecycle precondition that fails plan. Implement bucket resources (versioning and replication) for at least one provider. Make backup-config.test.sh run terraform plan instead of grep.
findings.retest: terraform plan -var environment=production must exit non-zero without a replica, and also when replica == backup region. With an EU replica it passes.

findings.title: reticora-backup.sh scheduler crashes on RETICORA_BACKUP_HOUR=08/09 and silently mis-schedules invalid values
findings.repro: In timescale/timescaledb:2.17.2-pg16 (busybox sh), eval seconds_until_hour from reticora-backup.sh:38-43 under set -eu. HOUR=08 or 09 gives 'sh: arithmetic syntax error'. HOUR=24 and HOUR=abc give the same wait as hour 0 (midnight), with no error (SP/work/verify-B13/scheduler-hour-busybox.log).
findings.expected: Validate 0-23 at start, and parse '08' correctly.
findings.actual: For 08/09 the run loop exits after start-up. On restart, a backup already exists, so it crash-loops without taking daily base backups; health is unhealthy only after 26 h. For 24/abc, backups silently run at 00:00 UTC.
findings.user_impact: Daily base backups stop after a plausible config value (WAL archiving by postgres continues, so the restore window grows), or run at an unexpected time.
findings.cause: $(( HOUR - … )) treats a leading-zero 08/09 as invalid octal; a non-numeric HOUR evaluates to 0; there is no validation.
findings.recommendation: Strip leading zeros, validate 0..23 at start and exit with a clear message.
findings.retest: backup-config.test.sh: HOUR=0/08/23 give 0<secs<=86400; HOUR=24/-1/abc give a non-zero exit at start.

findings.title: pgBackRest tarball not checksum-verified; base image unpinned (also in the signed release image)
findings.repro: deploy/docker-compose/postgres/Dockerfile:7 has ARG TIMESCALE_IMAGE=timescale/timescaledb:latest-pg16; lines 12-17 run curl | tar xz with no sha256. release.yml:127-129 builds reticora-postgres with no build-args, so the signed release image also floats on latest-pg16.
findings.expected: A reproducible, integrity-checked DB image (TEC-15 spirit).
findings.actual: A floating base and an unverified download.
findings.user_impact: Supply-chain and reproducibility risk; a rebuild can silently change the TimescaleDB version.
findings.cause: No pinning or checksum.
findings.recommendation: Pin the base by version or digest (2.17.2-pg16 as in CI) and verify the tarball sha256.
findings.retest: A static test asserts the digest/sha256; the CI image build succeeds.

wps.title: Restore-Nachweis RPO 15 min / RTO 4 h
wps.user_goal: An operator gets a measured PITR restore proof (RPO 15 min / RTO 4 h), kept as an artifact and in the docs, and the workflow fails when a limit is exceeded.
wps.implementation:
- tests/restore-pitr.sh:35-39: limits RPO 900 s and RTO 14400 s; WRITE_SECONDS default 420.
- restore-pitr.sh:137-151: scenario 1, PITR exactness.
- restore-pitr.sh:153-170: scenario 2, data-volume loss, RPO = last_commit - restored_last.
- restore-pitr.sh:172-186: archiving after restore, report and exit code.
- .github/workflows/restore-test.yml (pitr job, nightly, artifact restore-pitr-report).
- docs/backup-dr.md:126-161: proof description and the measured table.
wps.tests: No test exercises the script's limit logic, and no baseline entry exists. A local run is impossible: the verifier attempted the pgBackRest image build plain and with the proxy+CA workaround from /root/.ccr/README.md. Both failed (SP/work/verify-B13/pg-image-build.log 'DNS lookup error'; pg-image-build2.log 'dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org … Permission denied'). Host curl gives 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403' for the Alpine CDN and 403 for the GitHub pgBackRest tarball. RETICORA_POSTGRES_IMAGE cannot help because no prebuilt image exists locally. The CI pitr run is not observable.

criteria.criterion: restore-test.yml runs a PITR restore to a point in time and measures duration and data loss; result as artifact and in docs/backup-dr.md
criteria.evidence: Implemented (restore-pitr.sh:137-170; restore-test.yml artifact plus summary; backup-dr.md:150-157). Not executable here; the blocker was reproduced by the verifier. The documented figures come from a 30 s write run, not the committed default of 420 s.

criteria.criterion: If the proof exceeds the limits, the workflow fails
criteria.evidence: The exit code is propagated (restore-pitr.sh:186), so exactness and RTO violations would fail. The RPO comparison cannot fail with the defaults: restored_last >= the scenario-1 target time, so rpo <= ~2 s + rto_pitr + 420 s < 900 s. The doc's own run (RPO 52 s with 30 s of writes, so zero write-phase rows recovered) was reported as passed.

layers.ux: N/A
layers.api: N/A
layers.data: GAP: PITR exactness is implemented but never executed observably.
layers.e2e: GAP: blocked locally (reproduced); the CI run is not observable.
layers.robustness: GAP: the RPO assertion is non-discriminating. There is no negative run (missing WAL segment, archive_timeout > 900 s, wrong cipher), and RTO is measured on a 50k-row toy database only.

wps.soll_ist:
Required: a measured PITR proof that fails on a limit violation.

Actual:
- The script and workflow are structurally present but cannot be executed here (a real network-policy blocker).
- The RPO limit check cannot fail with the defaults.
- The documented figures come from a different parameterisation.

wps.dependencies: WP-100 (pgBackRest image/compose); network access to the Alpine CDN and GitHub for the image build; GitHub Actions for an observable run

findings.title: RPO limit check in restore-pitr.sh cannot fail with default parameters
findings.repro: tests/restore-pitr.sh:39 sets WRITE_SECONDS=420. Lines 157-169 set rpo = last_commit - restored_last and FAIL only if rpo > 900. restored_last >= the max(at) of the phase-A rows, which are restored by WAL replay to the scenario-1 target, so rpo <= 2 s + rto_pitr + overhead + 420 s. That is < 900 s whenever restore succeeds on a small database. Empirical: docs/backup-dr.md:150-157 reports RPO 52 s with a 30 s write window. 52 > 30 means no write-phase row was restored, yet it was reported PASS.
findings.expected: The workflow fails when the achieved RPO exceeds 15 min, e.g. with archive_timeout misconfigured above 900 s (criterion 2).
findings.actual: With archive_timeout=3600, the 420 s write window would still give rpo < 900 and PASS. Only the separate `pgbackrest check` catches a totally broken archive_command.
findings.user_impact: False assurance that RPO 15 min is proven; regressions in archive cadence go undetected.
findings.cause: The measurement window is shorter than the limit.
findings.recommendation: Write longer than the limit (RESTORE_WRITE_SECONDS >= 1000), or assert RPO <= archive_timeout + margin (<= 360 s). Add a negative self-test with archive_timeout=1200 that must fail.
findings.retest: An archive_timeout=1200 override run exits 1 with an 'RPO … FAIL' row. A run with defaults passes with RPO < 360 s.

findings.title: Documented restore figures stem from a non-default 30 s run on a toy dataset
findings.repro: docs/backup-dr.md:150 says 'Measured on 2026-10-12 with a 50,000 row workload and 30 s of writes' (RPO 52 s, RTO 5 s). tests/restore-pitr.sh:39 defaults to 420 s, and backup-dr.md:139-140 claims writes run 7 minutes.
findings.expected: The doc table corresponds to the committed proof, with an RTO statement for realistic data volume.
findings.actual: Stale, non-default figures.
findings.user_impact: Misleading NFR-05 acceptance evidence.
findings.cause: The measurement was not repeated after the default changed.
findings.recommendation: Re-run with the defaults, update from the CI artifact, and add a representative-size run.
findings.retest: The doc table equals the latest restore-pitr-report.md artifact.

wps.title: Signierte Releases: cosign, SBOM, verpflichtende Signaturprüfung im Updater
wps.user_goal: Operators and collectors install and auto-update only release artifacts signed keyless by the project's release workflow, with an SBOM per release (TEC-15, COL-06).
wps.implementation:
**.github/workflows/release.yml:**
- Triggered on tag v*; the outage job is a prerequisite (lines 23-28, 108).
- binaries job: collector and agent for amd64/arm64, syft SBOMs, cosign sign-blob --bundle, verify-blob, updater manifests.
- images job (113-169): server, collector, frontend and postgres to ghcr.io/datahub-chiemgau with tag ${{github.ref_name}}; SBOM, cosign sign, attest and verify.

**edgecore/update/update.go:**
- 117-162: Apply requires a Verifier and a SignatureBundleURL (ErrUnsigned), then download, checksum, bundle and Verify before the swap; on failure the staging file is removed.
- 249-296: CosignVerifier runs verify-blob with the anchored identity regexp ^https://github\.com/DataHub-Chiemgau/Reticora-CMDB/\.github/workflows/release\.yml@refs/tags/v.+$ and the GitHub OIDC issuer.

**Wiring:** collector/collectorcmd/update.go:28 (only production caller).

**Install paths:** install.sh, install-cloud.sh and install-vm.sh contain no cosign or signature check. install-vm.sh:487-498 and 550-556 download the source and Go toolchain unverified and build locally.
wps.tests:
results-edgecore.tsv: pass edgecore/update tests:
- TestApplyRefusesUnsignedAndWronglySignedReleases, all 5 subtests (unsigned_release, no_verifier, bundle_not_found, wrong_signature, valid_signature).
- TestCosignVerifierPinsTheReleaseIdentity: exact argv including the anchored identity regexp and issuer; a failing cosign propagates.
- TestFailedStartsRollBackTheUpdate, TestConfirmKeepsTheUpdate, TestHTTPSourceReadsTheChannelManifest.

The verifier is always a fake or a stubbed run func; no real cosign is involved. release.yml was not executed (needs GitHub OIDC).

criteria.criterion: Release workflow builds images/binaries, creates SBOM and signs with cosign keyless (E-31)
criteria.evidence: Implemented in release.yml (syft, cosign sign-blob/sign/attest plus self-verify). It cannot be executed outside GitHub Actions, and no release run is observable.

criteria.criterion: edgecore/update refuses updates without a valid signature
criteria.evidence: The 5 subtests pass and assert the refusal error, an untouched binary and no staging leftovers. Verify happens before the swap (update.go:154-162). The only production caller wires CosignVerifier (collectorcmd/update.go:28). The identity regexp is anchored to this repo's release.yml tags. Limitation: real cryptographic verification is not exercised.

criteria.criterion: TEC-15 (closed by WP-102): signature check before installation
criteria.evidence: grep -rl cosign shows only release.yml, edgecore/update, collectorcmd/update.go and docs. No install path verifies signed artifacts. install-vm.sh builds the collector from an unverified source tarball or git clone (487-498) and an unverified Go toolchain tarball (550-556). Compose defaults to locally built images (docker-compose.yml:33, 281, 362).

layers.ux: N/A: docs only (docs/README.md:927-958, docs/betrieb/collector-updates.md).
layers.api: OK: Apply fails closed (verifier and bundle required, verify before swap), proven by unit tests.
layers.data: OK: atomic swap with rollback (TestFailedStartsRollBackTheUpdate, TestConfirmKeepsTheUpdate pass).
layers.e2e: GAP: no manifest to real cosign verify to install path, and the release workflow was never observed running.
layers.robustness: GAP: no real-cosign test (tampered artifact, wrong identity). Installation has no signature check (TEC-15).

wps.soll_ist:
Required: a signed release with SBOMs, and signature checks before installation and on auto-update.

Actual:
- The updater's refusal logic is unit-proven and wired to CosignVerifier.
- The release pipeline exists but is unexecuted.
- No signature check exists before installation.
- The K8s overlays do not even reference the published signed images.
wps.evidence: results-edgecore.tsv (all edgecore/update tests pass); update.go:117-162, 249-296; collectorcmd/update.go:28; grep cosign results; install-vm.sh:487-498, 550-556; SP/work/verify-B13/k8s-prod.yaml (images reticora-cmdb/server:1.0.0, reticora-cmdb/postgres:1.0.0).
wps.deviation: No executed release evidence. The signature check is proven only with a fake verifier. There is no install-time signature verification (TEC-15). Docs list 3 instead of 4 images, and the K8s overlays reference images the release never publishes.
wps.dependencies: GitHub Actions OIDC (Fulcio/Rekor); WP-104 outage gating; WP-099 (k8s overlays); WP-148 (collector channels)

findings.title: No signature verification before installation (TEC-15 'Signaturprüfung vor Installation')
findings.repro: grep -rln cosign --include=*.sh --include=*.go --include=*.yml . lists only .github/workflows/release.yml, edgecore/update/*, collector/collectorcmd/update.go and docs. install-vm.sh:487-498 does `curl -fsSL $base/archive/refs/heads/$REPO_REF.tar.gz` or git clone, then builds the collector locally (575). install-vm.sh:550-556 downloads the Go toolchain without a checksum. Compose images default to the local builds reticora-*:latest.
findings.expected: Signed artifacts are verified before installation (TEC-15), not only on auto-update.
findings.actual: Installations never consume or verify the signed release artifacts; they build from unverified downloaded source.
findings.user_impact: The signed supply chain is bypassed for every fresh installation, so tampered source or toolchain downloads go undetected.
findings.cause: WP-102 only implemented the updater side of TEC-15.
findings.recommendation: Offer an install mode that uses the signed release binaries and images with `cosign verify(-blob)` before use (fail-closed), or at least verify the checksums of the downloaded source and toolchain. Document it.
findings.retest: An install-vm test with a tampered artifact or bundle aborts before installation; a valid bundle installs.

findings.title: K8s overlays reference images the release never publishes
findings.repro: kustomize build deploy/k8s/overlays/prod renders image: reticora-cmdb/server:1.0.0 and reticora-cmdb/postgres:1.0.0 (SP/work/verify-B13/k8s-prod.yaml). release.yml:20 and 150 push ghcr.io/datahub-chiemgau/reticora-<name>:<v-tag>, which differs in both name and tag.
findings.expected: Production manifests consume the signed release images.
findings.actual: The names and tags do not match, so pods get ImagePullBackOff unless the operator overrides them with unsigned or self-built images.
findings.user_impact: The signed images are not used by the K8s deployment path.
findings.cause: No kustomize images newName and no 'v' prefix in newTag.
findings.recommendation: Set images newName to ghcr.io/datahub-chiemgau/reticora-server (and -postgres) and newTag to v1.0.0, ideally pinned by digest.
findings.retest: kustomize build overlays/prod shows ghcr.io/datahub-chiemgau/reticora-* images that exist in the release.

findings.repro: docs/README.md:933 lists 'reticora-server, reticora-collector and reticora-frontend'; release.yml:127 also builds reticora-postgres.
findings.expected: Docs match the signed artifact set.
findings.actual: The signed reticora-postgres image is undocumented.
findings.user_impact: Operators may not verify or use the signed DB image.
findings.cause: The doc was not updated with WP-100.
findings.recommendation: Update docs/README.md.
findings.retest: Doc review.

wps.title: Betriebsbeobachtung: Worker-Fehlermetriken und Alarmregeln
wps.user_goal: Operators see run, error and backlog metrics of every background worker and are alerted on outage or backlog through the chain configured in deploy/monitoring, and via NTF channels once WP-137 exists (OPS-05).
wps.implementation:
**Metrics:**
- backend/internal/observability/workers.go defines reticora_worker_{errors_total,runs_total,last_success_timestamp_seconds,enabled,up,backlog} and ObserveWorkerRun.
- backend/internal/server/workers.go: StartWorkers sets enabled/up and samples backlog.

**ObserveWorkerRun callers (7 workers):** webhook/dispatcher.go:506/510, jobs/scheduler.go:191 (scheduler), monitoring/evaluator.go:96, notify/notifier.go:316, discovery/consumer.go:829/854 (ingest), export/worker.go:216, events/publisher.go:97.

**config.WorkerNames (config.go:346-358) has 11 workers.** jobs, nats_edge, credential_bundles and discovery_scopes have no worker_* run or error metrics. natsedge.go, scope_handler.go and credential/bundle.go import neither prometheus nor observability. Jobs do have job-level reticora_job_failures_total{kind} (jobs/service.go:175, 316) and reticora_job_backlog{kind} (router.go:337, 599), but no alert or dashboard uses them. A worker backlog function exists only for webhook_dispatcher, export and ingest (main.go:525, 545, 604).

**Monitoring:**
- deploy/monitoring/worker-rules.yaml (a PrometheusRule CRD, not referenced by any kustomization or compose).
- deploy/monitoring/alertmanager.yaml (no global SMTP, placeholder receivers, no NTF).
- deploy/grafana/dashboard-overview.json: 3 worker panels.
wps.tests:
results-backend.tsv: pass backend/internal/server tests:
- TestWorkerMetricsAreRegisteredAndRecorded (fake workers calling ObserveWorkerRun directly);
- TestWorkerAlertRulesCoverTheWorkerMetrics (string-contains);

findings.title: PATCH height_units accepts a height below existing mounts (mounts end up outside the rack)

wps.title: Durchgängige Hierarchie Org → Client → Site mit Scopewirkung belegen
wps.user_goal: The hierarchy Org -> Client -> Site -> location tree -> CI/Asset is one structure, and its scope takes effect on every level, so a scoped user sees only their part.
wps.implementation:
Test only: backend/internal/locations/hierarchy_integration_test.go:26-113. Mechanism under test:
- permission/pg_repository.go:164-230 AccessGrants: a site-only role_assignment becomes Grant{Sites:[site]} with no Clients.
- identity/principal.go:196-232 aggregateScope/unionDimension: an unrestricted dimension becomes All.
- middleware/auth.go:259-283 TenantScopeFor: All becomes a NULL app.client_scope.
- RLS: contact/credential/asset policies check client_scope only.
- asset has location_id but no site_id (information_schema).
docs/schema-baseline.md is listed in the WP but unchanged.
wps.tests: results-backend.tsv pass backend/internal/locations TestHierarchyScopeOnPostgreSQL (0.5s). Lines 105-106 assert that the site-1 and site-2 principals both see asset2 of client 2, which is placed in a room of site 2. Verifier probes: SP/work/verify-B14/probe-sitescope-chain.log (TestV14ProbeSiteScopeChain, full production chain) and SP/work/verify-B14/probe-rerun.log (TestB14ProbeSiteScopeClientRows).

criteria.criterion: Nach Konsolidierung existiert eine einzige Standortstruktur; Integrationstest belegt Scopewirkung über Org → Client → Site → Location → CI/Asset

Site -> Asset and site -> client-level objects: the test asserts the opposite (a site-1 principal sees a client-2 asset located at site 2). Full-chain probe with a viewer assigned scope_site_id=site1 (client 1): the resolved scope is clients={All:true}, sites=[site1]. That principal sees contact client2=true, asset client2@site2=true and the unplaced client-2 CI=true. Only the client-2 CI placed at site 2 is hidden.

layers.data: FAIL: a site-only grant leaves app.client_scope NULL. Every table with client_id but no site_id is readable across clients: contact (PII), credential, asset, consumable, sla and others; so are CIs without a site. asset carries no site_id although it has location_id (TEN-02).
layers.e2e: GAP: no real-session check of a site-scoped user.
layers.robustness: FAIL: the only test of the site level encodes cross-client visibility as expected; there is no negative test.

wps.soll_ist: Target: proven scope effect through the whole hierarchy. Actual: proven for the location tree and placed CIs only. A site-scoped principal is not confined to its site's client: it reads other clients' contacts, assets (even ones placed at other sites) and unplaced CIs. The WP's own integration test asserts this leak as correct.
wps.evidence:
SP/work/verify-B14/probe-sitescope-chain.log:
- 'viewer role scope=org; grants=1; resolved scope clients={All:true IDs:[]} sites={All:false IDs:[<site1>]}; db scope clients={decided:true all:true}'
- 'site-1 viewer (site of client 1) sees: contact client1=true contact client2=true asset client2@site2=true ci client2 unplaced=true ci client2@site2=false'
Also: hierarchy_integration_test.go:105-106 (site 1 wants asset2:true). psql audit_db_13 pg_policies: contact/credential/asset policies check app.client_scope only; information_schema: asset(location_id, client_id) has no site_id.
wps.deviation: The site scope is not transitive to the site's client, and assets have no site scope at all. This violates RBA-03 ('Eine org-weite Rolle setzt den jeweiligen Scope auf NULL': only org-wide roles produce NULL), TEN-01 (Client above Location) and TEN-02 (tables with a location reference carry site_id).
wps.dependencies: WP-065 (rls-matrix), RBA-03 scope aggregation (identity), TEN-02 asset/quantity_item site_id, WP-108.

findings.title: A site-only grant leaves the client scope NULL, so site-scoped users read other clients' contacts, credentials, assets and unplaced CIs
findings.repro: go test -overlay SP/work/verify-B14/overlay/overlay.json -run TestV14ProbeSiteScopeChain ./internal/locations/ (TEST_DATABASE_URL=audit_db_13). Steps: insert role_assignment(viewer, scope_site_id=site1 of client1); AccessGrants -> ResolveAccess -> TenantScopeFor; SELECT contact/asset/ci of client2 under RLS. Reachable in production via POST /api/v1/invitations {scope_type:site} (user/invitation.go:390-394) or a role assignment with a site scope.
findings.expected: A principal restricted to site 1 (client 1) sees no client-2 data. Per RBA-03 only an org-wide role sets a scope dimension to NULL.
findings.actual: contact client2=true, asset client2 located at site2=true, CI client2 without location=true. Only CIs that carry site_id are filtered.
findings.user_impact: In MSP organizations a technician restricted to one customer site can read contact PII, credential metadata and assets of all other customers. This is a confidentiality breach between clients inside the org.
findings.cause: identity/principal.go:213-232 unionDimension returns All when no grant restricts a dimension; permission/pg_repository.go:205-215 sets only grant.Sites; middleware/auth.go:259-266 maps All to an unrestricted client scope; client-level RLS policies test only app.client_scope.
findings.recommendation: When resolving a site grant, also restrict Clients to the site's client (lookup site.client_id), or treat unrestricted dimensions of scoped grants as empty rather than All. Change TestHierarchyScopeOnPostgreSQL so that site 1 must not see asset2.
findings.retest: Re-run TestV14ProbeSiteScopeChain and TestB14ProbeSiteScopeClientRows: all client-2 rows invisible, client-1 contact visible. The updated hierarchy test passes.

findings.title: asset (and quantity_item) carry location_id but no denormalized site_id, so the site scope cannot apply to placed assets
findings.repro: psql audit_db_13: information_schema.columns shows asset(location_id, client_id) and quantity_item(location_id, client_id) without site_id. Probe TestV14ProbeSiteScopeChain: a client-2 asset placed in a room of site 2 is visible to a site-1 principal. TestHierarchyScopeOnPostgreSQL lines 105-106 assert the same.
findings.expected: TEN-02: tables with a location reference carry a denormalized site_id, and RLS filters by app.site_scope.
findings.actual: No site_id column. The asset RLS policy checks client_scope only.
findings.user_impact: Site-scoped principals see assets of all sites. Even with the client fix, assets of other sites of the same client stay visible.
findings.cause: The asset/quantity_item schema was not extended with a derived site_id plus a site-scope policy (as was done for ci).
findings.recommendation: Add site_id derived from location_id via trigger (like ci), plus a site_scope clause in the asset policies; extend the hierarchy test.
findings.retest: Hierarchy test: site 1 does not see an asset placed at site 2; site 2 does.

test_gaps.description: Site-scoped principal confined to its client and site for client-level and location-bearing tables (production chain, negative)
test_gaps.proposed_test: Fixture: client1/site1, client2/site2; contact, credential and asset for each client; asset2 placed at site2; CI2 without location; an org-wide contact (client_id NULL). Insert role_assignment(viewer, scope_site_id=site1) and resolve it via AccessGrants -> ResolveAccess -> TenantScopeFor.
