findings.title: Per-IP signup limit is a fixed clock-hour bucket: 10 signups within 61 s pass
findings.repro: go test -overlay SP/work/verify-B14/overlay/overlay.json -run TestV14ProbeSignupWindowBoundary ./internal/signup/ : Protection.Check from one IP 6 times at 10:59:30 and 6 times at 11:00:31.
findings.expected: At most 5 signups per IP in any hour (E-33: 'höchstens 5 Signups je IP und Stunde'), and a Retry-After matching the remaining wait.
findings.actual: 5 accepted plus 1 refused at 10:59:30, then 5 accepted again at 11:00:31: 10 within 61 s. Retry-After is always 3600 even when the bucket resets seconds later.
findings.user_impact: Abuse protection is half as strong at hour boundaries; legitimate users may be told to wait an hour when seconds would do.
findings.cause: signup/protect.go:187-189 ipKey uses p.now().Unix()/3600 (fixed window). writeProtectionError sets a constant Retry-After 3600.
findings.recommendation: Use a sliding window (e.g. a sorted set of timestamps or two-bucket weighting) and compute Retry-After from the oldest counted signup. Or document the fixed-window approximation as accepted.
findings.retest: Probe: at most 5 accepted in any 3600 s span; Retry-After <= remaining seconds.

findings.title: No grant ceiling: a client-scoped user:manage holder issues org-wide org_admin invitations (privilege escalation)
findings.repro:
go test -overlay SP/work/verify-B14/overlay/overlay.json -run TestV14ProbeInvitationGrantCeiling ./internal/user/ (audit_db_13).
1. role_assignment(org_admin, scope_client_id=client1) for a delegate.
2. Resolve the principal via AccessGrants -> ResolveAccess -> TenantScopeFor.
3. POST /api/v1/invitations {role_id: org_admin, scope_type: org}, then POST /api/v1/invitations/accept.
findings.expected: 403/422: a principal must not hand out roles or scopes beyond its own. A client-1 delegate may invite only within client 1 and only roles whose permissions it holds.
findings.actual: Issue 201 and accept 201. The new user is org-wide with user:manage. Inviting into client 2 is refused (422) only because RLS hides that client; scope_type org bypasses it.
findings.user_impact: A delegated customer admin in an MSP org can create an org-wide administrator and gain access to every client, entitlement, audit and API key. POST /api/v1/role-assignments has the same unchecked pattern (user/handler.go:712 AssignRole, role:manage).
findings.cause: user/invitation.go:235-262 checkInvitationTargets returns nil for scope_type org and never compares the target role or scope with the issuer's grants. The route needs only user:manage (route_permissions.txt:421).
findings.recommendation: Enforce on issue (and renew, and role assignment): invited permissions must be a subset of the issuer's permissions in the target scope, and the target scope must be within the issuer's scope (scope_type org only for an org-wide issuer). Answer 403 otherwise.
findings.retest: Probe gives 403 for org_admin/org from the client-1 delegate; viewer within client 1 gives 201. API test for role-assignments likewise.

findings.expected: Issue and renew notify the invitee with an acceptance link (NTF-05 Phase-1 event 'Einladung'; template notify/subscriptions.go:82-92 addresses the invitee e-mail).
findings.actual: No event, no mail. The admin must copy the raw token from the API response.

findings.title: Interface delete fails (misleading 404) when its address also exists without an interface in the same VRF
findings.repro: go test -overlay SP/work/verify-B15/probe/overlay-ipam.json -run TestVerifyProbeInterfaceDeleteUniqueCollision ./internal/ipam (audit_db_14): POST interface eth0; POST /ips {10.66.0.1, interface eth0} gives 201; POST /ips {10.66.0.1} (reserved, no interface) gives 201; DELETE /network-interfaces/{eth0} gives 404 'network interface not found'; GET gives 200 (the interface still exists). SQL: net03-uniq.log shows 'duplicate key ... uq_ip_address_org_vrf_address_no_interface' from 'UPDATE ... SET interface_id = NULL'.
findings.expected: The interface is deleted (its addresses unbound, merged or removed by a defined rule), or a 409 explains the conflict.
findings.actual: ON DELETE SET NULL turns the bound address into a second unbound row, which violates the no-interface partial index. The delete rolls back, and DeleteInterface maps every error to 404.

findings.cause: ip_address_interface_id_fkey ON DELETE SET NULL combined with uq_ip_address_org_vrf_address_no_interface; handler.go:514-516 maps every error to 404.
findings.recommendation: Define the unbinding rule (delete or merge the bound address on interface delete, or 409 with the conflicting address) and map non-not-found errors through api.WriteRepoError.

findings.title: Manual verified port-level edges are silently deleted when discovery removes an interface (ON DELETE CASCADE)
findings.repro: Probe TestB16VManualEdgeInterfaceSync (full router + PG): (1) insert network_interface Gi1/0/1 on sw1. (2) POST /api/v1/relationships {sw1→sw2, connected_to, source manual, source_interface_id Gi1/0/1} → 201 (manual/verified). (3) Call ipam.PGRepository.SyncDiscoveredInterfaces(org, sw1, [{Name:'Gi1/0/2'}]) 3 times (the ingest path, router.go:378). After the 3rd sync the interface is deleted and the edge row is gone. No ci_change or audit entry records the edge removal.
findings.expected: REL-05: manual edges never disappear through discovery. A removed interface should detach the edge (e.g. SET NULL to CI level, or keep the interface while a manual edge references it), and any removal must be recorded.
findings.actual: The edge is deleted by FK cascade inside the discovery transaction, without a trace.
findings.user_impact: Manually curated port-level connections (impact and topology input) vanish without notice. This can happen when an interface is renamed or replaced, or when a manually created interface name differs from what SNMP reports: REC-07 also counts manual interfaces.
findings.cause: migrations/000114_relationship_rel02.up.sql: source_interface_id/target_interface_id REFERENCES network_interface(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, combined with ipam/pg_repository.go:630-686 missAndRemove → DELETE FROM network_interface.
findings.recommendation: Change the FKs to ON DELETE SET NULL, resolving a uq_ci_relationship_edge collision by merging into the CI-level edge, or have REC-07 skip interfaces referenced by manual edges. Record a relationship_change/audit entry when an edge loses its interface. Add the regression test below.
findings.retest: PG test: a manual verified edge on an interface, then 3 SyncDiscoveredInterfaces calls without that interface → the edge still exists (interface ids null, or the interface kept), and a history or audit entry exists. Negative: a discovery edge on the interface may be removed per TOP-02.

findings.title: No production job uses the NATS work queue; bulk/snapshot jobs run as goroutines and stay 'running' after a crash
findings.repro: Static and exhaustive: jobs.Queue is referenced only in cmd/server/main.go:270-300 (create, Setup) and :599-600 (Run). There is no jobQueue.Handle and no Queue.Submit; consume() (queue.go:289-300) creates consumers only for registered kinds, of which there are none. Runtime: TestB16VMain sends POST /api/v1/cis/bulk with 100 ids to a router built without any NATS → 202 ci.bulk, and the job reaches 'succeeded' in-process (ci/bulk.go:116 `go s.runBulkJob`). Service.ReapTimeouts has no caller, so a job claimed (running) by a process that dies is never reaped or redelivered.
findings.expected: JOB-01/TEC-14: jobs execute through the NATS work queue; a crashed worker's job is redelivered after its timeout and taken over, as the framework test shows for registered kinds.
findings.actual: No kinds are registered; jobs run as in-process goroutines; nothing reaps timed-out running jobs.
findings.user_impact: After a crash or rolling deploy, bulk changes and snapshots stay 'running' in the Job Center forever. Users cannot tell whether the operation finished and cannot cleanly retry it.
findings.cause: Job kinds are not registered with jobQueue.Handle, and the code uses Enqueue+goroutine instead of Queue.Submit (ci/bulk.go, jobs/service.go RunDetached). The queue is not passed to the router or services, and no ReapTimeouts is scheduled.
findings.recommendation: Register the bulk, snapshot and review-merge kinds with jobQueue.Handle and submit through Queue.Submit when NATS is configured. Without NATS, schedule ReapTimeouts in the scheduler. Add a wiring test.
findings.retest: Integration (PG+NATS): build the queue as main.go does, submit a bulk job, kill the handling replica → a second replica finishes it (attempts=2). Wiring test: registered kinds equal the documented list. Crash test: a claimed job past its timeout is requeued or failed by the reaper.

findings.expected: Only exports whose replica died are resumed (lease or heartbeat).
findings.actual: Reclaim is purely time based.
findings.user_impact: Duplicate work and possibly an orphaned blob for very large exports; the final status stays consistent through the status=running guard.
findings.cause: No lease renewal or heartbeat on running export jobs.
findings.recommendation: Renew started_at periodically during rendering, or reclaim only when the owner's lease has expired.
findings.retest: PG test with a slow renderer and a fake clock past StaleAfter while the owner renews → a second worker's ResumeStale returns 0.

findings.title: Route audit is written after the response in a separate transaction; failures are only logged (not gap-free)
findings.repro: VP/probe/b16v_probe_test.go TestB16VAuditFailure: NewRouter with Options.RouteAuditor returning an error → POST /api/v1/vrfs answers 201, the VRF row is persisted, and there are 0 audit_log rows for it; the only trace is a log line (middleware.go:134-139).
findings.expected: Title/AUD-07: gap-free capture of all mutations; the audit entry commits atomically with the change (or the change fails), or is retried from an outbox.
findings.actual: Best-effort: a DB or pool error, or a process crash between the mutation commit and the audit insert, loses the entry silently.
findings.user_impact: Undetectable gaps in the audit trail: the chain stays intact because the entry never existed.
findings.cause: Route-level audit is post-response middleware (pgRouteAuditor, router.go:629-633) rather than part of the repository transaction.
findings.recommendation: Write the entry in the mutation's transaction (tx-scoped recorder), or use an outbox with retry; at minimum add an alerting metric.
findings.retest: Failure-injection integration test: either the request fails and the mutation rolls back, or the entry is retried until stored; assert there is no mutation without an audit row.

The run probe shows that API relationship create and delete write no event.

wps.soll_ist: Target: transactional outbox with ordered at-least-once delivery to NATS and webhooks for all EVT-02 events, and a stable contract. The webhook consumer silently drops events on transient errors (reproduced). Several producers write the outbox outside the mutation tx. Stream retention is hard-coded.

findings.title: EVT-02 event types never emitted (relationship.created, collector.enrolled, review.resolved, entitlement.warning; relationship.removed only on discovery cleanup)
findings.repro: Scratch probe W/mod/backend/internal/relationship/zz_b17_probe_test.go (scopetest org, relationship.NewHandler(relationship.NewPGRepository(f.App)) as wired in production via server/repositories.go:142): POST /api/v1/relationships → 201, DELETE → 204, SELECT count(*) FROM event_outbox → total=0 relationship.*=0. Static: grep of non-test code finds no reference to RelationshipCreated, CollectorEnrolled, ReviewResolved or EntitlementWarning outside envelope.go, webhook.go and notify/subscriptions.go.
findings.expected: Relationship create/remove via API, collector enrollment, review resolution and entitlement warnings each write their event in the mutation tx
findings.actual: No event; webhook subscriptions and NATS consumers for these types never fire
findings.user_impact: Integrations subscribed to relationship, collector or review lifecycle events silently receive nothing
findings.cause: Outbox producers were wired only for CI (and a few system jobs)
findings.recommendation: Append these events in the transactions of relationship create/delete (repository), collector enroll, review resolve and the entitlement check; add one test per type
findings.retest: Turn the scratch probe into backend/internal/relationship test (expects 1 relationship.created and 1 relationship.removed); equivalent tests for enroll, resolve and entitlement

findings.title: Webhook consumer drops events on transient errors while the outbox marks them published
findings.repro: Scratch probe W/mod/backend/internal/zzb17probe/consume_probe_test.go: webhook.NewDispatcher with a repo whose ListByEvent fails. d.Consume(...) returns <nil>. Then append ci.created in org A, events.NewPublisher(f.App, nil, d).PublishPending → published_rows=1 attempts=1 last_error=NULL.
findings.expected: A failed hand-off keeps the outbox row pending and retries
findings.actual: Event marked published; webhook delivery lost; only a log line
findings.user_impact: Webhook integrations lose events during short DB outages, defeating the outbox guarantee
findings.cause: Consume (dispatcher.go:256-268) ignores the errors that dispatchAs only logs (:281-284 list error, :332-337 enqueue error)
findings.recommendation: Return errors from dispatchAs and propagate them from Consume; make enqueue idempotent by (event id, subscription)
findings.retest: Durability test: failing ListByEvent or Enqueue → Consume returns an error; publisher leaves published_at NULL and increments attempts; after recovery exactly one delivery

findings.title: Domain events written after commit in a separate transaction (review.created, export.completed, job.failed, webhook.dead)
findings.repro: events/outbox.go:168-175 PGEmitter.Emit opens its own WithTenant tx. jobs/service.go:185-196 emits job.failed after Transition committed. router.go:676-681, export/worker.go:170 and dispatcher.go:611 do the same; errors are only logged.
findings.expected: WP-136 criterion: outbox in the same transaction as the mutation
findings.actual: A crash or DB error between the business commit and Emit loses the event (only logged)
findings.user_impact: Rare missing notifications or webhooks for these events
findings.cause: Emitter API is post-commit for these producers
findings.recommendation: Pass the mutation tx to Outbox.Append in these producers (as CI does), or record a pending marker in the business tx
findings.retest: Fault-injection test: make Emit fail after the business commit → event still present (or the business tx rolled back)

findings.title: Webhook receivers get no event id or entity_seq; redeliveries carry a new delivery id
findings.repro: dispatcher.go:298 marshals only env.Data; deliveryID per dispatch (:309,:339); headers only Event/Delivery/Signature (:697-702). The publisher redelivers to all consumers when a later consumer fails (publisher.go:194-200).
findings.expected: EVT-01: idempotent consumers in entity_seq order need id, sequence and entity_seq
findings.actual: Receivers cannot recognise duplicates or restore order
findings.user_impact: Duplicate or out-of-order processing in integrations
findings.cause: Webhook body is the event data, not the envelope
findings.recommendation: Send X-Reticora-Event-ID/Sequence/Entity-Seq headers (or the envelope) and derive the delivery id from event id plus subscription
findings.retest: Dispatcher test asserting the headers; a duplicate Consume of the same envelope yields the same idempotency key

findings.title: Stream retention not configurable (EVT-01 '30 Tage / 10 GB pro Stream (konfigurierbar)')
findings.repro: envelope.go:38-39 constants; no config key
findings.expected: Configurable per installation
findings.actual: Hard-coded 30d/10GB
findings.user_impact: Operators cannot adapt stream size or age
findings.cause: Constants instead of config
findings.recommendation: RETICORA_EVENTS_MAX_AGE/MAX_BYTES with an NFR-06 minimum
findings.retest: Config test plus Setup test asserting the configured MaxAge

test_gaps.description: Producer test per EVT-02 type (positive) and absence on rollback or refusal (negative)

test_gaps.proposed_test: Dispatcher with failing ListByEvent, then failing Enqueue → Consume returns error; PublishPending leaves published_at NULL, attempts=1, last_error set; after the repo recovers, exactly one webhook_delivery row. Start from the scratch probe TestB17ProbeWebhookConsumeSwallowsErrors.

test_gaps.description: Real-stack webhook delivery of a UI mutation
test_gaps.proposed_test: With RETICORA_EGRESS_ALLOW_PRIVATE for a local receiver: subscribe ci.created; create a CI in the UI → one signed POST with the CI id and an event-id header; the NATS stream holds events.<org>.ci.created; delete → ci.deleted.

test_gaps.description: Poison event and post-commit loss
test_gaps.proposed_test: Consumer failing forever for event N → assert a max-attempt or dead-letter policy and a metric once implemented (today N+1.. stay pending). Fault-inject Emit failure after commit for job.failed → event must not be lost.

wps.upgrade_conditions: Producers for all EVT-02 types with passing per-type tests; Consume propagates errors with a passing durability test; event id and entity_seq exposed to webhook receivers; post-commit producers moved into the mutation tx (or a documented, tested recovery). Optional: configurable stream retention and an e2e-real webhook delivery run.
wps.verifier_note: Agreed with TEILWEISE and P1. Turned both static findings into run evidence with scratch probes on audit_db_16. (1) Relationship create and delete through the production PG repo leave event_outbox empty. (2) A failed ListByEvent makes Consume return nil, and the publisher marks the row published (attempts=1, last_error NULL). Both set to cause_confirmed=true. Re-ran TestOutboxAgainstPostgres with NATS: PASS. Added the post-commit emitter finding: the WP's own criterion requires the same transaction. The poison-event gap remains at code level.

wps.user_goal: An organisation can define notification channels (central or own SMTP, in-app, webhook) with encrypted provider configuration. Messages go out through a common provider abstraction (NTF-01, TEC-13).
wps.implementation: backend/internal/notify/channel.go:63-96 Validate (format only; any host and port accepted), :164-211 Sealer; smtp.go:41-87 SMTPConfigFrom/Validate, :154 PlainAuth with stored credentials, :187-200 dial with a plain net.Dialer (no egress policy); inapp.go:100-140 webhook provider over the egress client; handler.go:171-185 redact (password and secret only; url not redacted), UpdateChannel keeps stored secrets when the placeholder is sent; pg_repository.go:66,120 seal; migrations/000121 (FORCE RLS); cmd/server/main.go:360-379 (egressPolicy used only for the webhook provider).
wps.tests: results-backend.tsv: pass notify TestChannelValidation, TestSealer, TestEmailOverSMTP, TestInAppAndWebhookChannels, TestChannelsAgainstPostgres 0.46, TestNotificationAPI; rls TestRLSMatrix/notification_channel; config smtp subtests. Real stack: SP/work/bulk-jobs-export/final.log N01 ✓ (in-app channel created via POST /notification-channels and used). Scratch probes: W/mod/backend/internal/notify/zz_b17_probe_test.go TestB17ProbeChannelSecurity (FAIL = reproduced); W/mod/backend/internal/zzb17probe/authz_probe_test.go TestB17ProbeNotificationRoutePermissions.

criteria.criterion: Package backend/internal/notify with channel model per NTF-01 (email/SMTP per TEC-13, in-app, webhook)
criteria.evidence: channel.go/smtp.go/inapp.go; TestEmailOverSMTP, TestInAppAndWebhookChannels, TestChannelValidation pass; the real-stack N01 run delivered through an in-app channel

criteria.criterion: Table notification_channel with RLS; secrets encrypted (platform/crypto)
criteria.evidence: At rest: FORCE RLS, per-row DEK and ciphertext-only storage proven (TestChannelsAgainstPostgres, TestRLSMatrix). In use, the protection is defeatable (probe). PATCH with a new host and password '********' keeps the stored password, and the provider then sent 'AUTH PLAIN |svc-cmdb|corp-secret-123' to the new host. Webhook URL tokens are returned to every webhook:read holder, which includes the default viewer and engineer roles.

layers.ux: GAP: no channel admin UI (the e2e-real N01 comment confirms that channels are set up via REST)
layers.api: FAIL (security): no egress check for own-SMTP host and port (Validate accepts 169.254.169.254, 10.0.0.5, 127.0.0.1:22); secret-preserving PATCH accepts a new destination; url not redacted

wps.soll_ist: Target: channel model with SMTP (central and own), in-app and webhook providers, and encrypted configuration in an RLS table. Actual: model, providers and at-rest encryption are implemented and tested. The secret handling around it is weak, and all three points are reproduced: (1) any webhook:manage holder can redirect the stored SMTP password to a host of their choice; (2) own-SMTP hosts reach internal ranges without the egress policy; (3) webhook URL tokens are readable by viewers.
wps.evidence: results-backend.tsv pass notify channel tests and TestChannelsAgainstPostgres, TestRLSMatrix/notification_channel. W/probes-backend.log: 'Validate smtp host=169.254.169.254 port=22 -> <nil>'; 'patch to attacker host: 200'; 'AUTH received by redirected host: [|svc-cmdb|corp-secret-123]'; 'list contains webhook token: true'. Authz probe: 'GET /api/v1/notification-channels requires webhook:read; viewer has it: true'.
wps.deviation: Channel secrets at rest are encrypted, but the stored SMTP password can be exfiltrated by changing the host (SEC-08/SEC-04 style). Own SMTP bypasses egress protection. Webhook channel URL tokens are visible to read-only roles.
wps.dependencies: WP-136, WP-047; used by WP-139/140

findings.title: Stored SMTP password is sent to a new host set by a PATCH that never knew the password
findings.repro: Scratch probe TestB17ProbeChannelSecurity (handler + MemoryCenter, same handler logic as production). (1) POST /api/v1/notification-channels {provider:smtp, config:{host:mail.corp.example, username:svc-cmdb, password:corp-secret-123}} → 201, password redacted. (2) PATCH {config:{host:127.0.0.1, port:<fake>, tls:none, username:svc-cmdb, password:'********'}} → 200; stored password kept. (3) EmailProvider.Send → the fake server receives AUTH PLAIN '|svc-cmdb|corp-secret-123'. With tls/starttls a remote attacker host with a valid certificate receives it the same way.
findings.expected: Changing host, port or TLS mode of a channel requires re-entering the secret (or the secret is dropped)
findings.actual: Secret kept and delivered to the new destination
findings.user_impact: A webhook:manage holder who must not see the SMTP credentials can capture them (credential disclosure)
findings.cause: UpdateChannel restores secret values for the placeholder regardless of destination changes (handler.go UpdateChannel; asserted as intended in TestNotificationAPI:44-50)
findings.recommendation: Reject the placeholder when host, port, tls, username or url change; require the secret again
findings.retest: Handler test: PATCH with a new host and password '********' → 400; with the real password → 200

findings.title: Own SMTP channel host bypasses the egress policy (internal connections from the server network)
findings.repro: Scratch probe: Channel{provider:smtp, host 169.254.169.254, 10.0.0.5 or 127.0.0.1, port 22}.Validate() → nil for all. The provider dials 127.0.0.1 and the local fake server accepts the session. smtp.go:191-197 uses a plain net.Dialer; main.go:360 egressPolicy is passed only to the webhook provider. last_error is visible in GET /notification-deliveries.
findings.expected: Tenant-supplied destinations are checked against private, link-local and metadata ranges (SEC-08), at least in SaaS mode; SMTP ports restricted
findings.actual: Any host and port is dialled
findings.user_impact: Org admins in SaaS can probe internal services and read banners via last_error
findings.cause: SMTP dialing does not use internal/egress
findings.recommendation: Resolve the host and apply egress.Options (AllowPrivate only when configured); restrict ports to 25/465/587
findings.retest: notify unit test: own-SMTP channel to 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 or ::1 is refused unless AllowPrivate

findings.title: Webhook channel URL (token) returned unredacted to every webhook:read holder, including viewer and engineer
findings.repro: Probe: GET /api/v1/notification-channels lists config.url '.../services/T0/B0/TOKENXYZ' (secret redacted, url not; handler.go:174 secretKeys=password,secret). Authz probe: route requires webhook:read, and permission.StandardRolePermissions('viewer') and ('engineer') contain it (role_matrix.go:42,54).
findings.expected: Token-bearing incoming-webhook URLs are treated as secrets; channel administration is org_admin-only (RBA-02 notification:manage)
findings.actual: Every viewer can read Slack/Teams webhook URLs
findings.user_impact: Read-only users can post into the organisation's chat channels or exfiltrate the tokens
findings.cause: Redaction list too narrow, and channel reads are mapped to webhook:read
findings.recommendation: Redact url (path and query) for provider webhook, and map channel routes to notification:manage
findings.retest: API test: viewer GET /notification-channels → 403 (or url redacted); admin sees a placeholder

test_gaps.description: Secret-preserving update must not accept a destination change
test_gaps.proposed_test: (-) PATCH host change with password '********' → 400. (+) PATCH host change with the new password → 200 and the new password stored. (+) PATCH name only with the placeholder → 200 and the secret kept. Same for webhook url and secret.

test_gaps.description: Egress check for own SMTP hosts (after fix)
test_gaps.proposed_test: Validate or Send with 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, ::1 or 10.0.0.5 → refused in SaaS mode; allowed with AllowPrivate. Port 22 → refused.

test_gaps.description: Own SMTP over real TLS and STARTTLS with certificate verification
test_gaps.proposed_test: Fake SMTP with a TLS listener and a test CA. (+) Trusted CA → delivered. (-) Untrusted certificate → x509 error. (+) STARTTLS upgrade path works. (-) tls=none to a server requiring TLS → error.

test_gaps.description: Channel read authorization and redaction through the router
test_gaps.proposed_test: NewRouter with PG Center: viewer GET /notification-channels → 403 (after remap to notification:manage), or a redacted url. Admin GET → secret and url token redacted.

wps.upgrade_conditions: Secret placeholder refused on destination change (test passes); egress policy applied to own-SMTP hosts and ports (test passes); webhook url redacted and channel reads restricted to notification:manage (API test passes). Optionally a TLS verification test.
wps.verifier_note: Refuted the pass. The at-rest criteria hold (tests re-read, all pass), but scratch probes reproduced three secret-handling defects in the delivered channel model. (a) The SSRF hypothesis is now confirmed: internal hosts validate and are dialled. (b) New: the stored SMTP password is delivered to an attacker-chosen host after a placeholder PATCH; the existing test TestNotificationAPI:44-50 even asserts that the password is kept after a host change. (c) The webhook url leak was raised P3→P2 because the default viewer role holds webhook:read (authz probe). Downgraded to TEILWEISE BESTANDEN. Positive: the real-stack N01 run uses an in-app channel created over REST.

wps.title: Empfängerauflösung nach Rolle/Scope (NTF-03)

findings.title: Client contacts (NTF-03) are not a recipient source
findings.repro: recipients.go:18-47: Audience has Roles, TeamIDs, UserIDs, AllWithPermission, CIID+ContactRoles and Direct only; contacts are resolved only via ci_contact for a CIID (:124-131). contact.client_id exists (psql information_schema).

wps.title: Schlüsselrotation (SEC-06)
wps.user_goal: Operators can rotate the master key and organisation DEKs without data loss or downtime. Every ciphertext knows its key version, a job re-encrypts, and the old key is retired afterwards; webhook secrets rotate with a 24h overlap.
wps.implementation: platform/crypto/crypto.go:43-50 (key id in the wrapped DEK), :85-104 previous keys, :109-113 Derive (HMAC under the CURRENT master key only), :120 IsCurrent, :126 Rewrap; jobs/rotation.go:73-88 schedules, :107-134 RewrapMasterKey (org_dek, notification_channel, collector_ca), :217 RotateOrgDEKs; credential/pg_repository.go:321-391 RotateOrgDEK, :396 RewrapOrgDEK; webhook RotateSecret and ClearExpiredSecrets; discovery/natsedge.go:176-190 DeriveEdgeSecrets (issuer seed and password from Derive), :302-316 ExportEdgePKI writes edge.conf ('picks up new files on reload'); cmd/server/main.go:121 cursor key from Derive, :482-484 registration; deploy/docker-compose/docker-compose.yml:131-146 and deploy/k8s/base/components/nats-edge/nats-edge.yaml:50-55 (nats-server started once, no reload); docs/ops/workers.md:68-76 runbook ('without downtime', no nats-edge step).
wps.tests: results-backend.tsv: pass jobs TestKeyRotationAgainstPostgres 0.61, crypto TestMasterKeyRotation, identity TestSigningKeyRotationOverlap, webhook TestRotatedSecretSignsDuringOverlap. Verifier re-run on audit_db_16: TestKeyRotationAgainstPostgres PASS 0.46s. Scratch probes: W/mod/backend/internal/zzb17probe/ca_rewrap_probe_test.go TestB17ProbeCollectorCARewrap PASS ('rewrap n=1', 'CA key readable with only the new master key … isCurrent=true'); W/mod/backend/internal/zzb17probe/derive_probe_test.go TestB17ProbeDerivedSecretsAcrossRotation ('cursor key stable across rotation: false', 'nats-edge issuer stable: false, password stable: false', 'cursor issued before rotation decodes after rotation: err=invalid cursor: signature does not verify').

criteria.criterion: Key version per ciphertext
criteria.evidence: Wrapped DEKs carry the master key id (IsCurrent); credential and org_dek key_version increment to 2 in TestKeyRotationAgainstPostgres. All ciphertext columns in the DB (psql: collector_ca.key_dek, notification_channel.config_dek, org_dek.encrypted_dek; credential and pii_subject under org_dek) are covered by RewrapMasterKey.

criteria.criterion: Rotation job re-encrypts
criteria.evidence: TestKeyRotationAgainstPostgres: rewrap of ≥2 keys, a second run changes 0, the org DEK rotates after 400 d (audited) and the credential still decrypts. Collector CA rewrap is untested in the repo but works per scratch probe.

criteria.criterion: Old key retired after completion
criteria.evidence: The test builds an encryptor with only the new key after the rewrap; credential and channel stay readable. Retirement itself is a manual config step (docs/ops/workers.md:68-73).

criteria.criterion: (Requirement closure SEC-06) master key rotation without downtime
criteria.evidence: Derived secrets change with the current master key (probe). nats-edge receives a new issuer and password in edge.conf but never reloads (compose and k8s run nats-server once), so the server's auth callout cannot authenticate and collectors cannot connect until nats-edge is restarted. The runbook does not mention this. Pagination cursors issued before the restart fail with 'signature does not verify'.

layers.ux: N/A: operator procedure
layers.api: OK: POST /webhooks/{id}/rotate-secret (webhook:manage); API-key rotation elsewhere
layers.data: OK: atomic per-org rotation, audit entry; all ciphertext stores covered by the rewrap
layers.e2e: GAP: the restart-based master key rollout with a running collector was never exercised; the chain-level analysis shows a collector-channel outage
layers.robustness: FAIL: derived secrets change on rotation (reproduced). GAP: RotateOrgDEK failure atomicity untested; JWT 90-day cadence is manual

wps.soll_ist: Target: versioned ciphertexts, a re-encryption job and safe retirement of old keys, with master key rotation without downtime (SEC-06). Actual: versioning, rewrap and org DEK rotation work and are tested on PG, and the collector CA rewrap works per probe. However, the documented master key rotation changes the derived NATS-edge credentials and the cursor key, which interrupts the collector channel until a manual nats-edge restart.
wps.evidence: results-backend.tsv pass TestKeyRotationAgainstPostgres, TestMasterKeyRotation, TestSigningKeyRotationOverlap, TestRotatedSecretSignsDuringOverlap; verifier re-run PASS; W/probes-backend.log TestB17ProbeDerivedSecretsAcrossRotation and TestB17ProbeCollectorCARewrap; compose and k8s nats-edge definitions without reload
wps.deviation: SEC-06 'Master-Key-Rotation … ohne Downtime' not met: master-key-derived secrets (NATS-edge issuer and auth password, cursor key) change, and nats-edge does not reload, so the collector channel is down until a manual restart. Collector CA rewrap and RotateOrgDEK atomicity are not covered by repo tests.
wps.dependencies: WP-131, WP-047; PII vault (WP-240..242) shares org_dek; collector NATS edge (COL-08)

findings.title: Master key rotation changes derived secrets (NATS-edge issuer and password, cursor key); nats-edge does not reload, so the collector channel is down
findings.repro: Scratch probe TestB17ProbeDerivedSecretsAcrossRotation: before=NewEnvelopeEncryptor(old), after=NewEnvelopeEncryptor(new, old) as the runbook prescribes. Derive('reticora/pagination-cursor/v1') differs. DeriveEdgeSecrets: IssuerKey and Password differ. A cursor encoded before decodes after with 'invalid cursor: signature does not verify'. ExportEdgePKI (natsedge.go:313-316) rewrites edge.conf on start; nats-edge runs 'exec nats-server -c nats-edge.conf' once (docker-compose.yml:137-140; k8s nats-edge.yaml:50-55), so it keeps the old issuer and password. The edge-auth service connects with the new password (natsedge.go:408).
findings.expected: Master key rotation without downtime (SEC-06; runbook docs/ops/workers.md:68)
findings.actual: After the restart the auth callout cannot log in to nats-edge until nats-edge is restarted; new collector connections are not authorised; in-flight pagination cursors return 400
findings.user_impact: Discovery and heartbeats of collectors fail after a key rotation until an operator restarts nats-edge; the runbook does not say so
findings.cause: Derive uses only the current master key (crypto.go:109-113); no stable derived-secret source and no nats-edge reload
findings.recommendation: Derive from a dedicated stable secret, or try previous keys for verification (cursor) and keep the edge secrets stable; otherwise signal a nats-edge reload and document the step
findings.retest: Unit: DeriveEdgeSecrets and the cursor key stay equal across NewEnvelopeEncryptor(new, old) (or the old cursor is accepted). Real stack: rotate the key, restart the server, collector heartbeat over NATS still succeeds without restarting nats-edge.

test_gaps.description: Collector CA rewrap in the repo test (scratch probe shows it works)
test_gaps.proposed_test: Seed collector_ca (state previous) with key_dek wrapped by the old key; RewrapMasterKey(new, old) → IsCurrent; an encryptor with only the new key unwraps the DEK and decrypts key_ciphertext. A retired CA is left untouched.

test_gaps.description: Failure atomicity and concurrency of RotateOrgDEK
test_gaps.proposed_test: Corrupt one credential ciphertext → RotateOrgDEK errors, and org_dek and all credentials keep version n. A credential create during rotation is readable afterwards.

test_gaps.description: Derived secrets and collector connectivity across a rotation
test_gaps.proposed_test: DeriveEdgeSecrets and the cursor key are equal for NewEnvelopeEncryptor(old) and NewEnvelopeEncryptor(new, old) (after fix), or the old cursor decodes. e2e-real: rotate the master key on the stack, restart the server only → the collector heartbeat via NATS edge continues.

wps.upgrade_conditions: Derived secrets stable across rotation (or an automatic nats-edge reload plus a documented step) with a passing test; collector-CA rewrap and RotateOrgDEK failure atomicity covered by repo tests.
wps.verifier_note: Refuted the pass for the SEC-06 'ohne Downtime' closure. The three acceptance criteria hold: test re-read and re-run PASS; all ciphertext columns found in psql are covered by the rewrap; the collector CA rewrap works per scratch probe. The auditor's hypothesis on derived secrets is reproduced. Cursor key, NATS-edge issuer and password change with the documented key setup, old cursors fail, and nats-edge (compose and k8s) has no reload, so the collector channel needs a manual restart that the runbook omits. Raised P3→P2, set cause_confirmed=true, downgraded to TEILWEISE BESTANDEN.

wps.user_goal: Admins mark attributes as searchable or unique (per org or client) in the CI type admin. Bundle requests (Authorize: revoked/disabled) and scope lists (scope_handler.go:351) ARE refused. Scope-run results and subnet reports have no status check (code review).
findings.user_impact: An administrator cannot stop a compromised or misbehaving collector at once: for up to 24 h it can keep injecting discovery data into the CMDB.
findings.cause: The auth callout runs only at CONNECT; UpdateCollector only revokes DB rows; EdgeIngest has no collector-status check; no kick or revocation is sent to nats-edge.
findings.recommendation: On disable, actively disconnect (system-account kick or short-lived JWTs plus a revocation list), and reject disabled or unknown collectors in EdgeIngest and the scope-run/subnet handlers.
findings.retest: Integration test with a real nats-server: connect, disable; within ≤5 s the connection closes or a publish raises a permissions violation; EdgeIngest for a disabled or unknown collector → 403; an active collector is unaffected.

findings.title: No automatic certificate renewal; collectors lose connectivity 90 days after enrollment
findings.repro: `grep -rn '\.Renew(' --include=*.go .` finds only edgecore/enrollment/enrollment_test.go:138,147, and collector/ has no renewal logic (grep -i renew). Renew posts with a Bearer token (edgecore/enrollment/collector.go:141), but enrolled collectors have no HTTP credential: e2e-onboarding-real.log:15 'heartbeat completed status 401' and :19 'upload failed with status 401' with mtls:true. Expired certificates fail Authorize (natsedge.go:103-106, Verify with CurrentTime).
findings.expected: COL-04: automatic renewal from 60 % of 90 days over the existing channel.
findings.actual: Never renewed. At day 90 the edge refuses the certificate and the HTTP fallback answers 401.
findings.user_impact: Every collector silently stops delivering after 90 days until it is re-enrolled with a new code (new collector id, scope assignments must be redone).
findings.cause: Renewal exists only as a library designed for bearer HTTP and was never wired into collectorcmd.
findings.recommendation: Renew over the mTLS NATS channel, bound to the authenticated identity; run a daily check; persist the new key and certificate via keystore and reconnect.
findings.retest: Collector unit test with a fake clock: no request at 53 days; at 55 days a new certificate is persisted (0600) and NATS reconnects. Server test: renewal via NATS for its own identity succeeds; for another collector it is refused.

findings.title: Renewal endpoint is not bound to the collector: a discovery:ingest principal mints a collector certificate for its own key and can open that collector's credential bundle
findings.repro: Probe TestVerifyB18RenewalNotBoundToCollector (SP/work/verify-B18/probe_b18_verify_test.go; go test -overlay SP/work/verify-B18/overlay.json -run TestVerifyB18 ./internal/discovery/, audit_db_13). A tenant user context posts /api/v1/collectors/Y/certificate with a CSR of its own key for collector Y, which has no certificate → HTTP 201. Same for enrolled X with its certificate aged to 55 of 90 days → HTTP 201; X's legitimate certificate stays unrevoked. The minted certificate has CN=X and the caller's public key. BundleGate.VerifyBundleTarget accepts it (target key == caller key), and a bundle sealed for that target opens with the caller's private key. The route requires only discovery:ingest (authz.go:262; asserted by the passing TestAuthorizationMiddlewareEnforcesPermissions/POST_/api/v1/collectors/{id}/certificate). API keys can be scoped to [discovery:ingest] (identity/apikey_handler.go:99-155).
findings.expected: Only the collector itself, proven by its current certificate or mTLS identity, can renew. Plaintext credentials never reach a third party (COL-02).
findings.actual: Issuance is gated only by the route permission and the 60 % rule; after day 54 the rule is always satisfied because nothing renews.
findings.user_impact: Privilege escalation from an ingest-only API key or custom role to impersonating a collector on the public edge (4222) and decrypting the SSH/SNMP/Redfish credentials of its scopes. The built-in engineer and org_admin already hold credential:decrypt, so the escalation applies to scoped API keys and custom roles; rated P1 for that reason.
findings.cause: RenewCertificate (ca.go:442-475, pg_repository.go:708-737) has no proof of possession of the current key and no binding between caller and collector; the old certificate is not revoked on renewal.
findings.recommendation: Remove the HTTP renewal route or require the collector's mTLS identity (or a signature by the current key over the CSR). Never issue for collectors without a valid certificate. Revoke the predecessor after a grace period and audit every issuance.
findings.retest: API test: an API key with [discovery:ingest] renewing collector X → 403; X renewing over its own channel → new serial; X for Y → refused; a collector without a certificate → refused; audit entry per issuance.

findings.title: Bootstrap via RETICORA_ENROLL_TOKEN / RETICORA_CLOUD_URL not implemented
findings.repro: `grep -rn 'RETICORA_ENROLL_TOKEN\|RETICORA_CLOUD_URL' --include=*.go --include=*.sh --include=*.yml .` (outside docs/spec, audit and plan) matches only the comment edgecore/enrollment/collector.go:75. Enrollment exists only as `collector enroll --server --code` (collector/collectorcmd/cli.go:43, :60-110).
findings.expected: COL-04: a start with RETICORA_ENROLL_TOKEN and RETICORA_CLOUD_URL performs CSR enrollment.
findings.actual: A collector started with these variables does not enroll.
findings.user_impact: No unattended self-enrollment for container or automated deployments; an extra interactive step is needed.
findings.cause: Env bootstrap never implemented.
findings.recommendation: Enroll on first start when no keystore exists and the token is set, then persist; or document a replacing decision in entscheidungen.md.
findings.retest: Collector unit test with an httptest enroll server: the first start enrolls and writes the keystore; the second start does not call enroll; an invalid token exits non-zero with a message.

findings.title: CA roll-over cannot be triggered, and after a roll-over enrolled collectors no longer trust the edge server certificate
findings.repro: (1) `grep -rn 'Rollover(\|RetirePrevious(' backend --include=*.go | grep -v _test` finds only the definitions (ca.go:238,250); there is no API, CLI or job. (2) Probe TestVerifyB18RolloverBreaksEnrolledCollectorTrust (audit_db_13): enroll (the collector stores IssuedCert.CABundlePEM, as enrollment/collector.go:120 does), ExportEdgePKI, Rollover, ExportEdgePKI again. Verifying server.pem against the enrollment bundle gives 'before roll-over err=<nil>; after roll-over + export err=x509: certificate signed by unknown authority'. The collector trusts only that bundle (natsconn.go:73) and refreshes it only in the unused Renew (collector.go:145-146).
findings.expected: COL-04: CA roll-over with a transition phase of two trust anchors and no collector outage.
findings.actual: Dual trust exists only for server-side client verification. A roll-over would take every enrolled collector offline at the next nats-edge restart, and operators cannot trigger one.
findings.user_impact: A CA change (e.g. after key compromise) is impossible without a fleet-wide outage.
findings.cause: Library-only roll-over; the server certificate is re-issued from the new CA at once; the new anchor is never distributed to collectors.
findings.recommendation: Add an operator roll-over/retire command; keep issuing the edge server certificate from the previous CA until all collectors hold the new bundle (deliver it over the channel); retire only afterwards.
findings.retest: Integration test with a real nats-server: enroll, roll over, export; the old collector still connects and a new collector connects; after retire the old client certificate is refused.

findings.title: Concurrent edge-PKI export by several server replicas leaves a mismatched or missing server key/certificate
findings.repro: Probe TestVerifyB18ConcurrentEdgePKIExport (SP/work/verify-B18/probe_b18_pki_race_test.go via -overlay SP/work/verify-B18/overlay-race.json, audit_db_13): two CA instances (= replicas) call ExportEdgePKI concurrently on an empty directory, 200 runs. Output: '3 with a server key/cert pair that does not load, 181 with an export error; server-key.pem mode 644'. First error: 'tls: private key does not match public key'; export error 'rename server-key.pem.tmp … no such file or directory'. The k8s prod overlay runs 3 server replicas sharing the RWX PVC reticora-collector-pki. A mismatched pair persists because the next export keeps a valid, non-due certificate without a key check (natsedge.go:320-324), and RunEdge only logs export errors (:366-369).
findings.expected: Exactly one consistent key pair; nats-edge starts.
findings.actual: Race reproduced in-process; nats-edge then cannot load its TLS pair until the server certificate is due (60 % of 397 days).
findings.user_impact: In multi-replica Kubernetes deployments all collectors can be offline after a rollout until manual cleanup of the PKI volume.
findings.cause: No lock or leader election; key and certificate written separately; shared fixed temporary file name; no key/certificate consistency check.
findings.recommendation: Use pg_advisory_lock around issuance, unique temporary names, an atomic swap of key and certificate together, and a tls.X509KeyPair check before keeping an existing pair; key mode 0600/0640.
findings.retest: The same probe as a unit test, 200 concurrent runs: 0 mismatches, 0 errors, key mode ≤0640.

findings.repro: Probe TestVerifyB18BundleFlattensPerProtocol (SP/work/verify-B18/probe_b18_scopecreds_test.go via go test -overlay SP/work/verify-B18/overlay-collector.json -run TestVerifyB18 ./collectorcmd/ in collector/). A bundle holds two snmp_v2c credentials: cred-scope-a (community-A) and cred-scope-b (community-B). Output: 'namespaced=map[snmp.community:community-A]; credentials used for scope a (ids [cred-scope-a]) and scope b (ids [cred-scope-b]): map[snmp.community:community-A] (same map, no scope input)'. `grep -rn CredentialIDs collector --include=*.go | grep -v _test` finds only the struct field (scopes.go:38).
findings.expected: Each scope is scanned with its own assigned credentials (DIS-09, COL-02 scope relevance).
findings.actual: One credential per protocol for all scopes; the second credential is dropped.

findings.title: Collectors without enabled scopes receive all client and org-wide credentials
findings.repro: natsedge.go:446-458 sets CredentialIDs only when count(enabled scopes)>0; otherwise bundle.go:161-171 returns every credential with an empty client_id or the collector's client. Executed evidence: TestBundleSelectsScopeCredentials asserts that a target without CredentialIDs receives 'own' and 'shared'; TestCollectorNATSEndpointAuthorization (lines 102-103) asserts 'without scopes the bundle selects by client'. No decision in docs/plan/entscheidungen.md covers this fallback.
findings.expected: Only scope-relevant credentials (WP criterion).
findings.actual: Broad fallback set; disabling all scopes of a collector widens it from scoped credentials to the full client and org set.
findings.user_impact: Over-provisioning of secrets to edge devices; higher exposure if a collector is compromised.
findings.cause: Backward-compatibility fallback for env-configured collectors.
findings.recommendation: Return an empty bundle without enabled scopes, or require explicit credential assignment; document any exception as a decision.
findings.retest: Integration test: zero or all-disabled scopes → 0 credentials; one enabled scope → exactly its IDs.

findings.title: Auto-update needs cosign on the host, but the VM installer does not provide it
findings.repro: `grep -n cosign install-vm.sh` finds nothing (it also never prompts for RETICORA_UPDATE_URL). CosignVerifier executes 'cosign' from PATH (update.go:272-291); without it every Apply fails with 'cosign verify-blob: exec: "cosign": executable file not found' and the update is refused.
findings.expected: A VM-installed collector with auto-updates enabled can verify and install signed releases.
findings.actual: Updates are refused until cosign is installed manually (documented in collector-updates.md:43).
findings.user_impact: Auto-update silently does not happen; fail-closed, no security impact.
findings.cause: Runtime dependency not provisioned.
findings.recommendation: Install a pinned cosign in install-vm.sh when updates are enabled, or embed sigstore-go; warn at start when RETICORA_UPDATE_URL is set and cosign is missing.
findings.retest: Shell test of install-vm.sh with an update URL: cosign present; or a unit test asserting the startup warning.

findings.title: Contradictory capability documentation (icmp.go vs Dockerfile)
findings.repro: collector/plugins/sweep/icmp.go:19-20 says 'image: file capability on the binary'; collector/Dockerfile:20-23 says 'No file capability is set' (unprivileged ICMP sockets via ping_group_range).
findings.expected: One consistent statement of the capability requirement.
findings.actual: The code comment contradicts the shipped image.
findings.user_impact: Operators may chase a non-existent file capability when ICMP is unavailable in a container.
findings.cause: Comment not updated after the Dockerfile decision.
findings.recommendation: Align the comment with the Dockerfile and add an operator note (sysctl net.ipv4.ping_group_range or --cap-add NET_RAW).
findings.retest: Documentation review.

findings.title: Sweep spawns one goroutine per target before acquiring the 256-slot semaphore
findings.repro: Probe TestVerifyB18GoroutinesForLargeScope (SP/work/verify-B18/probe_b18_sweep_test.go via go test -overlay SP/work/verify-B18/overlay-sweep.json in collector/): 65,536 targets, a pinger blocking 10 ms. Output: 'baseline goroutines 2, peak 63356 (MaxConcurrency 256)'. Cause: sweep.go:92-145 runs wg.Add and go func for every target and acquires sem inside.
findings.expected: Resource use bounded independently of scope size.
findings.actual: About 63k goroutines at once for a /16 (at least 2 KiB of stack each, roughly 124 MiB or more).
findings.user_impact: Memory pressure or OOM risk on small collector VMs when sweeping large ranges.
findings.cause: Semaphore acquired inside the goroutine instead of before spawning.
findings.recommendation: Acquire the semaphore before `go`, or use a fixed worker pool reading from a channel.
findings.retest: The same probe as a unit test: peak goroutines ≤ MaxConcurrency + 50.

findings.title: Every swept device gets a (recurring) false unclassified_device review, even when SNMP/SSH/Redfish classified it
findings.repro: Overlay test SP/work/verify-B19/overlay/zz_verify_b19_classify_test.go in package discovery (memory repo, real collector profiles.Default()). (1) Ingest an SNMP record (sysObjectID 1.3.6.1.4.1.9.1.2494) -> CI switch. (2) Ingest the sweep record of the same IP/MAC as sweep.go builds it (openPorts only) -> classified_by=fallback. (3) An unclassified_device review 'no_profile_match' is opened. (4) Dismiss it and ingest the next sweep record -> the review is open again.
findings.expected: DIS-02: only a device without any profile match becomes generic_device plus an unclassified_device review. A dismissed review stays dismissed.
findings.actual: The sweep record is classified alone (ObservationOf uses only that record), always falls back, and the server opens a review before identity resolution, for a CI that is already a switch. reviews.Open re-opens after dismissal.
findings.user_impact: With the default plugins (sweep+snmp per scope, sweep/snmp/ssh by env) the review inbox fills with one false 'unclassified device' item per swept host every sweep. Genuine unclassified devices drown in noise and reviewers cannot work the queue.
findings.cause: Classification per protocol record without merging or evidence carry-over (collectorcmd.go:588, profiles/classify.go:218-243). Server-side noProfile check (discovery.go:1172, :1238-1256) ignores the matched CI's type and uses Open, not OpenUnlessDismissed.
findings.recommendation: Do not mark evidence-less sweep records as classified_by=fallback (e.g. classified_by=none, no review), or merge the records of one target before classification. On the server, open unclassified_device only if the matched or created CI is still generic_device after identity resolution, keep dismissals (OpenUnlessDismissed), and auto-resolve the review when raiseGenericType upgrades the CI.
findings.retest: Backend integration (PG): SNMP record plus sweep record of the same device -> 0 unclassified_device reviews. A sweep-only device -> 1 review; dismiss plus re-sweep -> still dismissed. Collector unit test: a sweep record is not marked fallback.

findings.title: WMI plugin sends credentials in cleartext (HTTP Basic over http://target:5985)
findings.repro: SP/work/verify-B19/overlay/zz_verify_b19_wmi_test.go: listener on 127.0.0.1:5985; wmi.New().Collect(ctx,'127.0.0.1',{username:'CORP\admin',password:'S3cret!'}) -> listener logs 'tls=false basic=true user="CORP\\admin" pass="S3cret!"'. Production registers wmi.New() (collectorcmd.go:130), and nothing sets UseHTTPS.
findings.expected: COL-02: plaintext credentials exist only in collector memory; device credentials are never sent unencrypted or to unverified endpoints.
findings.actual: Each WMI Collect sends the (alias: SSH) account base64-encoded over plain HTTP to whichever scope host answers on 5985. The HTTPS mode would use InsecureSkipVerify.
findings.user_impact: Network sniffers or rogue hosts on 5985 in a scanned range harvest privileged credentials.
findings.cause: wmi.go:42 UseHTTPS=false, :47 InsecureSkipVerify, :155-162 http URL, :209 SetBasicAuth; no config path enables HTTPS or verification.
findings.recommendation: Use HTTPS 5986 with certificate verification (scoped CA/pin like Redfish) and Negotiate/NTLM or Kerberos with message encryption. Refuse plain HTTP unless explicitly allowed per scope. Apply the same to NAS (POST body, verified TLS).
findings.retest: wmi unit tests: a plain HTTP listener receives no Authorization header; an untrusted cert is refused; a trusted CA succeeds. Same for nas.

findings.title: Vault credentials of kind 'wmi' never reach the WMI plugin; SSH credentials go to WMI and NAS targets instead
findings.repro: SP/work/verify-B19/overlay/zz_verify_b19_collector_test.go TestVerifyB19CredentialRouting: bundle {kind wmi} -> CredentialsFor('wmi') = map[]; bundle {wmi, ssh_password} -> wmi and nas get the SSH username and password.
findings.expected: Kind wmi (backend credential.KindWMI) is what the WMI plugin uses; SSH secrets never reach other protocols.
findings.actual: plugin.go:74-78 aliases wmi->ssh and nas->ssh, while bundle.go:105-108 namespaces kind wmi as 'wmi'.
findings.user_impact: WMI inventory with the dedicated credential type does not work (Collect: 'credentials required'), and SSH secrets are disclosed to Windows/NAS targets.
findings.cause: Inconsistent namespace tables in plugin.go and bundle.go.
findings.recommendation: Remove the wmi/nas->ssh aliases (add a 'nas' kind or map it explicitly) and add a contract test from every backend credential kind to its plugin.
findings.retest: collectorcmd unit test: a bundle with wmi + ssh_password -> WMI gets only the wmi keys, SSH only the SSH keys, NAS none of the SSH keys.

findings.title: WMI Collect reports success with empty fields when WinRM refuses auth or answers protocol-conformantly
findings.repro: SP/work/verify-B19/overlay/zz_verify_b19_wmi_test.go: a 401 + WWW-Authenticate: Negotiate server -> 'Collect err=<nil> ... serial=""'. A server answering the Enumerate with only an EnumerationContext (as WS-Man DSP0226 specifies without OptimizeEnumeration) -> 'err=<nil> serial="" hostname=""'. The existing TestCollectUnreachableWinRMReturnsEmptyFields even enshrines success for an unreachable WinRM.
findings.expected: DIS-04/WP-152: WMI delivers the DeviceRecord fields; DIS-08: failures are reported with a cause (auth_failed, unreachable).
findings.actual: wsmanEnumerate (wmi.go:204-230) ignores transport errors and HTTP status and returns ''. The Enumerate body (:233-255) has no OptimizeEnumeration, Pull or wsa:MessageID, so a real WinRM is not expected to return items in the Enumerate response. Default WinRM also refuses Basic over HTTP. Real Windows behaviour could not be verified here (no Windows host).
findings.user_impact: Windows servers appear as reachable 'windows-server' records without serial, model or OS. The scope shows OK, so operators never learn that WMI fails.
findings.cause: Errors swallowed in wsmanEnumerate; incomplete WS-Man Enumerate/Pull handshake; the fixture returns data directly in the Enumerate response.
findings.recommendation: Return errors on transport failure and non-2xx (401 -> auth_failed). Implement Enumerate with OptimizeEnumeration plus Pull and MessageID headers. Replace the fixture with a protocol-faithful fake (EnumerationContext + Pull).
findings.retest: wmi unit tests: 401 -> error classified auth_failed by backend ClassifyCause; EnumerationContext + Pull fake -> fields filled; unreachable -> error, not a success.

findings.title: scope_suggested bypasses discovery:manage and leaks across clients (list and permanent dismiss proven)
findings.repro: pg.json probe: a client-1-scoped principal lists 3 scope_suggested items, including 10.62.0.0/24 of collector v19-c2 (client 2). It dismisses that item (err=<nil>), and the client-2 collector's re-report opens 0 new suggestions. It accepts its own suggestion and creates a scope. Route POST /api/v1/review-items/{id}/resolve requires only review:resolve (route_permissions.txt:452); reviews/handler.go:89-110 has no per-kind check. Out of the box, client_technician has review:resolve but not discovery:manage or discovery:read (role_matrix.go:56-65), so it can resolve by id; listing needs a client-scoped role with discovery:read.
findings.expected: DIS-09: scope creation requires discovery:manage. TEN: client principals see and modify only their client's items.
findings.actual: Any review:resolve holder can create scopes via accept and permanently suppress other clients' suggestions. Client principals with discovery:read see all clients' subnets and collector names.
findings.user_impact: Users without discovery permission can trigger network scans or block another client's onboarding. Subnet information of other clients is disclosed.
findings.cause: review_item RLS is org-only (policy review_item_isolation); SuggestScopes does not bind the item to a client; no per-kind permission on resolve.
findings.recommendation: Bind scope_suggested items to the collector's client (client column plus RLS) and require discovery:manage for resolving scope_suggested.
findings.retest: Router API test on PG with real role assignments: client_technician accept or dismiss -> 403. A client-1 principal list excludes client-2 items; dismiss of a foreign item -> 404.

findings.title: Scopes larger than ~4096 addresses are silently truncated by the collector
findings.repro: collector.json probe: discoveryPasses for scope 172.17.0.0/16 -> 4095 targets (172.17.0.1-172.17.15.255); range 10.0.0.0-10.0.255.255 -> 4097 targets. The backend accepts up to 65,536 addresses (scope.go:39, NormalizeScopeTarget), and the onboarding suggests /16 networks (real log: 172.17.0.0/16, 172.18.0.0/16).
findings.expected: A scope accepted by the API is discovered completely, or the API refuses sizes the collector cannot scan. Truncation is reported as a scope error (DIS-08).
findings.actual: expandSubnets stops at maxSubnetExpansionTargets=4096 (collectorcmd.go:502-521) with only a log warning. The range cap (scopes.go:182) is silent. The run is reported without an error.
findings.user_impact: About 94% of a /16 scope is never discovered while the scope health shows OK, so the inventory is incomplete without notice.
findings.cause: Mismatch of backend MaxScopeAddresses (65536) and collector cap (4096); no runError on truncation.
findings.recommendation: Align the limits (raise the collector cap or lower MaxScopeAddresses to 4096) and report truncation as a scope run error.
findings.retest: Collector unit test: a /16 scope expands to 65534 targets (or the API refuses >4096); a truncated scope produces a runError visible in health.

findings.retest: Vitest posting site_id/vrf_id/credential_ids/plugins; e2e-real asserting the DB row.

findings.title: Scope schedules (cron/interval) are ignored at collector start: every scope sweeps immediately and again after each restart
findings.repro: SP/work/verify-B19/overlay/zz_verify_b19_collector_test.go TestVerifyB19ScopeExpansionAndCron: a fresh scheduler at 2026-10-15 10:07Z -> cron '0 2 * * *' scope due=[sweep], 24h scope due=[sweep]. scheduler.due (schedule.go:95-104) treats unseen keys as due; runDiscoveryLoop creates a new scheduler at each start (collectorcmd.go:396). CollectorScope (scope_handler.go:289) carries no next_run_at, so the collector cannot restore it.
findings.expected: DIS-09/DIS-10: a cron '0 2 * * *' scope sweeps at 02:00; a 24 h scope sweeps 24 h after its last run (the server holds last_run_at/next_run_at).
findings.actual: All scopes sweep immediately whenever the collector starts or first receives a scope, including during business hours and after auto-update restarts.
findings.user_impact: Unexpected scan load in production networks during the day, which defeats the operators' cron windows.
findings.cause: In-memory scheduler without initialisation from server next_run_at and without cron-aware first scheduling.
findings.recommendation: Send next_run_at/last_run_at with CollectorScope and initialise the scheduler from it. For cron, schedule the first run at cron.next(now); run immediately only for never-run scopes.
findings.retest: collectorcmd unit test: a cron scope at 10:07 is not due until 02:00; a 24 h scope with last_run 1 h ago is not due after restart; a never-run scope is due at once.

findings.title: Poll intervals are configurable per organization/protocol only, not per scope; cron is evaluated in UTC
findings.repro: scopes.go:236-245 protocolSchedule uses p.intervals.pollInterval(protocol) (org-wide); collectorScope has no poll field. schedule.go:212 cronSpec.next uses t.UTC().
findings.expected: DIS-10: 'pro Scope und Org konfigurierbar (Minimum 5 min für Polls)'. Users expect cron in the organization's timezone.
findings.actual: The scope only sets the sweep schedule; cron hours are UTC.
findings.user_impact: No per-scope poll tuning; cron windows shift by 1-2 h for German organizations.
findings.cause: Design choice/spec interpretation; no timezone handling.
findings.recommendation: Clarify DIS-10 (per-scope poll override). Evaluate cron in organization.timezone or label it UTC in the UI.
findings.retest: Unit tests for a per-scope poll override (if decided) and cron with Europe/Berlin.

findings.title: Installed collector does not match the UI enroll command (binary name and credentials path differ)
findings.repro: 1) The UI shows `reticora-collector enroll --server <origin> --code <code>` (DiscoveryPage.tsx:49-51). 2) install-vm.sh installs /opt/reticora-collector/collector (:607) with no reticora-collector on PATH; the Docker image provides /usr/local/bin/collector (Dockerfile:19,31). 3) install-vm.sh:456 sets RETICORA_CREDENTIALS_PATH=/opt/reticora-collector/credentials.json in collector.env (the EnvironmentFile). 4) The CLI default without that env is /var/lib/reticora-collector/credentials.json (enrollment.go:18). A shell enroll writes to /var/lib/..., while the service reads /opt/....
findings.expected: INS-06/WP-156: one configuration path; the UI command works on an installed collector.
findings.actual: Command not found, or the identity lands where the service does not look. The docs disagree (deploy/README.md:227 vs docs/README.md:595).
findings.user_impact: Zero-Config onboarding on the supported installer paths fails or needs manual workarounds (full binary path, --credentials, env export).
findings.cause: Installer, image and docs were not aligned with the WP-156 single path and binary name.
findings.recommendation: Use /var/lib/reticora-collector/credentials.json in install-vm.sh (or leave the env unset), install or symlink /usr/local/bin/reticora-collector (also in the image), offer enroll inside the installer, and align the docs.
findings.retest: Shell test asserting collector.env, binary location and unit path; e2e on an installed VM: run the UI command, restart the service, collector connects.

wps.user_goal: Discovered, observable CIs that discovery has not seen for more than 3x their scope interval become unknown and are announced via ci.offline. Manual and non-observable CIs are exempt, and the detector runs as a switchable scheduler job.

findings.title: One tenant's zoned IPv6 range scope stops the offline detector for every org sorted after it
findings.repro: cd /home/user/Reticora-CMDB/backend && TEST_DATABASE_URL='postgres://reticora:reticora@localhost:55432/audit_db_22?sslmode=disable' go test -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Reticora-CMDB/fbd8a132-b968-552a-84eb-515fd3e8f807/scratchpad/work/verify-B20/overlay-zone.json -count=1 -run TestVerifyB20ZoneTarget -v ./internal/discovery/ . The lower org creates the range scope 'fe80::1%eth0-fe80::5%eth0' via POST /api/v1/discovery-scopes (201) and has one discovered CI; the higher org has a CI last seen 400h ago; then OfflineDetector.Run.
findings.expected: Each tenant is checked independently. A bad scope affects at most its own org, and the API rejects targets the detector cannot evaluate.
findings.actual: Run returns 'organization <lower>: observable CIs: invalid input syntax for type inet: "fe80::1%eth0" (SQLSTATE 22P02)'. The higher org's stale CI stays active and no ci.offline is written. The scheduler repeats this every 5 minutes as long as the scope exists.
findings.user_impact: Any tenant admin can, deliberately or by pasting an 'ip addr' value, silently disable offline detection for an unpredictable share of other tenants (and for itself).
findings.cause: NormalizeScopeTarget (scope.go:269-280) accepts IPv6 zones via netip.ParseAddr, but PG inet does not. offline.go:144-147 casts s.target to inet unguarded, and Run (offline.go:82-86) returns on the first org error.
findings.recommendation: Reject zoned addresses in NormalizeScopeTarget (a.Zone() != ''). In Run, log and collect per-org errors (errors.Join) and continue. Optionally guard the casts in SQL (only cast targets that passed validation).
findings.retest: Rerun TestVerifyB20ZoneTarget: expect the POST to return 422. With a malformed row inserted by admin, Run processes the later org (stale CI -> unknown) and reports the failing org.

findings.title: ci.online documented but practically never emitted on recovery

findings.expected: docs/README.md:890 and offline.go:20: a CI seen again becomes active with ci.online.
findings.actual: The ingest sets unknown -> active itself (discovery.go:1413-1419) without appending ci.online. The detector then finds no unknown CI to recover.
findings.user_impact: Webhook and notification consumers get ci.offline without a matching recovery event.
findings.cause: The recovery transition lives in the ingest path, which does not emit ci.online.
findings.recommendation: Append ci.online in the ingest transaction when the status changes unknown -> active, or correct the documentation.
findings.retest: Same probe: expect an outbox row ci.online after the re-ingest.

findings.title: LLDP neighbor stored with FDB confidence 0.6 when an FDB entry for it is listed first; value flaps between ingests
findings.repro: cd /home/user/Reticora-CMDB/backend && TEST_DATABASE_URL='postgres://reticora:reticora@localhost:55432/audit_db_22?sslmode=disable' go test -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Reticora-CMDB/fbd8a132-b968-552a-84eb-515fd3e8f807/scratchpad/work/verify-B20/overlay.json -count=1 -run TestVerifyB20LLDPAfterFDB -v ./internal/discovery/ (ingest via POST /api/v1/discovery/ingest: sw1 neighbors [fdb Gi1/0/5 MAC peer, lldp Gi1/0/1 MAC peer], sw2 the reverse, then sw2 again with FDB first).
findings.expected: TOP-01: an LLDP neighbor gives connected_to with confidence 1.0; FDB counts only where no LLDP exists.

findings.title: Replayed idempotent error keeps the old trace_id
findings.repro:
Verifier vrun1 TestVB21IdempotentErrorReplay: Chain(RequestID, IdempotencyWithStore(memory)); the handler answers the first call with api.WriteError 500. Two POSTs with Idempotency-Key vb21-key.
- First: 500, trace_id=1b37...3d16, X-Request-ID=1b37...3d16.
- Retry: 500, Idempotency-Replayed=true, trace_id=1b37...3d16, X-Request-ID=4d5c...b556. handler_calls=1.
findings.expected: ProblemDetail.trace_id equals the X-Request-ID response header (API-03/OpenAPI ProblemDetail description).
findings.actual: On replay trace_id != X-Request-ID. A transient 500 is also replayed for 24 h (WP-050 concern).
findings.user_impact: Support correlation is confusing. More importantly for WP-050, a retry after a transient 5xx can never succeed for 24 h.
findings.cause: idempotency.go executeAndStore stores the full body for every status; replayIdempotent writes it verbatim.
findings.recommendation: Do not store 5xx responses (WP-050). Either rewrite trace_id on replay or document it and expose the original id in a header.
findings.retest: Middleware test: replay of a stored 4xx has the documented trace_id semantics. A 5xx is not cached, so the retry reaches the handler.

findings.title: Several [B] list endpoints are bare arrays without pagination (credentials, permissions, role permissions, team members)
findings.repro:
Verifier vrun2 TestVB21FullRouterPG (PG full router, org_admin principal):
- GET /api/v1/permissions?limit=1: 200, bare array, 103 entries.
- GET /api/v1/roles/{id}/permissions?limit=1: 200, bare array, 103 entries.
- GET /api/v1/users/{id}/roles?limit=1: bare array.
- GET /api/v1/credentials?limit=1: bare [].
Real stack (headers.log F/G): /credentials and /permissions are bare arrays. Auditor run1: 3 credentials, limit=1 returns all 3.
findings.expected: API-02/WP-164: every [B] list answers {data, next_cursor}, limit default 50 / max 200.
findings.actual: Bare JSON arrays of all rows; limit ignored. The spec documents them as arrays, so the parity tests pass.
findings.user_impact: Clients cannot page these lists uniformly, responses are unbounded, and the contract is inconsistent.
findings.cause: Handlers encode slices directly (credential/handler.go:88-105, RBAC handlers). TestEveryListIsCursorPaginated only checks schemas that have a data array (pagination_test.go:91).
findings.recommendation: Convert to api.ListResponse with ParsePagination, keeping deprecated aliases if needed. Extend the architecture test to fail on GET operations whose 200 schema is type array, unless allow-listed with a reason.
findings.retest: GET /credentials?limit=1 with 3 rows returns data of length 1 plus next_cursor. /permissions?limit=1 returns 1 row plus next_cursor. The extended architecture test fails on a bare-array fixture.

findings.title: Empty IPAM lists return "data": null
findings.repro: Real stack (headers.log A/B), dev admin bearer: GET /api/v1/ips?limit=1 and GET /api/v1/ip-addresses?limit=1 on an org without IPs both return 200 {"data":null,"total":0,"limit":1,...}.
findings.expected: IPAddressListResponse requires data as an array (api/openapi.yaml:17694-17703), i.e. [] when empty.
findings.actual: data is null.
findings.user_impact: Generated or strict clients iterating data crash or mis-handle empty results.
findings.cause: ipam/pg_repository.go:252 declares `var out []IPAddress` (nil when there are no rows). api.WriteJSON/withNextCursor does not normalise nil Data; only CompleteList does.
findings.recommendation: Normalise nil Data to an empty slice centrally in ListResponse encoding (api.go withNextCursor) and initialise repository slices.
findings.retest: GET /ips on an empty org returns data == [] (runtime list-shape test).

findings.title: Complete lists ignore limit / max 200

findings.actual: All rows are returned regardless of limit.
findings.user_impact: Large responses are possible for orgs with many keys or invitations.

findings.recommendation: Paginate, or document these as complete lists in the spec and the architecture test.

test_gaps.description: The architecture test does not detect bare-array list endpoints.

A cursor from sort=name used with sort=-name gives 400. A cursor of org A used by org B returns only org B rows.
