wps.title: Listenfilter filter[field]-Operatoren, Sortier-Whitelist, fields, q
wps.user_goal: API users filter, sort, select fields and search CI lists with a shared parser whose whitelist comes from field metadata; unknown fields get 422.
wps.implementation:
- backend/internal/api/listquery.go:86-289 (ParseListQuery, parseFilter, parameterised Filter.SQL, LikePattern).
- ci/listquery.go:14-61: core-field whitelist as a static map; Sortable has 4 fields; Selectable comes from Item json tags.
- ci/handler.go:88-134.
- ci/pg_repository.go:155-171 attributeFilterKind: `SELECT data_type, bool_or(searchable) FROM attribute_definition WHERE key=$1 GROUP BY data_type ORDER BY bool_or(searchable) DESC LIMIT 1`. This is org-wide per key, not per CI type; the predicate (:210-230) is not restricted to types where the key is searchable.
- Only the CI list uses the shared parser (other lists belong to the M-S WPs).
wps.tests:
- results-backend.tsv pass: internal/api TestParseListQuery, TestParseListQueryErrors, TestFilterSQLAndMatch, TestSelectFields; internal/ci TestListFiltersAgainstPostgres (real PG).
- Auditor run3.log: integer+searchable vs text+non-searchable key collision; gte gives 400.
- Verifier vrun2.log TestVB21FilterNonSearchableViaCollision (PG, ci handler): key vb_s text searchable on type S and text NON-searchable on type N; CI of N has vb_s='secret'. filter[attributes.vb_s]=secret gives 200 [vb21-nonsearchable]; filter[attributes.vb_s][like]=secr gives 200 [vb21-nonsearchable]. Control: key vb_only_n non-searchable on N only gives 400 'is not searchable; mark it searchable...'.
- Verifier vrun2 router and real stack: filter[nope] gives 422 problem+json.

criteria.criterion: Shared parser per API-02 with a whitelist from field metadata; unknown fields -> 422; JSONB filters only on searchable attributes (else 400 with hint)
criteria.evidence:
Operators, sort/fields whitelists and 422/400 behaviour are proven on PG (TestListFiltersAgainstPostgres; vrun2; real stack 422).
- Searchability is resolved per key org-wide: a key that is searchable on one type lets callers filter (exact and like) on that key's values in CIs of a type where it is NOT searchable (vrun2).
- A type collision makes a valid numeric filter fail with 400 (auditor run3).
- Core-field whitelist is a static map, not derived from fieldmeta.

layers.ux: N/A (API only)
layers.api: OK: operators, sort whitelist, fields, q and status codes for the CI list. FAIL (edge): searchability not enforced per CI type.
layers.data: GAP: attribute predicates are not scoped to the CI types where the key is searchable (vrun2, run3).
layers.e2e: N/A
layers.robustness: OK: parameterised SQL, escaped LIKE. GAP: q, lte, dates and client scope + filter + cursor not covered on PG.

wps.soll_ist: Target: shared API-02 parser, metadata whitelist, unknown 422, non-searchable attributes 400. Actual: implemented and proven on PG for the CI list. Reproduced: through a key reused on another CI type, non-searchable attribute values become filterable (exact and like), and a valid typed filter can fail with 400.
wps.evidence: results-backend.tsv (5 tests incl. PG pass); auditor run3.log; verifier vrun2.log (non-searchable values filtered via collision; control 400).
wps.deviation: P3: attribute searchability and type are resolved org-wide by key (ci/pg_repository.go:158-159), and the predicate is not scoped to CI types. Non-searchable values can be filtered, and a valid numeric filter fails with 400.
wps.dependencies: WP-164, WP-116 (attribute definitions/searchable).

findings.title: Searchability/type of attribute filters resolved per key org-wide; non-searchable values filterable and valid typed filters fail
findings.repro:
Case 1, verifier vrun2 TestVB21FilterNonSearchableViaCollision (audit_db_23, ci handler on PG): org CI types vb21-s (vb_s text, searchable) and vb21-n (vb_s text, NOT searchable, plus vb_only_n not searchable). POST one CI per type. GET /api/v1/cis?filter[attributes.vb_s]=secret gives 200 names=[vb21-nonsearchable]; [like]=secr gives the same; filter[attributes.vb_only_n]=secret gives 400 with hint.
Case 2, auditor run3: integer+searchable vs text key gives 400 for gte=1.
findings.expected: API-02: JSONB filters only on searchable attributes (otherwise 400 with hint), with typed comparison per definition.
findings.actual: Filtering matches the value of a CI whose type defines the key as non-searchable. Mixed data types break the whole query with 400.
findings.user_impact: Orgs reusing attribute keys across CI types get wrong or failing filters. The searchable flag (index/performance control) can be bypassed.
findings.cause: attributeFilterKind uses bool_or(searchable) grouped by data_type over all definitions of the key; the WHERE predicate is applied to CIs of all types.
findings.recommendation: Resolve definitions per CI type and add `ci_type_id = ANY(<types where key is searchable with that kind>)` to the predicate, or reject ambiguous keys with 400 and a hint.
findings.retest: The vrun2 scenario returns only the searchable-type CI (or 400). The run3 scenario returns 200 with only the integer-type CI.

test_gaps.description: Type/searchability collision across CI types untested.
Several operators, q and client scope not exercised on PG.

wps.upgrade_conditions: BESTANDEN when attribute filters are scoped to the CI types where the key is searchable with a consistent type (collision test passes) and the extended PG filter test passes.
wps.verifier_note: Re-read attributeFilterKind (pg_repository.go:155-171) and the CI whitelist (ci/listquery.go). Wrote an independent PG probe (vrun2) that shows a direct API-02 violation the auditor had not demonstrated: non-searchable values are filterable through a key collision with exact and like, with a non-searchable-only control returning 400. Confirmed that the 422 path works on the real router and the real stack. Status and P3 kept; the finding is broadened and reproduced.

wps.title: Ratelimits: Session-Bucket, 6.000/min-Org-Bucket, X-RateLimit-Header
wps.user_goal: Each API key or session gets 600 req/min and each organization 6,000 req/min, shared across replicas in Redis. Responses carry X-RateLimit-* headers, so one client cannot starve others.
wps.implementation:
- backend/internal/middleware/ratelimit.go:20-23 (600/6000), :61-91 RateLimiterWithLimits, :111-143 take (increments every budget on every request, :123-138), :165-177 rateLimitKey (cred:<org>:<Credential>), :262-300 PreAuthRateLimiter (429 without Retry-After or X-RateLimit).
- auth.go:148 (apikey:<id>), :170-171 (session:<jti>); identity/handler.go:247 plus :304-309 (stampToken mints a new jti per refresh; old token stays valid until exp, session.go:27 15 min).
- cmd/server/main.go:157-169 (RedisStore, fatal without Redis outside dev), :667-676 (chain).
wps.tests:
- results-backend.tsv pass: internal/middleware TestRateLimitPerCredential, TestRateLimitPerOrganization, TestRateLimitHeadersAndDefaults, TestRateLimitFailsClosed (memory store only).
- Auditor run1/run5.
- Verifier vrun1.log:
  - TestVB21OrgDrainRedis (real Redis, limits 3/10): noisy API key 3x204 + 7x429. Victim session of the same org (fresh credential) then gets [429 429 429] after only 3 admitted org requests.
  - TestVB21SessionBucketPerToken (real AuthMiddlewareWithVerifier + Tenant + RateLimiter, PerCredential 3): token1 gives [204 204 204 429]; token2 (same sub/org, new jti) gives [204 204 204 429]; token1 again gives 429.
  - identity TestVB21RefreshMintsNewJTI: refresh 200, token1 and token2 both valid, different jti.
  - TestVB21PreAuth429Headers: pre-auth 429 problem+json with no Retry-After and no X-RateLimit-*.
- Real stack headers.log: 2xx and 422 carry X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset via Redis with configured limits; 401 carries none.

criteria.criterion: Buckets per API-04 in Redis (600/min per API key or session, 6,000/min per org)
criteria.evidence: Redis sharing works (auditor run5, real stack). Refused requests of one credential drain the org bucket: a victim session is locked out after 3 of 10 admitted org requests (vrun1, real Redis). The 'session' bucket is per access-token jti and a refresh yields a fresh budget while the old token stays usable (vrun1, identity probe).

criteria.criterion: Headers on all responses
criteria.evidence: Present on responses passing the limiter (tests, real stack 2xx/422). Absent on 401 (real stack E, auditor run1), on the pre-auth 429, which also lacks Retry-After (vrun1), and on the store-failure 429.

criteria.criterion: Test for the limits
criteria.evidence: Limit tests exist and pass with the memory store only. No suite test with Redis, none for cross-credential org isolation, none for refresh.

layers.ux: N/A
layers.api: FAIL: per-session semantics are per token; the org budget is consumed by refused requests (reproduced with Redis).
layers.data: OK: Redis INCR+EXPIRE fixed window shared across replicas (auditor run5; real stack headers).
layers.e2e: OK/GAP: real stack shows headers in the production chain with Redis. No suite test through the production chain.
layers.robustness: FAIL: one looping client locks out its whole organization (vrun1). OK: fail-closed on store error.

wps.soll_ist:
Target: isolated 600/min per key/session, 6,000/min per org, in Redis, headers on all responses. Actual:
- Redis buckets and headers on passed-through responses work.
- A refused credential keeps consuming the org budget, so one client blocks the whole org.
- The session budget restarts with every refreshed access token.
- Pre-limiter rejections carry no headers.
wps.evidence: Verifier vrun1.log (org lockout on real Redis; per-jti buckets through the real auth middleware; refresh mints a new jti; pre-auth 429 without headers); auditor run1/run5; real-stack headers.log; code ratelimit.go:123-138, auth.go:170-171, identity/handler.go:247,304-309.
wps.deviation:
- P1: org bucket drained by refused credential requests (noisy neighbour locks out the org).
- P2: session bucket keyed by access-token jti and renewed per refresh.
- P3: no X-RateLimit headers on 401/403/pre-auth 429; no Retry-After on pre-auth 429.
wps.dependencies: WP-163 (429 writer), WP-050 (chain order, pre-auth limiter), AUT-02 (session/refresh).

findings.title: Refused requests of one credential consume the organization budget, so one client locks out the whole org
findings.repro: Verifier vrun1 TestVB21OrgDrainRedis: real Redis (TEST_REDIS_URL 56379), RateLimits{PerCredential:3, PerOrganization:10}, fresh org id. 10 requests from apikey:noisy give 3x204 and 7x429. Then 3 requests from session:victim (same org, untouched credential) give [429, 429, 429], although only 3 org requests were admitted. Auditor run1 shows the same with the memory store.
findings.expected: API-04: the per-credential budget isolates clients; the org budget (6,000/min) limits admitted traffic. Another session should still be served.
findings.actual: Every attempt, including those refused by the credential budget, increments the org counter. A client making about 6,000 attempts/min (600 served) blocks every user of the org.
findings.user_impact: A misbehaving integration retrying on 429 makes the API (and UI) unavailable for the whole organization for as long as it keeps hammering.
findings.cause: ratelimit.go:123-138 increments all budgets unconditionally in one loop; the org counter is not skipped or rolled back for refused requests.
findings.recommendation: Check the credential bucket first and count only admitted requests in the org bucket (for example a Redis Lua script that checks both before incrementing, or a decrement on refusal).
findings.retest: Unit and Redis test: session A sends 2x its limit; session B of the same org still gets 204; the org counter equals admitted requests.

findings.title: 'Per session' bucket is per access token and resets on every refresh
findings.repro:
Verifier vrun1:
- identity TestVB21RefreshMintsNewJTI: login, then /auth/refresh returns 200. token1 jti=vac7... and token2 jti=tbYc..., same subject, both validate.
- TestVB21SessionBucketPerToken through AuthMiddlewareWithVerifier(issuer)+TenantMiddleware+RateLimiter(PerCredential 3): token1 gives [204,204,204,429]; token2 (same sub/org, new jti) gives [204,204,204,429].
findings.expected: API-04: 600 req/min per session (refresh family), independent of token rotation.
findings.actual: Each access token has its own budget; the old token stays valid (15 min), so a client gets up to 600 per token and can multiply its budget by refreshing (bounded only by the org bucket and the 20/min pre-auth limit).
findings.user_impact: The per-session limit can be bypassed by a client that refreshes deliberately.
findings.cause: auth.go:170-171 keys Credential on claims.TokenID (jti); stampToken (identity/handler.go:304-309) mints a new jti per refresh; there is no stable session id claim.
findings.recommendation: Carry the refresh-family/session id (sid) in the access token and key the bucket on it.
findings.retest: Integration: login, consume the limit, refresh, the next request in the same window gets 429. A different login session gets 204.

findings.title: X-RateLimit headers (and Retry-After) missing on responses rejected before the limiter
findings.repro:
- Verifier vrun1 TestVB21PreAuth429Headers: PreAuthRateLimiter(1), 2x POST /api/v1/auth/refresh. The second returns 429 problem+json with Retry-After='' and X-RateLimit-Limit=''.
- Real stack headers.log E: unauthenticated GET /api/v1/cis returns 401 without X-RateLimit-*.
- Auditor run1 shows the same.
findings.expected: WP criterion: headers on all responses; a 429 should carry Retry-After.
findings.actual: Headers only on responses that pass RateLimiterWithLimits.
findings.user_impact: Clients cannot read their budget or back-off on auth/entitlement errors and pre-auth throttling; minor.
findings.cause: The limiter is placed after Auth/Tenant/Entitlement per API-04 (main.go:667-676). PreAuthRateLimiter (ratelimit.go:279-283) writes no headers.
findings.recommendation: Clarify the criterion (responses that pass the limiter) and add IP-bucket headers plus Retry-After to the pre-auth 429 and the store-failure 429.
findings.retest: Chain test asserts the documented headers on 401/403 and on the pre-auth 429 (with Retry-After).

test_gaps.description: No test that refused credential traffic leaves the org budget for others.
test_gaps.proposed_test: RateLimits{3,10}, with the memory store and with RedisStore (TEST_REDIS_URL). Session A sends 10 (3 OK, 7 x 429). Session B sends 7 and expects all 204. X-RateLimit-Remaining of the org equals 10 minus admitted. Edge: exactly at the org limit.

test_gaps.description: No test of the session bucket across token refresh.
test_gaps.proposed_test: SessionIssuer plus RefreshSessions on Redis, through AuthMiddlewareWithVerifier and RateLimiterWithLimits(PerCredential 3). Login, 3 requests, Refresh, then with the new token the 4th request in the same minute gets 429; the old token also gets 429. A second login session gets 204.

test_gaps.description: The limiter is only tested with the memory store.
test_gaps.proposed_test: Two RateLimiterWithLimits instances on one RedisStore. Assert shared credential and org counters, key TTL <= 120s, window rollover resets (injected clock), and Redis down gives a fail-closed 429 with problem+json.

test_gaps.description: Production chain header behaviour.
test_gaps.proposed_test: main.go chain with Redis. 2xx and handler 4xx carry X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset. A limiter 429 carries Retry-After == X-RateLimit-Reset. The documented behaviour holds for 401/403 and the pre-auth 429 (Retry-After present).

wps.verifier_note: Tried to refute and could not. Independently reproduced the org lockout on real Redis: the victim was blocked after 3 of 10 admitted. Reproduced the per-jti session bucket through the real auth middleware, plus refresh minting a new jti while the old token remains valid; the auditor had this finding only code-inferred, now cause_confirmed=true by reproduction. Reproduced the pre-auth 429 without Retry-After or headers. The real stack confirmed headers on 2xx/422 and none on 401. FEHLGESCHLAGEN and P1 kept: the org-wide outage from one client contradicts the per-key/per-org budgets of API-04, the core of this WP.

wps.title: API-Lebenszyklus: Deprecation/Sunset-Header, No-DB-Profil-Parität
wps.user_goal: API consumers get Deprecation/Sunset/successor headers (at least 12 months notice) on operations the OpenAPI marks deprecated. Both server profiles (PostgreSQL and --no-db) serve exactly the documented operations.
wps.implementation:
- backend/internal/middleware/openapi.go:40-56, :86 (writeDeprecation runs in OpenAPIValidation, a RouteMiddleware after authz: router.go:203,316), :136-150 loadSpec (silently no headers when no spec is found), :152-203 ParseDeprecations, :205-230 writeDeprecation, :364-386 spec path resolution (env or relative api/openapi.yaml).
- backend/Dockerfile:29-30 (spec copied to /etc/reticora/openapi.yaml plus ENV).
- server/router.go:469-478 (audit routes in both profiles).
- 22 deprecated operations; sunset = deprecated-at + 12 months + 1 day.
wps.tests:
- results-backend.tsv pass: internal/middleware TestDeprecatedOperationsCarryLifecycleHeaders, TestDeprecationsNeedTwelveMonthsNotice; internal/server TestRoutesAndSpecificationAreInParity (profiles postgres/no-db x all/G1; profiles modelled via audit handler nil, parity_test.go:112).
- Auditor run4.log: PG router, 7 deprecated GETs with headers.
- Verifier vrun2.log: GET /export/cis returns 200 with Deprecation @1791936000, Sunset 2027-10-15 and Link </api/v1/exports>. GET /ip-addresses without permission returns 403 without Deprecation/Sunset.
- Real stack (native production binary, cwd SP/stack, no RETICORA_OPENAPI_SPEC_PATH) headers.log/paths.log: /ip-addresses, /audit and /auth/me return 200 with NO Deprecation/Sunset/Link; server.log has no openapi warning.

criteria.criterion: Deprecation/Sunset headers for operations marked in OpenAPI (x-sunset), at least 12 months notice
criteria.evidence: Unit tests plus full-router probes (auditor run4, verifier vrun2) with the real spec. Caveat: the headers depend on the spec file at runtime. findings.title: Deprecation headers silently disabled when the spec file is not found (observed on the real stack)
findings.repro:
Real stack: native backend binary from HEAD, RETICORA_ENVIRONMENT=production, cwd /tmp/.../scratchpad/stack, server.env without RETICORA_OPENAPI_SPEC_PATH. With the dev admin bearer:
- GET http://localhost:5173/api/v1/ip-addresses?limit=1 returns 200 Deprecation='' Sunset='' Link='';
- GET /api/v1/audit?limit=1 and GET /api/v1/auth/me: the same (headers.log A/C, paths.log M2).
- grep of stack/server.log for 'openapi' finds nothing.
findings.expected: Deprecated operations carry Deprecation/Sunset/Link; a deployment without the spec is visible (warning or failed readiness).
findings.actual: loadSpec (openapi.go:136-150) tries the relative candidates, none exists, v.deprecated stays empty, and nothing is logged.
findings.user_impact: Consumers of a misconfigured or native deployment get no deprecation notice. Supported deployments use the image with the spec (Dockerfile:29-30), hence P3.
findings.cause: No error/warn path for 'spec not found'; the default path is relative (api/openapi.yaml).
findings.recommendation: Embed the spec in the binary (go:embed) or log at error and fail readiness when no spec is loaded. Set RETICORA_OPENAPI_SPEC_PATH in the audit real stack before e2e-real lifecycle checks.
findings.retest: Start the binary outside the repo without the env: either the headers are present (embedded) or a warning or readiness failure is visible. The real-stack GET /ip-addresses carries Deprecation.

findings.title: Successor Link header carries unexpanded URI templates
findings.repro: Auditor run4.log: GET /api/v1/topology/cis/<id>/impact returns Link: </api/v1/impact/{ci_id}>; rel="successor-version".
findings.expected: RFC 8288 URI reference, e.g. /api/v1/impact/<id>.
findings.actual: The literal '{ci_id}' template.
findings.user_impact: Clients following the link get 4xx; cosmetic for humans.
findings.cause: openapi.go:226-228 writes x-successor verbatim.
findings.recommendation: Substitute path parameters from the matched route, or omit Link for templated successors.
findings.retest: Unit: deprecated /x/{id} with successor /y/{id}; a request to /x/42 gives Link </y/42>.

findings.title: No lifecycle headers on 401/403 of deprecated operations

findings.title: Unified CI history omits location_change table (re-parenting of the CI's location)
findings.repro: Verifier probe TestVerifyB22HistoryLocationChangePG (audit_db_24): site with buildings b1/b2, room under b1, CI with location_id=room; locations.PGRepository.Move(room -> b2).

findings.cause: unifiedCIHistory (history/pg_repository.go:66-77) selects only ci_change, entity_change and audit_log. The non-CI List (:117-148) reads only entity_change.

findings.title: CI history section unusable for all standard roles except org_admin

findings.expected: Operators who may read and edit a CI can see its change history (CI-06 lists Historie as a CI read function; GET /cis/{id}/changes is ci:read).
findings.actual: An engineer sees 'Die Historie konnte nicht geladen werden.' on every CI detail page.
findings.user_impact: The new WP-171 history is effectively visible only to org administrators; operators lose the CI change trail in the UI.
findings.cause: The unified CI history, which mixes CI changes and audit entries, is gated as a whole by audit:read; the UI does not check the permission.
findings.recommendation: Decide the contract. Either let ci:read see the ci_change/entity_change part (and audit entries only with audit:read), or hide the section without audit:read. Record the decision against RBA-02/E-13.
findings.retest: API test with engineer and viewer tokens: GET /history/ci/{id} returns the decided content (not 403), or the UI hides the section. An e2e-real check as an engineer.

Review merge: discovery/review.go:118-146 (probable_duplicate merge = ciRepo.Delete); reviews/service.go:173-190 runs it as a review job. Commit f6556c0 does not touch reviews/service.go although the WP lists it. UI: ReviewInboxPage.tsx:335-339 is the only merge action.

wps.title: CI-Unmerge innerhalb der Snapshot-Frist

Verifier probe TestVerifyB22UnmergeRestore (probe-ci.log). Auditor probe (RevertMerge works; interim survivor rename overwritten).

The probe shows before == after for: survivor attributes {x:s, tags:[a]} (merged state {x, rack:R1, tags:[a,b]} reverted), victim attributes, the asset link back to the victim, the victim IP via its interface (1), document_link (1), the ci_change history row (1) and victim deleted=false. Events: ci.restored (victim)=1 and ci.changed (survivor)=1. The repo test asserts 410 after expiry.

Survivor edits made after the merge are silently lost (auditor probe: a rename after the merge reverts to the pre-merge name). wps.soll_ist: Soll: within 30 days, unmerge restores both CIs and their references from the snapshot; afterwards 409/410. Ist: fulfilled and PG-proven, including the survivor's own state, documents, history, IPs, events, concurrency and scope. However, it silently discards all edits made to the survivor and the moved rows between merge and unmerge.
wps.evidence: results-backend.tsv pass TestUnmergeAgainstPostgres. probe-ci.log: 'WP-174 before={SurvivorAttrs:{"x": "s", "tags": ["a"]} ... VictimDeleted:false}', 'merged={SurvivorAttrs:{"x": "s", "rack": "R1", "tags": ["a", "b"]} ... VictimDeleted:true}', 'after =... equal(before,after)=true', 'parallel unmerge codes=[200 409] events ci.restored(victim)=1 ci.changed(survivor)=1', 'client2-scoped unmerge ... -> 404'. Auditor probe-ci.log: 'FINDING: interim change on the survivor was overwritten by the snapshot'.
wps.deviation: Post-merge edits are silently overwritten by the snapshot restore; there is no conflict detection or warning, and the contract is not documented in OpenAPI.

findings.title: Unmerge silently overwrites changes made to the survivor (and moved rows) after the merge
findings.repro: Auditor probe TestAuditProbeB22CIPG: svc.Merge(s,v); repo.Update(s, name='probe-b22-survivor-renamed-after-merge'); svc.RevertMerge(mergeID) gives survivor name 'probe-b22-survivor'. restoreRow (merge.go:653-677) sets every column from the snapshot.
findings.expected: The unmerge undoes the merge effect without silently discarding later unrelated edits, or refuses (409) or warns per a decided contract (no silent data loss).
findings.actual: All columns of both CI rows and the changed reference rows are reset to the pre-merge state; there is no version or conflict check.
findings.user_impact: Edits made in the up-to-30 days between merge and unmerge (names, attributes, relationships, overrides) are lost without notice.
findings.cause: Snapshot restore by full-row overwrite with no version/updated_at comparison.
findings.recommendation: Compare each restored row's version or updated_at with the merge time and refuse with 409 (with an explicit force option) or re-apply the post-merge changes. Document the contract in OpenAPI and record a decision.
findings.retest: PG test: merge, update the survivor and a moved relationship, unmerge, then expect the decided contract (409, or preserved changes).

wps.upgrade_conditions: A decided contract for post-merge edits (refuse, preserve, or an explicit decision accepting the snapshot overwrite and documenting it in OpenAPI), covered by a PG test. The verifier probe assertions ported into repo tests.
wps.verifier_note: Confirmed TEILWEISE, with the evidence gap closed. My probe proves the criterion fully: survivor attributes and tags, asset link, IPs, documents, history and events restored; parallel unmerge [200,409]; client-scope 404. The remaining blocker is the silent overwrite of post-merge edits. OpenAPI (openapi.yaml:938-944) says both CI rows are restored but does not warn about later edits; no decision exists. I kept it P2 because the audit hunts silent data loss in the Data layer. Rows deleted after the merge not being restored is plausible from the code but was not probed.

findings.title: Blast radius lists connected_to-only (heuristic) CIs as affected without a heuristic marker
findings.repro: Verifier PG probe TestVerifyB22BlastRadiusHeuristicPG: switch connected_to server, vm hosted_on server, server powered_by pdu. GET /api/v1/cis/{switch}/blast-radius and GET /api/v1/impact/{switch}.
findings.expected: IMP-03: CIs reached only over connected_to are second-class heuristics and marked as such wherever impact is reported (the CI detail impact section uses blast-radius).
findings.actual: /impact marks server and vm heuristic=true; blast-radius returns affected_count=2 with vm and server and no flag. For the pdu, blast-radius counts 3 including the switch.
findings.user_impact: Operators see network neighbours as certainly affected in the CI detail impact analysis, which overstates the blast radius.
findings.cause: GetBlastRadius (impact.go:95-146) copies graph nodes in the impacted set into AffectedCIs ([]Node) and ignores impactHit.heuristic; BlastRadius has no heuristic field.
findings.recommendation: Carry the heuristic flag (and hops/via) in affected_cis, or split heuristic CIs into a separate list excluded from affected_count; render the marker in ImpactSection.
findings.retest: PG test of /cis/{id}/blast-radius for the probe graph: certain and heuristic CIs are distinguished; affected_count follows the decided semantics.

TopologyPage.test.tsx:70-95 asserts propagation along source->target and passes.

findings.title: Redundancy postfilter reports a redundantly supplied CI as impacted when the depth cuts off the alternative supply
findings.repro: Org with: server powered_by pdu-a, server powered_by pdu-b, vm hosted_on server. Call GET /api/v1/impact/{pdu-a}?depth=1, or /api/v1/impact?ci_ids={pdu-a}&depth=1, or /api/v1/topology/cis/{pdu-a}/impact?depth=1. Probe f1 output: impacted=[server] (HTTP 200). Without depth, or with depth=2, the result is [].
findings.expected: The server is not impacted at any depth, because pdu-b still supplies it.
findings.actual: The server is listed as impacted (certain) at depth=1.
findings.user_impact: API users and integrations that use a limited depth (maintenance windows, quick checks) see redundant systems reported as failing. This can lead to wrong outage decisions. The UI uses the default depth and is not affected.
findings.cause: writeImpact builds each failed CI's graph with buildFromRoot(depth) (impact.go:591). TraverseFrom loads only the edges of the first depth hops, and redundantProviders (redundancy.go:40-55) collects providers only from those edges. The server–pdu-b edge is missing, so allDown([pdu-a]) is true.
findings.recommendation: For every redundant-type dependent that is reached, load its incident redundant-type edges with one extra frontier query, regardless of depth. Alternatively, treat an unknown provider as up. Add a PG regression test.
findings.retest: Commit probe f1 as a PG test: depth=1 and /impact/{ups}?depth=2 (chain ups→pdu-a) must not list the server; with both PDUs failed, the server and the vm must be listed.

findings.title: Topology simulation silently shows a direction-naive client-side impact when /impact fails
findings.repro: Open /topology?simulate=<ids>, and let /impact fail (4xx/5xx) or still be loading. useImpactMany has retry:false and its error is ignored (TopologyPage.tsx:145). outageImpact falls back to computeOutageImpact (:147-153), which follows edge.source→edge.target. Backend edges are mapped with source=source_ci_id (dependent) and target=target_ci_id (provider) (:51-52). For 'server powered_by ups', a failing ups therefore marks nothing, and a failing server marks the ups.
findings.expected: An error or 'analysis unavailable' notice. A different impact set must never be shown.
findings.actual: The client BFS set is shown with no error indication.
findings.user_impact: Users can act on an impact set that has the wrong direction and no redundancy, without noticing.
findings.cause: TopologyPage.tsx:145-153 ignores the query error. The source→target semantics are asserted by the passing Vitest 'computeOutageImpact marks all transitively dependent nodes' (TopologyPage.test.tsx:70-83).
findings.recommendation: Render the error state of useImpactMany. Use the client computation only as a labelled preview while loading, or drop it.
findings.retest: Vitest: an /impact stub that returns 422 or 500 leads to visible error text and no impacted badges.

findings.title: GET /topology with an unknown or other-organization root_ci_id answers 500 instead of 404

findings.expected: 404 Not Found, as /topology/cis/{id}/neighbors and /impact answer.
findings.actual: 500 Internal Error. Nothing of the other tenant is leaked.
findings.user_impact: A stale or foreign root link shows an internal error instead of 'not found'. Error metrics and alerting count false 5xx responses.
findings.cause: buildFromRootViaTraversal returns ciRepo.GetByID's plain 'not found' error (topology.go:273-276). GetTopology passes it to api.WriteRepoError, which maps unknown errors to 500 (topology.go:137-140).
findings.recommendation: Map a missing root to 404, as GetNeighbors does at topology.go:155-157, or use a sentinel error that WriteRepoError maps to 404.
findings.retest: API test: an unknown uuid, an other-org CI and an other-client CI as root → 404; a malformed id → 400.

wps.soll_ist: Soll: each requested ID is either changed or reported with its error, and a user's bulk change is a manual change (API-07 rank ≥ 92). Ist: IDs whose status has a protected override are skipped but reported ok/200. Changed CIs keep their version and get no override. Malformed ids are reported as 500. Cancelling a running job leaves all changes applied and discards the report. The UI flow works for up to 25 visible rows.

findings.title: Bulk set_status silently skips CIs with a manual status override and reports them as ok
findings.repro: PATCH /api/v1/cis/{a} {status:maintenance} creates a protected override. Then POST /api/v1/cis/bulk {action:set_status, ids:[a,b], status:inactive}. Probe f2: HTTP 200, succeeded=2, both items ok/200. DB: a is still maintenance, b is inactive.
findings.expected: a is set to inactive (the manual change wins), or the item reports an error.
findings.actual: The status of a is unchanged, and the report says ok.
findings.user_impact: Any CI whose status was ever edited manually ignores bulk status changes while the UI shows a success toast. The CMDB state is silently wrong.
findings.cause: runBulk calls Service.Update without req.Manual (bulk.go:152). PGRepository.Update runs dropOverriddenFields (pg_repository.go:787-789, 1606-1638), which nils req.Status. No set clause remains, so the update returns 'before' without an error (pg_repository.go:845-848).
findings.recommendation: Set req.Manual = &ManualChange{Author: user} (and a change reason) in runBulk, as PATCH does (handler.go:486). Report 'unchanged' or an error when nothing was written.
findings.retest: PG test: an override on status, then a bulk change → the DB status equals the target and the item is ok. Negative case: a refused write is reported as an error.

findings.title: Bulk changes are not manual writes: no version bump, no protected override
findings.repro: Probe f2: after the bulk change to inactive, CI b still has version 1 and no ci_field_value override for status.
findings.expected: version+1 and a protected override, as PATCH does (API-07, OVR-01).
findings.actual: The version is unchanged and there is no override.
findings.user_impact: Optimistic concurrency does not see bulk changes, so a stale If-Match still succeeds. The next discovery run may overwrite the bulk status.
findings.cause: The same missing req.Manual: pg_repository.go:853-856 bumps the version only for Manual/Authoritative, and recordManualOverrides runs only for Manual.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same fix and add tests for the version and the override.
findings.retest: PG: after a bulk change the version increments and an override row exists. A PATCH with the pre-bulk ETag → 412.

findings.title: Cancelling a running bulk job does not stop it and discards its report
findings.repro: POST /cis/bulk with 500 ids → 202. Then HTTP DELETE /api/v1/jobs/{id} while it runs. Probe f2: 200 'cancelled' when 2 CIs are changed. After 8 s, 500/500 CIs are changed, the job is 'cancelled' with result_len=0, GET /jobs/{id}/result → 409 'the job has no result (status cancelled)', and the log shows 'cancelled → succeeded' refused.
findings.expected: No further CIs are changed after the cancel and the partial report is kept, or the cancel of a running job is refused with 409.
findings.actual: All changes are applied, the job shows cancelled, and the result is lost.
findings.user_impact: A user who cancels from the JobCenter believes nothing more happened, while every CI was changed and the per-ID report is gone.
findings.cause: runBulkJob and runBulk never check the job status or a cancellation context (bulk.go:124-169). jobs.Service.Cancel only transitions the status (service.go:200-209), and the later Succeed fails.
findings.recommendation: Check for cancellation between items, stop, and store the partial report with status cancelled. Otherwise refuse the cancel of running ci.bulk jobs with 409.
findings.retest: PG test: 500 ids, cancel after the first items → fewer than 500 changed, and the job is cancelled with the partial result.

findings.title: A malformed id in a bulk request is reported with item code 500
findings.repro: Real stack B04: POST /cis/bulk {ids:['not-a-uuid', <valid>], status:'inactive'} → the item {id:'not-a-uuid', result:'error', code:500, error:'the CI could not be updated'}, while PATCH /cis/not-a-uuid answers 400.
findings.expected: The item code is 400 (the status the single change answers, as stated in the OpenAPI bulkCIs description).
findings.actual: 500 with a generic message.
findings.user_impact: The report blames the server for a caller error, and 5xx metrics or alerts count false errors.
findings.cause: validateBulk (bulk.go:74-100) does not validate the id format. PG rejects the uuid, and bulkError falls through to 500 (bulk.go:191).
findings.recommendation: Validate each id as a UUID in validateBulk, or map invalid-uuid errors to 400 per item.
findings.retest: API test: a malformed id → item code 400, and the other ids are applied.

findings.title: UI can never use the job path: selection is limited to 25 visible rows
findings.repro: CIListPage.tsx:34 sets limit=25. Selections outside the visible page are dropped (:46-54). Real-stack J01 had to start the 100-id job through the API.
findings.expected: Bulk for up to 500 IDs (API-08) can be started from the UI, with per-ID errors also for jobs.
findings.actual: At most 25 IDs per action. The 'queued' branch is unreachable in practice.
findings.user_impact: Mass changes need many page-by-page actions.
findings.cause: A fixed page size and a visible-only selection.
findings.recommendation: Offer 'select all matching the filter' (ids from the server), poll the job, and show its per-ID report.
findings.retest: Vitest and e2e-real: select 150 → 202 → the job result is rendered with its failures.

criteria.criterion: Revert gemäß E-25

layers.ux: N/A for the API itself. The JobCenter (UI-16) offers cancel for running jobs, which inherits the cancel defect (real-stack J01 covers list, filter and result).
layers.api: FAIL: DELETE on a running job reports success without stopping it. Jobs and their results ignore client scope. Permissions and 409s are otherwise correct.

wps.soll_ist: Soll: GET, DELETE (cancel), revert, result and job metrics within the caller's scope. Ist: all endpoints exist and work, and metrics are correct on PG. Cancelling a running job is only a status change: the work continues and its result is discarded. Job data is visible across clients of the same organization.
wps.evidence: Probe f2 reproduces the ineffective cancel through the real HTTP DELETE. Probe f8 reproduces the cross-client job result disclosure. The other operations have executed evidence (unit tests, PG probes f6 and f9, real-stack J01).
wps.deviation: The JOB-03 cancel semantics are not met for running jobs. Job visibility is organization-wide and ignores client scope (TEN-09 channel 'job').
wps.dependencies: WP-181 (ci.bulk runner), WP-183 (RunDetached), WP-130 (queue), UI-16 (JobCenter), WP-208 (channel matrix).

findings.title: DELETE /jobs/{id} on a running job marks it cancelled but the work continues and its result is lost
findings.repro: Probe f2: a 500-id ci.bulk job, HTTP DELETE /api/v1/jobs/{id} while running → 200 {status:cancelled}, with 2 CIs changed at that moment. Later 500/500 are changed, result_len=0 and GET /result → 409.
findings.expected: The running job stops at the next checkpoint, or the cancel of non-interruptible kinds is refused with 409.
findings.actual: 200 'cancelled', the operation completes, and the result is discarded.
findings.user_impact: Operators and users are misled about what happened, and the changes go unreported.
findings.cause: service.go:200-209 only transitions the status. runBulkJob (ci/bulk.go:124-134), RunDetached (service.go:328-353) and the queue worker never check for cancellation. Reproduced for ci.bulk; inferred from code for the other runners.
findings.recommendation: Provide a cancellation check (e.g. Service.IsCancelled, or a context cancelled by polling) and use it in the runners. Answer 409 for kinds that cannot be interrupted.
findings.retest: A PG test per runner kind: cancel during the run → the work stops, the status is cancelled, and a partial result is kept.

findings.title: Job API ignores client scope: a client-scoped principal lists and reads other clients' jobs and results
findings.repro: Probe f8: a client-1 user starts a 100-id bulk job. A client-2 principal (job:read, ci:read, ci:write) sees 0 of those CIs in GET /api/v1/cis, but GET /api/v1/jobs?kind=ci.bulk lists the job, and GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/result → 200 with all 100 client-1 CI ids.
findings.expected: Jobs of another client are not listed, and GET, result, DELETE and revert answer 404, as for the CIs themselves (TEN-09 lists 'job' as a channel).
findings.actual: Org-wide visibility of params and results. Cancel is allowed for any holder of the kind permission (mayControl).
findings.user_impact: In MSP setups a client-scoped user learns other clients' CI ids and per-ID outcomes, and can cancel their bulk jobs.
findings.cause: jobs handler List, Get and Result (handler.go:69-143) filter only by organization. The RLS policies job_isolation/job_system_select check organization_id only. mayControl (handler.go:147-157) ignores scope.
findings.recommendation: Record the creator's scope on the job and filter by it (or restrict to the creator plus org-wide principals). Make TestChannelMatrix assert the content of the job channel, not only the 200.
findings.retest: PG/API test: a client-2 principal gets an empty list, 404 on GET, /result, DELETE and revert of a client-1 job. An org-wide principal still sees it.

findings.title: Reverted job keeps status 'succeeded'; a second revert gives 409 with detail 'not found'
findings.repro: Probe f6: revert by the creator → 200 {reverted:true}. The job status is still succeeded. A second revert → 409 {detail:'not found'}.
findings.expected: The job records that it was reverted, and the second attempt gets a clear 409 ('already reverted').
findings.actual: No trace on the job, and a misleading detail.
findings.user_impact: The JobCenter cannot show reverted merges, and the error is confusing.
findings.cause: The Revert handler (handler.go:205-212) does not update the job, and the Unmerge error text is passed through.
findings.recommendation: Store reverted_at and reverted_by on the job, and map an already-unmerged state to a clear 409.
findings.retest: PG: revert → the job shows reverted; a second revert → 409 'already reverted'.

test_gaps.description: Client-scope isolation of the job API
test_gaps.proposed_test: Full router on PG: a client-1 user starts a 100-id bulk job. A client-2 principal: GET /jobs does not contain it, and GET /jobs/{id}, /result, DELETE and /revert → 404. An org-wide admin sees it. Extend TestChannelMatrix so the job channel asserts that no other-scope job id is present.

test_gaps.description: HTTP job API against PG with org isolation
test_gaps.proposed_test: NewAPIHandler(NewService(NewPGRepository)). The OrgA list excludes OrgB jobs. GET, DELETE and revert of an OrgB id → 404. Result of a failed job → 409. Status filter 'x' → 422.

test_gaps.description: Cancellation of running jobs
test_gaps.proposed_test: RunDetached with a run that loops over 100 steps and checks for cancellation. Cancel after step 10 → the run stops, the status is cancelled, Succeed is not attempted, and a partial result is stored. Same for a queue-worker kind and for ci.bulk via HTTP DELETE.

test_gaps.description: Revert of ci.merge via HTTP on PG
test_gaps.proposed_test: Commit probe f6: merge → revert by the creator 200 (victim deleted_at NULL); a stranger without ci:delete → 403; a second revert → 409; a non-revertible kind → 409.

test_gaps.description: Metrics scrape on PG

The auditor had noted org-level visibility as 'by design, not asserted', but TEN-09 lists jobs as a tenant channel. wps.user_goal: Long-running operations (review merge, state snapshot) appear as jobs with a status and a result, instead of running synchronously and invisibly.

Commit 84bc267 states 'Ergebnis der rekonstruierte Zustand' (the result is the reconstructed state).
wps.tests: results-backend.tsv: internal/reviews TestLongOperationsRunAsJobsAgainstPostgres passes. merge_job_integration_test.go:29-125 uses a STUB merge effect. Its snapshot part inserts a ci_change rename but asserts only result.entity_id (:121-123). Verifier probes on audit_db_21 (ov_rev.json): f7 TestAuditProbeSnapshotContent was changed to rename the CI through ci.Service.Update with Manual instead of a raw insert. It gives ci_change rows=1 and entity_change rows=0. The snapshot job succeeds with fields={} now, fields={} at T-2h, fields={} for a client-2 principal, and fields={} for an unknown id. f3 TestAuditProbeReviewMergeRetry: the first resolve fails, the retry succeeds and the item is resolved, but the review.merge job stays failed with error 'transient failure' (1 job per item). psql on audit_db_21: SELECT count(*) FROM entity_change → 0; no trigger function references entity_change.

criteria.criterion: Snapshot-Umfang nach JOB-04 (E-25)
criteria.evidence: JOB-04/E-25 define no explicit scope, and the replay content (AUD-08) is [P2]. Still, the delivered 'reconstructed state' is empty for every real CI, because TrailUpTo reads entity_change, which nothing writes (probe f7 with a real manual rename). The existing test masks this.

findings.title: Retried review merge leaves its job in status failed
findings.repro: Probe f3: resolve with merge while the effect fails → the job is failed. Resolve again while the effect succeeds → the item is resolved, but the job is still failed with error 'transient failure'.
findings.expected: The job of the successful retry shows succeeded, or each attempt gets its own job.
findings.actual: There is a single job per item (uq_job_ref), and it stays failed.
findings.user_impact: The JobCenter shows a failed merge that actually succeeded.
findings.cause: Track is idempotent per (ref_table, ref_id), and Mirror skips disallowed transitions from a terminal status (jobs/service.go:273-320).
findings.recommendation: Reset the job to queued or running on a new attempt (with an attempt counter), or create one job per attempt.
findings.retest: PG: fail, then retry → the job is succeeded with attempts=2.

findings.title: Review merge runs synchronously; the job only mirrors it
findings.repro: reviews/service.go:172-192 runs Track, then Mirror(running), then effect(ctx) inline in the HTTP request, then Mirror(terminal). Probe f3 shows that Resolve returns only after the job is already terminal.
findings.expected: JOB-04: large operations run as an asynchronous job.
findings.actual: Synchronous execution with a mirrored job record.
findings.user_impact: Long merges block the request, and the merge gets no retry or timeout from the job model.
findings.cause: A design choice in runEffect.
findings.recommendation: Decide (as a follow-up to E-25) whether the mirror is sufficient. If not, enqueue the merge and answer 202.
findings.retest: A review or decision record, and a test asserting 202 for a merge resolution if it becomes asynchronous.

findings.title: Numeric comparison on a dynamic attribute aborts the whole query when any visible CI stores a non-numeric value under that key
findings.repro: VP/probe/zz_verify_b24_sv_test.go (go test -overlay VP/probe/overlay-sv.json -run TestVerifyB24SavedViews -v ./internal/savedview/, TEST_DATABASE_URL=audit_db_22). Seed CIs with attributes ram_gb 64, 32 and "16GB". POST /api/v1/search/query {"where":{"field":"attributes.ram_gb","op":"gte","value":16}}
findings.expected: 200 with the CIs whose numeric ram_gb ≥ 16; non-numeric values simply do not match
findings.actual: 400 'count query results: ERROR: invalid input syntax for type numeric: "16GB" (SQLSTATE 22P02)'. The same query combined with another predicate returned 200 (evaluation-order dependent).
findings.user_impact: Saved views and queries such as 'RAM ≥ 16' or 'vlan = 10' fail for the whole organisation once a single CI carries a text value for that key (discovery data, another CI type reusing the key).
findings.cause: fieldKind (filter.go:342-351) chooses kindNumber from the JSON value type; comparison (filter.go:459-465) casts (attributes->>key)::numeric for every row without a jsonb_typeof guard
findings.recommendation: Guard the cast, e.g. CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(attributes->key)='number' THEN (attributes->>key)::numeric END (same for eq/ne/in with numbers), or use a safe-cast function; add a PG test with mixed types
findings.retest: PG integration: CIs with ram_gb 64, 8 and "16GB"; gte 16 → 200 with exactly the 64-GB CI; eq 8 → exactly the 8-GB CI

findings.actual: 400 with 'invalid input syntax for type uuid/timestamp with time zone ... (SQLSTATE 22P02/22007)'; in [{}] → 200 data:null

findings.recommendation: Validate values per field kind (uuid, RFC3339/date, numeric, bool) including `in` elements and return ASTError → 422; log DB errors and return a generic message

findings.title: PATCH without 'shared' silently unshares an org-shared view
findings.repro: VP/probe/zz_verify_b24_sv_test.go: owner POST /api/v1/saved-views {name, entity_kind:ci, shared:true, sort, columns}; owner PATCH /saved-views/{id} {"name":"Shared renamed"}; another org member GET /saved-views/{id}; SELECT shared FROM saved_view
findings.expected: PATCH changes only the name; the view stays shared and readable for the org
findings.actual: 200 with shared=false; DB shared=false; the other member gets 404 (sort/columns stay, since they are nil-checked)
findings.user_impact: Colleagues silently lose access to a shared view after any PATCH by an API client or integration. The current UI never PATCHes (savedViewApi.update is unused), so a future edit UI would trigger it.
findings.cause: UpsertRequest.Shared is a plain bool with omitempty (model.go:40); Update always appends `shared = $n` with req.Shared (pg_repository.go:153-155)
findings.recommendation: Use *bool for Shared (and for other PATCH fields) and update shared only when it is sent
findings.retest: PG integration: create shared → PATCH name only → GET as another member 200 with shared=true

findings.title: Any holder of saved_view:write can rename, unshare or delete another user's org-shared view
findings.repro: Probe: owner creates {shared:true}; another org member (saved_view:write) PATCH {"name":"hijacked","shared":true} → 200; DELETE → 204; DB rows = 0
findings.expected: An explicit, consistent rule. Role-shared views are read-only for members (model.go:20-21, probe DELETE 404), so org-shared views would be expected to be owner-edited too.
findings.actual: Non-owners with saved_view:write (engineer, org_admin, custom roles) edit and delete org-shared views. Viewers cannot, because they lack saved_view:write (permission/role_matrix.go viewer list; route_permissions.txt:45,319).
findings.user_impact: Shared team views can be renamed or deleted by any engineer without owner consent (no undo)
findings.cause: Update/Delete WHERE (shared OR owner_id = $n) (pg_repository.go:157,175). This is documented as intended since 3a2a512 (comments :112,:171); VIE-01 defines no edit rights.
findings.recommendation: Record a decision (owner-only, or an admin permission). If owner-only, restrict the predicate and hide the delete button for foreign views.
findings.retest: PG integration: a non-owner PATCH/DELETE on an org-shared view → 404/403 with the DB unchanged; owner → 200/204

findings.title: Collector metric uploads (sweep reachability, UPS values, SNMP poll) are rejected with 401 and never reach the server
findings.repro: (a) Code: uploadSamples → uploadMetricSamples → postMetricsPayload (collector/collectorcmd/collectorcmd.go:1068-1115) POSTs /api/v1/monitoring/metrics with only Content-Type, X-Organization-ID and X-Collector-ID, no Authorization. Ingest and heartbeat use the mTLS NATS edge (edge.go:61,86), but there is no edge subject for metrics (edge.go:22-23; backend discovery/edge_ingest.go:23-24). (b) Real stack: the identical curl → 401 'missing bearer token' (middleware/auth.go:295-331; no client-certificate authentication on the HTTP API). (c) Real collector log /tmp/reticora-e2e-discovery-SuPITb/collector.log: the same uploader client gets 401 on its HTTP fallbacks.
findings.expected: Collector samples accepted (202) and stored with ci_id, so the CI detail shows sweep and UPS lines
findings.actual: 401; uploadSamples logs 'metric sample upload failed' (collectorcmd.go:1625-1632) and drops the samples
findings.user_impact: On real installations the CI metric line stays empty: MON-02 baseline metrics (reachability, UPS, interface counters) never exist
findings.cause: The metrics transport was not moved to the collector's edge identity, and the HTTP API has no collector credential. The collector tests post to an unauthenticated httptest server (schedule_test.go:133) and cannot catch this.
findings.recommendation: Add a '.metrics' edge subject handled server-side under the collector's certificate identity (org from the certificate), or issue an ingest credential the collector sends as a bearer. Add a real-collector E2E.
findings.retest: Real stack with the simulated collector: after a sweep, metric_sample holds rows with ci_id of the simulated CIs, and GET /cis/{id}/metrics returns sweep_reachable points

wps.title: Topologie-UI: Startdialog über 2.000 Knoten, Simulation mit mehreren Ausfall-IDs
wps.user_goal: Above 2,000 CIs the topology does not load everything at once: a start dialog first asks for a site or CI type. The failure simulation accepts several failing CIs together (UI-06 addition, IMP-05).
wps.implementation: frontend/src/pages/TopologyPage.tsx:129-131 (422 sets tooLarge), 258-263 and 371-418 (TopologyStartDialog: site and type selects, submit disabled until one is chosen), 96-102 and 181-186 (?simulate=a,b), 145-153 (server joint impact with a silent client BFS fallback), 341 (node badge shows the raw ci_type). frontend/src/api/hooks.ts:214-225 (useImpactMany). Backend: topology/topology.go:26 (MaxTopologyNodes=2000), 212-224 (buildFull returns 422 when total>2000), 120-142 (GetTopology: type id, site_id, client_id), 270-277 (GetByID error passed through, giving 500); topology/impact.go:434 and 445-472 (GetMultiImpact).
wps.tests: results-frontend.json: TopologyPage.test.tsx 17/17 passed. All use stubbed fetch, and TopologyGraph is mocked. The start dialog is tested only via the site path. results-backend.tsv: pass internal/topology TestMultiImpactAgainstPostgres (2001 CIs give 422; type filter gives 200; joint impact of 2 PDUs; 400/404/422 negatives). Mocked Playwright: topology.spec.ts passed on chromium and mobile-chrome (e2e-mocked.log). Real stack: e2e-onboarding-real.log #6 (/topology?simulate=<one id> shows 'Ausfallsimulation'); tenant-iso-final.log T10 passed and T15 failed (500). Verifier probe TestProbeV25TopologyLimit (audit_db_23): exactly 2000 gives 200 with 2000 nodes; 2001 gives 422 (field root_ci_id); root with 2001 gives 200; site_id gives 200 with 10 nodes; client_id gives 200 with 11 nodes; ci_type=not-a-uuid gives 400; site_id=not-a-uuid gives 400. Re-run of TestProbeB25TopologyForeignRoot: foreign and random root both 500; neighbors and impact 404.

criteria.criterion: Start dialog with site/type selection above 2,000 nodes; multi-selection for the simulation (with WP-180)
criteria.evidence: The server side is now fully proven on PostgreSQL: 2000/2001 boundary, site, client and type narrowing, root unaffected, and invalid filters give 400 rather than 422, so the dialog cannot be triggered by mistake (verifier probe). Joint impact is proven on PostgreSQL. The UI dialog (site path only) and the multi-failure UI are proven only with stubbed fetch and mocked Playwright. No real UI→API→DB run of the dialog or of a 2-CI simulation exists. The real stack covers only rendering (T10) and a single-CI simulation.

layers.ux: OK: the dialog is a labelled form with submit disabled until a choice is made, and error and empty states exist. GAP: the node badge shows the type UUID (TopologyPage.tsx:341; probe body shows ci_type 'c8b23944-…'). Impact errors are silently replaced by the BFS fallback. The start-dialog state is not covered by the axe scan.
layers.api: FAIL: GET /topology?root_ci_id=<foreign or unknown> returns 500 (re-run on audit_db_23; real T15). Boundary and filters are OK (verifier probe).
layers.data: OK: read-only. The limit is enforced server-side; site, client and type narrowing are proven on PostgreSQL by the probe.
layers.e2e: GAP: the dialog and multi-failure flow never ran UI→API→DB.

wps.evidence: results-frontend.json 17/17; results-backend.tsv pass TestMultiImpactAgainstPostgres 1.96s; e2e-mocked.log; e2e-onboarding-real.log #6; tenant-iso-final.log T10 ✓ and T15 ✘. findings.title: Server impact errors are silently replaced by client-side BFS
findings.repro: Simulate more than 100 CIs or a CI the server refuses: useImpactMany errors (422/404), and the page shows computeOutageImpact on the loaded edges without a notice (TopologyPage.tsx:145-153; the impact error is never read).
findings.expected: A visible warning that the authoritative analysis failed.
findings.actual: The fallback is shown as authoritative and ignores rel_type and edges outside the loaded graph.
findings.user_impact: A possibly incomplete impact assessment without any warning.
findings.cause: No error branch for the impact query (code read; not executed).
findings.recommendation: Show an inline warning when impact.error is set, and mark the fallback as provisional.

wps.title: Review-Inbox mit Diff, Einzel- und Bulk-Auflösung
wps.user_goal: Operators work through reconciliation review items in one inbox: filter them, compare observation and CI in a diff, and resolve them one by one (merge, new, accept, dismiss) or in bulk.
wps.implementation: frontend/src/pages/ReviewInboxPage.tsx:57-73 (reviewDiff), 82-88 (bulk actions without merge), 140-175 (filters), 177-210 (bulk), 278-355 (detail, diff, candidate select with raw ids at :290-296, per-type actions). frontend/src/hooks/useReviews.ts:22-34 (REVIEW_ACTIONS mirror backend reviews/model.go:70-82), 61-67 (fixed limit=100), 69-74 (POST /review-items/{id}/resolve). Backend: routes registered by discovery/discovery.go:719 with the real effects in discovery/review.go:48-60. resolveCIReview :118-212: merge requires a candidate ci_id; new builds ci.Item with CITypeID = payload ci_type_name with no type lookup (:172). reviews/service.go: 409 if already resolved, 422 for a disallowed action.
wps.tests: Vitest: ReviewInboxPage.test.tsx 7/7 passed (stubs). Backend: pass internal/reviews TestTST01ReviewResolution (PostgreSQL, but the effects are STUBBED via WithEffect returning (false, nil), so it proves only transitions and allowed actions), TestReviewRepositoryOnPostgreSQL; pass internal/discovery TestResolveReviewItemMerge and TestResolveReviewItemCreate (memory repositories); pass TestResurrectedDeviceIsReactivatedOrNew (PostgreSQL merge for resurrected). Mocked Playwright review.spec.ts passed. REAL STACK (missed by the auditor), discovery-override.spec.ts in SP/work/discovery-override/final.log and verify-discovery-override/full.log, all passed: D04 (inbox filtered by type, diff row 'model' shows the observed and CI values marked 'abweichend', and the accept and dismiss buttons are present); D05 (accept and dismiss via the UI; after reload the items are listed under resolved/dismissed; the database has status, action, resolved_by and resolved_at; the CI is back on the observed value or the override is kept; re-resolve gives 4xx; merge on override_conflict gives 4xx; the next discovery run creates no new item); D06 (bulk accept of 2 items: '2 erledigt, 0 fehlgeschlagen.', both stored as resolved/accept, persisted after reload). Also e2e-onboarding-real #6 (single dismiss) and tenant-iso T08 and T10. Verifier probe TestProbeV25ReviewEffects (PostgreSQL, /api/v1/review-items/{id}/resolve, items produced by a real ingest): merge into the chosen candidate gives 200, the candidate management_ip is set to 198.18.77.1/32, and the item is resolved; new on ambiguous_identity gives 200 and the CI is created; new on unclassified_device (unknown type) gives 400 'a field value has an invalid format or is out of range' and the item stays open.
