POST /api/v1/review-items/{id}/resolve {"action":"new"} (exactly what the inbox button sends).
findings.expected: A CI is created (for example after choosing a type), or a clear 4xx explaining that a type must be chosen first. The UI does not offer an action that cannot succeed.
findings.actual: 400 'a field value has an invalid format or is out of range'; the item stays open. For reason no_profile_match the backend refuses with 409 by design (review.go:165-167). So 'new' never succeeds for this kind, although REVIEW_ACTIONS offers it.
findings.user_impact: Operators cannot create a CI for an unclassified device from the inbox and see a meaningless error. They must create it manually and dismiss the item.
findings.cause: discovery/review.go:172 sets CITypeID = payload 'ci_type_name' (an unresolved type name) and passes it to ciRepo.Create; the PostgreSQL uuid column rejects it (22P02 mapped to 400). The memory-repository test TestResolveReviewItemCreate accepts any string and masks it.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the type name to an id (as the ingest does, discovery.go:1157-1166), or accept a ci_type_id in the resolution and let the UI ask for a type. Otherwise do not offer 'new' for unclassified_device and explain the next step.
findings.retest: Integration test (PostgreSQL): unclassified_device with type created in the meantime, or with a ci_type_id in the resolution: 'new' gives 200 and the CI exists. Without a resolvable type: a 4xx with a clear message, and the UI shows it.

findings.title: Inbox caps at 100 items without paging; 'select all open' covers only the loaded page
findings.repro: Tenant with more than 100 open items: /reviews and 'Alle offenen auswählen'.
findings.expected: Paging, or a scope statement, for the bulk selection.
findings.actual: useReviews.ts:62 always sends limit=100; has_more and total are ignored.
findings.user_impact: Large post-sweep backlogs cannot be fully worked from the inbox.
findings.cause: Fixed limit and no pagination UI.
findings.recommendation: Add paging and show 'x of total'.
findings.retest: Vitest: with has_more=true the next page requests offset=100.

findings.title: Merge candidate selector lists raw CI UUIDs
findings.repro: ambiguous_identity with 2 candidates: the 'Kandidat' select options are UUIDs (ReviewInboxPage.tsx:295).
findings.expected: Candidate names and key identifiers.
findings.actual: options = candidates.map(id => ({value:id,label:id})).
findings.user_impact: Higher risk of merging into the wrong CI.
findings.cause: No name resolution for candidates.
findings.recommendation: Resolve candidate names via GET /cis?ids= or useCI.
findings.retest: Vitest: option text equals the CI name.

test_gaps.description: merge into a chosen candidate and new have never run UI→API→DB
test_gaps.proposed_test: Seed via ingest an ambiguous_identity item (MAC on 2 CIs) and an unclassified_device item. In the UI, filter the kind, pick candidate B by name, click 'Zusammenführen', and assert via the API that the item is resolved with action=merge and CI B has the observed management IP, while CI A is unchanged. 'Neu anlegen' on a second ambiguous item creates exactly 1 new CI with the observed fields. Negative: the same item resolved in a 2nd tab gives a 409 alert. A viewer sees the inbox but resolve gives a visible 403. Tenant B sees none of A's items and cannot resolve them (403/404).

test_gaps.description: Real backend effect of 'new' for unclassified_device and of 'merge' for ambiguous_identity not covered by repo tests on PostgreSQL (TestTST01ReviewResolution stubs effects)
test_gaps.proposed_test: PostgreSQL, through POST /api/v1/review-items/{id}/resolve with discovery.NewHandler(PG repos). ambiguous merge with ci_id = candidate gives 200 and management_ip set; ci_id not a candidate gives 400. ambiguous new gives 200 with the CI created and attributes.review_item_id set. unclassified_device (unknown_ci_type) new gives either 200 with a type supplied or a clear 4xx (not the generic 400), and the item stays open. no_profile_match new gives 409 with an explanation.

test_gaps.description: Status filter, escalation-only, single new/accept 422 and paging branches untested; no WCAG scan of /reviews
test_gaps.proposed_test: Status 'Erledigt' requests status=resolved, disables checkboxes and shows no action buttons. A 422 on single resolve shows role=alert. has_more shows paging. Add /reviews (with an item selected) to the axe MAIN_PAGES: 0 wcag2a/2aa violations.

wps.upgrade_conditions: (1) A real E2E passes for merge into a chosen candidate and 'new', with database assertions and the 409/403 negatives. (2) 'new' for unclassified_device either succeeds or is not offered, proven by an integration test. Optional: paging beyond 100 and candidate names.
wps.verifier_note: Status upheld; priority raised from P3 to P2 because of a new reproduced defect. I added evidence the auditor missed: real-stack discovery-override D04, D05 and D06 passed in two runs (final.log and verify full.log), proving filter, real diff, accept and dismiss persistence and bulk accept. Correction: TestTST01ReviewResolution replaces all effects with stubs (reviews/tst01_integration_test.go:31-36), so it does not prove backend effects; TestResolveReviewItemMerge and TestResolveReviewItemCreate use memory repositories. My PostgreSQL probe shows merge and new on ambiguous_identity work, but new on unclassified_device returns 400 and the item stays open (review.go:172 passes the type name as CITypeID). The remaining UI gap is merge and new via the real browser.

wps.title: Benachrichtigungs- und Jobcenter
wps.user_goal: Users see unread and read in-app notifications in a bell panel and can mark them read. A job center lists the organization's jobs with progress, lets them cancel active jobs and shows the result of finished ones.
wps.implementation: frontend/src/components/NotificationCenter.tsx:15-118 (bell count from unread total; panel; mark one and mark all; no isError branch, :22-23 and 72-76). frontend/src/hooks/useNotifications.ts:18-44. frontend/src/pages/JobCenterPage.tsx:33-164 (filter, progressbar, cancel for every queued or running job at :119-128, 'Ergebnis' for every succeeded job at :129-133, cancel error alert at :72-75). frontend/src/hooks/useJobs.ts:35-64. Backend: notify/handler.go; jobs/handler.go:127-140 (result 409 without a stored result), 161-180 (cancel authz); jobs/service.go:200-209 (Cancel is only a status transition) and 273-317 (Mirror never sets Result). Production wiring server/router.go:335 and 359 (exportWorker.Tracker = jobService). export/worker.go:134-176 never reads the generic job status.
wps.tests: Vitest: NotificationCenter.test.tsx 2/2 and JobCenterPage.test.tsx 3/3 passed (stubs). Backend: pass internal/notify TestNotificationsAgainstPostgres and TestNotificationAPI; pass internal/jobs TestJobAPIListGetResult, TestJobAPICancel, TestJobAPIRevert (memory) and TestJobsAgainstPostgres. REAL STACK (missed by the auditor): frontend/e2e-real/bulk-jobs-export.spec.ts, passed in SP/work/bulk-jobs-export/final.log and SP/work/verify-bulk-jobs-export/final.log. J01: a 100-id bulk job (202, kind ci.bulk). /jobs shows the row reaching 'Erfolgreich' with progressbar aria-valuenow=100. The status filter failed gives 'Keine Jobs' and succeeded shows the row. The 'Ergebnis' dialog shows "succeeded": 98, "failed": 2, the missing id and 'CI not found'. The API result has 100 items. The change persists (98 inactive after reload). DELETE on a finished job gives 409. Tenant A gets 404 on the job and its result and does not see it in its list. N01: an export completion creates an in-app notification; the bell label equals the API unread total; the panel entry has data-unread=true; 'Als gelesen markieren' gives POST 204 and read_at is stored; after reload it stays read; tenant B neither sees nor marks it (404). Re-run of the auditor probes on audit_db_23: mirrored export 'generic job status=cancelled; export job status=completed'; mirrored job result 'GET /jobs/{id}/result -> 409 the job has no result (status succeeded)'.

criteria.criterion: Notification center (read/unread)
criteria.evidence: Real UI→API→DB (N01, 2 runs): unread count equals the API; mark read persists read_at across reload; tenant isolation holds. PostgreSQL per-user isolation (TestNotificationsAgainstPostgres). Only 'Alle gelesen' and the error state are proven with stubs only.

criteria.criterion: Job center (progress, cancel, result)
criteria.evidence: Progress, filter and result are real for a native kind (J01). Cancel via the UI never ran on the real stack (only the API 409 for a finished job). Cancel of a mirrored export job is cosmetic: the export completes (probe re-run). 'Ergebnis' for mirrored kinds (export, review merge, ci_merge, discovery) answers 409 (probe re-run plus code: Mirror never sets Result).

layers.ux: OK: accessible bell label, dialog panel, progressbar, filter, cancel error alert (verified in J01 and N01). GAP: the notification panel shows 'Keine Benachrichtigungen' on a load error (no isError). Job kinds are not translated (J01 shows 'ci.bulk'). 'Ergebnis' is offered for result-less jobs. Not in the axe scan.
layers.api: FAIL: DELETE /jobs/{id} on an export job returns 'cancelled' while the export completes. /jobs/{id}/result returns 409 for every mirrored succeeded job. Otherwise OK (real J01 and N01).
layers.data: GAP: generic job and export_job states diverge after a cancel (cancelled vs completed). Notification read state persists (N01).
layers.e2e: PARTIAL: the notification center and the job center (progress, filter, result for ci.bulk) are real. UI cancel and mark-all are not.
layers.robustness: PARTIAL: finished-job cancel gives 409 and cross-tenant gives 404 (J01 and N01 real). GAP: 403 cancel by a non-creator via the UI; notification load failure.

wps.soll_ist: Target: a notification center with read/unread, and a job center with progress, cancel and result. Actual: the notification center works end to end. The job center works end to end for native jobs (progress, filter, result). Cancel is ineffective for mirrored export jobs, and 'Ergebnis' dead-ends with 409 for mirrored kinds. UI cancel is unproven on the real stack.
wps.evidence: SP/work/bulk-jobs-export/final.log and SP/work/verify-bulk-jobs-export/final.log: '✓ J01 … job center follows to the end …' and '✓ N01 … notification center; read state persists'. SP/work/verify-B25/rerun-auditor-probes.log: 'generic job status=cancelled; export job status=completed', 'GET /jobs/{id}/result -> 409'. results-frontend.json 5/5. results-backend.tsv: pass TestNotificationsAgainstPostgres and TestJobsAgainstPostgres.
wps.deviation: Cancel does not stop mirrored export jobs. 'Ergebnis' errors for mirrored kinds. UI cancel is not proven on the real stack. The notification panel has no error state. Job kinds are untranslated.
wps.dependencies: WP-182 (jobs API: mirror and cancel semantics), WP-189 (export worker), WP-139 (notifications).

findings.title: Cancelling an export job in the job center does not stop the export
findings.repro: go test -overlay SP/work/audit-B25/overlay/overlay-export.json -run TestProbeB25ExportCancelViaJobCenter ./internal/export/. POST export creates a generic job kind=export; DELETE /jobs/{generic id} (the JobCenterPage 'Abbrechen' button) gives cancelled; then worker.ProcessOne. Production wires the same tracker (server/router.go:359).
findings.expected: The export does not render or store the file and ends cancelled in both models, or the UI does not offer cancel for kinds without real cancellation.
findings.actual: The generic job is cancelled while the export_job is completed and the file is stored. The later Mirror(succeeded) is ignored, so the states diverge.
findings.user_impact: Users believe an export was stopped while it completes and stays downloadable. The job center and the export page disagree.
findings.cause: jobs/service.go:200-209 only transitions the row; export/worker.go:134-176 never checks the generic status; there is no per-kind cancel hook.
findings.recommendation: Propagate cancel (the worker checks the generic status before claim and before CompleteJob, or a kind cancel hook) or hide cancel for mirrored kinds.
findings.retest: Integration (PostgreSQL): create an export, DELETE /jobs/{id}, run ProcessOne: the export_job is not completed, no blob is stored, and no export.completed is emitted.

findings.title: 'Ergebnis' button is offered for every succeeded job but mirrored jobs never have a result (409)
findings.repro: go test -overlay SP/work/audit-B25/overlay/overlay.json -run TestProbeB25MirroredJobResult ./internal/jobs/ gives status=succeeded, result="" and GET /jobs/{id}/result 409. JobCenterPage.tsx:129-133 shows the button whenever status=succeeded.
findings.expected: A result (for example an export download link or a merge summary) or no button.
findings.actual: The modal shows the 409 text for export, review merge, ci_merge and discovery jobs.
findings.user_impact: A dead-end button for common kinds.
findings.cause: Mirror (service.go:273-317) never sets Result; handler.go:127-140 returns 409; the UI ignores job.result.
findings.recommendation: Show the button only when job.result is present, and/or store a result for mirrored kinds.
findings.retest: Vitest: a succeeded job without result shows no button. Integration: an export mirror success stores a result.

findings.title: Notification panel hides load errors as 'no notifications'
findings.repro: Make /api/v1/notifications fail (500 or 403) and open the bell: count 0 and 'Keine Benachrichtigungen' (NotificationCenter.tsx:22-23, 72-76; no isError branch).
findings.expected: An error state with retry.
findings.actual: A silent empty state.
findings.user_impact: Missed alerts without any indication.
findings.cause: No isError branch (verified by code read).
findings.recommendation: Render an error and retry when unread.isError or all.isError.
findings.retest: Vitest with a 500 stub: an error message is visible.

test_gaps.description: Cancel via the job center UI never ran on the real stack (native and mirrored kinds)
test_gaps.proposed_test: Start a 100-id bulk job and an export, and in /jobs press 'Abbrechen' while queued: both rows show 'Abgebrochen', the bulk changes nothing (the database CIs keep their status), the export_job is not completed and the export page offers no download. Negative: user C (same org, not creator, no kind permission) presses 'Abbrechen' and a 403 alert is shown with the job unchanged. A finished job shows no cancel button. Tenant B cannot cancel A's job (404).

test_gaps.description: Cancel propagation for mirrored export jobs
test_gaps.proposed_test: PostgreSQL with Tracker = jobs.Service(PG). DELETE /api/v1/jobs/{id}, then worker.ProcessOne: export_job.status is not completed, there is no blob key and no export.completed event. Cancel between MarkRunning and CompleteJob is still not completed. Cancel after completion gives 409.

test_gaps.description: Result button only with a result; mark-all and error branches
test_gaps.proposed_test: A succeeded job without result has no 'Ergebnis'. DELETE 403 shows role=alert. /jobs 500 shows ErrorState with retry. Notifications 500 shows an error text. Escape closes the panel. Real stack: 'Alle gelesen' sets read_at on all of the user's items but not on another user's.

wps.upgrade_conditions: (1) Cancel really stops mirrored export jobs, or is hidden for them (integration test). (2) 'Ergebnis' appears only where a result exists. (3) A real E2E of UI cancel (native and export) with the 403 negative passes. The notification center part is already proven.
wps.verifier_note: Status and P2 upheld, but the evidence is corrected. The auditor wrote 'No real UI run of the bell or the job center', which is wrong: bulk-jobs-export.spec.ts J01 and N01 passed on the real stack in two separate runs (SP/work/bulk-jobs-export/final.log 12:11 and verify-bulk-jobs-export/final.log 16:40). I read both bodies; they assert UI against API and database, persistence across reload and tenant isolation. The notification criterion is now met. I re-ran both job probes on audit_db_23 and both defects reproduce. Production wiring of the export tracker is confirmed at router.go:359.

wps.title: Provenienz-Tooltip mit Zeit und Auswahlbegründung für alle typisierten Felder
wps.user_goal: For every typed field of a CI the user sees where the value comes from, when it was recorded or observed, its source rank and why it was selected, including override reason, author and covered value (REC-10).
wps.implementation: backend/internal/ci/provenance.go:58-77 (14 typed fields), 87-106 (GET /cis/{id}/provenance; another org gives 404), 111-150 (BuildProvenance), 152-172 (fromRecord: reason override or source_rank, rank, recorded and observed times, author, reason, covered value). Route ci/handler.go:65, wired in server/router.go:651. OpenAPI CIFieldProvenance. Frontend: components/cmdb/ProvenanceTooltip.tsx:18-79 (hover and focus, role=tooltip, Escape; author rendered raw at :66), CIDetailSections.tsx:219-305 (ProvenanceSection; no error branch), api/cmdbHooks.ts:266-272.
wps.tests: Backend: pass internal/ci TestProvenanceAgainstPostgres (PostgreSQL: observed, override and record reasons, empty fields omitted, cross-org 404). Vitest: ProvenanceTooltip.test.tsx 4/4 passed. REAL STACK (missed by the auditor): frontend/e2e-real/discovery-override.spec.ts, passed in SP/work/discovery-override/final.log and SP/work/verify-discovery-override/full.log. D02: on a real discovered CI, every typed field carrying a value has provenance with source, rank > 0 and a time (soft assertions, which fail the test if violated); model, manufacturer, serial and management_ip match {source: sim source, rank: REC-03 rank, reason: source_rank} with observed_at from this run and not in the future. The UI tooltip for model shows 'Höchstrangige Quelle', Quelle, Rang, Beobachtet and Erfasst with real values, and the row shows the Effektiv value. D03: an override set via the 'Override setzen' dialog (the reason is required; without it nothing is stored); the API has override_reason, override_author, protected, discovered_value and source; after reload the tooltip shows 'Manueller Override', Begründung = reason, Autor present, Überdeckt = discovered value, and Erfasst; the audit actor is set. tenant-iso T05 passed (B cannot read A's provenance).

criteria.criterion: API delivers provenance for all typed fields
criteria.evidence: TestProvenanceAgainstPostgres (PostgreSQL) plus real-stack D02, which iterates all 14 typed fields carrying a value. The cross-org 404 is shown on PostgreSQL and on the real stack (T05). Structural columns (ci_type_id, location, parent) are not observable fields; an override on them is refused with 422 (D03).

criteria.criterion: Tooltip with source, time, rank / override reason
criteria.evidence: Real browser against the real API and database: D02 (observed field: reason, source, rank, observed and recorded time) and D03 (override: reason, author, covered value, time). REC-10 elements (source, reported value, timestamp, effective value, selection reason) are all asserted across D02 and D03 (Discovery, Override and Effektiv columns plus the tooltip).

layers.ux: OK: info button per field, tooltip on hover and focus, aria-describedby, Escape (Vitest); real hover verified in D02 and D03. GAP (P3): the author is shown as a raw user id (D03 asserts override_author equals the user id; the tooltip renders it unchanged). There is no error state (an API failure shows 'Noch keine Provenienz-Daten').
layers.api: OK: CompleteList sorted by field; 404 for a foreign or unknown CI (PostgreSQL plus T05); 422 for a structural override (D03).
layers.data: OK: correct precedence on PostgreSQL. Override author, time and reason persisted (D03) and audited.
layers.e2e: OK: real UI→API→DB for the observed and override paths (D02 and D03, 2 runs each).
layers.robustness: OK: cross-tenant 404, required reason, structural refusal. GAP (low): the asset reason path and the attribute provenance path are untested; the record-reason tooltip is covered only by Vitest.

wps.soll_ist: Target: the API delivers provenance for all typed fields, and a tooltip shows source, time, rank or override reason. Actual: fulfilled and proven on PostgreSQL and in a real browser against the real stack, including tenant isolation. Only minor UX deviations remain.
wps.evidence: results-backend.tsv: pass backend/internal/ci TestProvenanceAgainstPostgres 0.55s. SP/work/discovery-override/final.log: '✓ 2 … D02 every typed field … provenance with source, rank and time; the tooltip shows it' and '✓ 3 … D03 … stored with author, time and reason'. SP/work/verify-discovery-override/full.log: ✓ D02, ✓ D03. tenant-iso-final.log ✓ T05. results-frontend.json 4/4.
wps.deviation: Minor (P3): the override author is shown as a user UUID. The provenance section shows 'no data' on API errors. The asset and attribute paths are untested.
wps.dependencies: WP-060, WP-084, override repository.

findings.title: Override author shown as raw user id in the tooltip
findings.repro: Real stack D03: override_author equals the user id (asserted in the spec); ProvenanceTooltip.tsx:66 renders provenance.override_author unchanged.
findings.expected: Display name or e-mail of the author.
findings.actual: A UUID.
findings.user_impact: 'Who decided' is only partly explainable.
findings.cause: No user-name resolution in the API (provenance.go:159) or the UI.
findings.recommendation: Add override_author_name server-side or resolve it via the users API.
findings.retest: Vitest and real E2E: the tooltip 'Autor' shows the display name.

findings.title: Provenance section shows 'no data' when the API fails
findings.repro: Make GET /cis/{id}/provenance return 500: 'Noch keine Provenienz-Daten (erstellt bei der nächsten Discovery).' (CIDetailSections.tsx:298-305 checks only isLoading).
findings.expected: An error state with retry.
findings.actual: A misleading empty state.
findings.user_impact: Users conclude that no provenance exists.
findings.cause: No isError branch (code read).
findings.recommendation: Render ErrorState when values.isError.
findings.retest: Vitest with a 500 stub shows the error text.

test_gaps.description: Asset and attribute provenance paths and the record-reason tooltip untested against real data
test_gaps.proposed_test: PostgreSQL: a CI linked to an asset with serial S1 and a CI serial S2 gives serial_number with reason=asset and value S1. Attribute rack_unit=12 is listed with reason=record. An attribute with an override row answers from the row. Real UI: the tooltip for 'name' shows 'Wert des CI-Datensatzes'.

test_gaps.description: Error state and author name
test_gaps.proposed_test: /provenance 500 shows ErrorState with retry. An override with an author id shows the resolved display name.

wps.upgrade_conditions: Already BESTANDEN. Downgrade only if D02, D03 or TestProvenanceAgainstPostgres fail in the final run. The UX deviations are optional.
wps.verifier_note: UPGRADED from TEILWEISE to BESTANDEN. The auditor's only missing criterion was 'tooltip not shown on a real CI detail page with real API data'. That evidence exists: discovery-override.spec.ts D02 and D03 (committed in cc74764) passed in SP/work/discovery-override/final.log and again in SP/work/verify-discovery-override/full.log. I read both bodies (spec lines 639-705 and 706-778): they assert API provenance for all typed fields with values and the real tooltip content for the observed and override paths, with persistence after reload. The P3 findings are kept and confirmed (D03 itself asserts that the author is the user id).

wps.title: Onboarding-Flow: Registrierung → Verifikation → Scope-Bestätigung → erste CIs
wps.user_goal: A new customer is guided through self-signup, e-mail verification, collector enrollment, scope confirmation and the first CIs, with a visible progress indicator (UI-17).
wps.implementation: frontend/src/pages/OnboardingPage.tsx:19-43 (5 steps; currentStep), 50-92 (progressbar plus step list), 94-151 (signup with ALTCHA), 153-214 (verify; 410 and 404 messages), 216-248 (enrollment code), 250-299 (scope suggestions: accept, dismiss, 'Weiter'), 301-335 (10s polling; scopesDone = local skip flag or no open suggestions with CIs > 0). Route App.tsx:301-309. There is no link to /onboarding anywhere else (grep: only App.tsx:303 and OnboardingPage.tsx:175; LoginPage.tsx has no signup link).
wps.tests: Vitest: OnboardingPage.test.tsx 7/7 passed (stubs). Backend: pass internal/signup (19 tests), pass internal/discovery TestDiscoveryScopes (accepting scope_suggested creates the scope, PostgreSQL). Real stack: SP/runs/e2e-onboarding-real.log 6/6 passed. #5: signup, Mailpit verification, trial, login and dashboard. #6: enrollment code from the UI, real collector, progress leaves 2, at least 30 CIs, done text. The collector log shows 'local subnets reported … suggested:3', so scope suggestions existed, but onboarding.spec.ts:243-255 clicks 'Bestätigen' and 'Weiter' only if visible and asserts nothing about scopes. The collector's first HTTP upload got 401 before mTLS was up and was delivered from the spool 10s later (log lines 15-24), which shows the spool works.

criteria.criterion: Guided flow with progress indicator across signup, verification, collector enrollment, scope confirmation through to first CIs
criteria.evidence: Real stack proves signup, verification, trial, login, enrollment code, real collector, CIs, done, and the progress leaving step 2. Scope confirmation via the UI is not asserted on the real stack (conditional click; no check of the discovery scope or review status); it is proven only by Vitest (POST body) plus TestDiscoveryScopes (PostgreSQL).

layers.ux: OK: progressbar with aria values, step list, error messages, DE/EN. GAP: no in-app entry to signup or onboarding. The skip state is local only (OnboardingPage.tsx:306).
layers.api: OK: signup, verify, enrollment-codes, scope suggestions and resolve, cis and collectors were all used on the real stack.
layers.data: OK: org creation and 30+ CIs persisted (real). Scope creation is proven on PostgreSQL but not via this UI.
layers.e2e: PARTIAL: most of the chain is real; the scope step is unasserted.
layers.robustness: OK: the expired-link message (Vitest) and signup protection (backend). GAP: no real negative for a reused or expired token or a duplicate e-mail through the UI.

wps.soll_ist: Target: a guided 5-step flow with progress. Actual: implemented and largely proven on the real stack. Scope confirmation is optional in the real E2E, and there is no visible entry point to signup.
wps.evidence: SP/runs/e2e-onboarding-real.log: '✓ 5 … self-signup, verification, trial, login and dashboard (4.7s)', '✓ 6 … collector, scopes, 30 simulated devices, review, impact and export (25.3s)', '6 passed (34.8s)'; collector log 'local subnets reported … suggested:3'. results-frontend.json 7/7. results-backend.tsv: pass TestDiscoveryScopes.
wps.deviation: Scope confirmation is not demonstrably exercised end to end. There is no signup or onboarding entry link.
wps.dependencies: WP-111/112, WP-156, real stack (Keycloak, Mailpit, collector).

findings.title: No in-app entry point to self-signup / onboarding
findings.repro: /login has no 'Registrieren' or 'Konto anlegen' link. grep -rn '/onboarding' frontend/src (non-test) finds only App.tsx:303 and OnboardingPage.tsx:175. The navigation and CommandPalette have no entry.
findings.expected: Discoverable signup from login (when enabled) and a way back into an unfinished onboarding.
findings.actual: Users must know the /onboarding URL.
findings.user_impact: Self-service registration is hard to find, and an interrupted onboarding is hard to resume.
findings.cause: No link was added.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Konto anlegen' link on LoginPage and a dashboard entry until the onboarding is done.
findings.retest: Vitest and Playwright: /login shows the link, which navigates to /onboarding.

test_gaps.description: Scope confirmation not asserted in the real onboarding run
test_gaps.proposed_test: After the collector reports, assert progressbar aria-valuenow=3 and at least one CIDR suggestion is visible. Click 'Bestätigen' unconditionally, then assert via GET /discovery-scopes?collector_id=… that the scope exists and the review item has status resolved and action accept. Assert 4 and then 5 after CIs arrive. Negative: 'Verwerfen' on a second suggestion creates no scope. Tenant B does not see A's suggestions.

test_gaps.description: Real negative paths of signup and verification

findings.title: Mocked ci.spec.ts passes although the real CMDB create form fails (ci_type_id sent as type key → 400)
findings.repro: Real stack: /cmdb, then 'Anlegen', CI-Typ 'Server', fill the fields and submit (ci-lifecycle.spec.ts L01). POST /api/v1/cis body {"ci_type_id":"server",…} returns 400 'a field value has an invalid format or is out of range'. Reproduced in SP/work/ci-lifecycle/final.log and SP/work/verify-ci-lifecycle/single-L01.log. Mocked frontend/e2e/ci.spec.ts passes because the mock accepts any body and asserts only name and discovery_source (:70).
findings.expected: The form sends the CI type UUID from GET /ci-types, the CI is created (201), and the core-flow spec fails when the request does not match the API contract.
findings.actual: CIFormModal.tsx:30 and 66-74 use a hard-coded list of type keys as option values. The backend expects ci_type_id as a UUID, so 400 and nothing is stored. The spec stays green.
findings.user_impact: Users cannot create CIs through the CMDB form on a real installation (org-specific types are also never offered), and the TST-03 suite does not detect it.
findings.cause: Static ciTypeValues in CIFormModal plus a permissive, non-contract-validated mock (backend.ts:72-79) and a weak body assertion in ci.spec.ts.
findings.recommendation: Load the type options from useCITypes (value=id, localized label). In ci.spec.ts assert ci_type_id is a UUID from the mocked /ci-types and validate mock requests and responses against api/openapi.yaml. Add the real-stack L01 to the gate.
findings.retest: Real ci-lifecycle L01 is green (201 plus database row). Mocked ci.spec.ts fails if ci_type_id is not one of the mocked /ci-types ids.

findings.title: Mock backend silently answers unknown API routes with 200, masking wiring errors
findings.repro: frontend/e2e/support/backend.ts:72-79: an unmatched route gets 200 with EMPTY_LIST or {}. A misspelled or removed endpoint renders 'empty' and the spec passes.
findings.expected: Unknown routes fail or are reported, and mocks are validated against OpenAPI.
findings.actual: Silent success (contributes to the P1 above).
findings.user_impact: E2E specs cannot detect UI→API contract breaks.
findings.cause: Permissive default handler.
findings.recommendation: Add strict mode (fail on unhandled /api/v1 routes, with an explicit allowlist) and OpenAPI schema validation of request and response bodies.
findings.retest: Rename an endpoint used by a page; its spec must fail.

findings.title: CMDB list CSV export button fails on the real stack (401 missing bearer token)
findings.repro: Real stack ci-lifecycle.spec.ts L10b: on /cmdb click the CSV export button; the request answers 401 'missing bearer token' (SP/work/verify-ci-lifecycle/single-L10b.log).
findings.expected: The CSV of the listed CIs downloads (200).
findings.actual: 401; nothing downloads. The mocked export.spec.ts covers only the /export job page and cannot detect this.
findings.user_impact: The quick export from the CMDB list does not work; users must use the export page.
findings.cause: The download request is issued without the Authorization header (observed 401 'missing bearer token'; the exact code line was not traced in this pass).
findings.recommendation: Download via fetch with the bearer token (blob) or a signed URL; add a spec.
findings.retest: Real L10b green; a mocked spec asserts the Authorization header on the export request.

findings.title: Seeded CIs have no site/room/location: the seed's site_id/room_id are nulled by trigger ci_derive_location
findings.repro: Run cmd/seed (any size) on a migrated DB. Then: SELECT count(*), count(site_id), count(room_id), count(location_id) FROM ci WHERE organization_id = <seeded org> → 40|0|0|0 (and 10000|0|0|0 for a 10k seed). The seed (seed.go:219-227) sets site_id/room_id from md5 ids but no location_id. The BEFORE INSERT trigger ci_derive_location sets site_id := NULL and room_id := NULL when location_id IS NULL.
findings.expected: SIM-01 'Standortkette mit 2 Racks, 40 CIs … Mounts': the 40 rack-mounted CIs sit in the HQ server room (site/room/location), the rest in their client's site
findings.actual: All seeded CIs have no location. The 40 mounted CIs are linked to the racks only via rack_mount; the CI carries no site/room.
findings.user_impact: In the demo, CI detail, site/room filters and location-tree counts show no CIs. Site-scope isolation tests on the seed prove nothing, because RLS admits site_id IS NULL for every site scope. The defect is silent: the seed code reads as if it set the location.
findings.cause: The seed predates neither WP-054 nor accounts for it: the WP-054 trigger (02eef58, 2026-10-05) derives site/room only from location_id, and the seed (952b09a, 2026-10-14) still writes the legacy columns. TestSeedSIM01 does not assert CI location.
findings.recommendation: Set location_id to the room location (40 base CIs) or the client's site location in seed.go, and assert site_id/room_id/location_id in TestSeedSIM01.
findings.retest: TestSeedSIM01: count(location_id IS NOT NULL) == objects for both orgs; CI 21 has room 'Server room hq' and site 'Site hq'; GET /cis?filter[site_id]=<hq site> returns the expected CIs.

criteria.criterion: Query-budget/N+1 assertions and EXPLAIN check of central queries (ABN-02)
criteria.evidence: Statement-count (N+1) assertions are sound. The EXPLAIN checks in TestCIQueryBudget are vacuous. The verifier built a test-shaped fixture (10k CIs with rack attributes, org about 50% of ci) in a rolled-back tx. As reticora_app, `attributes @> '{"rack":"R7"}'` → 'Index Scan using idx_ci_org … Rows Removed by Filter: 9790'. planUsesSeqScan returns false, so the check passes while the whole org is read and no attribute index is used. The product predicate attributes->>'k' = v gives the same plan. The 'hostname' check uses lower(hostname), not the product column hostname_lc. Only TestIdentityHitsMatchSingle asserts index names.

layers.ux: N/A: no UI.
layers.api: OK: k6 drives real endpoints with an API key (verifier: http_req_failed 0/9,393).
layers.data: OK: budget tests run against PostgreSQL under RLS with 10k-row fixtures. GAP: the seed lacks attributes, search documents and locations, so attribute filters and global search cannot be load-tested.

wps.soll_ist: Soll: a harness that measures every NFR-02/03 budget, plus ABN-02 N+1 and missing-index checks of the central queries. Ist: the harness and workflow exist and run, and the N+1 budgets are well tested. The search and attribute-filter budgets are measured on proxies, relationship search is missing, and the EXPLAIN checks are vacuous. They would pass with no identity or attribute index at all, and they do not catch the confirmed unused attribute index under RLS.
wps.evidence: Verifier probes on audit_db_24 (work/verify-B26/probe.txt): P1 owner 'Index Scan using idx_attr_vb26probe … Execution Time: 0.704 ms'; P2 reticora_app 'Seq Scan on ci … Rows Removed by Filter: 10119 … 6.247 ms'; P3 @> as app role, Seq Scan 5.48 ms. probe-testform.txt: T1/T2 'Index Scan using idx_ci_org … Rows Removed by Filter: 9790'. TestCIQueryBudget re-run PASS 12.40 s on the same DB. api-1.txt:1385/1387/1411: list p95 645.69 ms ✗, search p95 534.18 ms ✗, thresholds crossed.
wps.deviation: Search budget measured on the CI-list name filter. Attribute-filter budget measured on column filters. No relationship-search scenario. EXPLAIN checks are vacuous (org-index scan passes) and do not use product SQL. Attribute expression indexes are unusable under RLS and undetected.
wps.dependencies: WP-203 (seed); SR-04 (non-leakproof expressions under RLS); WP-142 (attribute index DDL); search indexer; WP-206.

findings.title: Indexed attribute filters cannot use their expression index under RLS; ABN-02 EXPLAIN check is vacuous and does not detect it
findings.repro: Rolled-back tx on 10k CIs of one org. Create the index exactly as citype.IndexStatement does: CREATE INDEX … ON ci (organization_id,(attributes->>'asset_tag')) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND (attributes->>'asset_tag') IS NOT NULL AND organization_id='<org>'. EXPLAIN ANALYZE `… WHERE organization_id=<org> AND deleted_at IS NULL AND attributes->>'asset_tag'::text='AT-04242'` as owner, then as reticora_app with app.org_id set (work/verify-B26/probe.sql). Separately, EXPLAIN TestCIQueryBudget's `attributes @> '{"rack":"R7"}'` on a test-shaped fixture (probe-testform.sql).
findings.expected: The runtime index of a searchable attribute serves filter[attributes.<key>] for the app role, and the ABN-02 test fails when it does not
findings.actual: Owner: Index Scan idx_attr_*, 0.70 ms. App role: Seq Scan, 10,119 rows removed, 6.25 ms (auditor: Parallel Seq Scan at 50k, 25 ms). The test form passes 'no Seq Scan' through 'Index Scan using idx_ci_org' with 9,790 rows removed by the filter, so the assertion holds without any attribute index.
findings.user_impact: Attribute filters cost linear time in the org size, and the 'indexed attribute' promise is void for the app role. A regression that drops identity or attribute indexes would also not be caught by TestCIQueryBudget.
findings.cause: Plan difference reproduced. jsonb_object_field_text (->>) and jsonb_contains (@>) are not leakproof, so the qual cannot become an index qual below the RLS barrier (same class as SR-04 and the hostname_lc fix in migration 000134). planUsesSeqScan accepts any non-Seq-Scan node.
findings.recommendation: Use a stored column or side table for searchable attributes, or a vetted leakproof wrapper. Rewrite the EXPLAIN tests to run the repository-emitted SQL (captured via a pgx tracer) and assert specific index names plus rows read, as TestIdentityHitsMatchSingle does. Add idx_attr_* to SR-04.
findings.retest: Integration test: searchable attribute definition, DDL job, 10k CIs plus a second 10k org. Capture ci.PGRepository.List SQL with filter[attributes.asset_tag]=X, EXPLAIN it as the app role and assert 'Index Scan using idx_attr_<id>'. Negative: drop the index in a tx and the test fails.

findings.title: NFR-02 'Suche' budget measured on CI-list name filter, not global search; global search not load-testable on the seed
findings.repro: tests/load/api.js:74-77 calls GET /cis?search=srv-NNNNN → `name ILIKE '%…%'` (ci/pg_repository.go:207-210). The frontend global search calls /api/v1/search (client.ts:1381-1384), which reads search_document. The seed writes no CI search documents (verifier probe).
findings.expected: The search budget (< 500 ms at 10k objects) is measured on the search users run, against an indexed corpus of 10k CIs
findings.actual: The global search path is never load-tested, and its corpus is empty for seeded CIs
findings.user_impact: NFR-02 compliance of global search is unproven. SR-04 states the FTS expression index is unusable under RLS, so the risk is real.
findings.cause: Harness design, and the seed bypasses the indexer
findings.recommendation: Reindex in load.yml after the seed and add a global_search scenario with p95<500 ms. Keep the list search as a separate budget.
findings.retest: api.js global_search scenario meets p95<500 ms on 10k indexed CIs in repeated runs on the reference host.

wps.title: Reconciliation über 10.000 CIs hinaus (seitenweise Identitätssuche)
wps.user_goal: Discovery reconciliation finds the matching existing CI however large the inventory is (no 10,000 cap), through an index-based, paged identity search.
wps.implementation: backend/internal/discovery/pg_repository.go:801 identityPage=1000. :803-850 IdentityCandidates: keyset paging, uncapped. :852-870 DiscoveryEdge. :903-946 identityFilter: OR of serial/uuid/primary_mac/`attributes @> ANY($n::jsonb[])` (one term per MAC)/management_ip/hostname_lc/fqdn_lc. identity.go:99-105 incomingMACs includes primary, fingerprint and every interface MAC. identity.go:727-768 single path. discovery.go:1266-1273: per-record single path when !prefetched or frame.locking. discovery.go:1120-1123: with locks a record re-reads its candidates. lanes.go:114-116: locking = canLock && (lanes>1 || fromQueue), i.e. production with NATS. topology.go:325: Limit 10000 fallback only for repos without DiscoveryEdge. reconciliation.go exists.
wps.tests: results-backend.tsv: pass internal/discovery TestReconciliationBeyondTenThousandCIs 9.26 s: 10,500 CIs; newest serial found; 2,345 shared hostnames with equal created_at → 2,345 distinct; edge 1,200 via DiscoveryEdge; wrong rel_type not found. It asserts no index use. pass TestIdentityOverWholeInventory 8.75 s (HTTP ingest, 10,050 CIs). pass TestIdentityHitsMatchSingle 11.23 s: batch path; EXPLAIN asserts index names per branch except fingerprint_mac, which is only logged (identity_batch_integration_test.go:155-162).

criteria.criterion: Identity search index-based/paged without upper bound
criteria.evidence: Paging without a cap is proven at >10k (three passing tests). Index-based is proven for the batch path, except fingerprint MACs. The single path is not index-based for any record carrying MACs. Verifier probe (work/verify-B26/probe.txt, 10k CIs, reticora_app): P4 serial OR ip → BitmapOr idx_ci_serial+idx_ci_mgmt_ip, 0.129 ms. P6 serial OR primary_mac OR ip → BitmapOr including idx_ci_primary_mac, 0.156 ms. P5 adds `attributes @> ANY(…)` → Seq Scan, 10,119 rows removed, 6.282 ms. In production (NATS queue → locking) every known device re-reads candidates through this single path, and every SNMP record with interfaces carries MACs.

criteria.criterion: Test with > 10,000 CIs
criteria.evidence: TestReconciliationBeyondTenThousandCIs (10,500) and TestIdentityOverWholeInventory (10,050, handler→DB) pass in the baseline.

layers.ux: N/A: backend only.
layers.api: OK: the HTTP ingest handler reconciles against a CI beyond the first 10,000 (TestIdentityOverWholeInventory).
layers.data: OK: keyset paging with id tie-break, no duplicate candidates. GAP: a MAC-bearing predicate reads the whole org under RLS.
layers.e2e: GAP: no test of the queue/locking path re-discovering a known device with MACs beyond 10k. The load test ingests only new devices without MACs.
layers.robustness: OK: empty identity returns nil; wrong rel_type negative case; deleted-candidate cap of 1,000 by design (CI-13). GAP: index use of DiscoveryEdge and of the single path is not asserted.

wps.soll_ist: Soll: index-based, paged identity search without a cap, proven with >10k CIs. Ist: the cap is gone and paging is correct at repository and handler level with >10k CIs. Index use holds for every identity kind except MACs. Because interface MACs are identity values, practically every real SNMP record makes the single-path query an org-wide Seq Scan under RLS. On the production queue path that query runs for every known device, in addition to the per-batch fingerprint scan. Docs (lasttest-g1.md open item 8, SR-04) describe this only as 'once per batch'.
wps.evidence: Verifier probe.txt lines: '== P4 … Bitmap Index Scan on idx_ci_serial … idx_ci_mgmt_ip … Execution Time: 0.129 ms'; '== P5 … Seq Scan on ci … Rows Removed by Filter: 10119 … Execution Time: 6.282 ms'; '== P6 … Bitmap Index Scan on idx_ci_primary_mac … 0.156 ms'. Code: discovery.go:1266 `frame.prefetched[i] && !frame.locking`; lanes.go:115; discovery.go:1120-1123 ('with them … a record reads its candidates again under its own'). Auditor probe identity-explain.txt: 4.675 ms at 10k.
wps.deviation: Not index-based for MAC-bearing records: an org Seq Scan per known record on the production queue/lanes path, plus one per batch for fingerprint MACs. Correctness unaffected; cost is linear in org size. Docs understate the scope as 'per batch'.
wps.dependencies: WP-086 (identity), WP-203; SR-04 follow-up (fingerprint-MAC side table); WP-333/334 (batch/lanes paths); WP-206 (NFR-03 representativeness).

findings.title: Identity search with MACs is an org-wide Seq Scan under RLS; on the queue path it runs per known record, not only per batch
findings.repro: Seed 10,000 CIs (cmd/seed -objects 10000). As reticora_app with app.org_id set, EXPLAIN ANALYZE the identityFilter shape (pg_repository.go:924-946) for a record with serial+MAC+IP: `… AND (serial_number=$s OR primary_mac = ANY($m::macaddr[]) OR attributes @> ANY($j::jsonb[]) OR management_ip=$ip) ORDER BY created_at,id LIMIT 1000` (work/verify-B26/probe.sql P5). Control: drop only the attributes term (P6).
findings.expected: Index-based lookup (BitmapOr of identity indexes), as without MACs (criterion 'indexbasiert')
findings.actual: Seq Scan on ci, 10,119 rows removed, 6.28 ms at 10k (linear; auditor 25 ms-class at 50k for the same plan type). Without the attributes term: BitmapOr including idx_ci_primary_mac, 0.16 ms. So the single leaky term breaks the whole OR.
findings.user_impact: In production with NATS (locking), every re-discovered known device whose record carries interface MACs costs an org-wide scan. At 200 rec/s and 10k objects that is about 1.2 CPU-s/s of DB time, rising about 5x at the 50k headroom. NFR-03 headroom risk; correctness unaffected.
findings.cause: Plan reproduced and isolated to the `attributes @> ANY` term: jsonb_contains is not leakproof, so the OR cannot be promoted to index quals below the RLS barrier. The path selection is confirmed by code: locking → single path for non-created records (discovery.go:1266, :1120-1123; lanes.go:115), and incomingMACs includes interface MACs (identity.go:99-105). findings.title: Site-Scope-Bypass im Rack-Kanal: fremde Racks lesbar und löschbar
findings.repro: Scratch-Probe TestVerifyB27RackSiteScope (SP/work/verify-B27/tree/backend/internal/tenant/rls/zz_verify_b27_rack_test.go) mit dem Router aus newChannelEnv und audit_db_21. Ablauf: Org-Admin legt per POST /api/v1/racks ein Rack in einem Raum von site1 an. Der Principal mit Scope Sites=only(site2), Clients=all ruft auf: GET /racks (enthält das Rack), GET /racks/{id} (200), GET /racks/{id}/layout (200), POST /bff/graphql { rackLayout(rackId) } (200 mit Name) und DELETE /racks/{id} (204, Zeile gelöscht, location-Eintrag bleibt).
findings.expected: 404 auf allen Pfaden für Objekte außerhalb des Site-Scopes, so wie bei Rooms, Buildings und beim Client-Scope.
findings.actual: Site-fremde Racks sind sichtbar, und leere Racks lassen sich löschen; dabei bleibt ein verwaister location-Eintrag zurück.
findings.user_impact: Ein auf eine Site beschränkter Nutzer (role_assignment.scope_site_id) sieht die Rack-Infrastruktur aller Sites seiner Organisation und kann fremde leere Racks löschen. Das ist ein Bruch der Scope-Isolation, der nach docs/audit/README.md:14 als Critical gilt. Die Organisationsgrenze bleibt gewahrt; deshalb P1 statt P0.
findings.cause: rack/pg_repository.go:58 rackVisible = EXISTS(room LEFT JOIN building … AND (building.site_id IS NULL OR EXISTS(site …))). Die Policy building_isolation filtert nach app.site_scope; die fremde building-Zeile wird unsichtbar, der LEFT JOIN liefert NULL, und die NULL-Klausel macht das Rack sichtbar. rack selbst hat nur eine Org-Policy. ListRacks, GetRack, DeleteRack und requireVisible verwenden dasselbe Prädikat.
findings.recommendation: INNER JOIN auf building verwenden (oder 'room.building_id IS NULL OR EXISTS(building … site …)'), die Fremdlöschung samt location-Sync korrigieren. Dasselbe Muster in desk/pg_repository.go:62 beheben (Spätphase). Test ergänzen (siehe Test-Gaps).
findings.retest: Die Probe oder der neue Matrixtest ergibt: Site-Principal erhält auf GET, Layout, GraphQL und DELETE des site1-Racks 404, die Zeile bleibt erhalten.

wps.upgrade_conditions: Rack-Site-Scope-Defekt behoben, und ein Repo-Test (Matrix oder Rack-Scope) belegt 404 für Liste, Detail, Layout, GraphQL und DELETE unter Site-Scope sowie die Konsistenz des location-Eintrags. Die Matrix ist um Locations unterhalb von Sites, die org-weiten Schreibpfade mit Positivkontrollen, alle GraphQL-Felder und exakte Negativstatuscodes erweitert (500 behoben) und läuft gegen PostgreSQL grün. Die TST-02-Zuordnung zeigt auf TestCollectorPKI.
wps.verifier_note: Alle zitierten Tests geprüft: in results-backend.tsv pass, Testkörper gelesen (:118-465). Die Lücken des Auditors sind bestätigt. Status von TEILWEISE auf FEHLGESCHLAGEN, Priorität von P2 auf P1. Grund: Die eigene Probe gegen audit_db_21 zeigt eine reale Verletzung genau des von TEN-09 genannten Pfads (Cross-Site, Locations). Ein Site-Principal liest Racks fremder Sites und löscht sie per DELETE mit 204, dabei verwaist der location-Eintrag. Ursache verifiziert im Code (rack/pg_repository.go:58 LEFT JOIN plus building-RLS) und in der Kontrollgruppe (Client-Scope 404, Rooms und Buildings korrekt gefiltert). Die Aussage des Auditors 'Ein Sicherheitsdefekt wurde nicht gefunden' ist damit widerlegt. Die Schreib-Probe des Auditors habe ich mit Positivkontrollen nachgestellt (404 ist echte Isolation, kein defekter Pfad). Neu sind außerdem 500 bei Topologie und Fremdkante (deckt sich mit Real-Stack T14/T15) und die SQL-Text-Preisgabe im Team-Pfad. Der Befund zum Matrix-Umfang steigt von P3 auf P2, weil er einen realen Defekt verdeckt hat.

findings.title: SR-11 als 'Low' eingestuft, obwohl CI-13-Reaktivierung in Produktionsverdrahtung 501 liefert
findings.repro: Probe TestVerifyB27SR11 (SP/work/verify-B27/tree/backend/internal/tenant/rls/zz_verify_b27_sr11_test.go), audit_db_21. Router über server.NewRouter in zwei Varianten: (a) repos.CI nackt (PG), (b) wie main.go:327 und :355 (search.NewCIIndexer, dann ai.NewCIChunkIndexer). Ablauf: CI per POST anlegen, DELETE, review_item resurrected_device mit Kandidat anlegen, POST /api/v1/review-items/{id}/resolve {action:merge, ci_id}. Ergebnis (a): 200, deleted=false, review resolved, GET 200. Ergebnis (b): Restore-Schnittstelle fehlt, 501 'this repository cannot reactivate CIs', deleted=true, review open, GET 404.
findings.expected: Reaktivieren aus CI-13 [B] funktioniert, oder das Review führt den Defekt nach dem eigenen Schema als High und damit gate-blockierend.
findings.actual: review-g1.md:145 führt SR-11 als Low und offen; das Review ist freigegeben.

findings.title: Onboarding-Impact-Schritt prüft keine betroffenen CIs
findings.repro: onboarding.spec.ts:292-297: Für impact = apiGet('/impact/{id}') wird nur expect(Array.isArray(impact.impacted)).toBe(true) geprüft.

findings.user_impact: Ein defekter Impact würde die Abnahme (d) nicht scheitern lassen.
findings.cause: Die simulierte Flotte erzeugt keine garantierten Beziehungen.

findings.retest: onboarding.spec.ts real grün mit der verschärften Assertion.

findings.title: Gate-Checkliste führt CI-13 [B] als PASS trotz bestätigtem Defekt SR-11 (Reaktivieren → 501)
findings.repro: g1-gate.md:333 '| CI-13 | [B] | PASS | resurrect_test.go |'. Probe TestVerifyB27SR11 (SP/work/verify-B27/tree/backend/internal/tenant/rls/zz_verify_b27_sr11_test.go) gegen audit_db_21, kompletter Router. Variante bare-pg: POST /api/v1/review-items/{id}/resolve {action:merge} liefert 200, das CI ist reaktiviert. Variante main.go (Such- und KI-Decorator): 501 'this repository cannot reactivate CIs', CI gelöscht, Review open, GET /cis/{id} 404.
findings.expected: Nach GATE-02 stehen alle [B]-IDs auf PASS; eine ID mit bekanntem, reproduziertem Produktionsdefekt steht auf FAIL bzw. blockiert das Gate, oder der Defekt wird vorher behoben.
findings.actual: CI-13 steht auf PASS, und G1 gilt als bestanden.
findings.user_impact: G1 wird mit defekter [B]-Funktion freigegeben: Ein wiedergesehenes, gelöschtes Gerät lässt sich in der Produktion nicht reaktivieren (die UI bietet 'merge' an).
findings.cause: Der Status je ID wird aus Traceability-Zeilen abgeleitet, offene SR-Befunde werden nicht abgeglichen. resurrect_test.go:96-100 nutzt das Repository ohne die Decorator-Kette aus main.go.
findings.recommendation: SR-11 beheben (Restore und UniqueConflicts im Decorator durchreichen) und mit einem Test der main.go-Kette absichern. Bis dahin CI-13 auf FAIL setzen und das Gate-Ergebnis anpassen. rep01-Abgleich ergänzen: Offene SR- bzw. PT-Befunde mit ID-Bezug verbieten PASS.
findings.retest: Probe-Variante main.go liefert 200 und reaktiviertes CI; der rep01-Abgleich ist grün.

findings.title: Gate meldet 'kein offenes Critical' und 'Isolationstest vollständig' trotz reproduziertem Site-Scope-Bypass (Racks)
findings.repro: g1-gate.md:55 ('Es gibt kein offenes Critical') und GATE-03-Tabelle (TEN-09 vollständig). Probe TestVerifyB27RackSiteScope (rack-site-scope.log): Ein Principal mit Sites=only(site2) liest site1-Racks (Liste, Detail, Layout, GraphQL) und löscht eines (204).
findings.expected: Ein bekannter Scope-Isolationsdefekt (nach docs/audit/README.md:14 Critical) blockiert GATE-01 und GATE-03 oder wird vorher behoben.
findings.actual: Das Gate gilt als bestanden; der Defekt ist nirgends geführt.
findings.user_impact: Die Gate-Freigabe überdeckt eine Scope-Isolationslücke.
findings.cause: Die Kanalmatrix (WP-208) deckt den Pfad nicht ab; der Gate-Status vertraut ihr.
findings.recommendation: Den Defekt beheben (siehe WP-208), bis dahin im Gate als offenen Befund führen und GATE-03 'Isolationstest vollständig' nicht auf PASS setzen.
findings.retest: WP-208-Test für Racks unter Site-Scope grün; das Gate führt den Befund als behoben.

findings.title: PASS-Status ohne Test-/Traceability-Nachweis (Erklärungen, selbstreferenzielle Traceability, veralteter Installationsnachweis)
findings.repro: g1-gate.md:154-170 ('PASS (Erklärung des Auftraggebers)' für AUT-05, AUT-06, NET-04, NFR-08; dazu ABN-01 a/b und GATE-03). docs/traceability.csv: AUT-05, AUT-06, NET-04 und NFR-08 zeigen nur auf docs/acceptance/g1-gate.md. Scratch-Probe: TEN-09-Zeilen durch einen Verweis auf g1-gate.md ersetzt ergibt TestTraceabilityFile PASS 219/219 (trace-negative.log). g1-gate.md:30-31: 'Der CI-Lauf auf dem Release-Kandidaten steht aus'.
findings.expected: 'PASS-Nachweis per Test/Traceability' (Akzeptanzkriterium) und GLO-11 'mindestens eine Testart'. Nicht Belegtes steht auf offen bzw. als begründete Ausnahme außerhalb von PASS.
findings.actual: Die Gate-Checkliste meldet 'G1 bestanden'; die Blockade wird durch Verweise auf die Checkliste selbst erfüllt; 8 [B]/[Q]-IDs haben keine Testdatei.
findings.user_impact: Der Gate-Entscheid ist für Dritte nicht überprüfbar; fehlende Lieferungen (Pentest, v2-Texte, Subprozessoren) sind verdeckt.
findings.cause: Die Freigabe des Auftraggebers ist als PASS modelliert; Validate prüft nur die Existenz der Datei, nicht die Testart.
findings.recommendation: Eigenen Status 'ACCEPTED-BY-DECLARATION' bzw. 'offen' einführen. Für [B]/[Q] mindestens eine Testdatei verlangen und Verweise auf docs/acceptance/g1-gate.md als Nachweis verbieten, mit expliziter Ausnahmeliste.
findings.retest: TestTraceabilityFile mit neuer Regel meldet die heutigen 8 IDs; die Checkliste spiegelt den Status wider.

findings.title: rep01 GATE-01-Prüfung erkennt Formatvarianten, Anhangzeilen und offene High-Befunde nicht
findings.repro: Scratch-Kopie SP/work/verify-B27/rep01 (Symlinks plus kopiertes docs/security und Skript): An pentest-g1.md angehängt ergibt '| PT-01 | High | offen |' 47/0, '| PT-03 | **Critical** | offen |' 47/0, '| PT-04 | Kritisch | offen |' 47/0, '| PT-05 | critical | offen |' 47/0; nur '| PT-02 | Critical | offen |' ergibt 46/1 (rep01-negative.log). Ursache ist der Regex in rep01-structure.test.sh:60 (grep -E ohne -i, exaktes Wort, nur SR- und PT-IDs, Anhang nicht geprüft).
findings.expected: GATE-01 erkennt jede offene Critical-Zeile unabhängig von der Formatierung; GATE-03 (Pentest High/Critical) wird ebenfalls geprüft.
findings.actual: Die Prüfung ist textuell eng und lässt sich umgehen.
findings.user_impact: Eine nachgereichte Befundliste mit offenem High oder anders formatiertem Critical lässt das Gate nicht scheitern.
findings.cause: Strikter Regex ohne Normalisierung; GATE-03 ist nicht automatisiert.
findings.recommendation: Severity normalisieren (Fettdruck entfernen, Groß-/Kleinschreibung, Kritisch/Hoch), alle Befundtabellen inklusive Anhang prüfen, eigene GATE-03-Prüfung für High und Critical der PT-Zeilen ergänzen.
findings.retest: rep01 mit den fünf Probezeilen ergibt jeweils FAIL, ohne sie grün.

findings.title: KI-Chunk-Indexer (Add-on 'ai') ist in der G1-Voreinstellung aktiv
findings.repro: Probe TestVerifyB27AIChunkInG1 (zz_verify_b27_sr11_test.go): Router wie main.go (KI-Decorator unbedingt bei :355, Module erst ab :404 ausgewertet), kein Modul aktiv. findings.actual: Jede CI-Änderung schreibt in G1 lexikalische Chunks in ai_chunk; die KI-Routen sind nicht registriert.

tests.name: T01 A creates a site in the location tree UI; B can neither see, resolve, change nor reference it
tests.proves: Chain UI to API to DB to UI. A creates a site in the /locations form (client chosen in the Mandant select). The POST returns 201 and the site appears in the tree. GET as A shows organization_id = A and A's client. B gets 404 on GET, PATCH and DELETE /locations/{id} and on GET /sites/{id}. B's /locations, /locations/tree, ?search=, ?parent_id=, /sites and /search contain neither the name nor the id. B is refused (4xx) a CI with location_id = A's site and a building under A's site. B's /locations page does not show the site. Afterwards A sees it unchanged and with no foreign children, both via API and in the UI after a reload.

tests.name: T02 A adds a relationship on the CI detail page; B can neither see nor change it
tests.proves: A adds a depends_on edge through 'Beziehung hinzufügen' on /cmdb/{ci1}. The POST returns 201, the link appears and the edge is stored with A's organization_id. B gets 404 on PATCH and DELETE /relationships/{id}. B's /relationships, ?ci_id= and /cis/{A}/relationships are empty and never contain the id. Afterwards A's edge is unchanged (same verification_state) and still shown in the UI.

tests.name: T03 B's lists, search, topology, impact, export, audit and review inbox contain nothing of A
tests.proves: Positive controls first: as A, search finds ci1, the audit log holds ci1, the export contains ci1 and the review inbox holds A's override_conflict item. As B, /cis lists exactly B's own CI (total 1). 24 B endpoints return 200 and none contains any marker of A (org id, user id, e-mail, client, site, CI ids, names, serial, relationship id, review id, export or job id): /cis?q=, ?search=, /search (CI name, serial, site, client), /topology, /locations(+tree), /clients, /sites, /relationships, /audit, /audit-log, /review-items (+open), /discovery/review-items, /exports, /export/jobs, /jobs, /export/cis json/csv/datev, /impact/{B}. B's asynchronous export (POST /exports 202, then completed) is downloaded from the presigned URL and contains B's CI only.

tests.name: T04 B's GraphQL BFF reveals nothing of A
tests.proves: Positive control: A's ci(id) returns its name. B's ci(id: A's CI) returns null. B's cis returns totalCount 1 (B's own CI only). B's relationships(ciId:A), topology, topology(rootCiId:A), searchEverything(A's name), reviewInbox and jobs contain no marker of A.

tests.name: T05 B cannot read, change, delete, restore, retype or merge A's CI by id (session and API key)
tests.proves: 13 operations return 403 or 404 both with B's session token and with B's own API key (X-API-Key), never 2xx: detail, detail with include, provenance, PATCH, DELETE, restore of an active CI, restore and GET of A's soft-deleted CI, type change, merge in both directions, unmerge, GET of A's merged victim. Bulk set_status with A's id reports succeeded 0 and item code 404. A snapshot taken by A before and after is identical (status, name, version, updated_at, location, edges, site, children). A's deleted CI stays deleted, and A itself can still restore it (200), which proves B's restore did nothing.

tests.name: T06 B reads no sub-resource, neighbours, impact or blast radius of A's CI
tests.proves: For 12 endpoints, B gets either 403/404 or 200 with zero rows, and never any marker of A: /cis/{A}/relationships, changes, contacts, interfaces, fields, blast-radius, dependencies, /topology/cis/{A}/neighbors, /topology/cis/{A}/impact, /impact/{A}, /impact?ci_ids=A, and the mixed /impact?ci_ids=B,A (404, no partial answer).

tests.name: T07 B cannot attach A's location, client or parent CI to its own data
tests.proves: Eight write paths are refused with 400, 403, 404 or 422: B's POST /cis with location_id, client_id or parent_ci_id of A; PATCH of B's CI with each of these; POST /locations as a building under A's site; a site of A's client. Afterwards B still has exactly one CI, with no location, client or parent, and no locations. A's snapshot is unchanged.

tests.name: T08 B cannot read or resolve A's review item, export job or job; the download URL cannot be bent to A's file
tests.proves: B gets 403 or 404 for GET /review-items/{A}, resolve with dismiss and with accept (on both /review-items and /discovery/review-items), GET /exports/{A}, /export/jobs/{A}, /jobs/{A} and POST /jobs/{A}/cancel. Afterwards A's review item is still open and A's export job is still readable. B's own presigned download URL rewritten to A's object key is refused by object storage (status >= 400, no A data beyond the key B sent).

tests.name: T09 organization headers and query parameters do not switch the tenant
tests.proves: The forged headers X-Organization-ID, X-Org-ID, X-Tenant-ID (A's org) and X-Client-ID (A's client) have no effect: /org returns B's organization, and GET/PATCH /cis/{A} return 404. 12 list endpoints with organization_id, org_id, client_id, site_id or filter[client_id] of A (/cis, /topology, /export/cis, /search, /audit-log, /locations?parent_id) return only B's rows or reject the parameter, and never an organization_id of A. A's CI is unchanged.

tests.name: T10 B's UI shows nothing of A: CI URL, CMDB list, command palette, locations, topology, audit, reviews
tests.proves: Direct navigation as B to /cmdb/{A's CI}: the API answers 404 and the page shows 'Das Configuration Item konnte nicht geladen werden' without any A data, while A sees the CI heading. B's /cmdb list shows B's own CI and no marker of A. In the Ctrl+K palette search, A finds 'name · ci' and B gets 0 options for the same query. On /locations, /topology, /audit and /reviews, A's page shows A's marker (site name, CI node, A's actor id, 'Konflikt mit Override'). B's page has loaded its own content (empty state, own node, own actor) and shows no marker of A anywhere in the page text.

tests.name: T11 B's relationship form rejects A's CI id and stores nothing
tests.proves: B enters A's CI id in 'CI-ID der Gegenstelle' on its own CI page. The POST fails (>= 400), the dialog stays open with an alert, and after cancelling the page still shows 'Keine Beziehungen vorhanden'. The API shows no edge for B and no edge involving B's CI in A's data.

tests.name: T12 A's audit trail records none of B's attempts and its hash chain is intact
tests.proves: After further PATCH and DELETE attempts by B, A's /audit-log has no entry with actor_id = B's user and no entry of another organization. POST /audit-log/verify returns intact true, and A's CI keeps its name.

tests.name: T13 B can neither read nor change A's contact and shared saved view
tests.proves: A creates a contact and a shared saved view (both 201 and readable by A). B gets 403 or 404 for GET, PATCH and DELETE of both. B's /contacts, /saved-views and /search?q=<contact> contain neither names nor ids. Afterwards A reads both unchanged.

tests.name: T14 B's relationship to A's CI is rejected with a client error and nothing is stored
tests.proves: Isolation part passes: POST /relationships by B with A's CI as target, as source, or both is never 2xx and nothing is persisted (B has no edges, A's snapshot is unchanged; DB: ci_relationship has 0 cross-org edges). Status part fails: the refusal is 500 Internal Error instead of a client error (404/422 per API-03).

tests.name: T15 the topology rooted at A's CI answers B with 'not found', like neighbours and impact
tests.proves: Neighbours of A's CI answer B with 404 and no A data. GET /topology?root_ci_id={A} answers 500 instead of 404. It leaks no data, and an unknown uuid also gives 500, so it reveals no existence.

tests.name: T16 A creates a CI through the CMDB form; it is stored in A's organization and invisible to B
tests.proves: The 'CI erstellen' form with name and type 'Server' sends POST /cis, which returns 400 'a field value has an invalid format or is out of range'. No CI can be created through the UI, so this UI to DB step fails before the isolation checks (A stores, B cannot see) are reached.

defects.title: POST /relationships with a CI of another organization (or any unknown CI id) answers 500 Internal Error instead of 404/422
defects.failing_test: frontend/e2e-real/tenant-isolation.spec.ts › T14 B's relationship to A's CI is rejected with a client error and nothing is stored
defects.repro: Sign up tenants A and B. As A, create CI a1. As B, create CI b1 and send POST /api/v1/relationships {source_ci_id:b1, target_ci_id:a1, rel_type:'depends_on', source:'manual'}. Also try a1->b1 and a1->a2. Each answers 500 {"detail":"the request could not be completed"}. The same 500 comes back for a random uuid such as 00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000ff.
defects.expected: The refusal is a client error naming the unknown reference (API-03 RFC 7807 table: 404 or 422 with violations on source_ci_id/target_ci_id), the way POST /cis with a foreign location_id or parent_ci_id answers 422 'location not found' / 'parent CI not found'.
defects.actual: 500 Internal Error. Nothing is stored, so there is no isolation breach. The UI relationship dialog shows the generic message 'the request could not be completed' instead of a field error on 'CI-ID der Gegenstelle', and every such attempt is logged as a server error.
defects.user_impact: There is no leak. A user who types a wrong or foreign CI id in the relationship dialog gets an internal-error message instead of being told the target does not exist. Monitoring counts these as 5xx errors.
defects.evidence: Final run T14: '0fbdbe30-…->fb1052c2-…: 500'. Probe: trace 61650391cf48ecb5afcbba3705af7fbd in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Reticora-CMDB/fbd8a132-b968-552a-84eb-515fd3e8f807/scratchpad/stack/server.log has status 500 on POST /api/v1/relationships; a random uuid also gives 500 (trace 4604ecd53ba267b7023e66d18d2112dd). Read-only DB probe: ci_relationship has no row for the attempted CIs, and cross-org edges (source or target CI in another org than the edge) count 0.
defects.cause: backend/internal/relationship/pg_repository.go:191-222: the INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE EXISTS(ci $2) AND EXISTS(ci $3) affects no row because RLS hides the foreign CI. The ErrNoRows is turned into fmt.Errorf("not found") (line 222), which is no sentinel or pg error. backend/internal/relationship/relationship.go:608 passes it to api.WriteRepoError, and backend/internal/api/dberrors.go:83-87 maps every unknown error to 500.
defects.verdict_reasoning: I tried to refute this and could not. (1) The test is not at fault. It asserts only that the refusal is any client error (400|403|404|422), and the isolation part of T14 passes. (2) Requirement: API-03 [B] says errors are RFC 7807 with a status table 'wie v2'. The v2 table is not in the repo (E-01, task A-02 still open), so the exact code is not fixed by the spec. A 500 for a request that refers to a missing CI is still wrong under any reading, and it contradicts the product's own conventions on the same stack: POST /cis with a foreign location_id or parent_ci_id answers 422 with violations, an interface of another CI in POST /relationships answers 422 (pg_repository_integration_test.go:200), and GET /topology/cis/{id}/neighbors answers 404. (3) Code path, confirmed: backend/internal/relationship/relationship.go:521-608 has no existence check before repo.Create. In pg_repository.go:191-222 the INSERT…SELECT…WHERE EXISTS(ci) matches no row (RLS hides the foreign CI), and ErrNoRows becomes fmt.Errorf("not found"), which is not a sentinel. api.WriteRepoError (dberrors.go:83-87) maps that to 500. (4) It is not tenant-specific: a random uuid in A's own org also gives 500. There is no data leak and nothing is stored, so P2, not P0. It does break validation feedback in a core UI form: the relationship dialog shows the English generic text 'the request could not be completed' instead of saying the target CI does not exist.

defects.title: GET /topology?root_ci_id=<CI of another organization or unknown id> answers 500 instead of 404
defects.failing_test: frontend/e2e-real/tenant-isolation.spec.ts › T15 the topology rooted at A's CI answers B with "not found", like neighbours and impact
defects.repro: As tenant B, send GET /api/v1/topology?root_ci_id=<CI id of tenant A>. It answers 500 {"detail":"the request could not be completed"}. A random uuid gives the same. GET /topology/cis/<id>/neighbors and /impact/<id> correctly answer 404 'ci not found'.
defects.expected: 404 Not Found (as for neighbours and impact), or a 422 field error on root_ci_id, per API-03.
defects.actual: 500 Internal Error, with no data leaked. The GraphQL topology(rootCiId) returns an error 'not found', which is acceptable.
defects.user_impact: There is no leak. A stale or foreign deep link to a topology root yields an internal error instead of 'not found', and these show up as 5xx in monitoring.
defects.evidence: Final run T15: 'GET /topology?root_ci_id={A} as B → 500'. Probe trace c4f40d7d470e01537199272f66a2c178 (foreign CI) and ab2fb9ba37dc3396362c388ffee2b29d (random uuid), both status 500 in server.log. As A with its own root the answer is 200 with nodes and edges.
defects.cause: backend/internal/ci/pg_repository.go:315 GetByID returns fmt.Errorf("not found") on ErrNoRows. backend/internal/topology/topology.go:274-276 (buildFromRootViaTraversal) passes it on, and topology.go:139 api.WriteRepoError maps it to 500. GetNeighbors (topology.go:155-158) checks GetByID first and writes 404 itself.
defects.verdict_reasoning: Not a test bug. In the same test, the neighbours endpoint for the same CI correctly answers B with 404, which shows the flow and tenant are right. Requirement basis: API-03 (RFC 7807 status table, v2 text missing), TEN-09/TEN-06 (a cross-org access answers 'not found' or 0 rows), and consistency with GET /topology/cis/{id}/neighbors and /impact/{id}, which answer 404 'ci not found'. Code path, confirmed: ci/pg_repository.go:313-315 GetByID returns fmt.Errorf("not found"). topology.go:274-276 (buildFromRootViaTraversal) passes it on, and GetTopology (topology.go:133-139) sends it through WriteFieldError/WriteRepoError, which gives 500. GetNeighbors (topology.go:155-158) checks GetByID itself and writes 404. There is no leak (unknown uuid also gives 500, so existence is not revealed), and GraphQL topology(rootCiId) returns the error 'not found'. User impact: the UI deep link /topology?root=<id> with a stale or foreign id gets 500. P3 is appropriate. One note: T15 accepts only 403/404. A 422 field error on root_ci_id would also be defensible under the unspecified API-03 table, but this does not change the verdict because the product answers 500.

defects.title: CI creation form ('CI erstellen') sends the type key 'server' as ci_type_id; every manual CI creation through the UI fails with 400
defects.failing_test: frontend/e2e-real/tenant-isolation.spec.ts › T16 A creates a CI through the CMDB form; it is stored in A's organization and invisible to B
defects.repro: Log in as a freshly signed-up org admin. Open /cmdb, click 'CI erstellen', enter Name 'x', choose CI-Typ 'Server', click 'Anlegen'. POST /api/v1/cis {ci_type_id:'server', ...} answers 400 'a field value has an invalid format or is out of range', and the dialog stays open with that message.
defects.expected: CI-03 (manual creation with name and type) and UI-04: the CI is created (201), appears in the list and is stored in the user's organization.
defects.actual: 400. No CI can be created through the UI form for any of the eight offered types, because the server expects the CI type UUID (for example cc9fc361-… for key 'server').
defects.user_impact: The central manual CMDB function, creating a CI in the UI, is blocked. Users can only create CIs through the API, import or discovery.
defects.evidence: Final run T16: 'POST /cis sent by the CMDB form: {"detail":"a field value has an invalid format or is out of range","status":400,...trace_id 069a8ad331e2d42627967b66d49ed3d7}'. The same request with the UUID of ci-type key 'server' (GET /ci-types) answers 201. Code: frontend/src/pages/CIFormModal.tsx:30 (const ciTypeValues = ['server','switch',...]) and :146 (ci_type_id: values.ci_type_id). The plan names this exact defect in WP-239 ('CI-Dialog mit acht festen Typen, sendet "server" als UUID-Typ-ID'), which is marked 'G1-Umfang: nein, verschoben (E-03)'.
defects.cause: The CI dialog has a hard-coded list of type keys and sends the key in place of the ci_type_id UUID. The fix is planned but deferred (WP-239, E-03).

defects.title: Audit page reads fields the API does not return (created_at/entity_type/entity_id vs timestamp/resource_type/resource_id): time shows 'Invalid Date', object column shows '—'
defects.failing_test: none in this spec (seen while writing T10; confirmed by API probe and code)
defects.repro: As any admin with audit entries, open /audit. The 'Zeitpunkt' column renders new Date(undefined), which shows as Invalid Date. The 'Objekt' column renders '—' for every entry.
defects.expected: The audit viewer (UI-01..UI-10 audit viewer, AUD-05) shows the time and the object (type/id) of each entry.
defects.actual: GET /api/v1/audit-log entries carry timestamp, resource_type and resource_id. A probe shows created_at null, entity_type null, entity_id null.
defects.user_impact: The audit viewer does not show when an action happened or which object it concerned, so the audit UI is of little use for review.
defects.evidence: API probe (tenant A): {action:'ci.created', resource_type:'ci', resource_id:'0662c09d-…', entity_type:null, entity_id:null, created_at:null, timestamp:'2026-10-15T07:43:19.899245Z'}. frontend/src/pages/AuditPage.tsx:113 (new Date(entry.created_at)) and :118 (entry.entity_type ? ... : '—'). frontend/src/api/client.ts:2085-2101 (AuditEntry interface with entity_type/entity_id/created_at).
defects.cause: Contract drift between the frontend AuditEntry type and the backend audit-log JSON field names.
defects.verdict_reasoning: This had no failing test in the reported run. I reproduced it with an independent probe and added T17 to the spec, which encodes the requirement and now fails. Contract drift, confirmed: api/openapi.yaml components.schemas.AuditEntry and backend/internal/audit/audit.go:31-49 serialize timestamp/resource_type/resource_id. The hand-written frontend type (frontend/src/api/client.ts AuditEntry: entity_type, entity_id, created_at) and AuditPage.tsx:113/118 read fields that never arrive. AuditPage.test.tsx:21-23 passes only because its fixture uses the frontend's wrong field names. Requirement: AUD-07 [B] (every change stores who, when and what; the data is stored correctly) and the audit viewer of UI-01..UI-10 [B]. The detailed UI contracts are N/P (v2 text missing, E-02), but the page defines its own columns 'Zeitpunkt' and 'Objekt' and fills them with 'Invalid Date' and '—' for every entry. I re-rated from P3 to P2: the only UI view of the audit trail cannot show when an action happened or which object it concerned. That is a relevant functional limitation, not a cosmetic one. Audit data integrity is not affected; the API and hash chain are intact (T12 passes).

e2e.uncovered:
1. Cross-client, cross-site and team scopes inside one organization (TEN-05, WP-009, WP-065) are not covered. Self-signup tenants have a single org-wide admin, and client- or site-scoped principals need role assignments; this spec only covers cross-organization isolation.
2. Channels of TEN-09/WP-208 not exercised: webhook delivery, notifications, collector ingest (WP-208 ingest→webhook), monitoring metrics (/cis/{id}/metrics answers 403 'feature monitoring not in plan' for trial orgs), assets, documents, tickets, IPAM, rackLayout via GraphQL. A had no data there, so a negative check would have proved nothing.
3. Ambiguity on status codes: for detail, update, delete, restore, type change and merge on A's id I demand 403/404 strictly. For sub-collection reads of a foreign CI (relationships, changes, contacts, interfaces, fields) I accept 200 with zero rows, following TEN-06 ('eine falsche Org liefert 0 Zeilen'), although the task text said 'never 200'. Bulk set_status answers 200 with a per-item 404 and succeeded 0; I accepted that as the API-08 partial-failure format.
4. DB-level evidence comes from manual read-only psql probes (0 cross-org edges, CI locations, location parents and CI parents; the UI-created site belongs to org A), not from inside the spec, which has no DB access.
5. A's own location search hit (SRC-01 for locations, WP-186) is not asserted; for the UI-created site only B's negative search is.
6. Because the CI form is broken (T16 / WP-239), A's CI fixtures are created through the REST API the UI uses. Clients have no UI form and are also created via API. The UI paths covered are the location tree (T01), the relationship dialog (T02, T11), CI detail and list, command palette, topology, audit and review pages (T10).
7. Harness note: the server allows 5 signups per client IP per hour (E-33), and all real-stack specs share 127.0.0.1. Each tenant of this spec sends its own X-Real-IP (198.18.x.y). The server trusts that header only from trusted proxies, and the vite preview proxy passes it through. The production nginx overwrites X-Real-IP with $remote_addr (deploy/docker-compose/nginx-tls.conf.template:68), so this is not a product finding.
8. Playwright restarts the worker after each failed test and beforeAll builds a new tenant pair. For that reason the tests are ordered with the expected failures last, and every write attempt is followed by an 'A unchanged' check in the same test.
