All 6 failures are confirmed product defects. None are selector or flow bugs.
prettier --write and eslint on both files: clean.

tests.name: 01 admin invites a viewer; the invitee accepts and signs in with exactly the viewer rights
tests.proves: In a fresh self-signup tenant, POST /invitations returns 201 with a one-time token, status pending, scope org, role viewer and an expiry of 7 days (±5 min). GET /invitations does not repeat the token, and the DB keeps only a 64-character SHA-256 hash. Public POST /invitations/accept returns 201 and creates the Keycloak account. Exactly one app_user is created, with exactly one role_assignment (viewer), and the invitation becomes accepted. The invitee signs in through the Keycloak UI (PKCE), and /me returns the same user and org. /me/permissions contains ci:read, location:read and topology:read and none of the 22 RBA-02 write or admin keys, and no credential:* key.

tests.name: 02 an invitation is accepted only once: a second acceptance is refused and creates nothing
tests.proves: Accepting the same token again returns 404, as the contract says. Two parallel acceptances of one token give exactly one 201 and one 404. Exactly one user and one assignment exist per address.

tests.name: 03 revoked invitations and the old token of a renewed invitation are refused; conflicts are reported
tests.proves: Revoke returns 204, the invitation leaves the list and its token returns 404 with no user created. Renew returns 200 with a new token; the old token returns 404 and the new one 201. An accepted invitation cannot be revoked or renewed (409). A second pending invitation for the same address returns 409. A role id from outside the organization returns 422 and a malformed e-mail 400. An org_admin invitation to an existing user's address returns 409 on accept, and the existing viewer does not become org_admin.

tests.name: 04 an expired invitation is refused with 410 and can be renewed for seven more days
tests.proves: Once expired, the invitation is listed as expired, accept returns 410 and no user is created. Renew returns 200 with status pending and 7 more days, and the new token is accepted (201). To expire it, a psql fixture moves expires_at of exactly this test's own invitation row into the past, because no API can produce an expired invitation.

tests.name: 05 an invitation sends the invitee an e-mail (NTF-05 event "Einladung")
tests.proves: After an enabled central_smtp e-mail channel was created and an invitation issued, no mail reached Mailpit within 60 s. This is product defect D1.

tests.name: 06 the viewer reads CIs, but every write, delete and administrative call is refused with 403
tests.proves: The viewer gets GET /cis, /cis/{id} and /org with 200. Each of these returns 403: create, edit, delete and bulk on CIs; create user, deactivate or delete the admin; create, edit or delete roles; list, issue, renew or revoke invitations; list or create API keys; create or delete webhooks; PATCH /org settings; create team; create notification channel; audit log. Checked afterwards as the admin: the CI is unchanged (name and version), and none of the attempted objects exists or changed. The org settings and the admin's active status are untouched.

tests.name: 07 the viewer cannot raise its own rights through role, user, invitation or key endpoints
tests.proves: These self-escalation calls all return 403: POST /role-assignments with self as org_admin, POST /roles/assign, PATCH /users/{self} with a role, PUT /roles/{viewer}/permissions adding user:manage, PATCH /roles/{viewer}, an org_admin invitation for a second own address, and an API key with admin scopes. PUT and POST /users/{self}/roles return 4xx. Afterwards the DB still holds only the viewer role and the viewer role has no new permissions. A cookie refresh still issues viewer-only rights.

tests.name: 08 viewer UI: CIs are visible; creating or editing a CI is not offered or ends in a visible error
tests.proves: The viewer sees the admin's CI in the /cmdb list. In the 'CI erstellen' dialog, 'Anlegen' gets POST /cis 403; the dialog stays open with a non-empty role=alert. On the detail page, 'Bearbeiten' then 'Speichern' gets PATCH 403 with an alert. Through the admin API, no CI was created and the CI was not renamed.

tests.name: 09 viewer UI: user, role and invitation management is not offered; refused pages say so
tests.proves: On /users (tabs Benutzer, Teams, Rollen) there are no invite, create, assign, delete, deactivate or remove controls. /audit shows an explicit error alert naming the missing permission instead of an empty log.

tests.name: 09b the roles tab presents the four RBA-02 roles as system roles, not as custom roles
tests.proves: org_admin, engineer, viewer and client_technician are all labelled 'Custom' in the Roles tab. This is product defect D6.

tests.name: 09c viewer UI: saving a webhook is refused visibly, not silently
tests.proves: POST /webhooks from the form returns 403, which is correct, but the page shows no alert, toast or error text. This is product defect D5.

tests.name: 10 a Keycloak account of the organization without invitation is refused (403); with an invitation it is admitted
tests.proves: A Keycloak user was created through admin REST with organization_id set to the tenant and no invitation. Its UI login gets POST /auth/callback 403, and the callback page shows the invitation-required error. There is no session, /cmdb redirects to /login and no app_user is created. After the admin issues an invitation to that address, the first login is admitted with exactly the viewer role and the invitation is marked accepted.

tests.name: 10b a Keycloak account without organization attribute is refused and gets no session
tests.proves: A Keycloak user without organization_id gets callback 401/403, no session and no app_user.

tests.name: 11 an admin role change (viewer → engineer) takes effect at the next refresh and sign-in
tests.proves: POST /cis returns 403 before the change. The admin's POST /role-assignments (engineer) returns 201. A cookie refresh with a JSON request issues a token that can POST /cis (201). After a new sign-in, /me/permissions has ci:write, ci:delete and collector:manage but not user:manage. In the UI, 'Bearbeiten' then 'Speichern' renames the CI; the change shows after reload and in the DB.

tests.name: 12 after the upgrade the user creates a CI through the UI form (UI → API → DB → UI)
tests.proves: The engineer's form submit sends ci_type_id 'server' and gets 400, so no CI is created. This is product defect D4.

tests.name: 13 an admin can revoke the role again and the user loses the rights at the next sign-in
tests.proves: DELETE /role-assignments/{id} returns 404 because the route does not exist, and the engineer assignment remains. This is product defect D3.

tests.name: 14 the SPA renews an expired access token with the refresh cookie instead of signing the user out
tests.proves: The stored access token was invalidated and the page reloaded. The SPA's own POST /auth/refresh, sent without a Content-Type, gets 400 'Content-Type must be application/json', so the session is dropped. This is product defect D2.

defects.title: D1 Invitations send no e-mail: the NTF-05 event 'Einladung' (invitation.created) is never emitted
defects.failing_test: roles-authz.spec.ts › 05 an invitation sends the invitee an e-mail (NTF-05 event "Einladung")
defects.repro: 1) As the org_admin of a fresh tenant, POST /api/v1/notification-channels {name, kind:'email', provider:'central_smtp', config:{}, enabled:true} (201). 2) POST /api/v1/invitations {email:'x@audit-e2e.de', role_id:<viewer role id>} (201, token in the response). 3) Search Mailpit (http://localhost:8025/api/v1/search?query=to:"x@audit-e2e.de") for 60 s.
defects.expected: NTF-05 [B] lists 'Einladung' among the Phase-1 notification events, and WP-140 requires each of them to create a notification via outbox and notifier. The invitee should receive an e-mail with the invitation link and expiry (template in notify/subscriptions.go:82-92).
defects.actual: No mail arrives. The token exists only in the API response to the admin.
defects.user_impact: An invited person is never told about the invitation. Inviting users only works if the admin passes the raw token on by hand. The SPA has no invitation UI at all, neither for issuing nor for accepting, so for end users the TLC-03 invitation process cannot be used without the API.
defects.evidence: Read-only psql on the final-run tenant 4de6d9ed-8c56-47d3-bb45-5447723b321e: user_invitation has 9 rows (6 accepted); event_outbox has only ci.created ×2 and ci.changed ×1, no invitation.created; notification_delivery has 0 rows; notification_channel has central_smtp enabled=t. Same picture for the run-1 tenant 1ae96afe-…: 8 invitations, outbox only ci.created. grep in backend: events.InvitationCreated is referenced only in events/envelope.go:62,72, notify/subscriptions.go:82 and webhook/webhook.go:136, so nothing produces it. user/invitation.go IssueInvitation (l.203-232) inserts the row and an audit entry but appends no outbox event. grep in frontend/src finds no invitation page or route (only api/generated/schema.d.ts).
defects.cause: PGInvitations.IssueInvitation (and RenewInvitation) never append an events.InvitationCreated envelope to event_outbox, so the subscription in notify/subscriptions.go is dead code.
defects.verdict_reasoning: The requirement holds. NTF-05 [B] (07-api-suche-jobs-lebenszyklus.md:80) lists 'Einladung' among the Phase-1 notification events, and the WP-140 acceptance criterion says each of the eight events produces a notification via outbox and notifier. The product's own subscription (notify/subscriptions.go:82-92) addresses the invitee's e-mail directly. I tried to refute the defect three ways. (1) The channel is present: central_smtp is enabled for the tenant. (2) The mail path works: Mailpit received 93 signup mails, and the notifier delivered other events (notification_delivery has 'export' rows with status sent). (3) Timing is not the cause: the test waits 60 s, and the event never enters the outbox at all. The cause is in the code. PGInvitations.IssueInvitation (user/invitation.go:203-232) and RenewInvitation insert the row plus an audit entry but append no event. events.InvitationCreated is referenced only in events/envelope.go:62,72, notify/subscriptions.go:82 and webhook/webhook.go:136. The baseline test notify/events_integration_test.go:85 injects the event by hand, so it passes without any producer. The test flow is correct. P1 stays: the invitation process (TLC-03) only works if the admin hands the raw API token over by hand, and the SPA has no invitation UI.

defects.title: D2 SPA session refresh always fails: POST /auth/refresh without Content-Type is rejected with 400 by the OpenAPI validator
defects.failing_test: roles-authz.spec.ts › 14 the SPA renews an expired access token with the refresh cookie instead of signing the user out
defects.repro: Sign in through the UI. In the browser console run fetch('/api/v1/auth/refresh',{method:'POST',credentials:'same-origin'}), which is exactly what frontend/src/auth/session.ts:22-25 sends. Alternatively let the access token expire (15 min) or make it invalid and reload a page.
defects.expected: AUT-02 and WP-066 ('Frontend nutzt Cookie-Refresh') require the rotating HttpOnly cookie to renew the session: 200 with a new token, the user stays signed in, and role changes apply at the refresh.
defects.actual: The response is 400 {"detail":"Content-Type must be application/json","title":"Validation Error"}. refreshSession() returns false, clearSession() runs and the user is sent to /login. The identical request with 'Content-Type: application/json' and body {} returns 200 with a new token.
defects.user_impact: Every user is signed out at the latest when the 15-minute access token expires; the first API call after that drops the session. Role changes never reach an open SPA session through refresh.
defects.evidence: Probe on the real stack (scratchpad probe-authz/refresh.probe.ts): 'SPA_FETCH 400 {"detail":"Content-Type must be application/json","instance":"/api/v1/auth/refresh",...}' versus 'REFRESH_JSON 200 {"expires_at":...,"token":...}'. Test 14 assertion message: 'SPA refresh (Content-Type: none) → {"detail":"Content-Type must be application/json",...}'.
defects.cause: backend/internal/middleware/openapi.go:93-100 requires an application/json Content-Type on every POST that has an OpenAPI entry, even when the operation has no requestBody (api/openapi.yaml:525 /auth/refresh has none). frontend/src/auth/session.ts:22 sends the refresh POST without body or Content-Type.

defects.title: D3 A role assignment cannot be removed: no DELETE /role-assignments/{id} and no other revoke path
defects.failing_test: roles-authz.spec.ts › 13 an admin can revoke the role again and the user loses the rights at the next sign-in
defects.repro: As the admin, POST /api/v1/role-assignments {user_id:<user>, role_id:<engineer id>} (201). GET /role-assignments?user_id=<user> to get the assignment id. Then DELETE /api/v1/role-assignments/<id>.
defects.expected: API-05 names role-assignments as a resource, RBA-03 defines role_assignment, and AUT-02 says role changes take effect at the next refresh. An administrator must be able to take a granted role away, and the user must lose its rights at the next sign-in.
defects.actual: 404 {"detail":"the requested resource does not exist"}. The assignment stays and the user keeps the engineer rights.
defects.user_impact: A role granted by mistake (even org_admin) cannot be withdrawn; the only option left is to deactivate the user. Least privilege cannot be restored.
defects.evidence: Final run: role_assignment rows for user 7f365077-65f6-4eef-85be-880faaeef5d2 after the DELETE attempt are viewer b6e2b0fa-… and engineer f6c017ad-… (read-only psql). backend/internal/user/handler.go:88-120 registers only GET and POST /api/v1/role-assignments, POST /roles/assign and GET /users/{id}/roles. UpdateUserRequest (user/model.go:97-101) has no roles field, and no DELETE FROM role_assignment exists in internal/ outside tests.
defects.cause: The revoke operation of the role-assignments resource is not implemented (router, repository and OpenAPI all lack it).
defects.verdict_reasoning: API-05 names 'role-assignments' as a REST resource, and WP-168 also lists role-assignments as a resource to align. RBA-03 defines role_assignment, and AUT-02 says 'Rollenänderungen wirken spätestens beim nächsten Refresh'. An assignments resource without revocation cannot implement role changes downwards. The catalog implies revocation rather than stating it literally, which is the only possible counter-argument; I still consider it required. To rule out the test using the wrong route, I probed every plausible alternative, and all fail. Routes (user/handler.go:88-120) and OpenAPI (/api/v1/role-assignments has only get and post) contain no delete. UpdateUserRequest (user/model.go:97-101) has no roles field. No production code deletes from role_assignment or user_custom_role. The only remaining option is to deactivate the user. P1 stays: a mistakenly granted role, including org_admin, cannot be withdrawn, so least privilege cannot be restored. Add WP-168 to the affected WPs.

defects.title: D4 Creating a CI through the UI form fails with 400: the form sends a CI type key ('server') where the API expects the CI type id
defects.failing_test: roles-authz.spec.ts › 12 after the upgrade the user creates a CI through the UI form (UI → API → DB → UI)
defects.repro: As an engineer or admin on /cmdb, click 'CI erstellen', enter a Name, choose CI-Typ 'Server', click 'Anlegen'.
defects.expected: CI-01: the CI is created (201), the dialog closes and the CI appears in the list.
defects.actual: POST /api/v1/cis with {"name":"engineer-ui-ci-…","ci_type_id":"server","status":"active","discovery_source":"manual"} returns 400 'a field value has an invalid format or is out of range'. The same API call with ci_type_id cc9fc361-89a1-4763-9dee-31cb25181177 (the id of type key 'server' from GET /ci-types) returns 201.
defects.user_impact: Users cannot create CIs manually in the UI on the real backend. The mocked e2e/ci.spec.ts hides this because its mock accepts any ci_type_id.
defects.evidence: Test 12 assertion message shows the request body and the 400 response. A curl probe as the admin gives 201 with the UUID and 400 with 'server'. frontend/src/pages/CIFormModal.tsx:30 hard-codes ciTypeValues = ['server','switch',…] and sends values.ci_type_id unchanged (l.150); the seeded CI types are UUID rows keyed by 'key'.
defects.cause: CIFormModal offers hard-coded type keys instead of the tenant's CI types (GET /ci-types id/key), so ci_type_id is not a UUID.
defects.verdict_reasoning: CI-01 requires manual creation, and the UI 'CI erstellen' dialog is the user path for it. The test selected option 'Server' and clicked 'Anlegen', which is the correct flow, and the request body is logged. frontend/src/pages/CIFormModal.tsx:30 hard-codes ciTypeValues ['server','switch',…] (8 keys) and sends values.ci_type_id unchanged (l.146). The tenant's CI types are UUID rows: 23 types, key 'server' = cc9fc361-…. The backend rejects the key. The same call with the type id succeeds, so permissions and the rest of the payload are fine. The mocked e2e suite hides the defect. P1 stays rather than P0, because the API and discovery still create CIs. It borders P0, since no user can create a CI manually in the UI on a real backend.

defects.title: D5 Webhook page: a refused save (403) gives no feedback, so the viewer gets a silent failure
defects.failing_test: roles-authz.spec.ts › 09c viewer UI: saving a webhook is refused visibly, not silently
defects.repro: Sign in as a viewer (an invited user with the viewer role), open /webhooks, fill Name, URL and Geheimnis, tick ci.created, click 'Speichern'.
defects.expected: Without webhook:manage the control should be absent or disabled, or the refusal should be shown explicitly. This is the audit charter's UI rule for permission boundaries; UI-01..10 refer to v2 texts, which are missing (E-01).
defects.actual: POST /api/v1/webhooks returns 403 (the API boundary holds), but the page shows no alert, toast or error text. The form keeps its values as if nothing happened.
defects.user_impact: Users without the right cannot tell why saving does nothing. The navigation also shows admin pages (Webhooks, Audit, Sicherheit, Benutzer) to viewers because it is filtered only by entitlements and modules, not by permissions.
defects.evidence: Error context of test 09c: after the 403 the snapshot shows the filled form and no alert or status. frontend/src/pages/WebhooksPage.tsx never renders createWebhook.error (grep finds no '.error' for mutations), and main.tsx's QueryClient has no global mutation error handler.
defects.cause: WebhooksPage ignores the mutation error state of useCreateWebhook, useDeleteWebhook and useTestWebhook.

defects.title: D6 The Roles tab labels the four built-in RBA-02 system roles as 'Custom'
defects.failing_test: roles-authz.spec.ts › 09b the roles tab presents the four RBA-02 roles as system roles, not as custom roles
defects.repro: Sign in (any role with role:read), open /users and the Rollen tab.
defects.expected: RBA-02 calls org_admin, engineer, viewer and client_technician 'Systemrollen', so the UI should label them System.
defects.actual: Each row reads e.g. 'org_admin | Organization administrator with full access | 103 | Custom'.
defects.user_impact: Administrators are misinformed about which roles are built in and cannot be changed or deleted.
defects.evidence: Error context of test 09b: four rows with the cell 'Custom'. GET /api/v1/roles returns is_builtin:true and is_system:false for these roles. backend/internal/user/pg_repository.go:594-596 selects 'false AS is_system' for rows of table role, and UserManagementPage.tsx RolesTab chooses the label from role.is_system.
defects.cause: The API reports system roles as is_builtin=true but is_system=false, and the UI looks only at is_system.
defects.verdict_reasoning: RBA-02 calls org_admin, engineer, viewer and client_technician 'Systemrollen'. The OpenAPI Role schema (api/openapi.yaml:18261-18267) itself says the seeded standard roles are is_builtin=true. The API returns is_system=false for them: user/pg_repository.go:594-596 selects 'false AS is_system' from table role. UserManagementPage.tsx:175-176 decides the label from is_system alone. The test's row selector matched the right rows, and every row ends in 'Custom', so the selector is not the cause. This is a display and labelling defect only, so P3 stays.

e2e.uncovered:
- No invitation UI and no invitation mail. The SPA has no page to issue, list, renew or revoke invitations and no page to accept them; the backend sends no invitation mail (D1). The invitation chain was therefore driven through the API: issue as admin, then public accept with the token from the response. Only the invitee's sign-in and the later checks went through the real UI. Whether UI-01..10 require such pages cannot be decided, because they point to v2 texts that are not in the repo (E-01); that part is UNKLAR.
- Role change through the UI. The user-management UI is read-only for everyone, so role changes and admin changes were done through the API as the admin.
- Ageing an invitation (test 04). No API can make an invitation expire, so the test writes to the DB: one UPDATE of expires_at on the test's own user_invitation row (helper ageInvitation, guarded by UUID checks). It is skipped if psql cannot reach the DB.
- Signup rate limit. The shared stack limits self-signup to 5 per client IP and hour, and every agent reaches it through the same local proxy. The spec's setup context therefore sends a per-run X-Real-IP from 198.51.x.x, the same mechanism as the production nginx (frontend/nginx.conf:87). Note: in this test stack, vite preview passes a client-supplied X-Real-IP through and the server trusts 127.0.0.0/8, so the IP limits can be bypassed here. This is a test-stack artifact; production nginx overwrites the header.
- Not tested:
  - AUT-10 pre-auth limit on invitation acceptance; the stack runs RPM=600 and the limiter is shared with other agents.
  - The 15-minute token lifetime itself; test 14 simulates expiry with an invalidated token.
  - Scoped invitations (client/site) and client_technician 'C' semantics, which need clients/sites.
  - Cross-tenant use of invitation tokens.
  - The extra first-login admission 'first user of an organization without users' (user/pg_repository.go:1050). It is not in the AUT-01 list (invitation, self-signup, SCIM) and needs an organization with zero users.
  - MFA for org_admin (AUT-09).
- Observations not asserted:
  - GET /roles/{id} returns 404 for built-in roles that GET /roles lists; the OpenAPI calls it 'custom role'.
  - The AUT-01 refusal is shown in the German UI as the English technical message 'identity: first login requires an invitation…'.
- Assertion choices:
  - Viewer UI tests accept 'control absent or disabled' or 'explicit error', per the task charter.
  - Self-escalation via the non-existent methods PUT/POST /users/{id}/roles is checked as 'any 4xx'.
  - All other mapped write routes must return exactly 403.

e2e.summary:
Running 10 tests using 1 worker. L01 ✓, L02 ✘, L03 ✓, L04 ✓, L05 ✘, L06 ✓, L07 ✓, L08 ✘, L09 ✓, L10 ✓.
  3 failed
    e2e-real/locations-racks.spec.ts:411:3 › L02 names are unique per parent level and the rack height is 1–60 (explicit 0 → 422)
    e2e-real/locations-racks.spec.ts:672:3 › L05 deleting a site, building or room with child locations through /sites, /buildings or /rooms is refused (409)
    e2e-real/locations-racks.spec.ts:862:3 › L08 moving a mounted CI is recorded in ci_change, audit and the unified history shown on the CI page
  7 passed (43.3s)
All 3 failures are product defects. Each was checked with an API response and a read-only DB probe. prettier --check and eslint on both files: clean.

tests.name: L01 the tree UI builds site → building → room → rack with derived client, site and path
tests.proves: The full chain UI → API → DB → UI. A site is created in the tree page with a client, then building, room and rack through '+ Unterpunkt'. Each dialog offers only the kinds the parent matrix allows (site: Gebäude/Lager, building: Raum, room: Rack), and a rack offers no child. Via the API, parent_id, client_id, site_id and the ltree path are derived correctly at every level. GET /locations/tree nests all four levels. In the DB, the location rows and the 1:1 specialist rows (site.client_id, building.site_id, room.building_id, rack.room_id) are correct. A rack created in the tree has the LOC-06 defaults (42 HE, 600 mm, 1000 mm). After a reload the nested tree is shown and the rack is offered on /racks.

tests.name: L02 names are unique per parent level and the rack height is 1–60 (explicit 0 → 422)
tests.proves: A duplicate site name in the same client, created through the tree dialog, gets 409. The dialog stays open with an error and only one row exists in the DB. The same name in another client is allowed. Duplicate building, room and rack names are refused, both through /locations and /racks, and the counts in the DB are unchanged. The same building name below another site is allowed. height_units 0, 61 and -1 get 422 naming height_units on POST, and 0 and 61 on PATCH. 60 is accepted and the default is 42/600/1000. A rack made via /racks is a tree node. POST /sites with a duplicate returns 409 with field=name. FAILS (soft assertion, line 434): the 409 from POST /locations, which the UI dialog uses, carries no field reference (WP-107 'Konflikte liefern 409 mit Feldbezug'). Every other assertion in the test passed.

tests.name: L03 a cycle or a parent-matrix violation is refused with 422 on parent_id and changes nothing
tests.proves: Each of these attempts gets 422 with violations=[parent_id]: PATCH building below its own room or rack (cycle), room below itself, site below its building, rack below a building. Same for POST room below a site, building without a parent, and rack below a rack. A site without a client gets 422 on client_id. Afterwards nothing has changed: parent/path/site are identical via the API, no location_change rows exist, no invalid node exists in the DB, and the tree UI is unchanged.

tests.name: L04 a non-empty location cannot be deleted in the tree UI (409), an empty leaf can
tests.proves: Clicking 'Löschen' on a site that has children gets 409 with dependencies containing 'location', and the UI shows the 'Löschen nicht möglich' alert. DELETE /locations of a room that holds a rack also gets 409. After a reload the subtree is intact in both the UI and the DB. An empty leaf building deleted through the UI gets 204: it is gone after reload, GET returns 404, the specialist row is gone, and the audit has a location.deleted entry.

tests.name: L05 deleting a site, building or room with child locations through /sites, /buildings or /rooms is refused (409)
tests.proves: Tests LOC-11 ('Locations mit … Kindern können nicht gelöscht werden (409 conflict)') on the specialist delete endpoints. Each endpoint gets its own hierarchy. FAILS: DELETE /rooms/{id}, /buildings/{id} and /sites/{id} all return 204 and silently delete the whole subtree (room+rack, building+room+rack, site+building+room+rack). The DB probe confirms the rows are gone.

tests.name: L06 a CI mounted at a U position shows in the rack layout and room plan after reload; location and scope are derived
tests.proves: PUT /racks/{id}/mounts/{ci_id} at U10, 2 HE, front returns 201. The layout lists the mount, front has 40 free units with U10–11 occupied, and rear has 42 free. The CI's location_id becomes the rack, with site_id and room_id derived (API and DB). The rack_mount row carries the CI's client_id and site_id. After a reload the racks page shows 'Position 10 · 2 HE · front' and the SVG label, and the rear face is empty. The room plan (/roomplan, building → room) lists the CI before and after a reload.

tests.name: L07 overlapping, face-colliding, out-of-range and composition-child mounts are refused
tests.proves: These mounts get 409: same unit, upper unit of a 2U mount, a 2U mount ending inside an existing one, 'both' over a front mount, U42 with 2 HE in a 42U rack, and U43. Position 0 or -1, height -1 and an unknown face are refused. Rear at the same U is accepted (face-aware). Once both faces are taken, 'both' and a move onto A get 409. A free 'both' slot is accepted. A composition child CI (parent_ci_id) cannot be mounted on its own. An unknown rack gets 404. The DB holds exactly the three accepted mounts and the layout shows them.

tests.name: L08 moving a mounted CI is recorded in ci_change, audit and the unified history shown on the CI page
tests.proves: Moving a mount from U10 to U20 returns 200, and the layout and DB show U20. ci_change has the mount (null → U10), the move (U10 → U20 with rack_id) and the location change (room → rack). The audit log has the mount and the move with before/after and actor_id. The unified history /history/ci/{id} has the move with site_id, plus audit entries. On the CI detail page the 'Historie' section, after reload, shows the entry with its time and site, and the racks page shows Position 20. Moving to rack 2 sets location_id to rack 2. Unmount returns 204, location_id goes back to the rack's room, and both ci_change and audit record the unmount. FAILS only on a soft API-contract assertion (line 969): GET /racks/{id}/layout of the now-empty first rack returns "mounts": null instead of [], although openapi.yaml RackLayout makes mounts a required array. Every functional assertion passed.

tests.name: L09 a rack with a mounted CI and its room cannot be deleted (409); empty again, the rack can
tests.proves: DELETE /racks/{id} with a mount gets 409 [rack_mount]. DELETE /locations/{rack} gets 409 [ci, rack_mount]. DELETE /rooms/{room} gets 409. In the tree UI, deleting the rack gets 409 with the alert, and after a reload the rack and the mount are still there. After unmount the CI sits in the room, so deleting the room still gets 409 [ci], while the empty rack is deleted (204) and its row is gone.

tests.name: L10 moving a room re-derives path and site of its subtree, CIs and mounts; location_change and audit record it
tests.proves: PATCH parent_id of a room to a building in another site returns 200 with the new path and site_id. The rack below follows (path and site). The specialist room.building_id is updated. The mounted CI keeps location_id with site_id re-derived, and rack_mount.site_id follows. location_change has exactly one row with old/new parent, old/new path, site and changed_by. The audit has a parent_id old/new entry. After a reload the tree shows the room under the new building only, and the room plan of the new building lists the mounted CI.

defects.title: DELETE /sites/{id}, /buildings/{id} and /rooms/{id} silently cascade-delete child locations instead of answering 409 (LOC-11)
defects.failing_test: e2e-real/locations-racks.spec.ts:672 L05 deleting a site, building or room with child locations through /sites, /buildings or /rooms is refused (409)
defects.repro: 1) Sign up a tenant and create a client. 2) Via POST /api/v1/locations, create site → building → room → rack with no CIs, assets or mounts. 3) DELETE /api/v1/rooms/{room_id} (likewise /buildings/{building_id} or /sites/{site_id} on a fresh hierarchy). 4) SELECT kind, name FROM location WHERE id IN (site, building, room, rack).
defects.expected: 409 Conflict with dependencies containing 'location'. The subtree stays untouched, as DELETE /api/v1/locations/{id} already does (L04 passes).
defects.actual: 204 No Content. The room is deleted together with its rack; the building together with its room and rack; the site together with its whole subtree. No 409 and no warning.
defects.user_impact: One API call removes a whole location hierarchy (buildings, rooms, racks with their specialist data such as floor plans and rack dimensions) without the deletion protection LOC-11 requires. The SPA tree uses /locations, which is protected, but API and integration clients using the documented /sites, /buildings and /rooms resources lose structure data silently. Subtrees that hold CIs, assets, mounts or role assignments are still refused, so CI data is not lost.
defects.evidence: Final run: 'DELETE /rooms/{id} with child locations: null – Expected: 409 Received: 204', and the same for /buildings and /sites; 'the subtree is untouched' fails in all three cases. Read-only DB probe after the run: SELECT kind||' '||name FROM location WHERE name LIKE 'L05 rooms %' OR … → only 'site L05 buildings Site 179206385747047', 'site L05 rooms Site …', 'building L05 rooms Building …' remain. No rack or room rows remain in the rack/room tables. Earlier run (stamp 1792052527052256): after DELETE /rooms only the site and building remain. The backend's own test encodes the cascade on purpose: backend/internal/locations/move_integration_test.go:202 'Without references the subtree goes: the room once its rack is empty' expects 204, so the baseline suite does not catch the deviation.
defects.cause: backend/internal/tenantapi/pg_repository.go:288-305 deleteLocation calls locations.CheckDeletable(ctx, tx, id, true) with subtree=true. In backend/internal/locations/dependencies.go:46-63 the dependencyQuery counts child locations only when NOT $2 ('location', NOT $2 AND EXISTS(children)), so children are never a dependency for the specialist endpoints, and the DELETE on the site/building/room table cascades to the subtree.
defects.verdict_reasoning: LOC-11 (katalog-v3/03-datenmodell-standorte-metamodell.md:58) says: 'Locations mit zugeordneten CIs, Assets, Mounts oder Kindern können nicht gelöscht werden (409 conflict)'. It makes no exception per endpoint. Sites, buildings and rooms are location rows (LOC-10, 1:1 specialist tables), so their own DELETE endpoints are bound by it. The test flow is correct: each endpoint gets a fresh hierarchy in the test's own tenant, with no CIs, assets or mounts, and the result is checked in the DB scoped by organization_id. I tried to refute it. The cascade is deliberate in the implementation: tenantapi/pg_repository.go:285-305 calls locations.CheckDeletable(..., subtree=true), and dependencies.go:46-50 counts children only when NOT $2. The OpenAPI deleteLocation description says 'Deleting a site, building, room or rack through its own endpoint checks the whole subtree', and move_integration_test.go:202 expects 204. But neither the catalog nor WP-055 has such an exception, and docs/plan/entscheidungen.md has no decision for it, so the behaviour deviates from the binding requirement text. A new finding makes it worse: only the target row's delete is audited (rooms.delete, buildings.delete, sites.delete). The cascaded child buildings, rooms and racks get no deletion audit entry. Priority stays P2, not higher: the SPA never calls these DELETE endpoints (frontend/src/api/client.ts has only GET/PATCH for them), and subtrees that hold CIs, assets, mounts or role assignments are still refused (control case: 409 [ci]), so no CI data is lost. Structural data (buildings, rooms, racks with their specialist columns) is removed without trace by one API call.

defects.title: POST /locations answers a duplicate name with a generic 409 without field reference (the tree dialog cannot point to 'Name')
defects.failing_test: e2e-real/locations-racks.spec.ts:411 L02 names are unique per parent level and the rack height is 1–60 (explicit 0 → 422) (soft assertion at line 434)
defects.repro: 1) In /locations click 'Standort anlegen' and create a site 'X' for client C. 2) Repeat with the same name and client. 3) Inspect the POST /api/v1/locations response. Compare with POST /api/v1/sites {client_id: C, name: 'X'}.
defects.expected: 409 naming the conflicting field (WP-107 acceptance criterion 'Konflikte liefern 409 mit Feldbezug'), e.g. field 'name' or violations[{field:'name'}], as POST /sites does.
defects.actual: POST /locations → 409 {"detail":"a record with the same unique value already exists","status":409,"title":"Conflict","type":"https://reticora.io/problems/409"} with no field. POST /sites → 409 with "field":"name" (that assertion passes).
defects.user_impact: The location tree dialog is the only UI that creates sites, buildings, rooms and racks. It maps API field violations onto inputs (LocationTreePage.tsx:67-69). Because no field is named, it shows the generic English problem detail as a general error instead of marking the Name field. The conflict is still refused and no duplicate is stored.
defects.evidence: run-final.log: 'Error: POST /locations: the 409 of a duplicate site names the field name … Received string: {"detail":"a record with the same unique value already exists","status":409,…}'. The same run's POST /sites soft check passed (409 with field=name). DB check in the same test: only one site row with that name.
defects.cause: backend/internal/locations/handler.go:146-163 writeError sends unique violations to the default branch api.WriteRepoError (line 161), which uses the sanitized generic 409 from backend/internal/api/dberrors.go:50-52. The tenantapi handlers map unique constraints to *ConflictError with a field through api.FieldDBError/WriteFieldError (backend/internal/api/fielderrors.go:37-61); the location tree endpoint has no such mapping.
defects.verdict_reasoning: The behaviour reproduces exactly. POST /locations with a duplicate site, or building, returns 409 {detail:'a record with the same unique value already exists', type:'https://reticora.io/problems/409'} with no field. POST /sites and POST /buildings return 409 with field:'name'. The cause is backend/internal/locations/handler.go:146-163: writeError has no case for unique violations, so they fall through to api.WriteRepoError. The test flow is correct. The UI part (dialog stays open, alert shown, one DB row) passes, and the assertion is soft. What I cannot settle is whether the requirement binds this endpoint. The only source for 'Konflikte liefern 409 mit Feldbezug' is WP-107, and the WP limits itself to tenantapi files ('Nicht Bestandteil: Änderungen außerhalb der genannten Dateien'). There the criterion is met: POST /sites returns field=name. /locations belongs to WP-026/WP-053/WP-108, and none of those has a field-reference criterion for uniqueness conflicts; WP-026 has one only for parent-matrix violations, which passes. API-03 only requires RFC 7807 with trace_id, which is met. On the other side, LOC-03 is in WP-107's scope, and the tree dialog is the only UI that creates a site. There the user sees the untranslated English generic text in the German UI and the Name field is not marked (aria-invalid null). So the user impact is real, but whether WP-107 requires it here is a matter of interpretation. The product owner should decide. If it is accepted as binding, it is P3.

defects.title: GET /racks/{id}/layout returns "mounts": null for an empty rack, contrary to the OpenAPI contract (required array)
defects.failing_test: e2e-real/locations-racks.spec.ts:862 L08 moving a mounted CI is recorded in ci_change, audit and the unified history shown on the CI page (soft contract assertion at line 969)
defects.repro: 1) Create a rack. 2) Mount a CI and move it to another rack (or leave the rack empty). 3) GET /api/v1/racks/{rack_id}/layout.
defects.expected: "mounts": [] (api/openapi.yaml:12252-12259 RackLayout: required [rack, mounts, free], mounts type array, not nullable).
defects.actual: "mounts": null, while free.front and free.rear correctly list all 42 units.
defects.user_impact: Small. The SPA guards with `?? []` (RackPage.tsx:57), but generated or strictly typed API clients that rely on the documented non-nullable array can crash or misreport an empty rack.
defects.evidence: Run 3 and the final run: 'Error: layout of an empty rack: mounts = null – Expected: true Received: false'. In the same test the semantic checks passed: no mount left, and 42 free units per face.
defects.cause: backend/internal/rack/handler.go:243-249 GetLayout passes the slice from repo.ListMounts directly into Layout{Mounts: mounts}. With no rows it is a nil slice, which encoding/json writes as null.
defects.verdict_reasoning: In api/openapi.yaml:12252-12259, RackLayout lists mounts as required, type array, not nullable. The generated client type (frontend/src/api/generated/schema.d.ts:6941) is 'mounts: RackMount[]', non-optional. WP-175 asks for the RCK-02 endpoints with their contract. The backend's own convention normalizes nil to []T{} (api.CompleteList, internal/api/api.go:101-105), so a null here is an oversight, not a design choice. Cause: backend/internal/rack/handler.go:243-249 passes the nil slice from repo.ListMounts straight into Layout{Mounts: mounts}. The test is not at fault: the semantic checks before it pass (lay.mounts ?? [] equals [], and 42 free units per face), and only the contract check fails. Impact is small: RackPage.tsx:57 guards with '?? []', so the SPA works, but strictly typed or generated clients get null where the contract promises an array. The same null-slice pattern also shows on GET /racks/{id}/mounts, which returns {"data":null,"total":0} for an empty rack. P3 is right.

e2e.uncovered: 1) The UI has no form to mount, reposition or unmount a CI. RackPage is read-only and the CI form has no rack or position fields. The tree page also has no way to move a node, so it cannot produce the cycle case. Mounting, moving and cycle attempts therefore go through the REST API the SPA uses (PUT/DELETE /racks/{id}/mounts/{ci_id}, PATCH /locations/{id}). The UI checks only the results: racks page, room plan, tree and CI history after reload. 2) The status code is ambiguous for some invalid inputs. RCK-01 and RCK-02 fix 409 only for collisions and height overflow (asserted strictly). For position_u < 1, height_u < 1 and an unknown face no status is specified, so 400/409/422 are all accepted. LOC-04..06 do not name a status for duplicate building/room/rack names, so 409 or 422 is accepted; WP-107 states 409 with a field reference only for org/client/site, which is asserted. 3) Not covered: WP-078's asset case (a mount sets asset.location_id when the CI has an asset; only a CI without an asset was tested); LOC-08 warehouse/zone/shelf/bin (P2 scope); the room plan showing the U position (it only lists the CI per room); the /audit UI page (audit checked via API GET /audit-log); and whether ci_change and audit are written atomically (both were observed, but a failing transaction was not provoked). 4) Tenant isolation of locations and racks across organizations is not repeated here; tenant-isolation.spec.ts covers it. 5) Since the backend integration test move_integration_test.go:202 deliberately expects 204 for DELETE /rooms of an empty subtree, the cascade on /sites, /buildings and /rooms looks like a design decision that contradicts the literal LOC-11 text. No decision in docs/plan/entscheidungen.md documents it, so it is reported as a defect and needs confirmation by the product owner.

e2e.summary:
Final full run, 2026-10-15 ~11:50 UTC. Log: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Reticora-CMDB/fbd8a132-b968-552a-84eb-515fd3e8f807/scratchpad/work/ci-lifecycle/final.log. Prettier reports the file unchanged and ESLint is clean.
  8 failed
    :362 L01 a CI created through the CMDB form is stored with all fields in the own organization and opens on its detail page
    :503 L03a a double click on the create button of the CMDB form creates exactly one CI
    :645 L05 clearing a field in the edit form removes the stored value (merge patch)
    :673 L05b PATCH is a JSON merge patch: null removes a typed field, absent members stay
    :746 L07 the audit viewer shows the CI change with time, actor, action and object; the chain verifies
    :987 L10b the CSV export button of the CMDB list downloads the CIs of the list
    :1180 L12b two sessions edit different fields of the same CI: no change is lost and the edits merge field by field
    :1298 L14 names and fields with quotes or backslashes are stored like any other text (API create, edit form)
  10 passed (2.4m)
Every failure is a product defect. Each one has a DB or API probe below. Earlier runs are in the same folder (run3.log and run4.log). In those runs L08 also failed on its UI-feedback checks (defect 7, intermittent).

tests.name: L01 a CI created through the CMDB form is stored with all fields in the own organization and opens on its detail page
tests.proves: Fills every field of the CMDB 'CI erstellen' form and submits it. Expects POST /cis 201, then reads the CI back from the API with every field, the own organization_id, manual source and version 1, and then checks the list link and the detail page values. The form's POST gets 400 instead (defect 1).

tests.name: L02 required-field and format errors are shown in the form and nothing is stored
tests.proves: An empty name or type is blocked by the browser's required check or the form's own message, and no POST is sent. A name of only blanks shows 'Name ist erforderlich.' with aria-invalid. The IPs 300.1.2.3 and 10.0.0.x get 422 problem+json with a trace_id and a management_ip violation, shown at the field with an accessible description. The API also refuses a missing name and an unknown type with 4xx, and nothing is stored.

tests.name: L03a a double click on the create button of the CMDB form creates exactly one CI
tests.proves: A double submit of the create form should create exactly one CI. This cannot be checked yet because the form cannot create any CI (defect 1).

tests.name: L03b repeated API submits with one Idempotency-Key create exactly one CI, also in parallel
tests.proves: Repeating a request with the same Idempotency-Key returns 201 with the same id and Idempotency-Replayed: true. The same key with a different body is refused with 4xx and creates nothing. Four parallel POSTs with one key create exactly one CI.

tests.name: L04 editing on the detail page sends If-Match, raises the version and survives a reload
tests.proves: GET returns ETag "1". The detail-page edit form sends If-Match "1" and gets 200 with ETag "2". The DB has the new values at version 2, the untouched firmware value is kept, and the values survive a reload. In provenance, every manually changed field is a protected override.

tests.name: L05 clearing a field in the edit form removes the stored value (merge patch)
tests.proves: The user empties Firmware-Version and saves; the save returns 200 and the dialog closes. After a reload the page still shows 9.9.9 and the DB still has it (defect 2).

tests.name: L05b PATCH is a JSON merge patch: null removes a typed field, absent members stay
tests.proves: PATCH {firmware_version:null} returns 200, but the value stays 1.2.3. Per RFC 7396, null should remove it (defect 3).

tests.name: L06 the edit appears in the CI history and the audit trail with the acting user, old and new value
tests.proves: A rename through the UI form shows up in /history/ci/{id} and /cis/{id}/changes with the actor, old and new value, and time. The history section of the detail page lists the change with a datetime. GET /audit-log has ci.created and ci.updated entries with the actor, actor_type user, the old and new name, and the request_id of the UI request, and the seq order is correct.

tests.name: L07 the audit viewer shows the CI change with time, actor, action and object; the chain verifies
tests.proves: On the /audit page, the action and actor columns are right and 'Kette jetzt verifizieren' reports 'Intakt'. But the time column shows 'Invalid Date' and the object column shows '—' for every row (defect 4).

tests.name: L08 a relationship created on the detail page shows as neighbour and in the impact view along its direction
tests.proves: A double click on 'Anlegen' in the relationship dialog creates exactly one depends_on edge; any repeat is answered 409, never 5xx. After a reload the relationship card and the neighbour list show the other CI. /impact/{db} contains app and /impact/{app} does not contain db. The UI blast radius on db shows 'Betroffene CIs: 1' and lists app. Its UI-feedback checks (dialog closes, no error shown) failed in run3 and run4 and passed in the final run (defect 7, intermittent).

tests.name: L09 the CI is found through the list filter, the full-text search and the command palette
tests.proves: The list search narrows the list to 1 entry and keeps the query in the URL (?q=) across a reload, and the status filter combines with it. /search returns the hit with entity_type ci, the title and url /cmdb/{id}, and no other CI. Ctrl+K, typing the name and picking the option opens the detail page. After a rename only the new name is found.

tests.name: L10 an export job started in the UI completes and its download contains the CI
tests.proves: 'Auftrag erstellen' on /export returns POST /exports 202. The job list follows the job until 'Abgeschlossen' and row_count equals the tenant's CI total. The download link returns a UTF-8 file with BOM, separated by semicolons, with one row per CI. It contains the CI, whose name includes ';' and an umlaut, with the correct id.

tests.name: L10b the CSV export button of the CMDB list downloads the CIs of the list
tests.proves: Clicking 'CSV exportieren' on /cmdb should download a CSV containing the CI. Instead the browser navigates to /api/v1/export/cis and gets 401 'missing bearer token' (defect 5).

tests.name: L11 delete decommissions the CI, hides it from traversal and search; restore brings it back with its relations
tests.proves: Delete and restore go through the API, because the UI has no delete action. DELETE returns 204 and the CI is decommissioned with deleted_at set. The history gets a delete change with status decommissioned and the actor. Impact skips the CI, search no longer finds it, the UI list hides it, and a second DELETE returns 404/410. Restore returns 200 with the earlier status (maintenance); the relationship is kept and impact and search include the CI again. The UI lists the restored CI with its status and relationship. A second restore returns 404/409 and an unknown id 404. History and audit record ci.deleted and ci.restored with the actor.

tests.name: L12 two sessions edit the same CI: the later save on a stale version is refused and nothing is lost
tests.proves: Two browser contexts edit the same CI. Session 2 saves the model first. Session 1 saves its model with If-Match "1" and gets 409, the editor stays open with an alert, and the DB keeps session 2's value at version 2. After a reload session 1 saves with If-Match "2" and gets 200.

tests.name: L12b two sessions edit different fields of the same CI: no change is lost and the edits merge field by field
tests.proves: Session 2 changes the model and session 1, on its stale editor, changes only the manufacturer. Nothing is lost: session 2's model is kept. But session 1's save gets 409 'fields changed since the If-Match version: model', so its manufacturer change is refused, which is not the field-by-field merge API-07 describes (defect 8).

tests.name: L13 ETag and If-Match: unknown versions 412, conflicting fields 409, other fields merge, the org setting enforces If-Match
tests.proves: ETag matches the version. A stale If-Match on a field that changed since gets 409 with fields, current_version and trace_id. A stale If-Match on an untouched field merges and the version becomes 3. If-Match "999" or "abc" gets 412 problem+json. With the org setting require_if_match, a PATCH without If-Match gets 412 and the UI edit, which sends If-Match, keeps working.

tests.name: L14 names and fields with quotes or backslashes are stored like any other text (API create, edit form)
tests.proves: Names with an apostrophe or a backslash are created. A name with a double quote gets 400, and a model with a double quote saved through the edit form gets 400; the editor stays open and the value is not stored (defect 6).

defects.title: The CMDB 'CI erstellen' form cannot create any CI: it sends the type key ('server') as ci_type_id instead of the type's UUID, and the server answers 400
defects.failing_test: L01, L03a (frontend/e2e-real/ci-lifecycle.spec.ts)
defects.repro: 1) Log in to a new tenant and open /cmdb. 2) Click 'CI erstellen', enter a name, choose CI-Typ 'Server' (and optionally Status and Hersteller), click 'Anlegen'. 3) The browser sends POST /api/v1/cis with {"ci_type_id":"server",...}.
defects.expected: 201 Created, the dialog closes, and the CI is stored (CI-01 create path, CI-03 manual creation with name and type).
defects.actual: 400 {"detail":"a field value has an invalid format or is out of range"}. The dialog stays open and nothing is stored, so no CI can be created through the UI at all.
defects.user_impact: Users cannot create any CI by hand in the UI. The only ways to get CIs are the API, discovery and import. It also makes the form's double-submit protection impossible to verify.
defects.evidence: final.log L01: 'POST /cis sent by the CMDB form: ... status 400 ... trace_id fe7a5e7df388a5213a74779b4dd8b525'. DB: select count(*) from ci where name like 'lc-form-%' or name like 'lc-double-%' returns 0. The same payload with the type UUID returns 201 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Reticora-CMDB/fbd8a132-b968-552a-84eb-515fd3e8f807/scratchpad/work/audit-B15/probe-ci-ui-payload.log).
defects.cause: frontend/src/pages/CIFormModal.tsx:30 builds the type options from the hard-coded keys ['server','switch',...], and line 146 sends values.ci_type_id (the key) unchanged. backend/internal/ci/pg_repository.go:456ff inserts ci_type_id into a uuid column without mapping the key, so PostgreSQL rejects it (22P02), which is mapped to 400.
defects.verdict_reasoning: CI-03 [B] requires manual creation with name and type, and CI-01 covers the create path. The test flow is correct: it fills the real form labels and selects 'Server'. The cause is in production code: CIFormModal.tsx:30 hard-codes the type options as keys ['server','switch',...], and line 146 sends values.ci_type_id unchanged. The backend stores ci_type_id in a uuid column and maps the PG error to 400. The Playwright trace shows the exact payload the form sent. The same payload with the type UUID returns 201, so the form, not the test, is at fault. No CI can be created by hand in the UI, which is an essential function; there are workarounds through the API, discovery and import, so P1 rather than P0. L03a (double click on the create form) fails only as a consequence of this defect and is not a separate finding.

defects.title: Values containing a double quote break CI create and update (400): the audit hash function casts the JSON text to bytea
defects.failing_test: L14 (frontend/e2e-real/ci-lifecycle.spec.ts)
defects.repro: POST /api/v1/cis {"name":"probe \"Rack 7\"","ci_type_id":"<uuid>"} returns 400. Or PATCH /api/v1/cis/{id} {"model":"R \"7\""}, or in the edit form set Modell to R740 "XL" and click 'Speichern'.
defects.expected: The text value is stored and shown (CI-03, MET-11: text is a valid data type). The audit chain (AUD-04) records any value it is given.
defects.actual: 400 'a field value has an invalid format or is out of range'. The edit dialog stays open and nothing is stored. Names with an apostrophe or a backslash do work.
defects.user_impact: A CI name or field that contains " (for example a rack label or a quoted model name) can be neither created nor edited, and the user gets a generic error. Every CI write path that audits the full item is affected; ingest of discovered values that contain quotes is likely affected too (not verified).
defects.evidence: final.log L14: create of lc-quote-1792065033325871 "Rack 7" got 400 (trace 720663dffd210e4bcf24794f9bf283ae); the edit-form PATCH got 400 (trace e05d12e9e3e7aeda785d9cec021b670c). DB: no CI named like 'lc-quote-%"%'; lc-quote-edit-1792064772560714 still has model 'Plain' at version 1. Probe with a direct curl: 'probe a;b', 'probe Müller', 'probe C:\temp' and "probe O'Brien" return 201; 'probe "Rack 7"' and a PATCH of model 'R "7"' return 400. pg_proc audit_entry_hash: '(... || '}')::bytea'.
defects.cause: backend/migrations/000118_audit_fields.up.sql:53 (function audit_entry_hash, called by the audit_log_chain trigger) concatenates the canonical JSON as text and casts it with ::bytea. In bytea escape input, the JSON escape \" is an invalid escape sequence (22P02), so the audit insert fails and rolls back the whole CI transaction (ci/pg_repository.go recordAudit). The fix is convert_to(text,'UTF8') instead of ::bytea. Note the chain-verification code must hash the same way.

defects.title: The audit viewer shows 'Invalid Date' as the time and '—' as the object of every entry: the UI reads fields the API does not return
defects.failing_test: L07 (frontend/e2e-real/ci-lifecycle.spec.ts)
defects.repro: Change a CI (PATCH), then open /audit (Audit-Protokoll).
defects.expected: Each row shows a readable time, the actor, the action and the object (ci/<id>) (UI-01..10 audit viewer, CI-06 audit, AUD-07 who, when, what).
defects.actual: For every row the time cell is 'Invalid Date' and the object cell is '—'. The action and actor (UUID) are correct, and the chain verification shows 'Intakt'.
defects.user_impact: An auditor cannot see when a change happened or which object it concerned. The viewer cannot be used to trace changes.
defects.evidence: final.log L07 soft failures: 'time of the audit entry' received 'Invalid Date'; 'object of the audit entry' received '—'. The run3 page snapshot shows every row with cell 'Invalid Date' and cell '—'. L06 (passing) shows that the API returns timestamp, resource_type and resource_id.
defects.cause: frontend/src/pages/AuditPage.tsx:113 renders entry.created_at and :118 renders entry.entity_type/entity_id, following the client type at frontend/src/api/client.ts:2085. The API schema AuditEntry (api/openapi.yaml:13162-13187) and the response use timestamp, resource_type and resource_id.
defects.verdict_reasoning: UI-01..UI-10 [B] explicitly include the audit viewer, and AUD-07 requires who, when and what. The test locates the first ci.updated row of its own tenant and checks the time cell and the object cell. The defect is not row-specific: every row shows 'Invalid Date' and '—'. AuditPage.tsx:113 renders entry.created_at and :118 renders entry.entity_type/entity_id, following the outdated client type in client.ts:2085. auditApi.list does no mapping. The API returns timestamp, resource_type and resource_id, as in openapi AuditEntry (required timestamp, resource_type). Action, actor and chain verification work. The viewer cannot be used to tell when a change happened or which object it concerned, so P2.

defects.title: The 'CSV exportieren' / 'JSON exportieren' buttons of the CMDB list are dead: plain links to a bearer-protected endpoint return 401
defects.failing_test: L10b (frontend/e2e-real/ci-lifecycle.spec.ts)
defects.repro: Log in, open /cmdb and click 'CSV exportieren'.
defects.expected: The browser downloads a UTF-8 CSV with BOM and semicolons containing the CIs (EXP-01).
defects.actual: The browser navigates to /api/v1/export/cis?format=csv and shows the JSON {"detail":"missing bearer token","status":401,...}. Nothing is downloaded.
defects.user_impact: Both export buttons in the CI list do nothing useful and show the user a raw error. Exporting only works on the separate /export page (L10 passes).
defects.evidence: final.log L10b: 'the export button answered 401: {"detail":"missing bearer token",...,"trace_id":"7b4186fd5ce83e52265fd3a2b35cab74"}'.
defects.cause: frontend/src/pages/CIListPage.tsx:119 (and the JSON link below it) renders <a href={ciApi.exportCIs('csv')}>. The session token lives in sessionStorage and is only sent as an Authorization header by fetchAPI (client.ts:249), so a plain navigation carries no credentials. The endpoint is also deprecated in favour of /exports.
defects.verdict_reasoning: CIListPage.tsx:119/122 render <a href={ciApi.exportCIs(...)}>, i.e. a navigation to /api/v1/export/cis. The tenant API authenticates only with an Authorization: Bearer header (middleware/auth.go:184-187). The SPA keeps the token in sessionStorage and adds it only in fetchAPI (client.ts:249), and there is no cookie auth, so the link can never succeed in any deployment. The test's click and its download/response detection are sound. The same URL with the bearer header returns 200 text/csv with a BOM, so the endpoint itself works. EXP-01 is fulfilled through /export (L10 passes), but a visible primary action in the CI list (UI-01..10 CI list) shows the user a raw JSON 401. A workaround exists, so P2 stays.

defects.title: Clearing an optional field in the CI edit form is silently not saved
defects.failing_test: L05 (frontend/e2e-real/ci-lifecycle.spec.ts)
defects.repro: Open the detail page of a CI with Firmware-Version 9.9.9, click 'Bearbeiten', empty Firmware-Version, click 'Speichern' (200, the dialog closes), then reload.
defects.expected: The field is empty in the UI and in the DB. A manual change is stored field by field (CI-04).
defects.actual: The UI and the DB still show 9.9.9, although the save reported success. The version was raised (1 to 2) but no ci_change row was written.
defects.user_impact: A user cannot remove a wrong value (manufacturer, serial, IP, firmware) through the UI and is not told that the change was dropped.
defects.evidence: final.log L05: 'the cleared value is gone after a reload' expected '—', received '9.9.9'; 'cleared in the database' received '9.9.9'. DB: lc-clear-179206465064283 has firmware_version 9.9.9 at version 2.
defects.cause: frontend/src/pages/CIFormModal.tsx:46-49: optionalValue('') returns undefined. The updatePayload (lines 156-163) therefore omits the emptied field from the PATCH, and the server treats an absent member as unchanged.
defects.verdict_reasoning: CI-04 says PATCH is field-granular, and WP-057's acceptance criterion is RFC 7396. A user who empties a field and gets a successful save must find it empty. The trace shows the form's PATCH body is {"name":...,"status":"active","manufacturer":"Vendor To Keep"}, so firmware_version is missing entirely, because optionalValue('') returns undefined (CIFormModal.tsx:46-49, 156-163). The server keeps absent members by design. The API itself would clear the field with "": the probe PATCH {firmware_version:""} sets it to NULL. So the UI is at fault, not the test. The save reports success but nothing is cleared (a no-op version bump), and the user cannot remove wrong values through the UI, so P2.

defects.title: PATCH /cis/{id} ignores null for typed fields (200, value unchanged), contrary to JSON Merge Patch
defects.failing_test: L05b (frontend/e2e-real/ci-lifecycle.spec.ts)
defects.repro: PATCH /api/v1/cis/{id} {"firmware_version":null} on a CI whose firmware_version is 1.2.3.
defects.expected: Per RFC 7396 (CI-04, 'JSON Merge Patch'), null removes the member, so firmware_version becomes empty.
defects.actual: 200, and firmware_version is still 1.2.3. No error is returned either.
defects.user_impact: API clients that follow the declared merge-patch semantics cannot clear typed fields. The no-op answers 200, which hides the problem.
defects.evidence: final.log L05b: 'null removes the value (RFC 7396)' received '1.2.3'. DB: lc-null-1792064678403848 has firmware_version 1.2.3 at version 1.
defects.cause: backend/internal/ci/model.go:120-141: UpdateRequest typed fields are *string with omitempty, so JSON null decodes to nil and is indistinguishable from an absent member. MergePatch (mergepatch.go) is only applied to attributes. Only an empty string clears a column.
defects.verdict_reasoning: WP-057's acceptance criterion literally says 'PATCH /cis/{id} wendet RFC-7396 rekursiv an (NULL löscht)', and CI-04 says 'JSON Merge Patch'. UpdateRequest (ci/model.go:120-141) uses *string with omitempty, so JSON null decodes to nil, which looks the same as an absent member. Only attributes go through MergePatch. The probe shows that attributes:{foo:null} is handled, but firmware_version:null is a silent no-op (200, version unchanged). The test is a plain API call and clearly correct. API clients that follow the declared contract cannot clear typed fields and get no error, so P2.

defects.title: Relationship dialog after a double click can stay open with a conflict error although the relationship was created (intermittent)
defects.failing_test: L08 UI-feedback soft assertions (failed in run3 and run4, passed in the final run)
defects.repro: On a CI detail page click '+ Beziehung hinzufügen', choose depends_on, enter the other CI id, then double-click 'Anlegen'.
defects.expected: One relationship is created, the dialog closes, and no error is shown.
defects.actual: The data is correct: exactly one edge is stored and the repeat gets 409. But in 2 of 3 runs the dialog stayed open with the alert 'a record with the same unique value already exists'.
defects.user_impact: The user is told the create failed when it succeeded, and may retry or give up. There is no data damage.
defects.evidence: run4.log and run3.log L08: 'the dialog closes after the successful create' received visible; 'no error shown for a successful create' received 1. The run3 page snapshot shows a dialog alert with 'a record with the same unique value already exists'. Exactly one edge per run in ci_relationship (DB query: 1 per lc-app-*).
defects.cause: frontend/src/components/cmdb/CIRelationshipsCard.tsx:199 calls createRelationship.mutate(data, {onSuccess: done}) for each submit and nothing blocks a second submit before the next render. With TanStack Query, per-call callbacks fire only for the latest mutate call, so when the later request is the 409, done() (which closes the dialog) never runs and the error is shown. This mechanism is inferred from the code and the library semantics; the behaviour is confirmed.

defects.title: Edit form sends every field, so a stale editor gets a 409 even when the user changed only a field nobody else changed
defects.failing_test: L12b (frontend/e2e-real/ci-lifecycle.spec.ts)
defects.repro: Open the same CI in two sessions. Session 2 changes Modell and saves. Session 1, on its open editor, changes only Hersteller and saves.
defects.expected: API-07 says PATCH is field-granular with 409 only for fields changed in between, so session 1's manufacturer is saved and session 2's model is kept.
defects.actual: Session 1 gets 409 'fields changed since the If-Match version: model' and its manufacturer change is refused. Session 2's model is kept, so nothing is lost.
defects.user_impact: Users get unnecessary conflicts and have to reload and redo their edit when someone else changed a different field. This is safe but annoying.
defects.evidence: final.log L12b: 409 {"fields":["model"],"current_version":2}. DB: lc-merge-1792064756494221 has model M-session2 and manufacturer Vendor-0. L13 shows that the API itself merges non-overlapping fields correctly.
defects.cause: frontend/src/pages/CIFormModal.tsx:156-163 builds the PATCH from all form values (including unchanged, stale ones) instead of only the changed fields. backend checkPrecondition (ci/pg_repository.go:1562-1597) then sees 'model' in the request. This is open to interpretation, because API-07 is worded for the API.

e2e.uncovered:
- **Delete and restore in the UI:** no page offers deleting or restoring a CI (useDeleteCI in frontend/src/api/hooks.ts:291 is never used). L11 therefore checks DELETE and restore through the REST API and only their effect in the UI. Whether UI-01..10 ('wie v2') requires a delete or undo action in the UI is UNKLAR, so this is not reported as a defect.
- **Double-submit protection of the create form:** cannot be judged while defect 1 blocks creation through the form (L03a). Double submit is proven for the API Idempotency-Key (L03b) and the relationship dialog (L08).
- **History section of the detail page:** it shows only the change type, field, time and source badge, not the actor or old/new values. The API history has them (L06 passes). Whether the UI must show the actor is not explicit in CI-06/AUD-07, so it is not asserted.
- **CI-05 hard delete:** hard delete after 90 days, interface/IP cleanup, and asset unlink/relink on delete/restore are time-based or need asset fixtures, so they are not covered.
- **Browser matrix:** WP-201 asks for specs in the WP-193 browser matrix. Only Chromium is available here (network policy), so Firefox/WebKit/Edge are untested.
- **L12b / defect 8:** whether the UI must deliver API-07's field-granular merge is a matter of interpretation; it is reported as P3.
- **Defect 6 scope:** only CI create and update were verified. That other audited writes containing a double quote, such as discovery ingest of a sysDescr with quotes, fail the same way is inferred from the function source, not tested. A relationship with quoted notes was created fine, because its audit entry does not carry the notes.
- **Observation, not asserted:** a PATCH from the edit form that changes nothing (L05) raised the CI version from 1 to 2 without writing a ci_change row. API-07 does not clearly forbid this.
- **Defect 7 is intermittent:** the relationship double-click feedback failed in run3 and run4 and passed in the final run.
- **Run note:** Playwright restarts the worker after a failed test, so beforeAll signs up a fresh tenant for the following tests. The tests do not depend on each other's data.
- **Earlier run1 failure:** it came from a test bug (GET /me returns sub, not id). That is fixed. A probe tenant 'Audit cilprobe ...' was created for the curl probes; its token and scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Reticora-CMDB/fbd8a132-b968-552a-84eb-515fd3e8f807/scratchpad/work/ci-lifecycle/probe/.
