tests.name: D01 a collector enrolled with a code from the Discovery UI reports the simulated fleet; the code is single-use
tests.proves: Code minted in /discovery 'Collector verbinden' wizard (UI). Real collector enrolls with it (exit 0) and only one collector is registered. A second enroll with the same code fails and creates no second collector. The collector has a cert fingerprint, its cert is valid for 90 days, and it becomes 'active' after heartbeats. Exactly 30 sim-* CIs are persisted (API) with the discovered model, manufacturer, serial, management IP and source (snmp/redfish). The UI collector card shows 'Aktiv' and the CI detail shows Modell, Hersteller and Quelle.

tests.name: D02 every typed field of a discovered CI has provenance with source, rank and time; the tooltip shows it
tests.proves: GET /cis/{id}/provenance has an entry with source, rank and time for every typed field that has a value. model, manufacturer, serial_number and management_ip have source snmp, rank 80, reason source_rank and diverged=false, with observed_at from this run (not in the future) and recorded_at set. In the CI detail, hovering 'Herkunft von model' shows 'Höchstrangige Quelle', Quelle snmp, Rang 80 and formatted 'Erfasst'/'Beobachtet' times.

tests.name: D03 a manual value set in the 'Override setzen' dialog is stored with author, time and reason and becomes the effective value
tests.proves: Negative: without a reason the dialog stays open and nothing is stored. With a reason, the provenance has source manual_override, rank 100, reason override, override_reason, override_author = signed-in user, protected=true, recorded_at within the action window, and discovered_value C9300-48P (snmp), so both values are kept. GET /cis/{id} and the list return the override as the effective value. After reload the UI shows it in the overview and in the Override and Effektiv columns, with the 'geschützt' badge and a tooltip with author, reason and the covered value. Overriding the structural ci_type_id returns 422. The audit entry ci.override_set names the acting user.

tests.name: D04 a new discovery run does not overwrite manual values; the deviation is kept and surfaced once per field
tests.proves: Two manual values: one set in the override dialog (sim-core-01.model) and one in the normal 'Bearbeiten' edit form (sim-access-01.manufacturer, PATCH, which creates an override). The collector is restarted and the CIs are seen again. Both manual values survive in the detail and in the list. The provenance keeps the observed value (discovered_value C9300-48P / Cisco, observed_at newer than the restart) with diverged=true. Exactly one override_conflict item exists per field, with observed_value. The UI shows the 'abweichend' badge with the Discovery and Effektiv values. The review inbox, filtered to 'Konflikt mit Override', shows the diff row (observed vs CI value with 'abweichend') and the actions Übernehmen/Verwerfen.

tests.name: D05 the review inbox accepts and dismisses override conflicts; the result persists and holds in the next discovery run
tests.proves: After a run creates 3 conflicts, 'Übernehmen' and 'Verwerfen' are clicked in /reviews. After reload the items are listed under Erledigt / Verworfen. The API shows resolved/accept and dismissed/dismiss, with resolved_by = user and resolved_at set. Accept removes the override and the CI takes the observed value (API and UI). Dismiss keeps the override. Negative: resolving a resolved item again and the disallowed action 'merge' are refused with 4xx and change nothing. In a further run, the accepted value stays with no new item, the dismissed value stays suppressed with no new open item and the override kept, and the still-open item is not duplicated (one item per field).

tests.name: D06 several override conflicts are accepted at once in the review inbox (bulk)
tests.proves: Two override_conflict items (sim-pdu-a/b model) are checked in the inbox list, then bulk action 'Übernehmen' and 'Ausführen' are used. The UI reports '2 erledigt, 0 fehlgeschlagen.' Both items are persisted as resolved/accept by the user, both CIs are back on the observed value AP8959EU3 with no override, and both are listed under 'Erledigt' after reload.

tests.name: D07 'Override aufheben' in the CI detail returns the field to the observed value
tests.proves: Clicking 'Override aufheben' sends DELETE (200). The API (detail and list) and the provenance return the observed value FortiGate-100F with reason not override. After reload the overview and provenance show it, and the audit entry ci.override_cleared names the acting user. FAILS: without a reload the CI overview ('Modell') keeps showing the cleared override value for 30 s while the provenance row already shows the observed value. See defect 1.

tests.name: D08 a disabled collector can no longer deliver: heartbeats and results are refused, nothing new is persisted
tests.proves: Positive control first: the enabled collector's restart updates last_seen_at of all 30 CIs and its heartbeat. PATCH /collectors/{id} {status: disabled} works, and the /discovery card shows 'Deaktiviert'. The disabled collector is restarted, and its log shows at least 3 refused spool deliveries. It gets no edge heartbeat, no credential bundle and no subnet report over NATS, and no delivered spool. Nothing new is persisted: max last_seen_at, last_heartbeat_at, the CI count and the review count stay unchanged, and the status stays disabled. Server log confirms 'collector refused at the NATS endpoint ... collector certificate revoked' and heartbeat 401.

defects.title: CI detail shows the cleared override as the effective value until reload ('Override aufheben' does not refresh the CI overview)
defects.failing_test: frontend/e2e-real/discovery-override.spec.ts › D07 "Override aufheben" in the CI detail returns the field to the observed value (soft assertion at line 1071)
defects.repro: 1) Self-signup tenant, enroll the simulated collector (30 CIs). 2) Set an override: PUT /api/v1/cis/{sim-fw-01}/fields/model/override {value:'Audit-FW-…', reason, protected:true}. 3) Open /cmdb/{id}: overview 'Modell' shows Audit-FW-…. 4) Expand 'Herkunft & Overrides' and click 'Override aufheben' in the model row. DELETE …/fields/model/override returns 200. 5) Without reloading, check the overview 'Modell'.
defects.expected: WP-060 / CI-10: one consistent effective view. After the clear, the page shows the current observed value (FortiGate-100F) everywhere, as the API already does.
defects.actual: For more than 30 s (63 polls), the overview 'Modell' keeps showing 'Audit-FW-1792065946469978'. The provenance row on the same page already shows Effektiv "FortiGate-100F" and the 'Override setzen' button. Only a page reload fixes the overview.
defects.user_impact: After removing a manual value, the page shows two contradicting effective values (stale override in the overview, observed value in the provenance section). A user may think the clear failed, repeat it, or act on the stale value until they reload.
defects.evidence: Final run: 'Expected: "FortiGate-100F" / Received: "Audit-FW-1792065946469978"' (final.log). The hard assertions in the same test pass: GET /cis/{id}.model == FortiGate-100F, the list matches, provenance reason != override, and after reload the overview shows FortiGate-100F. Read-only DB probe on tenant 'Audit discovr 1792065888547953': ci.model = FortiGate-100F, ci_field_value(model).override_at = NULL, audit actions 'ci.override_set,ci.override_cleared'. The backend is correct and the UI cache is stale.
defects.cause: frontend/src/api/cmdbHooks.ts:296-301: useClearOverride's onSuccess only invalidates queryKey ['ci-fields', ciId]. The overview reads useCI (queryKey ['ci', id], frontend/src/api/hooks.ts:78), which is not invalidated. useSetOverride (cmdbHooks.ts:289-292) invalidates both, which is why setting an override refreshes the overview and clearing one does not.
defects.verdict_reasoning: I tried to refute this and could not. (1) It is required. OVR-01 (katalog 05:80) says that after removal the observed value applies again. WP-060 is titled 'Effektive CI-Sicht konsistent; Override-Clear synchronisiert'. The overview 'Modell' renders ci.model from GET /cis/{id}, which per WP-060 is the effective value, so after the clear it must show the observed value. (2) The test is not the cause. The sequence is: override set via API, then page.goto, so the overview shows the override (asserted). Then the real 'Override aufheben' button is clicked, DELETE returns 200, and the test polls for 30 s. The selector is correct: the same locator shows FortiGate-100F after reload. A user who sets the override in the dialog hits the same path, because useSetOverride invalidates ['ci', id] and the overview shows the override. (3) Code: frontend/src/api/cmdbHooks.ts:296-301 useClearOverride onSuccess only invalidates ['ci-fields', ciId]. CIDetailPage.tsx:74/138 reads useCI(id) with queryKey ['ci', id] (hooks.ts:78), which is never invalidated. useSetOverride (cmdbHooks.ts:289-292) invalidates both keys. With the global staleTime of 30 s (main.tsx:12) and no refetchInterval, the overview stays stale until reload, remount or a window-focus refetch after 30 s. (4) No frontend unit test covers useClearOverride. Priority stays P3: the persisted data and the API are correct, the provenance section on the same page updates, and a reload or tab-switch fixes the view. The page does show two contradicting effective values right after the action.

defects.title: Collector logs 'collector NATS endpoint connected over mTLS' although the endpoint refused it (disabled collector / revoked certificate)
defects.failing_test: None. Observed in the D08 run in the collector log and not asserted, because the server-side refusal itself works (D08 passes).
defects.repro: 1) Enroll the simulated collector and run it. 2) PATCH /api/v1/collectors/{id} {status:'disabled'}. 3) Restart the collector (RETICORA_SIMULATE=true, RETICORA_CREDENTIALS_PATH=…). 4) Read the collector stdout.
defects.expected: DIS-08: error states are visible in the logs. A collector whose NATS authorization is refused (COL-04: disabled → certificate revoked, NATS account locked) logs a connection or authorization failure, not a successful connection.
defects.actual: The collector logs '11:55:30.543 INFO collector NATS endpoint connected over mTLS url=tls://localhost:4222'. At the same moment the server logs '11:55:30.541 WARN collector refused at the NATS endpoint error=collector certificate revoked'. About 5 s later the collector logs 'discovery scopes not updated: nats: connection closed'. Data is correctly not delivered.
defects.user_impact: An operator troubleshooting a disabled or revoked collector reads a success message in the collector log, which hides the real cause (authorization refused). There is no data or security impact; the server refuses correctly.
defects.evidence: Collector log of the run2 disabled start, quoted in session: 'collector NATS endpoint connected over mTLS' followed by 'nats: connection closed'. Server log /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Reticora-CMDB/fbd8a132-b968-552a-84eb-515fd3e8f807/scratchpad/stack/server.log lines 5863/5866 (run2) and 7832/7851 (final run): 'collector refused at the NATS endpoint … collector certificate revoked'. Lines 7831/7884: POST /api/v1/collectors/{id}/heartbeat status 401.
defects.cause: collector/collectorcmd/natsconn.go:83 sets nats.RetryOnFailedConnect(true), so nats.Connect (line 101) returns without error before the connection is established and authorized. Line 107 then logs success unconditionally instead of waiting for a connected or authorization-error event.
defects.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced twice. In the D08 standalone run and in the D08 part of the full run, the disabled collector logs INFO 'collector NATS endpoint connected over mTLS' about 2 ms after the server logged 'collector refused at the NATS endpoint ... collector certificate revoked'. About 5 s later the collector logs only generic 'nats: connection closed' warnings. It never logs the authorization cause. Root cause confirmed in the code: collector/collectorcmd/natsconn.go:83 sets nats.RetryOnFailedConnect(true). In nats.go v1.54.0 (nats.go:3002-3007), a failed initial connect, including an authorization error, sets status RECONNECTING, starts doReconnect and returns err=nil. natsconn.go:101-107 therefore logs success unconditionally. nats.go closes the connection after the second consecutive auth error, which explains the 'connection closed' 5 s later. Refutation attempt: no requirement prescribes this collector log line. DIS-08 [Q] ('Fehlerzustände in UI, Metriken und Logs sichtbar') is generic, and the server log does show the refusal with its cause. COL-04 (disabled → certificate revoked, NATS account locked, connections dropped) is functionally met: D08 passes. The defect is still real: the log states a false success and hides the cause on the collector side, which goes against DIS-08's intent for operator troubleshooting. No data or security impact, so P3. No test asserts it: the spec has a comment acknowledging the behaviour (D08). I did not add an assertion, because the requirement text does not prescribe collector log content.

e2e.uncovered:
Not covered or ambiguous:
(1) No UI control to disable or re-enable a collector. CollectorCard only shows the status, so D08 disables via PATCH /collectors/{id} and checks the badge in the UI. WP-143 only requires the UI to show the status, so this is not reported as a defect; whether the spec expects a UI control is UNKLAR.
(2) REC-12 'dismiss suppresses until the next change': suppression of the same value is verified (D05). Re-raising on a changed observed value is not: the simulator always reports fixed values and there is no user-accessible ingest path (collector ingest needs mTLS).
(3) Not producible with the simulator: REC-06 / WP-089 criterion 1 (conflicting_values for a lower-rank serial/uuid, unchanged incoming value) and WP-084 rejection of records more than 5 min in the future.
(4) Not covered: COL-05 / WP-143 offline after 5 min without heartbeat (runtime budget), COL-04 certificate renewal at 60 %, CA rollover with dual trust, the CN = collector-id content of the certificate (only fingerprint and 90-day validity checked), and env-based enrollment (RETICORA_ENROLL_TOKEN / RETICORA_CLOUD_URL). Enrollment used the CLI with --server http://localhost:8080 as in onboarding.spec.ts, not the frontend origin printed in the UI command.
(5) REC-08 'notification on creation (NTF-05)': the notification center showed 0 unread after items were created. NTF-04 allows hourly review digests, so this is not asserted (ambiguous within the test window). The >14-day escalation is not covered.
(6) Bulk resolution is tested for accept only. The override dialog always sends protected=true and string values, so unprotected or non-string overrides are not covered. Behaviour of an open override_conflict after the override is cleared manually is unspecified.
(7) Chromium only (WP-201 browser matrix not available here).
(8) Observed, not a requirement: last_seen_at is stored with whole-second precision; the tests account for it by starting each discovery run on a fresh second.
(9) The spec writes a per-run state file and collector work dir under os.tmpdir(), so a worker restarted after a failure reuses the tenant and collector. The last test removes the state file.

tests.name: B02 a bulk action with one item that became invalid reports that item and applies the others (no silent loss)

The report is total 3, succeeded 2, failed 1, and the deleted id has code 404 with an error text. The UI shows the toast '2 CIs aktualisiert, 1 fehlgeschlagen' and the list 'Fehlgeschlagene CIs' with exactly that item and its reason. tests.name: B03 bulk limits and validation: 0 and 501 ids, unknown status or action, duplicates, CIs of another tenant
tests.proves: 0 ids gives 400 (field ids). 501 ids give 422 (field ids) and change nothing. An unknown status gives 422 (field status) and an unknown action 422 (field action), both without change. PATCH /cis/not-a-uuid answers 400, but the bulk item is reported as {code:500, error:'the CI could not be updated'}. The valid id in the same request is applied correctly. FAILS: product defect.

tests.name: J01 100 ids run as a job that the job center follows to the end; the result reports every id and the change persists
tests.proves: Uses its own tenant (trial limit 100 CIs). The request has 98 CIs, 1 deleted CI and 1 unknown uuid, 100 ids in total. It answers 202 with kind ci.bulk and Location /api/v1/jobs/{id}. The Jobcenter page shows the ci.bulk row reaching 'Erfolgreich' with progressbar value 100. The status filter works ('Fehlgeschlagen' shows 'Keine Jobs'). The 'Ergebnis' dialog shows succeeded 98, failed 2 and 'CI not found'. GET /jobs/{id} shows succeeded, progress 100, created_by = user and start/finish times. The result has 100 items with both invalid ids at 404. /cmdb?status=inactive shows '98 Einträge' before and after a reload, the filter value persists, and all 98 stored CIs are inactive (DB probe agrees: 98 inactive, 98 status_change rows). defects.title: Webhooks page silently swallows the server's refusal (egress protection / validation errors): no error message, the form stays as it was
defects.failing_test: e2e-real/bulk-jobs-export.spec.ts:1021 W01 a webhook to a local catcher is refused by the egress protection, not stored, nothing delivered, and the UI explains the refusal
defects.repro: 1) Sign in as an org admin and open /webhooks. 2) Name 'x', URL 'http://127.0.0.1:35323/hook', Geheimnis '...', tick event ci.created, click 'Speichern'. 3) Observe the page.
defects.expected: The refusal is shown to the user with its reason, e.g. 'destination is not allowed: 127.0.0.1'. SEC-08 requires validating the URL when it is stored, and UI-01..10 includes a webhooks page with feedback.
defects.actual: POST /api/v1/webhooks answers 400 {"detail":"egress: destination is not allowed: 127.0.0.1"}, but the page shows nothing: no toast, no inline error, the form stays filled and 'Abonnements (0)' is unchanged. The user cannot tell why the subscription was not created. The same applies to every other create error (missing fields, invalid event, 403).
defects.user_impact: An admin who enters an internal or blocked URL, which is a common case, gets no feedback. The click looks like it did nothing. They cannot tell the security block from a bug and may retry or give up. The protection itself works.
defects.evidence: Screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Reticora-CMDB/fbd8a132-b968-552a-84eb-515fd3e8f807/scratchpad/work/bulk-jobs-export/out/bulk-jobs-export-Bulk-oper-c0afa-the-UI-explains-the-refusal/test-failed-1.png (form unchanged, 'Abonnements (0)', no message). The API answer was captured in the test: 400, detail 'egress: destination is not allowed: 127.0.0.1'. Read-only DB probe: select count(*) from webhook_subscription where url ~ '^https?://(127\.|10\.|192\.168\.|169\.254\.|\[)' returns 0, so the backend refusal itself is correct. Reproduced in 3 full runs (run1/run2/final.log).
defects.cause: frontend/src/pages/WebhooksPage.tsx: submit() calls createWebhook.mutate(form, { onSuccess }) without onError, and the component never renders createWebhook.error / isError. Only subscriptions.isError and deadLetters.isError are rendered (lines ~62-80). useCreateWebhook (frontend/src/api/hooks.ts:738) has no onError. fetchAPI (frontend/src/api/client.ts:416) only throws an ApiError, and the QueryClient in main.tsx has no global mutation error handler or toast. ExportPage, for comparison, renders createJob.isError.
defects.verdict_reasoning: Refutation attempts. (1) Timing: W01 originally checked for the message only about 5+ s after the POST answer, and the app's toast store defaults to durationMs 6000 (frontend/src/stores/toast.ts), so a short-lived toast could in theory have been missed. A separate probe outside the spec sampled the page every 100 ms for 8 s right after the click. It found nothing: no [role=alert], [role=status] or [aria-live] text and no new body text. The form keeps 'vp-…' and 'http://127.0.0.1:9/hook', and 'Abonnements (0)' is unchanged. (2) Code: frontend/src/pages/WebhooksPage.tsx:51-56 submit() calls createWebhook.mutate(form, { onSuccess }) with no onError. createWebhook.error/isError is never rendered; only subscriptions.isError and deadLetters.isError are (lines 62-82). useCreateWebhook (frontend/src/api/hooks.ts:738-744) has no onError. The QueryClient (frontend/src/main.tsx:9-16) has no MutationCache/onError handler. The toast store is used only by CIListPage, AssetListPage and useUndoableDelete. So no code path can show the error, which confirms the defect is in the product, not the test. (3) Wrong flow or selector: no. The POST is sent from the UI form and answers 400 'egress: destination is not allowed: 127.0.0.1', and the server-side protection works (not stored, the catcher gets 0 hits). Requirement basis, stated precisely: no catalog text says 'show the error'. The anchor is UI-01..UI-10 [B] (docs/spec/katalog-v3/08-frontend-monitoring-nfr-tests.md:14), which require 'Seiten für Discovery-Scopes/Webhooks/Export/Einstellungen' as 'wie v2' (the v2 text is missing, E-02 still open). WP-049 adds 'URL-Validierung auch beim Speichern'. The report's attribution to WP-191 (scope switcher) and WP-192 (keyboard handling) is weak, since neither WP's acceptance criteria cover form feedback. Still, a mandatory [B] webhooks page whose only create action gives no feedback on any server error (400 validation or egress, 403, 500) is not a working user process. The product's own ExportPage renders createJob.isError, so the expected pattern exists in the product. P2 (relevant validation/UX limitation; the security control itself works, no data loss) is kept.

defects.title: Bulk report gives a malformed CI id code 500 'the CI could not be updated' instead of the 400 the single change answers
defects.failing_test: e2e-real/bulk-jobs-export.spec.ts:582 B04 a malformed id in a bulk request is reported with the status the single change answers (400, not 500)
defects.repro: POST /api/v1/cis/bulk {"ids":["not-a-uuid","<valid ci id>"],"status":"inactive"} as an org admin. Compare with PATCH /api/v1/cis/not-a-uuid {"status":"inactive"}.
defects.expected: Per the OpenAPI bulkCIs description, every id is reported with the HTTP status the single change would answer. A malformed id is a client error, so it should get code 400 (as PATCH answers) or 404, with a matching message.
defects.actual: Item {"id":"not-a-uuid","result":"error","code":500,"error":"the CI could not be updated"}, while PATCH /cis/not-a-uuid answers 400 'a field value has an invalid format or is out of range'. The valid id in the same request is applied correctly, so this is not data loss.
defects.user_impact: API clients and the UI failure list ('Fehlgeschlagene CIs') present a caller input error as an internal server error, with a misleading message. Automated clients may retry or raise alarms for a non-retryable input error.
defects.evidence: Test output in final.log: 'per-id status of a malformed id: {"id":"not-a-uuid","result":"error","code":500,"error":"the CI could not be updated"}; Expected: 400, Received: 500'. Server log (SP/stack/server.log): PATCH /api/v1/cis/not-a-uuid status 400. Probe 2 confirmed the same.
defects.cause: backend/internal/ci/bulk.go bulkError() maps only err.Error()=='not found', *api.FieldError, *ValidationError and the precondition errors; every other error becomes 500 'the CI could not be updated'. The single PATCH handler goes through api.WriteRepoError → api.ClassifyDBError (backend/internal/api/dberrors.go:61-64), which maps PostgreSQL 22P02 invalid_text_representation (the uuid cast) to 400. bulkError does not use ClassifyDBError.
defects.verdict_reasoning: Contract basis: api/openapi.yaml bulkCIs (around line 975) says the report lists 'every id with ok or its error and the HTTP status the single change would have answered'. The product's own code comment says the same (backend/internal/ci/bulk.go:171-172, 'maps the error of one id onto the status and message the single operation would answer'). Catalog API-08 (07-api-suche-jobs-lebenszyklus.md:18) only requires 'Partial-Failure-Report mit Fehlern pro ID'. That part is met in a coarse sense, because the item is reported as an error, so the violation is of the WP-181 contract (openapi.yaml is a WP-181 file), not of the bare catalog text. Refutation attempts. (1) Is 400 the right reference? PATCH /cis/not-a-uuid answers 400 'a field value has an invalid format or is out of range'. GET /cis/not-a-uuid answers 404, but the bulk action is a status change (PATCH semantics), and either way the answer is a 4xx client error, never 500. The test compares against the live PATCH status rather than a hard-coded value, so it is not over-fitted. (2) A test artefact? No. A direct probe outside the spec reproduces it, and a well-formed unknown uuid in the same request correctly gets 404 'CI not found'. Only malformed ids fall through. Cause: bulkError() (bulk.go:173-192) maps 'not found', FieldError, ValidationError and the precondition errors, and everything else becomes 500. The pgx 22P02 invalid_text_representation from the uuid cast is not classified there, while the single PATCH path uses api.ClassifyDBError (backend/internal/api/dberrors.go:61-63, 22P02 → 400). Impact: there is no data loss (the valid id is applied) and an injection-like id has no side effect. However, the 'Fehlgeschlagene CIs' list and API clients present a caller input error as a server fault with a misleading message, and automated clients may retry it. P3 is kept.

e2e.uncovered:
1) Bulk from the UI is limited to the visible page. CIListPage keeps at most the 25 rows of the current page selected and drops the selection on page change, so a bulk job (≥ 100 ids, API-08/JOB-04) cannot be started from the UI. J01 starts it through the endpoint the UI uses and follows it in the Jobcenter UI. WP-181 only requires 'UI nutzt die API und zeigt Einzelfehler', so it is unclear (UNKLAR) whether the UI must support ≥ 100-id selections. Not reported as a defect.
2) Notifications for a fresh tenant. A new tenant has no notification_channel, and the UI has no page to create one (only schema.d.ts references /notification-channels). Notifier.Notify (backend/internal/notify/notifier.go) only delivers over the org's channels, so out of the box an export or failed job produces no in-app notification. N01 creates the in-app channel via REST. NTF-01 lists channel kinds email|sms|pager and NTF-04/UI-16 require a notification center, but no requirement says an in-app channel must exist by default. UNKLAR, not asserted.
3) Bulk job completion notifications. NTF-05 promises only 'Export fertig' and 'Job fehlgeschlagen', not bulk success, so no bulk-success notification was expected. 'Job fehlgeschlagen' could not be triggered: runBulk never fails as a whole.
4) Cancel of a running job in the Jobcenter is not covered: the bulk job of 100 ids finishes in about 1 s and exports in milliseconds. Only the 409 for cancel or revert of a finished job is covered. Bulk revert (BLK-02) is P2; per E-25 only the 409 is asserted.
5) ci.bulk jobs run in an in-process goroutine (backend/internal/ci/bulk.go: go s.runBulkJob) rather than through the NATS work queue (JOB-01/WP-130). Resuming after a server restart cannot be tested without restarting the shared stack, which is forbidden.
6) Saved views within one org are not covered. A private view of another user in the same org (404) and role sharing (shared_with_roles) need a second user in the same org; only cross-tenant isolation is covered. There is no UI filter builder (SRC-03 click builder is P2), so the view is created from a preset.
7) Export scope: WP-035 criterion 3 (a client-scoped user's export contains no other client) needs a client-scoped user and is not covered; tenant-level isolation is. DATEV and JSON exports are not covered.
8) Egress at dispatch time is not covered. DNS rebinding, IP pinning and up to 3 re-checked redirects (SEC-08) need a hostname that resolves to a private IP (external DNS, blocked here). Save-time validation checks literal IPs plus localhost/.local/.internal names; DNS names that resolve privately pass the save check by design and are left to the dialer.
9) Permission checks (ci:write for bulk, job:read, export:run) with restricted roles are not covered here (roles-authz spec).
10) Side observation, not asserted: the server's /metrics label reticora_http_request_duration_seconds{path=...} contains raw resource ids, e.g. /api/v1/jobs/<uuid>, which means unbounded label cardinality.

It does not check that request paths use the request scope (OrgWideScope or WithSystem in a handler path is not flagged; e.g. webhook RotateSecret), and it does not cover database.Connect (*sql.DB, currently dead code).
